On the other hand, if you were to punish a student in front of everybody, your plan is very likely to back-fire. I, as a student, know that lots of people consider being punished as being "cool". I am not sure why, but that is the case with this generation. Instead of making the punishments worse and worse, I think we should attack their weakness--and by weakness, I mean jealousy.
When I was in fifth grade, our teacher gave the best rewards we could ever imagine. Sometimes it was milk tea drinks, and sometimes it was milk tea drinks, and sometimes it was the latest and coolest toy in the world. Either way, it always got the naughtier ones jealous. As we grew up over the years, I found that even they started to behave well, just for the sake of the rewards. By the end of our second year, our teacher had to order drinks for the entire class.
In conclusion, I would like to say that from my personal experience of being a student, I find that rewarding students is always better than punishing them, and I truly believe that through rewarding them, we can make them better.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are a lot of ways for teachers to lead their students to better learnings. Some use punishment, but some use rewards. In Taiwan, students are often hard to teach, so I prefer using harsh punishments.
Teachers have the duties to make their students love to go to school and learn in the most efficient way. By doing this, there should be rules in the class. These rules must be clear and fair. Students can even make the rules themselves if they are willing to follow them. Also, punishments of making serious mistakes should be written down clearly. Or else, students would think they are jokes and won't take them seriously. People may think that students are naive and don't deserve any punishments. Unfortunately, this is not what we see at schools.
Students have started to get evil since junior high schools. Simple rules cannot lead them to the correct path. Then, teachers should use more harsh punishments to control their behaviors and learning attitudes. I think rewards are required, but not too much. Students should be able to know and do things which are correct. That is the reason why they are studying at schools. It's very important to give students the correct thoughts of the society. They have to know the evil part of the world when they are still young, in order to prevent bad things happening afterwards.
Private schools always get better scores and attitudes. Students there are more polite and happy. Why? "Disciplines," said the principle. We need disciplines in Taiwan to movitate students' learning. Imaginations, organizations, and other important skills come from the punishments after failing. Education can be better if teachers can control the thinkings of students to lead them to the right way.
Without disciplines, private schools are nothing but a very expensive place to learn. Students will be joyful to taste the success after a lot of pains. Effective learning is very important, and it cannot be without punishments.

subject: HW1001
content:
All the teachers hope that their students can learn well and have good behaviors. Thus, some teachers use punishment to force their students to learn or to behave better; while others use gentle ways such as rewarding students for learning. I think that rewarding students will be better than punishing them.
Because of not getting punishment, some students will act well. Nonetheless, some students can't act well, they will feel bad when they get punish some will even live in a pesimisstic life. Thus, punishment won't be a good way to let students learn well.
Rewarding students for learning can let students have confident to themselves. When I was only seven, I often got C on my tests. One day I got B+ in math, my teacher gave me a chocolate and encourged me to do better. After all, I was interested in math and got A everytime! Therefore, I think rewarding will lead to better results.
Punishment can force students to learn; however, rewarding will not only make students learn, but also make them interested in learning. Therefore, teachers should reward students when they act well instead of punishing them when they don't do well.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are always pros and cons. Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn while others believe that rewarding students can lead to better results. In my opinion, I believe both are effective, but rewarding is more effective way. Professor Amabile at Harvard University did a research and indicated the intrisic motivation can be more effective than extrisic motivation. And she stated that proper rewarding can be viewed as a bonus to promote ones intrisic motivation.
However, some people may argue that punishment works when educating some lazy students. Thats true but I thought its just kind of short-term effect. Students can only learn when they want to learn in the long run. I was a teacher and had more than one hundren students. My belief drove me to teach them in positive way. And it did work. Everyone can be encouraged and improved, even the worse one, in positive mothod.
"Behaviors repeat when behaviors reinforced." Someone said that. I thought its to the point. Thus, I would say that rewarding is a better way.

subject: HW1001
content:
Teacher have many way of motivating students to work harder. Basicly, I distict them into two sections, punishing and rewarding. I personally prefer rewarding, but there are definantly some pros and cons.
In the past, teachers do have the right to punish students by spanking or yelling at them and by this, they did learn well. But the motivation toward learing wasn't for themselves, they didn't have passion toward learing. It was a serious problem, but people thought "oh well, they've learned well."
As for myself, I had a math teacher once, he was very nice that teaching math wasn't what he was really doing, but trying to make us love math. He designed games for us and we has easier questions on tests. I suddenly realized maybe math wasn't what I thought it was, because it was "fun". My teacher inspired me to learn math better by his encouragement and the funs we had during class.
Rewarding students for what they've done helps more because the last thing students like to do is being pushed. Rewarding is like playing computer games, you try to pass the first level and when you do, you gain one more life and go to the second level. When you don't pass the level, so what, try again! The price is alway there waiting for you to grab on, it's just how much effort you put in, how resposable you are to yourself. In conclusion, rewarding student for good attendance or participation is more effective than punishing student for bad behavior.

subject: HW1001
content:
School is always another home for children. They learn, meet new friends, know how to communicate with others and so on. Teachers are like their parents They teach, they guide the kids to the right path. But how? Do the teachers punish students to get them to higher level? Or they reward them with improvements and lead the students step by step?
In my own opinion, I prefer the method of rewarding students. We always learn from mistakes and we need to have a change. Teachers are the stairs who lead us to be higher. Their inspirations can strengthen one's confidence, and their encouragements can heighten one's success. Teachers teach with love and are to help students find their interests and unlimited imaginations. Despite the results wouldn't come out so quickly as punishing children, but the effects no doubt will be better
Erin Gruwell, a famous teacher in Long Island, New York She taught in a high school with different skin colors, backgrounds and most of them were in gangs or gun fights. At first she thought blaming students of punishing them would keep them listening in class, but she was wrong. Those students were harmed in the deepest of their heart, so she started to guide them to a whole new life Gruwell gave them a journal to write about their lives. She found out thousands of gangs, fights, drugs marked in journals, that gave her more power to the faith of changing them
She bought them a book "The diary of Anne Frank" and taught them about how unfair of the little girl's blood; and arranged a party about "Toast for a change". Gruwell wanted the students to share how they plan for their future. At the end of the senior life, she published their journals as a book and let them know they were all heros of themselves.
Conclude all my words, I support that the teachers should reward, encourage students to brighten their lives!

subject: HW1001
content:
In the past, teachers used to motivate students to study or change students' behavior through punishment. Today, with more and more people against this way of teaching, rewarding students for learning seems to be the main policy.
It goes without saying that both ways can make students study more. However, I still think that rewarding students for learning is the better way. If one can get some rewards after studying hard, he or she will definitely try the best. More important, this behavior is truly motivated by their heart. If a person studies for fear of being punished, then it is just fear that lies in the person's motivation.
When I was in junior high school, my teacher always gave us a little card after we got a high score. In the end of the semester, we could use the little cards to exchange some rewards. Because of the rewards, everyone studied hard and did the best in every tests. Thus after graduating, all of our class got into ideal senior high schools. Consequently, I think that rewarding students for learning might be the better and more effective way of teaching.

subject: HW1001
content:
Students are like plants waiting to be fertilized. Teachers are the patient gardeners which are responsible to offer the nutrients and the water for plants to flourish. Without a doubt, teachers should treat students with love and patience. The compliments they give to students are strong motivations for them to persue higher goals. So I think rewarding students for learning can be effective.
Here is a case in point. When I studied in elementary school, I was too clumsy and introverted to reach out to others. But my teacher kept encouraging me and giving me some tips to speak in public. She also promised that if I can open my mind to chat with others, she will bring me to amusement park. I was inspired by the reward, and plucked up my courage to speak loudly. Finally, I became an active person in the class, and also fulfilled the dream of playing in amusement park.
Without my teacher's reward and encouragement, I can not be talktive and extroverted now. The magical power of the rewards from teachers is effective for learning obviously.

subject: HW1001
content:
Giving punishment to students or not has always been a controversial topic in Taiwan, and there are always debates on the balance between students right and teaching efficiency. In my opinion, I am in favor of giving students punishment instead of rewarding. Since the past few decades, the concerning authorities has been promoting the teaching style of love and compliments. However, news of spoiled children joining the gansters and consuming drug occur more and more frequent nowadays. There are even some students trying to bully their classmates, teachers as well as their family. I suggest that these serious consequece might be result from the classroom being rid of scold, lecture, and punishment. Punishment to a proper content can stimulate students sense of responsibility, and thus motivate them to study harder and perform better behavior.
I firmly believe that proper stimulus can help boost students motivation, and I think that a more solumn classroom with a little punishment can lead to a better society in Taiwan.

subject: HW1001
content:
The issue of whether to have punishment in schools have been extensively discussed recently. Punishment can be regarded as a negative enhancement, while rewarding is one type of positive enhancements. Both are somehow effective to teaching and learning; however, it is still worth thinking that which one is more suitable for our education circumstance.
In my opinion, rewarding is a more effective way to help students with their learning. As a universaty students, I have several tutor experiences. It turns out that every time I gave rewards to my tutees, they did well on their studies. No matter it is oral rewardings or just a gift, students feel satisfied as they have achieved something well once they receive compliments from others. Hence, their self-confidence gained and it leads them do better on the next task.
On the other hand, according to the newsreport, there are so many problems caused by giving punishment in schools. For example, parents may get worried if their children are treated by unhuman ways; therefore, they sue the teacher and the school, which leads to serious problems and unnecessary tension.
In conclusion, rewarding really does effectively when it comes to education, but we should keep in mind not to misuse or overuse it. Becides rewarding, sometimes appropriate punishments are still needed. Most important of all, making students not to be afraid of learning and help them gain more interests in school is the priority thing which really matters.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think puninishments are rewarding should be adopted together and both of them have the pros and cons.
If teachers use punishments, some students will be afraid and think punishments are painful things. Therefore, they will supervise themselves to study hard. Also, students will think that being punished is a very shameful thing, so they will become much more diligent. However, overusing punishments will cause adverse effects. For instance, students will not be afraid any more and they will think it is not a big deal to be punished.
If teachers use the rewarding way to inspire students to study hard, I think it can make students much more confident and students will be proud of themselves. Thus, they will continue to study hard. Even they can have a big influence on others and encourage them to study. One of my example is that I win the first prize on the exam and I get the reward. Afterthat, I keep studying hard. So I think rewarding is a good way to motivate me to be diligent.
In conclusion, punishments and rewarding should be used in moderately. Then, it will cause the good effects.

subject: HW1001
content:
One says, "Spare the rod, spoil the children." This thought is still very common in our education system. Some teachers support this idea beccause they think children are always naughty and lazy. If teachers don't punish them, they will never behave well and make progress. In my point of view, I totally disagree this idea about any kind of punishment. As teachers, they should be patient with children. If they do anything wrong, teachers should point out and tell them in an understandable way. Punishment is useless because children are too young to understand the reason why you punish them. Conversely, not only physical but mental punishment turn out to be a huge wound in children's mind. Besides, all the teachers should respect their students no matter how old they are. Teachers don't have the right to punish students in a hurting way. They should correct their behavior and encourage them to do better and better.
Take myself for instance, one of my teachers in elementary school did so. She had a rod that other teachers frequently borrowed. She hit those who behaved badly in class, especially boys. Consequently, they became worse because they were not afraid of the pain. They even thought of punishment as a way to show off their courage. The whole things made me think in a different perspective that punishment is definitely not the best choice. In contrast, I appreciate another teacher's way. When we made mistakes, he taught us to take responsibilites and encourage us to solve the problems independently. Furthermore, he told us to remind each other when we almost lost ourselves. Therefore, I think rewarding, including giving students compliments and encouragments, or some gifts is better and more effective than punishing them.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are two methods to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. One is using punishment, anothe one is to reward students. In my opinion, rewarding students is more effective than using punishment, because when the teachers who use punishment will not only hurt the students' bodies, but also hurt their inside hearts. As a result, the students may be afraid of going to school and have a great pressure when testing or studying. Secondly, rewarding students can help them setting a goal to achieve. Students are more willing to study. After having the great grades, they will feel happy and have accomplishment not just be afraid to be punished. Finally, there are some bad students, if the teachers want to punish them, they will swear the bad words or threaten the teachers.
There are some examples to support my opinion. I remembered in my childhood I was punished by a teacher and my body left lots of wounds, I felt very painful, angry, and scared. At the same time, I didn't want to study anymore, because I thought if I took a bad grade, teachers should cheer me up and patiently teach me instead punishing me. Nowadays, there are many news on TV, the teachers are sued by students because of punishment. To sum up, it's ok for teachers to use little punishment. I think awarding students can really motivate students.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I consider rewarding students for learning is more effective than using punishment to motivate students to learn. Every one likes to do things which they are interested in and can have fun from. Therefore, if we want to encourage students to learn, we have to make them enjoy doing so. Rewarding students to learn can awaken their sense of pride and accomplishment. Once students have good experience on study, they will be more willing to do it. On the contrary, punishment only makes students scared. Students might get good grades out of stress and unwillingness, without any passion of learning. That's why I prefer rewarding to punishment.
Mary and Cindy are my friends. Mary performed well on study while Cindy didn't. However, Mary's parents were still strict to her and forced her to study harder. Cindy's parents encourage Cindly a lot, rewarding her once she advanced. Now, Mary and Cindy are both college students. In the free circumstances, Mary gets rid of learning, while Cindy enjoys absorbing new knowledge. Encouraging students is really better than punishing them.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students for learning would be a better choice for teachers. Punishing students in the class sometimes makes bad effect on children, which is unexpected for teachers.
I think a teacher should reward students instead of blaming them. Taking me as an example, when I was an elementary school student, our homeroom teacher always encouraged us to speak out our idea about what we were learning. In the science class, all of us came up with different kinds thought to do expirements. My teacher never rejected us, and she made us use our creativity at most. Because of her teaching, one of my classmates is good at physics researching in his university now. We all appreciated our teacher's encouragement.
Another case is my brother. He is going to take the entrance exam for the college. But because he is always taught by strict teachers. They disappointed him very much. One of his teacher used a mothed that is hitting students. The lower grade they got, the severe punishment they had. This experience made my little brother hate studying. He feels frustrated and wants to give up! However, our family try hard to tell him studying is important and he doesn't have to meet his teacher's expectation. To do his best is all he needs to do.
My brother and I have totally different prespective of studying, due to our different kinds of teachers. When we were young, we built self-confidence. If teachers could give us some encouragement properly, we would be braver to move on. So I think rewarding students would be more effective. Students grow up so much with punishment as with encouragement.

subject: HW1001
content:
It is very apparent that teachers affect students. But, in a good way or a bad way? It depends on how the teacher teaches. Most use punishments to motivate their students, while few use rewards. But I believe rewards are better than punishments.
Why do I believe so? Because I've been on the receiving end of both methods of teaching, and rewards worked a lot better for me. Giving students praises and pats on the head encourages them to do what they did to receive the special attention again. Punishments, on the other hand, discourages them to do what they did wrong but does nothing to help them improve. Therefore, I conclude that rewards are better than punishments.
I can actually prove this with something that happened on me. I've been the representative for our school in the Spelling Bee twice, once in second grade and once in fourth grade. In second grade, m language arts teacher asked me to memorize thirty words each day, and she tested me on them the next day. When I got over five wrong, she would make me fill a whole page with the words I spelled incorrectly. That year, I got ninth place. Then in fourth grade, my teacher would give me a piece of my favorite chewing gum whenever I got full points on the tests. When I got something wrong, she would just chide me to be more careful next time. That year, I was in fourth. To me, that was a notable difference, so I can say with confidence that rewards are the victor in this match.
Rewards or punishments, students who are clear of what they want or what they need to do should not be influenced by what they receive. Dreams are far too big to be destroyed by a mere teacher. So, no matter how terrible the consequence of a failed quiz may be, we shouldn't be bothered by a lecture or scolding but continue to look at the bigger picture and make our dreams come true.

subject: HW1001
content:
Whether using punishment to teach students or not is a big issue recently. When I turn on the TV, teachers are accused of punishing children in a wrong way are often in the media who spotlight.
What do I think about these teachers' behavior? As far as I am concerned, rewarding students for learning is much better than using punishment to motivate them. Because it is the compliment that can really raise students' interest in learning. When I get my teachers' praises, such as "Wow! You did a good job!" or "Well-done, girl.", I would be very happy all day. Even though I am not good at some subjects, if my teachers encourage me, I would try my best to learn that subject.
Take my sister for another example. When she was four years old, her kindergarten teacher would punish her because of her bad temper. She always went to school reluctantly in the morning. Finally, she couldn't put up with her teacher's strict behavior at all. As a result, she quitted her school.
To sum up, I think rewarding students is a better idea to raise their motive to learn. By doing so, students are more likely to gain their confidence and they can easily find out that learning is a lot of fun!

subject: HW1001
content:
Education, in my opinion, is the most important field that the government should focus on. The main character of education are students. When it comes to cultivate the useful social elites, teachers play the important role. In the past, undoubtedly, teachers tended to punish students whenever they did some bad behaviors, but the most common sight was that when the students got bad grades, teachers would take out their sticks, bit on the students' hand, and told the students that you should work harder.
Nowadays, physical punishment is banned in Taiwan, teachers are never allowed to use sticks. By contrast, teachers tend to encourage students. When you get bad grades, teachers will pat your head and tell you "It's ok! Keep working hard!"
As far as I'm concerned, due to I had experienced the two different style of instruction, I prefer the latter, and I think it's more effective. When I was eight years old, in the elementary school I met a teacher who was very strict. If my grades couldn't meet his expectation, my hands would suffer lots of pain. Therefore, I really hated to attend school that time. However, now I met a great teacher in senior high school. She always encourages her student and gives us confidence, making we all think that we can conquer every difficulties.
Now I'm facing an important exam, when I am confusing, doubting my own ability and even want to give up, it is my teacher who gives me confidence and tells me "You can make it!" It really helps me a lot.
That is what I think education should be. A teacher shouldn't confine students only to pursue good grades. There are still many values that are worth pursuing!

subject: HW1001
content:
I do not agree with the method of punishing students in order to control their behavior or to motivate them. I think rewarding and encouraging students is what should be done.
I have studied abroad before, in America. Therefore, I know pretty well just how much you can get from a student by encouraging them, and by punishing them. When I was in Taiwan, the teachers were all very strict. If I did not get an A on my test, I would be punished by my teacher with a wooden stick. Even though it hurts to be hitted by a wooden sitck, I still did not improve on my test, neither did my classmates.
When I studied abroad, the teachers were all very nice and encouraging. They did not punish me when I didn't get an A on my test. In fact, they awarded me because I improved my grades from C to B.
I am a very shy person. Whenever I am called on stage to make a speech, I become speechless. I think this is partly because the experience I had with my discouraging teacher and classmates. The first time I went up on stage, classmates laughed and pointed at me. So I didn't complete my speech and was even punished by my teacher. But when I studied abroad, the teacher and classmates there applaused for me and encouraged me, that gave me a lot of self confidence and even made me a happier person.
If you punish students instead of rewarding and encouraging them, they will lose self confidence and they wouldn't be happy students. That is why I prefer to reward students, if I ever have any. This is my experience: reward a person because no one likes to be punished!

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, many TV news report that some teachers punish students which causes the student's heart to be hurt. This aroused many people and experts debate on which way is the best way for teaching students.
In my point of view, when we teach students, there still needs moderate punishment. If we just always reward student or praise them instead of punish them, it will make students be more arrogant or selfish. They won't realize what is wrong of their behavior. They will think they are the best. Like adults, if we don't be punished, we'll never know which behavior is acceptable in our sociaty.
For example, some junior high school students could smoke, fight or skip the class. If we don't give them punishment and let them know they are doing wrong behavior, they will do those behavior more often. Students would be afraid of being punished, so use some moderate punishment can lead a better result.
To sum up, I think using punishment to improve students' behavior and learning will be more effective than rewarding them. Although punishment could hurt some students' feelings, there still have to build up some punishments to tell all students what to do and what not to do. These rules or punishments are important things to help teachers to teach students. When students grow up, they will obey the laws like they did when they were students. Our education will be success on teaching students well for their good behavior and learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
Everytime when I turn on TV and watch news, their almost some kind of news talking about school teacher punished their students or even worse, they hitted their students! Is punishment better than rewarding? or maybe punishment is necessary for teacher to teach student how to control their behavior.
In my opinion, both punishment and rewarding are necessary. All we must to do is to take balance between punishment and rewarding. We can not seperate one of other. We have to tell students why they can not act like chating, fighting and so on. If they did listen to your advices, you can give them some rewarding, but if they did not, you have to give them some punishment to motivate student to learn and to control their behavior.
I have many experience about how my teacher punish and reward me. I was a bad student in my high school year. I got into trouble almost every day like fighting, smoking, and so on. But when I have troble, my teacher will told me seriously not to make the same mistake again. And next time if I get into the same trouble, she will blame at me or even yielled at me, and told my monther what I did. But if I did not make the same mistake at the same situation, she would reward me. I think it is the best example in my life. Why punishment and rewarding can not been used together?

subject: HW1001
content:
To punish or to reward students is a big educational problem nowadays. The government has made a law to ban corporal punishment; however, this does not mean that teachers cannot use any other forms of punishment to deal with naughty students. To me, I think punishing is still the more effective way to educate students.
Educating is like gardening. Farmers not only have to water and fertilize the plants, but also need to trim the unnecessary branches. Meanwhile, teacher have to use punishment to control students' behavior in addition to reward them. Some students are education-refused, they cannot behave themselves well or get better academic performance. Punishing is a good way to control those students' manners, letting them know that it is their obligation to receive education, no matter on school work or behavior aspects.
To those despicable students, the law of non-corporal punishment is just an alibi to avoid any punishment. They are indulgent, disturbing the discipline of the whole class. Teachers must have some rights to modify those students' behavior. I don't think rewarding is useful in this case.
If education is like cooking, rewarding will be sugar, making students feel sweet and happy. Too much sugar will paralize their tastes. Punishment will be salt; however, we still cannot add too much to the dish. Both of the educational ways are equally necessary, but we should use either of them in different situations.

subject: HW1001
content:
Rewarding students for learning would be a better method in my opinion. First, we are human beings, not wild animals which should be tamed. That means, we can handle our both emotion or behavior on our own. Frankly speaking, punishment may work at beginning but will definitely fail in the long run. Because no one wants to be controlled, and the lack of encourage will build a wall which makes students hard to access the pleasure in learning.
Second, mood is important of all. Seldom do we finish something perfectly in bad mood. That is, staying in good spirits will help us achieve best situation.
Take my younger sister for example. She did not performed well in learning when she just entered high school. After I realized that, I have begun to assist her with care and encourage instead of scold. And at proper timing, I would provide her some comfort and reward with snacks or new-brand accessories. Finally, she won the first prize in the last exam, and I was glad about that. Whatsmore, this proves my method really works.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the old generations in Taiwan, teachers used punishment to motivate students to learn. But in the recent years, teachers have led children to better results by rewarding them. I'm of the opinion that the second method is more effective and better for students.
I have an example can support my opinion. My classmate has a part time job to teach elementary students. She told me that when she serves some snacks or small presents like pens and notebooks before the class, her students will finish their assignments quickly and do well on quizes. Therefore, I think motivate students in such way is more effective.
I think the factor of this successful case is giving a goal to let students want to attain. It is more positive than using punishment. Children may study hard to avoid punishment but it also make them be afraid and have bad effects on their mental health.
In conclusion, I think rewarding students is more effective than using punishment. Thanks to the educated program now, the way of regarding is used more.

subject: HW1001
content:
There has been a heated debate on whether to punish students for their improper conducts. As far as I am concerned, rewarding students for learning is more effective than punishments. Punishments often lead students to worry about being scolded. Those who often get punished for their behavior may be intimidated and become less confident. Worst of all, they might bear a grudge against their teachers and schools. They think teachers just like to pick on them.
On the other hand, if we take the correct method, namely to reward students for learning, can help improve their self-esteem and establish their sense of achievement.
Take myself for example, I spilled water on my textbooks in class when I was seven. Nervous and anxious, I took out the tissues from my drawer to soak up the water. Noticing this my teacher walked straight toward me. To my surprise she didn't scold me for the mess I made. Instead, she gave me a verbal praise about my quick wit to the problem on my own. I felt really proud then. So I think rewarding students for learning is a better method to employ.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some say punishment is the best way to make perfect performance in a short time for a student. Others say encouragement has far more better effect than punishment. As for my opinion, I think praises and rewards work better.
When I was still in elementary school, I had a mean techer who always punished students when they got bad grades. It seemed to work at the first place, the ones been punished usually got better grades next time. But then, when they forgot about how hurt it was to be punished, they went back again. And the next semester, we got a new teacher, she never said anything discouraging. She always praised the students that performed well and encourage those who could not catch up with the average students. What she did made every student thought they were still valuable even though they might not be that smart. The average grade of the whole class rised, but that did not mean that much for us anymore. The point is, we all found our self-confidence by her complements.
Rewarding and praising students may not have the instant effect. But in the long run, it is better than punishment not only for learning and behaving good, but also help to build their personality healthly.

subject: HW1001
content:
As far as I'm concerned, I think that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.
I think I have two reasons why I consider this method. First, rewarding students for learning encourages not only the students who usually get good grades, but also those who get poor grades. Take my school for example. Before we have an extrance exam, our school tells us that if the students reach the regulation of the grade, they can have $10,000 for each. After listening this information, we are very happy because everyone has opportunity to get the money if we work hard. Second, rewarding students for learning can give students the confidence of learning. Because if teachers usually punish the students who don't get good grade, the students may be afraid of learning and escape the class.
So, with this two viewpoints, I believe that rewarding students for learning can motivate students most.

subject: HW1001
content:
In schools, teachers use two methods to get the students' attention. One is punishment, and the other is rewarding. Compare to the two methods, I think rewarding is more effective way to lead to better results. There are some reasons to support my point of view.
First of all, people like to be treated nicely. When the teacher praise the students' attitude toward schoolwork, they will feel accomplished and are willing to do better next time. However, if teacher punish student in front of the class, he or she may feel embarrased and ashamed. For example, when I was in elementary school, my teacher used to punish the students by using the sticks. Therefore, many students were not only losing the motivation of learning, but also afraid of going to school. The problem was going worse and worse until we changed a new teacher. She always has a smile on her face, and often encourage students to try their best. What's more, she often give some candies to students who improve a little bit as a reward. My classmates and I like her teaching very much. Therefore, I think rewarding is more suitable than punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the past, we often heard about the teachers used severe punishments to punish students if they didn't do well on tests, but it is prohibit today. So teachers tend to reward students or talk to them patiently if they have better or worse performance.
As a student, in my opinion, punishment is just punishment, it doesn't solve the real problem, also punishment can sometimes lead to bad results. So why do I think the rewarding way is more effective?
My math teacher in junior high used punishment if we didn't do well on tests, however, my class' grade didn't really improve, in contrast, a year later he changed his way of treating us, it was encouragement and rewardings and it really changed my class' a better learning results, hence I support the idea that rewarding students.

subject: HW1001
content:
I believe that rewarding students for learning is more effective. I will elaborate my opinion by comparing my learning experiences on Biology and Chinese.
My Biology teacher is a great believer that punishment is the only way to push one to learn, but my Chinese teacher thinks that to find the interest in learning is most important. Thus, the learning routine in Biology class is teaching, memorizing, testing, and "love hand." Being hit by "Love hand," quoted from Biogrophy teacher, "Students can sense the love of learning." However, in fact Biology becomes the hatest subject to my classmates, we know nothing about the meaning to learn it, but we memorize it to avoid being hit. On the contrary, my Chinese teacher spreads the learning love diffrently. In class, we have theme-and-task oriented courses. She divides the texts into diffrent themes. For example, in the Romance theme, each of us has the task to note down love poems, from ancient to present, to give people we love. When copying by hand, and reading it again and again, we can sense the emotion of poems. Now, many of us are determined to take Chinese as major.
Hence, from my own experiense, I believe that instead of harshly punishing, spiritually rewarding is more effective to motivate students' learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
Different students have different attitude for studying. Therefore, we should use different methods to help the students to get their interesting on learning and study more efficiently and happily. Accordingly, what kinds of methods is more effective depend on what kind of student you teach.

If you teach a student who is lazy and everything he or she think is playing, it is more useful by using the punishment and being more serious. Take my college's child for example, he is just third grade in elementary school. One day, I taught him math and he told me he can't do this question. However, he didn't look at the question actually and want me just to give him the answer. Therefore, I took my pocker face and asked him to look at the question. After he finishing seeing the question, he fround he can do this question and apologized his attitude of studying for me. Indeed, he is not a stupid student, so I need to be more solemn to justify his study habits.

On the contrary, if the student you teach is active and care about the performence on their study, the most important thing for you to teach is to reward him or her and praise them frequently. Take myself for example, I am a person who needs other people's agreement to get the confidence then I can do jobs better and better. Therefore, if my teacher encourage me and say that I can do it well, I would study as best as I could to prove my ability to my teacher. Accordly, it is more effective to teach a active student by rewarding.

All in all, we can't just justify whether a student is good or not by only see the grades on study. We should find out different ways suit different students to help them to be successful on different stages in their life.

subject: HW1001
content:
Since the ancient times, scholars and teachers have been argueing on the issue that which is the better method to educate students. Some believe in using punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others use rewards to encourage students to lead them to a better development.
In my point of view, I consider rewarding students for learning is more effective. Here are the few reasons. To begin with, there is a theory from psychologists' report. Students tend to accept the advice more willingly when their teachers use encouraging words to advise them. Secondly, as a high school student, whenever the teacher gives praises to me or rewards me for some presents, I would always be very joyful and tell myself to do even better next time. Last but not least, punishments, whichever physically or mentally, are often turning out to be a harm to students. They will be scared, shameful and nervous but learn nothing.
Though there is an old saying, "Spare the rods, spoil the kids.", but just take a look at how many disadvantages it has, and we will believe that always use positive ways to encourage students is the best choice.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think punishment more effective, because some students ignore the rewarding and still don't learn. Only punishment can force them to reach maturity. But the priority is that the punishment must be appropiate so that students can really learn a lesson from it.
Take my class for example. My teacher, Ms. Lee, pays a lot of attention to her students' behavior more than their grades. She puts emphasis on our attitude toward responsibility. Once, my classmate didn't do the job of cleaning, and Ms. Lee immediately gave punishment. Then the student never neglected the job. If someone is late for class, he or she will be asked to do something related to the whole class, such as washing the trash can or cleaning the classroom. Such punishment is so useful that the students' bad behavior can be corrected. My teacher never hits or beats her students, only using her way to teach us.
To sum up, proper punishment is good to control students' behavior. sometimes people don't care about the rewarding at all, so only punishment could remind them of their duty and stop them from making the same mistake again.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teacher believe that punishment can make their students study hard, while others don't think so. Teachers who use punishment to motivate students believe that students will afraid of the punishment and will study harder to escape the punishment. Those who encourage students instead of punish them believe that students who study in a friendly enviroment will have better grade. Both of the opinion are reasonable, however, in my opinion, I prefer rewarding students instead of punishing students.
I think study is student's top priority, it can make your future brighter. Getting into a great school means that you have more opportunity to find a good job and have more money, so the student should study hard. Nevertheless, if you use punishment to force the student to study, they will not be happy and will forget that study is their responsibility. If you encourage the student by rewarding them, they will know that study is good for them and they will willing to study, or even like to study.
Take myself for example, when I was in elementary school, I always got thirty to forty foints on the exam, and everytime I got a bad grade, my teacher would punished me in front of my classmate, and that really made me embrassed. Because of that, I hated school when I was young, and I always thought study was a horrible thing. Luckily, I met a good teacher in my senior high school, she always encourages me to study, even I got fifty on the exam, she still told me that I could be better. When I gratuated from school, I got into a good school, and it was all because of the teacher made me not afraid of study. Because of my experience, I believe that rewarding students is much better than punishing students.

subject: HW1001
content: Some teachers punish students more than they reward them, while some do exactly the opposite. As for me, I would prefer teachers who use punishment. Well goes the saying, "Strict teachers bring about good students." My teacher in elementary school was a strict woman. She never wore smiles on her face. Every single student in our class was afraid of her due to her unfriendly appearance and the high frequency of her losing her temper. However, thanks to her, we were the best class in the entire school. All teachers that had our class liked us for our awesome behavior. One year later, the teacher was replaced, for some parents couldn't stand her anymore and thus launched a protest. The school replaced her with a really nice-tempered man as our homeroom teacher. The class then went bad day by day, for the teacher was too "nice" to us. Some people even skip classes without being punished! How ridiculous! As a result, due to my own experience, I strongly suggest that teachers use punishment often. It's without a doubt the best method to motivate students to behave themselves.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think rewarding students for learning is more effective than punishing them. As students, we are usually longing for the praise and encouragement from teachers as well as our parents. I believe every student is kind-hearted. If teachers reward students to motivate them to learn, they will feel confident and have more incentives to move on. However, I think punishing is the last way to motivate students. It can only solve a few problems such as punctuality, laziness, but can not change their attitude completely. If punishing too hard, students will feel disappointed with themselves and show no interest in striving for excellence.
For example, the government have gradually called for the love of Education instead of punishment in recent years. Also, many organizations dealing with student affairs are devoted to the right of students. It is obvious that punishment is out of fashion in the modern age. Many statistics show that students lead to better results by rewarding them Take the more concrete example, my English teacher at school always reward those who don't have good grades in English by letting them choose whom they want to sit with to ask questions. This makes them feel not being neglected and want to pay more attention to their schoolwork. To sum up, I think that we cannot overemphasize the benefit from rewarding and encouraging students.

subject: HW1001
content:
When students are naughty or do something wrong, a few teachers still punish them though punishing is illegal now. I think when students behave badly, rewarding students for learning is better than giving them punishments. Why?
Because if teachers punish their students, that the function is just frighten them from doing bad things again. Students won't do it again just depend on the memories of being punished. If teachers aren't by their sides, students might behave badly again.
Rewarding students for learning has more influence on them. Giving them memories of encouragement is better than leaving them memories of punishment. Being different from giving students punishment, rewarding students count on moral education for students. It stops them from being badly because of their own willing but not the fear of being punished. In this way, students will still behave well though teachers are not in front of their faces.
If a student does wrong, a teacher can comfort him and encourge him to do better next time. It won't hurt his feelings and it will surely do him good.

subject: HW1001
content:
As a teacher, it is inevitable to motivate students' learning by some methods. Which method is more effective, in my opinion, depends on time.
When students just enter school, I think teachers should use punishment as a way to regulate or to force students to pay more attention to their studies and behavior. But the punishment can't be too severe. The purpose of punishment is that students should know they are wrong.
However, punishment can't make students learn positively. So, after a period of time, when students can control their behavior, teachers should help students' learning in an encouraging way. With encouragement, students will have confidence in themselves and are willing to learn more. Those who get high grades after exams usually have positive learning attitude and have a desire to learn a lot.
If there were no punishment, students' behavior would be out of control and there would be more school bullies and violence. Nevertheless, without encouragement, students might lose confidence and stop learning. How to balance the two methods in teaching properly is an issue worth considering carefully.

subject: HW1001
content:
I had a great friend of mine in junior high school who never turned in homework and don't even mention getting good grades on exams. Studying was the last thing he would like to do, and it even got worse when our teacher decided to make him stand in the back of the classroom during class every time he failed to fulfill her expactation. Later on his mother thought of an idea of giving him allowence if he had his homework done. Though it sounded like a way for motivating children, to my surprise, it actually worked on him. Because of the reward his mother offered, he even tried to put more efferts on studying.
I believe that rewarding is a more effective method to motivate student to learn or to control their behavior. The only way for a student to improve is that he or she is willing to do it. Since they are attracted to the results they get if they work hard, they will surely be glad to do it. Rewarding is the first step and it's like a power to start a machine. Once they get on track, they will be able to keep running and to work hard to improve and achieve their goals of learning without pushing.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are many ways to let students learn more effectively. Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn while others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, I think the later method is more effective. Besides, the students will learn out of their free will instead of being afraid of punishment.
For example, my teacher rewarded me because I progressed on my schoolwork. Next time, I will try my best to have good grades and hope my teacher will like my work. On the contrary, if my teacher would punish me when I didn't do well in a test, I will try to reach the line my teacher set in the next time. However, I may hate my teacher and hate learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think we should maintain the current situation--giving punishments. But I don't really mean we should always use punishments as a mean to motive the learners to learn, but should only use it when it's necessary. And it's not necessary to be physical. At my college time I had been taking children tutoring courses while I'm specializing my degree of English Bachelor, because I want to become an English teacher. But the truth is, when you actually contacted with your new student, you'll know that sometimes you just have to call their names out loudly, with anger (which you pretend to be), in order to show them you're trying to teach them something serious. For example, playing with fire.
Like I said above, though you don't really need to punish them physically (like hit their palms), some oral tutorings are still necessary. I know your feeling, because most of the text books won't tell us these things. I know it. But if you really want to be a good teacher, then don't just give your students candy, but with some sticks!

subject: HW1001
content:
Teachers can teach their students by punishing them when they are wrong or rewarding them when they are well-behaved. The two methods above are totally different from each other, and in my opinion, to reward students is more effective than to punish them.
When I was ten years old, there was a bad boy in my class, and we called him "Bad John". He always came late, and never handed in any homework. At first, my teacher punished him when he was late by hitting his hands. However, instead of becoming a good student and not being late again, he decided to come even later, because he was mad at the teacher. The teacher was really upset, and she decided to try another method--she wanted to reward the boy instead of punishing him.
Bad John came to school at ten o'clock the next day. The teacher walked up to him and told him that she was really glad to see him, and he could get a candy if he came to school at nine the next day. That was a magic! Bad John came at eight the next day! He wasn't Bad John anymore. He was never late again!
Students needs rewards instead of punishment. Every teacher should know this, and they can become good friends with their students, their students can truly learn thing from them also.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Rewarding is not only one of the methods to motivate students to learn, and it can make students enjoy studying and be happy. Unlike rewarding, students studying in punishment are unhappy and not studying by their own. When they get old, the punishment could no longer control their behaviors. Students in rewarding will also have joy in studying in the future.
When I was in elementory school, my father promised that if I got 100 in math, he would buy me a TV game. It made me study hard and find the joy in math. In junior high school, my teacher punished me because of my bad Chinese, and then I don't like Chinese anymore. So I think that rewarding student is more effective.

subject: HW1001
content:
Every teacher has different ways to educate their students. It is reported that some people agree to use punishment rather than rewarding, and some people disagree with this opinion. In this essay, I'll discuss which way is suitable for students.
In my opinion, rewarding is better than punishment. Students will strive to achieve the goals which teachers want they to reach. For instance, if any student who answers the questions, the student can adds scores. Parents are pleased to see their children have excellent academic performance. Rewarding not only encourage students to study but also make their parents satisfied. The second example that I want to mention is teamwork. The teacher can divide students into groups. Let students have a competition with other groups. If one group does homework without any mistakes, they can get the reward. In a group, some students always don't concencrate on doing homework, but other group members can help those student to finish their homework. Rewarding is a strong motivation to let students learn from each other. The third example is self-confident. Because of personality, a few students are lack of confidence or are shy. Teacher provide an opportunity for students to get reward. This will motivate those shy students to have a chance to express their opinions in front of the whole class.
To sum up, I firmly believe rewarding is the best way for students. If teachers use punishment to let students calm down, students still don't know what is wrong based on their behavior. Moreover, most parents disagree with punishment. Rewarding is suitable for every student.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I believe that rewarding students is more effective. I think that all students have good personalities. As their teachers, we should be the lights to lead their goods showing. We encourage students and trying to be nice to them. When students understand that teachers treat them with their true mind, students will start to study hard with their whole heart. But if a teacher punish students to make good grades, students will hate that teacher. Even they still study hard to make good grades. However, it's for not being punished by teacher but not for themselves.
I'm a student studying in teacher education degree now. What I learn in my class is asking us to encourage student then blame them. "Punishment to motivate students to learn" is an education attitude which is out of time. In this society now, we need to reward students to make them know that they will get reward when they've good in learning. It's to prove, who will a 5-year-old boy like, mother who love him and give him candies or father alway hit him? The answer is easy to find. So we should throw away these unpropriated attitudes, trying to reward students to make them learning better.

subject: HW1001
content: The punishment or the reward is better? In my opinion, I think that rewarding students will be the better choice. The reason I think the second one is better is that punishment sometimes will cause the students fear to go to school or many mental problems. The first day I went to the junior high school, my homeroom teacher told us a story. She said, once upon a time, a teacher made an experiment. That teacher told A classroom's students that "All of you are the best of our school, so that you are here." Told B classroom's students that "All of you are the worst of our school, from now on, you will have lots of works to do." He always gave A class little homework to do, and always encouraged them. However, he gave lots of homework to B class, and was always unsatisified with their scores. By the end of the year, both class had the high scores, but the students in A class were cheerful and happy, the students in B class were under too much pressure and some of them even wanted to suicide. After telling this story, my homeroom teacher asked the class "Which one do you want?" No one answered, but the answer, was in our hearts

subject: HW1001
content:
I'm in favor of rewarding students for learning can lead to better results undoubtedly.
Everybody likes to be rewarded rather than be punished. While rewarding too much and often could bring about the consequence of spoiling students, it, at least, is way better than using punishment to motivate students. In addition, I really think those use punishments should be accused by law, or educate them to use disciplinary method instead.
The most disadvantage of punishment is that it would make students lose confidence, it might evince the side effects of rebelling the society or waging violences when they grow up. We can extract a multitude of cases to prove that punishment could only lead to the shadow to the students for their characteristics.
While I can't help but conduct punishment under unstopable furry at times, I regret it everytime after it happened. It is obvious that teaching students or children is improving yourselves within its process as well.

subject: HW1001
content: In the 1950s to the 1990s here in Taiwan, the kids were used to receive the punishment from teachers and regarded it as a normal action, while other countries had already banned the teachers on physical punishment. It's not until these days that this issue has been discussed. In my opinion, rewarding is more effective than punishment. In a research of a psychological center can support this point of view. They conducted a experiment toward primary school students, and used two classes to compare. The teacher of A class uses punishment instead of reward, while the teacher of B class uses encouragement to urge the students to learn. The result of this experiment is quite impressive. The students who usually receive praise and encouragement performed better on the exam than those who were always scolded by their teacher. This shows that we should always see the good side of our kids and tell them how good they are to make them feel confident, and let them grow up in happiness. Stop punishing the kids randomly, that won't do any good to them.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results and behavior. I oppose punishing our child to motivate them to study and to learn how to act good conduct. Punishing them can lead to their physical or even mental pain, which are hard to forget and can keep them away from leading a happy and healthy life.
Rewarding students is one of the best ways to motivate and encourage them. Compliments can be very effective to inspire their intelligence. For example, if a student doesn't do his assignment accurately, I firmly believe as long as we reward him or her through compliments such as "you have a very great beginning", the student will be full of confidence and try his best to improve himself and do the assignment perfectly.
In conclusion, we should reward students rather than just punish them. Students need encourgements not punishments.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, I agree the latter.
There are two reasons. First, students can not speak English very well in the begining. If they fortunately taught by a kindly teacher without punishment, they would not be afraid of speaking the foreign language. They could enjoy the classes even though they might make mistakes in spelling or grammer. Second, students have their own dignity. They feel shamed if they were punished by teachers. Then they hate to go to school. Finally they learn nothing from the teaches.
For example, my best friend, Tom, in the primary school was punished by our teacher due to forget his homework once. The teacher was so angery and punished him to stand outside. After that, Tom changed his mind to be a good student. I think it's really a pity. Another friend of mine, Judy, in junior high school was not smart then. Fortunately, she met an excellent teacher that believes rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Now Judy joined the famous colledge in Taiwan.
Therefore, do not punish students and reward them is the best way to teach.

subject: HW1001
content:
Many people are against using punishment to educate students. They think rewards are better ways to motivate them, but I think sometimes punishment is inevitable. Certainly, nobody likes to punish students, and students don't like to be punished either. However, sometimes punishment is just the best medicine to cure them.
I have heard a story. One renowned writer's children lost their transportation e-cards. Their mother, the writer's wife, was quite outrageous because it took much time to re-apply for the new cards. The writer, however, asked his children to make it on their own. He wanted his children to know how many times it takes to do. And consequently, the two kids never lost their cards again.
Students and the kids above are the same. If we still encourage them when they make mistakes, they won't really put it on their mind and still make the previous mistake again. Only punishment can teach them a lesson that not only their mistakes could cause inconvenience to others, but theirselves also spend lot of time and money to restore it.

subject: HW1001
content:
As long as we attempt to complete a project, it is necessary to have some pressure and good motivation for effective and efficient work. In my opinion, I believe students also need discipline to maintain their interest in study. But in terms of the methods we are using to teach studends the disciplines, personally I think that it should be put into practice by the means of communication, rather than punishment.
At the school now I'm attending, there are rules everywhere, but the students are willing to abide them. It is not on account of our fear toward the punishment, but we know those rules are reasonable and by controling our behaviors, those disciplines are doing good on our studies. If there are any regulations that are unreasonable, we can communicate with school and express our thoughts through the student council. As a result, students and teacher are both involved in the debate then attain concensus. In conclusion, I believe my school has offered a good example of effective communication and negotiation between pupils and school other than giving punishment to student which may leads to the lack of individuality.

subject: HW1001
content:
I prefer to rewarding students rather than just punishing and blaming them. No matter how noisy or naughty the students are, --even there are some big problems when they learn--I believe that rewarding students for learning is always the most positive way. This way gives students a chance to accept their failure and try again with confidence. It's an appropriate way to make the students have happy experience when they learn because childhood's memory would usually linger in their mind for a long time and even affect their behavior when growing up.
I'm poor at math just like a lot of people. But I think I was so lucky to meet a math teacher who had much patience and love. I was always blamed on and accepted punishment until the nice math teacher renew my attitude toward math. She never gave up, just giving me lots of acclamation when I got confused and depressed. Such a rewarding way really had an profound effect on me and my math scores. Through her rewarding, I knew I could do the impossible. Through her acclaiming, I plucked up my courage to try again.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, some of the teachers use punishment to motivate students to study hard and correct their behavior while others believe that rewarding students for learning can make them more concentrate to their studies.
I think whether to use punishment or to reward depends on the student's behavior and attitude. If the student feels regretful about what he has done and apologizes, the teacher should give him a chance. But if the student never apologizes and always thinks that he is right, the teacher ought to use some punishment to control his behavior. Most of the time, I think using punishment is more effcient than rewarding, because whatever the situation is, punishment can always fix the problem immidiately.
At my school, most of the teachers use punishment to motivate us and it really makes us study harder. My teacher always sets some punishment at the beginning of the semester because if he didn't do it, we would not concentrate during classes or do well on the exams. For example, last semester our homeroom teacher took a tour to America and another teacher took his place. The new teacher was so friendly and kind that we sometimes were not afraid to do something against the rules. It was a mess during that time. But when our teacher came back, all of us started to follow the rules again.
Using punishment is the most efficient way to make the students follow the rules. Although some of the students complain about the punishment, they are still afraid of doing something wrong. It's all because of the punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
Using punishment or rewarding students are two methods that most teachers use to motivate students to learn. In my opinion, I think rewarding students is more effective because I've seen a really effective example of using this method.
When I was in elementary school, there were a classmate who always did strange things in class and didn't hand in homework. At first, our teacher scold him and made him clean the classroom. He became angry and behaved even worse. A few weeks later, while he was still doing things that were different from other students, our teacher didn't punish him. Instead, our teacher gave him cookies when he did the right thing. The teacher also told him that if he hand in homework on time and had the behavior like others, she would give him a big gift at the end of the semester. After that, the boy behaved really normal as others and hand in homework on time.
In sum, I prefer the method of rewarding students. It's indeed more effective than the other one.

subject: HW1001
content:
The topic of how to let students learn more effectively can be approached from different points of view due to its complexity. Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. I have come to my own conclusion as well. There are two reasons why I think rewarding students is more effective.
One reason is encouragement. For example, my grades were very poor when I was in junior high school. Luckily, I had a great teacher. She always rewarded me with a box of chocolates and a big hug when I improved. This encouraged me to study hard, and now in senior high school, I am often at the top of the class.
The other reason is less pressure. Students have less pressure when rewarded than when punished. For example, my brother's teacher is very strict, and believes in punishing students when their grades are poor. This gives my brother a lot of pressure. He often studies until midnight, which is not good for his health. He had to stay at the hospital for a month because of this. When he recovered and went back to school, he couldn't catch up, and his grades got poorer still. Each of these experiences have influenced me on this issue.
In sum, rewarding students can let students learn more effectively because of the encouragement and less pressure.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think rewarding method is more effective. Although punishment may give students some positive pressure forcing them to be "excellent" or "outstanding," once they enter the society, the heaven of freedom, they will immediately become a selfish person persuing their own profit. However, rewarding can encourage students to learn how to interact with others, or divide their time to do what they consider important. Rewarding can help them build their own confidence. If students really know the advantages of good behavior, they will naturally do correct things at appropriate time. Take studying for example: although school grades are not the most important things in our lifetime, we can develop our abilities to control our behavior by preparing tests. I think a teacher shouldn't force students to study and do homework by punishment because the effects will be temporary, and students will only know how to avoid punishment, but they don't know how to apply their knowledge to their future. Nevertheless, by rewarding and encouragement, a teacher can help students develop their habits of studying, training them arrange their time independently. When developing the habits of studying, students will know how to use the knowledge and what kind of jobs they are really interested in.
Another benefit of rewarding mothed is that we can build good relationship between teachers and students. For example, I usually go back to visit my junior high school teacher, and she can always give me nice advice when I'm in adversity. The reason why we have such good relationship is that she always encouraged me, and helped me handle the problems about my future. I think a teacher is not only a provider of knowledge. A teacher should accompany the students to face every weather on the way of the life.

subject: HW1001
content:
Views are differed when it comes to the issue of whether the teachers should punish the students for improvement or not. My personal experience and actual observation of life have led me to conclude that students shouldn't be punished for improvement in their studies by teachers. Here are some reasons for why I think students shouldn't be punishment in the duration of studying.
First of all, some teachers hold the opinion the "Spare the rod, spoil the Child." As a result they teach by punishment rather than rewarding their students. At first glance, this claim appears to be somewhat convincing, but further reflection reveals that it is based on doubious assumptions. Should the children learn knowledgy only because they are afraid of being punished tomorrow if they didn't do their homework today? Should the Children absorb information not for the sake of interests but for responsibilities?
In addition, punishment could harm the children fragile mind. There's one experience my friend Eric had gone through. My friend Eric told me that he was once suffering from depression for the reason that he was punished by his junior high school teacher. Eric didn't hand in his final report on time and was humiliated by his classroom teacher in front of his classmates. After this incident, Eric had been upset and did not open his heart toward people nor any studies. Now though Eric has recovered from depression but he still deems punishment as a nightmare.
In conclusion, learning should be an interesting advanture that can enhance a child's creativity. The ubiquity of punishment will demage the child's passion. We like our child, our friends and our younger sisters or brothers. We have the rights to protect them from terrible learning experience and make a happy learning surrounding for them.

subject: HW1001
content:
Punishment and reward are ways to make students to learn better and control their behavior. However, I prefer reward rather than punishment.
Most students do not like being punished, so punishment just forces students to learn well and behaved themselves. Students are reluctant to do these things. In my opinion, a proper reward to students is more effective, because students are willing to learn and control their behavior if they could be rewarded. Take my classmates for example, if the teacher use punishment to motivate them, they would not like the teacher and do not want to follow the rules the teacher made. They will have no interest in that subject and they even do not hand in the assignment. However, if the teacher encourage them to learn and reward them in a good way, they would like this teacher and want to make friends with the teacher. They will be interested in this subject and study hard.
With that said, I am in favor for rewarding. The teacher have to understand when is the right time being strict, and when and how to reward them. It is true that most students like being rewarded.

subject: HW1001
content:
Actually, there are many methods that can be used to inspire motivation. I think that rewarding students is more effective than using punishment. Punishment may cause students to have negative attitude toward their works; when they're learning they don't learn for themselves, instead, they merely want to avoid punishment, not for wanting to do well. On the contrary, rewarding them will give them encouragement. They may have more confidence in themselves; they're likely to perform well in their grades or other works.
For instance, if a child get a good grade on his math test, his parents will buy him something or give him one hundred dollars to show their encouragement. Or, when students do well on their works, the teacher will praise them and maybe give them some extra scores. These are all ways of rewarding. These rewards can encourage students to study harder for the upcoming exams and make them feel that they're respected, not like wild animals which should be slashed or should be punished. They have their own dignity.
Everything has its merits and demerits. Though I'm a proponent of rewarding students, I think that this way of inspiring motivation should be appropriately used. Don't overdo. Otherwise, students may just learn for those rewards, not for their own advances and their futures.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. As far as I am concerned, I think both ways are effective as long as they are used under the appropriate circumstances.
As a teacher, I think both rewarding and punishment are essential in teaching students. If my students behave well or make some improvements on their studies, it is my job to praise them and to encourage them to perform even better. Some rewarding may be a good way to let them know that they achieve my requirement and they may work ever harder to expect the next rewarding. On the other hand, if my students do not behave well or make the same mistakes again and again, some punishment should not be avoided. However, we should remember that the reason we punish students is because we want them to be better and to improve themselves instead of hurting their feelings or dignity. They are punished only because of their not appropriate behaviors.
I used to have a naughty boy in my class. Every day, different girls would come to my office and complain about his behavior. I had discussed this to Peter several times but things did not get any better. So I punished Peter by asking him to memorize five poems a day during the breaks, which would be a torture for him because he could no longer play basketball with his buddies during the break. Little by little, he improved his behaviors and stopped teasing the girls in class. I praised his improvement in front of the class and he felt proud of himself as well. From this example I know that both punishment and rewarding are important when educating students as long as they are used under the appropriate circumstances.

subject: HW1001
content:
Using punishment to motivate students is an effective way in Chinese culture. Chinese people mostly are quiet and have no motivation to study themselves. However, in Western culture, children or students there have more sense of independence, which means they know what they are doing and what they want. In that case, rewarding would be a better way to arouse students to study harder.
Though using punishment to motivate students is good, sometimes there is some difference. Besides, what kind of way the teacher use matters. For example, while I was in junior high school, I did receive punishment from my teacher because of bad grades. I really felt angry at that moment. After that, he assigned a classmate to help me with studying. Since then, my grade become better and better. So, it is not only the punishment to improve my grade. That behavior was just to let you have strong memory in your mind. What it counts is that you come up with a way to improve yourself.
