To sum up, punishment is a better way to motivate students, but the most important of all is how the teachers assist students after it.

subject: HW1001
content:
To teach students how to learn and manage their emotion and behavior, some teachers use punishment to force them to do so, while others believe rewarding and praising instead of scolding and punishing can lead them to healthy life.
In my opinion, I prefer telling students piecefully to blaming students madly. When people fly into rage, it's almost difficult not to harm others; therefore, being rational is nearly impossible. Teachers are people too. They feel angry at times. As a resault, we can't make sure that teachers can keep sensible once they want to punish their students.
When I was a student in elementary school, a wide range of punishments were still allowed. That is, if you made mistakes, teachers could do anything without your or your parents' pernaissions. I remember I fought my classmate and made him hurt when I was in Grade 6. At that time, I just thought, "The rest of my life must be extremely miserable." To my surprise, after I came to my class teacher to prepare for "serving my sentence", she didn't do anything terrible to me. What she did was just ask the reason, share her experience, and talk to me. We talked a lot, and we were all very happy. Believe it or not, I haven't fought anybody anymore since then. Besides, I always make the best of myself to help others, and it makes me feel good constantly.
In conclusion, it is not only irrational but unfair to punish a student. If a teacher can teach students without punishments, he or she will be able to become a good educator because students will remember their words for a long time--even forever.

subject: HW1001
content:
Punishment and rewards are two ways to encourage students to give a better effort. As a student, I think the latter can lead to a better result. The reason is extremely simply, people like to be rewarded.
When you fail your exam, you are already feeling really bad, and here comes your teacher shouting loudly at you, how do you feel? Mad? Embarressed? Or simply want to cry out loud. The next time you see an exam paper, you are already half afraid due to the shocking experience.
In another case, a teacher who encourages you when you fail, awards you when you succeed will surely make a difference. In this case, even though you fail an exam badly, there is always someone on your side who encourages you, who thinks for you.
In conclusion, I should say that it really makes a huge difference between the two ways, while the former can be harmful, and the latter useful. So be sure to use the right ways to encourage people. With your help, they will surely improve a lot.

subject: HW1001
content:
When I was a kid, punishment in school is really normal and it happened everyday. But in nowadays, there is a lot of news about parents assuming teachers about the punish their children. I do not think punishment is a bad thing in education, on opposite, it might help in some way. Not every kids is easygoing and listen to the teacher all the time. Some children want to play all the time and against the school rule, ignore the teacher no matter what they are doing. This kind of children need more strict education to help them find out their duty and how they can improve their wisdom level. But all the punishment should be under the restrict not hurting the kids. Teachers should not make the kids feel afraid about learning or doing homework. The punishment should not over strict that hurt the children's mental and physical. That is, under the suitable restriction, I think of punishment is more effective.
For example, my mother was under the education which full of punishment, but my uncle does not. When I grow up, I found out their difference. My uncle aways shouted at others when he is in a bad mood, but my mother does not. He smoked and eat without any manners on the dinner table. Although this is not involved with school education, but family manner regulation is more important then any other knowledge. My mother has told me that if she did the wrong thing, her mom would stick a pin on her hand as for punishment. That was why she always keep those manners in her mind and try her best to be a graceful lady.

subject: HW1001
content:
What is a better option, to motive students using punishment or to motivate them using rewards? This type of question has been discussed by many parents and teachers. In my opinion, rewarding students based on their good performances can garner better results. In general, students who recieve rewards are more likely to do better next time because they like being rewarded. Another reason is that students feel the love and care from teachers, so they would try their best at learning.
Giving out rewards is more effective. Take my brother as an example. He loves to recieve rewards for what he has achieved in school. Whenever he gets a certificate for good grade in certain subjects, he feels proud and energetic. This "reward" can motivate him; whereas when he gets punished by doing something wrong, he just gets angry and frustrated.
Although I agree to some extent that punishments can show students the parts they have done wrong, this method is too aggressive. In contrast, recieving rewards can make students happy. Students get the rewards that the teacher prepared for them. Those rewards are symbols of encouragement and love. I believe learning should be a stressless and fun process. Without punishments, students won't be under pressure; thus the likelihood of success in their tasks increases. I remember when I was taking piano lessons, I get punished for hitting the wrong note. I began to hate the piano and I was afraid to make mistakes. Now I realize the importance of rewarding others for their learning instead of punishing, because punishing can create negative effects.
In conclusion, rewarding students for their outstanding behavior and learning is more effective than motivating through punishments. Students not only want to perform better to be rewarded, but also want to be loved and cared. It is safe to say that most students would rather learn in a happy environment than worrying about punishments if something goes wrong. Therefore, rewarding students can benefit both teachers and students.

subject: HW1001
content:
I believe that rewarding students is more effective, because punishment sometimes can't motivate students instead of frustrating them. Students like encouraging words, not whips. If our goal is to make students learn better, we have to tell them which thing they have done is good. That's why few teachers in senior high schools or in universities punish students.
My senior high school teacher, Jessie, always rewards us. She always tells the whole class who did a good job. As a result, every student in our class becomes aggresive. They are happy to learn.
On the other hand, my junior high school teacher, Miss Wang, always punishs students who failed the tests. This makes students become no confidence. They don't want to learn gradually, and the worst thing is that all the students hate her.
To sum up, I firmly disagree that punishing students is a good way to motivate them. I prefer to reward students for learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, in the educational field, a lot of debuts have been raised regarding to how to make students learn better. Some may consider carrying out the punishment to motivate students, while others hold different views on the issue.
As for me, I absolutely prefer to give students compliment and rewards during the period when they are learning. Through the encouragement, the students have more confidence in learning. Moreover, they know learning is beneficial to themselves rather than just a showing stuff.
For example, my younger sister used to play computer games all day without doing her homework or going outdoor for fun. To begin with, my mom was so furious that she told my sister that she refused to give her pocket money. My mom thought the method may make my sister quit. Hoever, it wasn't effective at all. So my mom turned to ask me for help. I told her that she should opt for other methods. At last, my mom decided to give my sister some temptation. She told her if she can kick out the habit of playing computers all day, she will give her a big present later on. Besides this, she often complimented my sister that she is a good girl. Eager to live up my mom's expectation, she really made it with determination finally.
In short, I always think that it's better to make a kid learn to grow up by himself/herself accompanied by other's rewarding and encouragement.

subject: HW1001
content:
Punishment or rewarding? Which one would you choose if you are a student? Most people must prefer rewards to punishment which usually lets you feel painful. However, giving certain punishment to students is often more effective than rewarding them though rewards always seem so great and appealing.
First, one of the worst charateristics of human being is laziness. If no one asks you to study demandingly, you might not study due to your own will. Some teachers can offer some correct punishment to stimulate you to concentrate on study against your laziness. Second, from now and now, people who are given pressure perform well so you'll get proper pressure from the feeling not to be punished. Last, instead of physical punishment, teachers can choose other alternatives such as running the playground or picking up litters on campus.
Punishment can be better than rewarding if it is used appropriately and motivate students to learn lots of things.

subject: HW1001
content:
Students in Taiwan are so poor owing to the stress of pursuing high education degrees. During the process of learning, I have seen a varity of ways to motivating students to be active and positive. In my point of view, I believe punishment would be better than improper rewarding.
Take me for example: I was born to a strict family and my father always punished me when I didn't get ideal grades on tests, even a little quiz. Performing well was the only thing I could do because the injury on my skin and pain in mind told myself: "I'd not like to be hit seriously. As time goes on, my dad's personality changes and he chooses to treat me with a gentle way. However, all the good habits cultivated for a long time gradually disappear including learning attitude, efficiency of finishing assignment, and the forth. Freedom turns me into an arrogant, reluctant boy. Even if more and more rewards are given to me, I can still find nothing inspiring me ahead.
Perhaps the following instance is just a personal problem but I still bear in mind: "Unless all of humans are prodigies, one way to improving and success is a little punishment."

subject: HW1001
content:
I think rewarding students when they have fantastic behavior is more effective for their learning. Though many teachers use both of the methods at the same time, the rewarding effects students more than punishment. If we only use punishment to control their behaviors, they will be afraid and may begin to hate "learning". With the fear of punishment, students may try to find some bad ways to get good grades, but that's not what the teachers want.
If we reward the students to encourage them keeping going on, they may study harder and harder. I tutored a junior-high student for math before. In the begining, I told him "If you don't try your best learning, I will tell your parents and ask them to punish you!" But it didn't work. His grades were not improved. So I tried the other way. I told him "I will decrease the time of the class and bring you around if you have higher scores on the next exam." He did it! When he gave me his grade with a big smile. I just couldn't believe my eyes! With this experience, I can tell every educator sincerely "Just reward your students and give them a push on their learning, and they will show you what they get!"

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control them, however, others believe that rewarding students can lead to better results. In my personal opinion, I consider that rewarding is better and more effective than punishment when we are educating these young students.
First of all, punishment forces students to obey the rules, but it's temporary and useless. Students have to obey the rules in heart, and they are even willing to accept these rules. Punishment cannot make it. Second, punishment could hurt the self-esteem of these young learners. All indiviuals need to be respected. Punishment often makes students feel lose their faces, and their anger will increase constantly. When the chance comes, these unseeing bombs will explosion. Last but not least, most studies show that rewarding students have more effcts than punishment them. It's obvious that students like to be affirmative or be encouraged by their teachers. The positive motivation will enhance the effcts and the will to learn. To sum up, educating in positive methods like rewarding is better than teaching in negative methods like punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, both of two methods should be applied to educate students. Rewarding is a positive method which is very effective because human beings like to be appreciated and be told "You are great!" or "Good job!" It's the nature of all of human beings and nobody is exception. Therefore, smiling and rewarding students always influence them positively and inspire them to think everything in a positive way. However, human is not perfect, which is so undoubtedly that no one can disagree it. If nobody punish me for breaking the rules, why do I need to observe it? Many people break rules or harm the others without conscience because they have this negative thinking when they are young. Punishment can tell students not to break rules and to be responsible for your behaviors if you break it.
My mom always tell me that army can tranform a child into a real man. I think it's not wrong. In army, punishment always drive a person to do the work and finish the task, and there is nobody covering you when you do something wrong, but it's so strick that not all can accept it. Children always want gums and don't like to be punished, but no one never fall down when he learned how to walk. Candy and punishment are the needed method to educate a student to be a responsible civilian.

subject: HW1001
content:
Punishing and rewarding have been the behavior-control strategies people had ever used from the past. Which is better?
In my opinion, it depends on situation. Some students don't find the joy of learning yet. If teachers using punishment method to motivate them maybe get a short-term good results. But the problem don't be solved. Another students' personality are laid-back and don't take seriously about their grades all the time. If teachers using rewarding method to motivate them must don't work. Of course, people always says: rewarding is better than punishment. I partly agree with it.
Take a example. In my senior high, my chinese teacher could tread us go to the movies when all of the students pass the final exam.
In the end, we all pass the final exam but don't go to the movies. Because someone got cheated by the teacher.
From above example, rewarding method isn't absolutely effective in controling students learning behavior.
All in all, the solution to this problem should be both. Good teachers should tell students the joy of learning and create the chance of achievement-getting, then using rewarding and punishment motivating method in the right time. In this way, students can get the most from learning and don't lead them to bad results.

subject: HW1001
content:
Teachers may not choose the same method to teach students. Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn while others believe that rewarding students for learning is an appropriate way.
During the study life of me, I have been treated in both two ways. My teachers use punishment to motivate us to learn when I was in junior high school. And other teachers use another way to teach us when I was in senior high school. In my opinion, I think rewarding studing for learning can lead to better results. The reason why I choose this is because I can still remember the time in junior high school was stressful. The only thing I have to worried about everyday is whether I would be punished by teachers because I failed the test. That was horrible to me. And I still didn't get good grades on the exams.
But the life in senior high was totally different. I didn't have to worried about being punished. Instead, I tried even harder to study because our teacher rewards us some special gifts. I didn't feel stressful and had more interests on studies. Finally, I enter into a nice college to study as a rewards to my teachers.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think the latter one is more effective and fesible. I think the rewards can provoke one to study harder, but the punishment sometimes acts reverse.
Although there are both advantages and disadvantages, you could spoil a student if you reward him too much. In contrast, you could also lead a student to give up his willing to study, if you punish him continuously. It is all depend on how you use the rewards and punishment.
As the saying goes "Rome wasn't built in a day" so is a student's characteristics and the way he acts. Therefore, you need to change a student slowly. After all "Haste makes waste."
I will take myself for an example, I prefer to the rewarding way. Because that's what my teacher does, she always rewards us when my classmates and I have a process in grades. I consider it workable, for my classmates and I are more willing to study. Maybe the reward just a candy, but I still think it works.

subject: HW1001
content:
Teachers often use two methods to motivate students: one is punishment, the other is reward. Sometimes, punishment seems to be useful, but students will not like the way at all. As a person, I like encouragement much more rather punishment. I don't think that anyone likes to be punished. On the other hand, reward and encouragement can help students lead to better results.
When I was a junior high school student, my math teacher was so strict. She hit students with stick when they didn't do well on the tests. My math wasn't good enough, so I was often hit. During that time, math class was my nightmare, and I felt discouraged and frustrated. Then, I hated math.
However, after I went to senior high, the situation changed. My new math teacher was kind and tolerant. He always encouraged students instead of punishing them. He often gave me positive encouragement rather than negative punishment. With his help, I did great improvement on my math.
Now, I am a tutor. I usually encourage my student, and give him confidence. He is improving step by step. So, I still believe: encouragement and reward are far better than punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
Rewarding students or punish them can all force them to study more. Students get the praise and self-confidence when being rewarded, so they are willing to study hard in order to be rewarded again. As for punishment, students will be afraid to be punished, and that force them not to be lazy when doing their assignment.
However, rewarding students is much more effective than punishing them. When we reward someone, we focus on how good they can perform. Students will get better and better because there's no limitation of their potential. In the other hand, punishment might prevent students from getting better because they only have to achieve what teachers told them to do.
If students know they will be rewarded, they won't be satisfied to get the same grade next time because otherwise there won't be any reward. However, students only try not to be failed in class or reach the standard set by teachers in order to avoid punishment.
To praise is better than to scold. Giving students encouragement can make them believe in themselves and looking things on the bright side helps conquer adversity while punishment sometimes causes frustration.

subject: HW1001
content:
For many years, people have discussed whether punishment or reward is effective for students. Being a student for eighteen years, I approve to the way rewarding.
There are three reasons why I support the theory of rewarding students. First, I believe it is the sense of achievement that encourages students to improve better. By giving them rewards can let them gain a sense of achievement and they will be willing to continue the behavior or to learn more. Second, rewarding them can also let them realize that behaving well can not only help them fit into the society but also benefit themselves in some other ways. Third, rewarding those well behaved students can influence other students to follow. The desire of being praised or rewarded can lead them to behave well without noticing.
To sum up, I support the theory of rewarding students. By doing so, I believe the result will be satisfying.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think "reward" is a better idea for teachers to motivate students to better results than "punishment". The magic of love and hope is more powerful than hate and fear.
Some surveys showed that students would be more confident and willing to study automatically in the happy learning environment. The learning effect is more significant in the class full of positive energy. Besides, students are more creatively.
Sometimes punishment could have result immidiately. Students do what teachers want or obey the rules immidiatly. However, students don't willing to do that. They only do that because they want to avoid to be punished. It is not a good motive and can not last long. Terrible learning experience may somehow follow them for a long time.
In summary, I would say reward is better than punishment for students.

subject: HW1001
content: Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn while others use rewarding students to do the same thing. No one can tell us which method is better. But in my opinion, I think rewarding students can lead to better results. Every teacher wants to make their students learn better, but how? I think happiness is an important element in the progress of learning. A happy student is always more willing to learn than A student in bad mood. As one is more willing to learn, it is very possible that he will learn better and have better performace. The hint is you have to make students interested in what they are going to learn and love it. I don't think a student who always be punished in school will love learning, a student who always be rewarded because of his good performace is more possible to. More over, a teacher is more able to give his knowledge to the students correctly and efficiently in a good, happy atmosphere. There is one example. My mom is a senior high school teacher. While she was young, she used to punish her students when they didn't reach her expectation. It seemed usefull that her students had good grades. But now, she is tired of punish her student because she is old. Then she discovered an amazing result that her students have better performance than before. What an interesting result!

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, the rewarding way is a more effective way. There are some reasons to support this view. First, rewarding can encourage students to learn new things in a happier environment. In contrast, punishment will deprove students' interest to getting now knowledge. Second, students will be more active in class, not just fearing to make mistakes in public. Third, sometimes punishment may leave a scar in a child's mind, and it may lead to some mental problems in the long run.
In my life, I have met a very special English teacher. It's really difficult for a new learner to get used to a foreign language, and the begining is always disappointing. However, with the teacher's encouragements and support, I started to become interested in learning English. She didn't use any punishment, and that's why I still appreciate her so much. Punishment may force students to behave better, but the encouragement and love should be the main elements of education.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think rewarding students for learning is better than using punishment. Some people regard using punishment to control students as the most effective way. But I think you can't change their behavior in this way. You just stop them doing the things you think is bad so they won't behave that way in front of you. But they are still the people they are.
For example, when a person do something illegal, the judge will sentence him, and he may be sent into the jail. But if we don't teach him which thing is right or which is wrong, he will be likely to do the same thing when he is free. Everyday I open the newspaper, and then I can read a few example just like what I have said.
Rewarding may not be the best way for teaching students, but is the most appropriate way nowadays. Maybe it's effection is not as soon as punishment, but it is really changing a person's behavior.

subject: HW1001
content:
In order to inspire students to study, some teachers may use punishment as a mean to urge them to study, while others encourage and support students. The two methods of teaching can results in diffierent and diverse characteristic of the students and the desire to study. Therefore, I think that the rewarding one instead of punishing is more effective on studying because no one likes to be punished.
There is new and strong evidence which points out that it's better to reward than to punish. According to a study, scientists put two champanzees in the separate rooms to teach them how to use chopsticks intead of hands when eating. One recieved only punishment when it did false reaction to the instructions while the other got a banana as a encouragement to reward the progressive champanzee. Eventually, they both learned the high intellectual skill to eat like a human, but they had turned into another characteristic compared with recieving the test before. The champanzee who got rewards learned faster than the other and showed great confidence. It was unfortunate that the one who got punishments had become melancholic and anxious. It is obvious that the study tells the difference between two methods. And this is convincing to believing that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. That's why I stand on the viewpoint of rewarding instead of punishing.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I agree that teachers reward students for learning. Some students are afraid of schools, if teachers punishes them for once, they might be good for once but keep escaping from learning. On the other hand, if teachers use rewards, students are more devoted to learning because they want to show how well performed they are to their teachers. If one student is often flattered by teachers, other students will try to learn from the good ones and get teachers' rewards.
Also, giving rewards can make teachers and students closer, students like teachers and are willing to pay more attention on class, for better learning, teacher might use giving little gifts to encourage students to check on data or do reports for the class. Therefore, students will try their best to do the job and build a harmony between teachers and them.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, there are many dilemmas in our society. One of the most known by us is whether to punish students or not. Some teachers punish their students to enhance their motivation in learning or discipline their behavior. Others choose to rewarding their student because they believe that it can lead student to get good performance in study.
As fas as I am concerned, I am in favor of punishing the students. And the following are the reasons I choose the former. First, when children are ill-behavior, you just scold them. In the beginning, they may know they are wrong this time. But if this condition happens again and again, they will think that you "small" scolding just nothing at all. Second, rewarding the students and children may be good idea, if you students are full of the minds to upgrade. When they don't have the minds, how great your rewarding is in vain.
When I was in elementary school, one of my classmates was just this situation. At that time, my teacher chose not punished the students, but my classmate acted more and more badly. It upseted my teacher very much. After others teacher told her to punished the students, my classmate should change his mind and his learning was iproving very much. As a result, I prefer punishing the students, but it should be moderate.
There are an arguement to be made for other answers. And there are many things I have failed to mention. However, I believe the reasons above is the most valid.

subject: HW1001
content:
It goes without saying that each teacher has his/her own way of educating students. Some teachers may prefer using punishment to motivate students, while others believe that rewarding students in order to promote their performence will be the best choice. As for me, I hold the latter opinion. As I explain in below.

First of all, as we all know, the message students receive from punishment is to scare at the person who operates this method. However, the feeling of fear is not a good way for teaching students the righ things, nor will it motivate them to acquire knowledge better from their heart.

On the other side, no one can disagree that we all like receiving accompliment from whoever say it with honest heart if we sure do a great job in certan things, so do students. That's to say, with rewarding - sometimes in vocal language, sometimes in giving out small gifts whatever they are. Student can feel motivate by what you have said and done for them, not just let them scare of you.
Take myself as example. I was once an elementary teacher before. At that time, in the beginning students got low grades because of the lack of strong motivation.
In stead of using punishment as my method, I told them if they can get improve in their school performance, I will treat them free dessert - ice cream whice is their favor. In the end to my surprise, most of them did improve - with large degree!

In short, due to the above listed reasons, I prefer the rewarding is the best policy to help and educate students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Not all the students want candies, but non of them enjoys being punished. As far as I am assured, punishment works far more than reward.
Corporal punishment has been on the headline for years, and teachers cannot deny that, without proper punishment, it becomes difficult to make students under control. In the view of psychology, when being rewarded, students will feel a sense of achievement. Nevertheless, this doesn't work on every student since not all of them will be eager to work hard simply for rewarding. After all it doesn't hurt if they get no reward. By contrast, when being punished, students will be fear and be shamed. These feelings will urge them at least live up to the standards that their parents or teachers set, In another word, it hurts,
Take my younger brother for instance, he doesn't like to study, and he always crams on the eleventh hour which leads to poor exam outcomes, My parents one day claimed that, if he squeezes into the class top 20, he can have extra 2 hours for computer games per week, However, that didn't function at all, My brother said that it was not a big deal to live without the extra 2 hours. Thus, my parents changed their policy, They said, "without top 20, no computer games at all." As soon as the sentence was made, my brother rushed into his room, and he even squeezed into the class top 15. I asked for the reason, and he told me, "this punishment spoke louder than the former reward."
In this light, compared with reward, the punishment counts, I totally agree that candies are important, but punishment is insistensable and cannot be overemphasized.

subject: HW1001
content:
As a matter of fact, I grew up in a family which do not use punishment, and I did have a happy childhood. Also I do believe that rewarding the students is more effective than the punishment because couragement build up healthier mind.
Then, here is why I agree more on rewarding. I work in a cram school, and I have encountered numerous students. I get angry with kids for sure, however, I use rewarding way and courage students on their good sides. Surprisingly, they adjust their bad behavior little by little. Even though it took some time, they are getting better, and they become eager to learn new things.
Punishments are not good because I have seen classmates of mine gave up on themselves due to the punishments. More over I have read a theory from the book which said that the power of encouragement is much more healthy, better, and stronger than punishment. In my opinion, I think to reward students is more effective.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my view, I deem both methods have their effectiveness, but they should depend on the demanding of parents.
In the past, most teachers used punishment to motivate and discipline students to enhance their study and behavior. That was because ordinary people in the past were in poverty, and parents expected their children could have bright future. Likewise, parent in the present hope for the same expectation and ask teachers discipline their children as they underwent. Under pressure teacher would do what parents want.
However, some parents hold different idea. They don't want their children to exprience traditional teacher method. Parents rather like the latter, rewarding. They believe children can learn faster than use punishment.
To sum up, both teaching methods have their effectiveness and advantages. Teachers use one of the two by parents demanding. What teachers do is to expect students to get better and better.

subject: HW1001
content:
Considering methods to motivate students to learn, punishment and rewarding them are the most common ways. In my opinion, punishment is always necessary, because laziness is an instinct, and no one would give up cozy life unless there is pressure or opression to an extent.
The famous musician, Mozart, is a vivid example for my opinion. Even though being praised as a genius when he is still a teenager, Mozart was forced to play the piano by his father when other kids were having fun in the play ground. The practicing process was painful for the young fellow, but this hard work laid the ground work for his way to success. Without pressure, laziness could take over and lead to failure.
While I emphasize the importance of punishment, it doesn't mean rewarding stundents is useless. It is an incentive to lure students to make every endeavor to perform well. I think punishment and rewarding should both exist in our education system, and I optimistically think that the consequences would be pretty efficient.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are many opinions on whether should the teachers use punishment to motivate students or they should reward students. As far as I'm concerned, the latter is a better approach.
I believe that rewarding students for learning is more effective than punishing them. Most of the children need to be encouraged, motivated, rather than be forced to do what the teachers want to please them. For instance, my cousin Johnny is studying in the elementary school. He cried every day after school last year. He told me that it was because he couldn't achieve his teacher's goal on studying and he was punished by her as a consequence. My cousin was very diligent but not quite smart as other people. How could a teacher be so impatient that she couldn't see the efforts my cousin made? This kind of thing happened again and again and my cousin became more discouraged.
Not until this semester did the circumstance become better. His teacher changed and she took an encouraging way when teaching. She gives students some prizes as long as they make progress, even though a little bit. My cousin became happy again because he could get senses of achievement when he made progress.
Although some people may disagree with my opinion, I still believe, through my cousin's example, that rewarding students is a better way than punishing.

subject: HW1001
content:
As my opinion, I think both methods work. And I also think both punishment and rewarding should exist and be used depends on different occasions.
When students are young, they might be lack of the ability to judge right from wrong. Furthermore, they might still be inmature and they learn most of the things from what they see on TV and what their friends at the same age behave. In this case, the teachers or parents should take some necessary actions to stop them from being wrong if persuasion does not work effectively. If students have wrong concepts but the grown-up don't correct them, it's even more like encouraging the misbehavior & the students won't have chance to get back on the right track.
However, if students are capable of differentiating the good and bad, then I believe rewarding works even better than simply punishment. Once students are recognized they are metally mellow, teachers might make use of words or verbal compliment to encourage them pursuiting for a higher level.
In a word, certain level of punishment is still requisit. Rewarding motivates the motion of improving. Both methods work and should be used depends on different cases.

subject: HW1001
content:
In order to let students learn better, there are many ways can do. However, for me, the best way is rewarding students for learning.
There are two advantages for rewarding students. First, rewarding students can encourage them to do better. Secondly, rewarding students can help them have more happiness. Take myself as an example. When I was in 1st year of elementary school, my grade was poor and all my happiness was ruined by punishment. However, when I got to 2nd year, my teacher told me that once I got better scores next time, she would bring me to the zoo. What a big surprise for me that time! After hearing that, I started to study hard and my grade also became better and better. As the reward by my teacher, not only I got better grade but also have more happiness. Therefore, due to my own experience, the best way to help student learn better is rewarding them.

subject: HW1001
content:
When teaching their students, many teachers apply punishments or rewards to motivate their students. In my opinion, I think rewarding students for learning is more effective because of two reasons: positive learning and good relationship between teachers and students.
First, rewarding students when they're doing good leads them to study happily. It is a more positive way than punishments. Students will study hard and try their best in order to get rewards. Second, rewarding students makes the relationship between teachers and students better. Unlike punishments, students would not scared of their teachers. Therefore, they are willing to get close to their teachers. When I was in the elementary school, the class teacher told the whole class that if our scores were over 90 in the final math exam, she would give us some secret presents. I studied very hard trying to get the presents. As a result, half of the class met the teachers' demand and each of us got candies from the teacher. Although the presents were very ordinary, they really motivated us to perform well.
The opinions of people about whether rewarding or punishing students is more effective differ a lot. But I think current education gradually tend to be positive. The students definitely will learn happily and make large progress under the rewarding ways.

subject: HW1001
content:
When it comes to the topic "Whether to punish students when regulating their behavior", it inevitably leads to a great controversy. In my opinion, I support to punish better than reward them. For one thing, if you have done something wrong, you surely need to take the consequence. Being punished will warn you no to do that again. For another, if you are always treated by reward, you will never make progress and do better. You may even take other people's kindness as granted in the future!
Looking back to my high school life, I feel very grateful to my math teacher. He always limited our daily school life and punished us immediately when we do something bad. Sometimes, he even made some silly and unreasonable punishments which embarrassed and annoyed us a lot However, that also regulated my poor behaviors and made me take more time on my study. If it had not been for his mean punishment, in the past, I would not have made gradually progress and finally achieve today's success.
We are anything but God, and we all take the wrong path sometimes. By taking moderate punishment, people could be corrected to the right road and keep going to the bright future. Sadness and bad memories would leave, and good ending will remain.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, many experts argue about whether to teach kids with punishment or reward. I believe the best way is to adequatly use both. Punishement is the traditional way which is effective since. Sometimes the punishment can mark the mistake we've made and let us learn our lesson by heart. However, over-punishing diminishes one's confidence, in this way, child who grew up with punishment only were tend to be compliant, well-behaved but low in self-esteem. On the otherhand, children who earn gifts or compliments in every event have high confidence, sometimes are overly confident. They are often spoiled because they had always heard what they wanted to hear instead of the truth.
My parents raised my brother and I in a moderate way, which made us polite, humble but confident at the sametime. I was shy when I was little, and once my mom took me to a family reunion. She asked me to greet the relatives with smile, yet instead of following her orders, I stood there like a statue and refused to say a word. With my bad manner, the reunion ended up in an aukward atmosphere. My mom punished me immediately when we got home, and gave me a lesson after that. In the next reunion, I tried to be lovely and cheerful, and she praised me right in front of all the relatives. Seeing people's happy faces, I realized how does it feel when being adorable. Since then I've always been lovely and cheerful and got rid of that timid, shy and glooming side of me.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, it is more effective to reward students for learning when it comes to educate students and control their behaviors. I think the impact of immediate rewards is much bigger than punishment. When students get rewards right after they make good performances, they will be joyful and try to become better to get more rewards.
Using reward is more effective in long term. Because students may change their behaviors for fear, they may just prentend to change their behavioral models instead of correcting their thoughts from heart. For instance, I have taught fifteen ten-year-old students English. When I punished students because of their bevaviors or grades, those who were naughty would do the same thing behind me and those who got failed could not find their problems after punishment. Instead, using right rewards to encourage students to improve themselves actively.
For reasons above, I believe that rewarding students is a more effective method. The sooner you reward students, the bigger the impacts will be.

subject: HW1001
content:
As a proverb goes, "Practice makes perfect", perhaps most of us believe in that proverb. For a long time, teachers have followed the way of punishment. While some teachers insist on using punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior, others, conversely, believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.
In my point of view, teachers should keep on punishing those who break rules and the punishment should never be canceled. By doing so, most students are not going to do what is forbidden to do. Although there perhaps are few exceptions, the strict rules and heavy punishment will directly stop them from breaking rules, also if necessary, limiting some of their rights. As for rewarding, rewarding must be based on one circumstances that everyone follows the rules.
Take one of my friend as example, after he entering high school, with no strict punishment, he began to smoke. Thanks to his teacher finally got aware of the problem; he changed. Not until someone punished him did he turn to be a good student. Rules are for those who need to learn. The more teachers ask for, the more well-behaved the students are.
At present, Taiwanese students exactly need to be taught with punishment. If teachers stopped punishing students, more problems would soon go on the surface. To sum up, rules still serve a purpose.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results, and I am convinced that rewarding is better and more effective than punishment. Punishment may have apparent effect immediately, but it can't be a long-term methods to descipline students. Oral or physical punishment can deter student from violating rules and force they to do things teachers appointed. However, students will abandon themselves as long as theses punishments disappear. On the other hand, rewarding can elevate student's dignity for self-descipline, accumulate their confidence to accept more challenging tasks. In psychology, this is called "self-efficacy" - when somebody think that he or she can success, then he or she will acheive his or her goal.
Take me for example, my mother never had scolded me or punished me for poor grades. Instead, she would encourage me to pay more efforts to score high, and comforted me always when I was despressed at my failure. Whenever I got high points in any subject or I was praised by teacher for my hardworking, she would be glad and proud of my acomplishment. From my point of view, the most precious rewarding is my mother's encouraging smile and her agreement to me. Consequently, there is no denying that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
On our long and far way of learning, teachers doubtless play an important role. Teachers use various means to make their students better. For me, I prefer the teacher who use tender ways to encourage students such as praising them and rewarding them. In order to gain the teacher's compliments, students will make progress and be much more attention to their behavior. Nevertheless, not every theacher has such thoughts towards students.
In my third grades in elementary school, I met the teacher who was extremely strict to students. We had to hand in our homework on time or we would be hit on the palm and forced to do another two times additionally. It is known widely that no matter how good the person is, he or she still has possibility to make mistakes. I had just forgot to bring my assignment and suffered from the lingering nightmare after my teacher's punishment. Although we had really excellent grades and great behavior, we lost our happy time in our childhood. Thinking that a happy childhood is much precious than a well-mannered one, I am disapproval of the heavy punishments of teachers.

subject: HW1001
content:
Many parents or teachers consider punishment as the best way or better way to teach their children or their students nowadays. But in my opinion, the more strict you are to children, the worse result you will get. Rewarding children to motivate them is the better way to teach, while punishment is necessary as well, I believe.
For example, in elementary school, students will try their best to behave well or tell themselves not to break the rules just to get the reward. Although the prize might be some small candies or just an eraser, they will be happy after all. However, sometimes when they did something wrong, they will get some punishments of course. Then they will know what they can do and what they can't do. But remember, never over punishing students, otherwise you will lose their trust on day, and it will be much harder to teach them or control them.
I have two younger sisters, and we don't live together because our parents divorced. Their mother prefers the punishing way, but it turns out that they are not very well-behaved. They are kind of selfish and confident. They also have bad tempor. Sometimes, they really drive my crazy, and I even want to hit them! Instead, I use the rewarding way to teach them, and they kind of like me more, and behave better than I expect.
So, in conclusion, rewarding is more effective, yet punishment is also necessary. Try to find the balance between both. And you will get a good result; and students will like you and trust you more.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think that rewarding students is more appropiate and effective way for students' learning and behavior. When people are rewarded or praised, they become more confident, and they will learn things more efficiently.
According to research in U.K., students in high school get higher grade when they were praised by their parents as they were baby. In the reaseach, I think the reason why they can perform better is that they have confident in theirselves, and we can find the importance of confidence as well, which supports my opinion. When a student is rewarded, they are encouraged to do better work. For some students who get low grade on exam, when they are rewarded to get better grade, they will probably make their effort to study harder to score higher.
In modern society, I think reward is better than punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Take me for example, when I was studying elementary school, I went to cram school every day since both of my parents worked. The teachers at cram school used punishment to motivate students to learn and control their behavior. we didn't like the teachers, but we were afraid of punished so we did our homeworks and prepared for the tests. However, we didn't do well on schoolwork. When I was in gunior high school, I met a different teacher. She didn't punish us when we get bad grades or make a mistake; instead, she rewarded us when we performed well and taught us patiently when we made fault. My classmates and I respected her and at the same time we studied hard and performed well on everything, including school clubs, writing contests and speech contests. I had confindence in myself and I believed that I could do everything perfect.
In the past, teachers used to use punishment to teach students because they believed it as the best way of all. However, though students finished their homeworks on time, they were not willing to do it themselves, the just didn't want to be punished. Nowadays, more teachers reward students because they believe that it can motivate the students to do everything well due to the honor and they learn for themselves. This is a good behavior which they can keep for all their lives.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think rewarding students for learning can lead better results than punishment. If teachers reward students properly, they not only make students control their behavior, but also motivate students to learn by themselves.
Many teachers claim that punishment is the most effective method of teaching, because it can help teachers to control students' behavior easily. That might be true and we can image that students seat in their classroom quietly. However, we have to consider wether punishment is a good method to make students love learning or not. If students love to learn, they will push themselves to study or to do some futher research. According to my experience, teachers' rewarding can make me have positive attitude about learning, and let me understand that I am not pushed to do anything I don't want to do. Therefore, I am not only encouraged to learn, but also have fun in the process. Therefore, students can learn by themselves by rewarding, and my experience proves that rewarding students is a truly effective method.
In sum, punishment can control students behavior, but it can not motive student to learn and to enjoy the process of learning. Rewarding is more effective method of teaching.

subject: HW1001
content:
There is no doubt that teachers need some appropriate methods to motivate students to learn and to control their benavior. In my opinior, I prefer rewarding to using punishments. First of all, I think giving some praise is a positive way while giving punishments is a relatively negative way. Second, if student want to get the rewards, he or she will work hard to the fullest and have a specific goal to reach. Last but not least, once the student got the rewards, the rewards motivate the students to succeed to win the rewards next time. Because of all the reasons above, I think rewarding students will lead to better results.
Here is the example I have in person. Many years ago when I began to learn English, I was really afraid to speak this foreign language. I was even not able to say a word in the English class. Then my mom told me if I tried harder to learn English, she would bring me to see the Harry Potter movie. Because of the well-known movie reward, I made efforts in learning English. What's better, when I done well and allowed to see the movie, I was eagerly to work harder in order to see the next eposide of Harry Potter series. Obviously, the reward, motivated me to do my best next time. To sum up, based on my personal experience, I consider rewarding to be a more effective method.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior, while others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. We can't deny that abolishing physical punishment has become the main stream opinion in our society. However, I don't think physical punishment is the absolutely wrong way to teach young students.
As we know, everybody should take responsibility for their behaviors. Therefore, if a person commits a serious crime such as murder, he will be sentenced in prison by the judge. Almost everyone can accept that adults who make a big mistake should be punished, and no one doubts that being in prison is a severe punishment. Why do we make differences towards young students? If a young kid makes a big mistake, doesn't he or she need to take responsibility for the wrong behavior?
Therefore, I don't think abolishing physical punishment is a good idea for education. On the other side, proper punishment could be the best way to let those young students remember their wrong behaviors forever and never make the same mistake again. Real society is very cruel, students should understand that since they are still young.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students for learning could lead to better results. Although some people might stand on using punishment to force students to study or to do homework, such like the proverb, "No pain, no gain." However, punishment is the only way to achieve better results. Here are some reasons I concerned.
First, encouraging and rewarding are benifital for promotion of self-efficacy. According to some research, students who learn with positive emotional support showed better achievement in the future. Students realize they could do much better than now, even want to do more right things.
Second, no one want to be punished. With teachers encouragemat, they feel they are wanted and with self-steam. Especially for those students are growing up, you might hurt their feeling with crude punishmant, even in public.
Finally, not only for students, but also for all people, rewarding symbolized they are approved for their behaviors or ability. In biology, these kind positive process could stimulate the endorphine in order to make them happy, even feel powerful to face the further challenges. That's why I stand on rewarding.

subject: HW1001
content:
Teaching method has been a controversial issue not only in Taiwan but the whole world in these decades. However, there is no denying that no identical method is suitable for different kinds of student. Some students do not work hard until are punished by teachers. In this case, punishment may be a kind of motivation for them. On the other hand, some students may work harder after they are praised. These students may be frustrated after being punished by teachers and thus lose their confidence on learning.
In my opinion, I think the latter is more effective for students. Though it is true that someone should be punished if he or she made mistakes, we may ignore the importance of rewarding. The following are some exsamples.
According to the research, students after being praised are more willing to learn than those who are punished by teachers. Punishments can regulate our behaviors, but sometimes make us optimistic. For example, if a teacher doesn't find out what exactly happened and punish students, this may hurt their confidence. We can't blame teachers punishing studen't for not proper reasons, since we human sometimes make mistakes. However, we can minimize this happen by switching our methods and attitudes toward students - reward them.

subject: HW1001
content:
Doubtlessly, in my opinion, rewarding is far more effective then punishment. Talking about the advantages of rewarding first. Rewarding provides students a close goal, when students always follow the goal, they do their studies step by step stably. Most of humans like having more benefits, if we take advantage to it well, we can bring more pleasure each other. Now it is time to think the problems behad punishment. The most direct thing that appears to your mind is punishment makes people unhappy. This unhappy emotion will cause students hate their teachers and parents. Students will try to escape from the punishment. Therefore, they starts cheating, leaving their home and school, more seriously, some extreme students will "treat who can punish them as bosses in a computer game." If they indeed do, it can become a big news. Punishment always produce lose-lose tregedies, so we must avoid it.
An obvious example happens to my family. My brother is a junior high school student. Due to his absolutely unprofessional mother, he hates studing. When he went to an elementary school, my mother hit him or scolded him loudly when he has just a little fault. He hae encountered this for seven years, of course, he became disappointed to his studies. My mother said that she will give my brother money if he can pass the exams, although it is effective, it only improved him a little since he has been hurted for seven years. I think money is not a proper reward, what he needs is more legal recreations. I used some computer games as prizes when he has a good performance on his studies, and it really works. My mother thinks I teached him a lot, but I never admit. Recreations help him the most. After I tell you the story, do you make up your mind stop using punishment and give students rewarding?

subject: HW1001
content:
Punishing or rewarding? This has been a long-time controversy of teaching ways, and many teachers also face the choice when they get to a new class.
In my opinion, I think rewarding students is a far more effective way than punishing them. I still remember my fifth grade in elementary school, when all my teachers are so harsh and mean, especially my English teacher. At that time, English class was such a nightmare for us that we would even pretend to be sick to avoid it. There was actually no problem on her teaching methods, considering that she was a good lecturer, let us do many conversation activities and gave us a lot of chances to talk in front of the class. However, nicknamed "big boss", she used a lot of heavy punishment. For example, she hit us when we couldn't meet her stendards at tests, and she made us copy half the textbook When we weren't dare to talk in front of others. Eventually, we started to hate English class and some students even began to think that if the teacher hated him.
I believe her teaching would have been much more successful if she had been willing to reward more. From a scientific perspective, when you are doing something and afraid of getting failure, you get nervous easily, can't be effective and are not active, just like why upsets happen in sports competition's world and like why some people get stomachache when taking math tests. On the other hand, when you are fighting for something without pressure, you can usually remember the feeling of doing the right thing and can enjoy the things you are doing, just like how we train our dogs. After all, everyone loves being rewarded, right?

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students is more effective for learning, because it make students learn from the bottom of their hearts, from their own motivation, insted of fear about punishments by others. Besides, punishments would leave bad affections to students. Those frightening experiences will not disappear and make students pay less respect to people in the future. They may treat others what they had been treated before during their learning age. On the other hand, rewarding students for learning can stimulate their honor. Students will "move" toward their own goal instead of "being pushed" toward "teachers' expectation".
During my junior high school life, I and my classmates suffered from many kinds of punishments. Our teacher often shouted at us and used the most critical words to blame us, whenever we did bad on our tests. And she used a stick to beat those students who had a bad behavior in front of all other classmates. We hated her, for all the insults she gave us in public. Whether we did well or bad on our school tests, we were not happy at all. Because of those punishments, we even considered that getting a high score is our responsibility, not something that can cheer us up. Finally, our class did not performed well in the High School Entrance Test.
When I entered the high school, our teachers were just like angels who didn't give us those punishments. They used many encouragements and lead us a great life in our school. "Punishments are meaningless if the students just don't love learning." He said. We then had a good memory in our high school. That's why I support rewarding.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior, while others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Still others, like me, think that using those two methods together might be the most proper way.
Although it would be effective for teachers to lead students in good discipline through punishment, students are not soldiers and the teachers are not generals, either. Students under too much pressure would behave nice on the surface, but they might not be willing to be like that on their inner minds. On the other hand, if teachers treat students kind and often reward them for having good manners, the possiblity of rebellion can be declined. However, students who have too much freedom and recieve too much passion at schools might not endure the crutial truth that they must to face with in such a realistic society.
As I am concerned, I always get good grades academically, but I am such a silly bone and not always behave in good manner. Because my teachers are emotional and mean, all I want to do is rebel, and I even ignore that they are elders I must respect for. Above this, I would choose the both methods to balance the benifits and the disadvantages.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion teachers should reward students for learning instead of punishing them. The reason is because no one wants to be punished. Rather, they like to be rewarded. So how on earth will a teacher really get students to learn by punishing them?
Take myself for example. My parents never punish me for getting bad grades. Instead, they just tell me to find out the reason why I got poor grades. Also, they give praise to me when I study hard. In this way, I develop responsibility for my own behavior. I feel learning is important for myself not for my parents. To many of my classmates however, they study for their parents and usually cheat on tests due to the punishments they might face if ending up having poor grades.
Another example is the two hard working teachers that teach us. They both give a lot of homework for us to practice and both give us many tests. However, one rewards us by giving us snacks if we do all of our homeworks or get high scores on our tests while the other punishes us instead if we don't complete what we should have done or didn't study well for our tests. Although our average grades are both higher than other classes. We perform even better on the subject that the teacher reward us. Why? It's because many people cheat on tests and copy homeworks for fear of being punished. On the contrary, students want to get the reward by their own efforts, therefore we get better results by being rewarded.
In sum, I think teachers should reward students instead of punishing them, because students like being rewarded and in this way it gives them a power to study.

subject: HW1001
content: I think punishment is not necessary when teaching students. If the students got poor grades, they shouldn't be punished. We can tell them how to improve their learning instead of scaring and forcing them to study. Furthermore, sometimes punishment leads to a bad result. For example, some children would have a worse behavior if they are punished. They don't want to get hurt again, so they stay away from teachers by skipping the classes. Then, there might be some arguments between children and parents. So, whe educating students, I think that to love students is better than to punish them. A slight punishment is fine, but it should be done in an early time. When childrens were young, parents educated them what can do and what can not do. As they grow elder, teacheres teach them by love and encourage them when facing difficulties. Children can contorl their behavior themselevs if parents educated well in an early age.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn while others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, rewarding students for learning will be the better way. I could tell that rewarding is better from two of my classmates' story.
My classmate in sixth grade, Kevin, didn't like to study. He was always playing games in class, and he liked to play jokes on others. My sixth grade homeroom teacher often told him not to play games in class and not to play jokes on others, and if he can get a higher score, He will give him some cool cards. Though Kevin didn't care about that at first, he tried to study more after our teacher kept telling him that he is smart enough to learn. Day after day, Kevin not only got better grades, but he was nice to others, and he was willing to learn more in class.
However, my classmate in 8th grade, Joe, didn't like to study, either. While he slept in class, our homeroom teacher always kicked him till he woke up, and made him do reports as a punishment. Day after day, Joe seldom came to school, and it was said that he joined a bad group, and that he was sent into prison.
From these two stories above, I would say that rewarding students for learning is much better than using punishments.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I believe rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Everybody needs to be encouraged, praised and loved, and students are especially eager for teachers' positive remarks. When I was in junior high school, my English teachers never punished us even if we got terrible scores in tests. My teachers encouraged us again and again. They were very patient whenever we felt frustrated. They praised us as long as we improved. That's why I love to learn English so much.
Now I am a mother, and I have two kids. I deeply believe that punishment can make things worse. I always try to encourage my kids when they learn. If they behavior themselves well, I'll kiss them, give them a hug or give them some rewards. I hope they are be loved and feel confident. If they do something wrong, that's ok, give them another chance. Don't punish them!

subject: HW1001
content:
We often see students who are punished by teachers end up with suiciding. That's because the punishments their teachers offer, makes the students lack of confidence.
In my opinion, rewarding students is a much better way than punishing them when motivating them to learn and behave. I believe if you reward them, not only do you bring them hope, but also makes them see themselves important. For example, my sister was a terrible student in junior high. She brings home nothing but bad grades and warnings of her unsatisfying behavior. However, my parents never blamed her or punished her. Instead, they chose to encourage her, and not giving her any pressure. In the end, my sister not only got excellent grades, but also became the best student of the semester. Ever since then, her teacher rewarded her whenever she did well on tests. On the other hand, giving punishments is something a teacher or parent should avoid doing. It brings the child only fear and lack of confidence. According to recent studies, nearly seventy percent of suiciding cases are students who gain too much pressure because of school work. Among the seventy percent, about half are those who have teachers who punish them. Some students even start to fight back when they're not satisfied with their punishments, which only makes them become worse.
In conclusion, rewarding a student definately leads to a better result than punishing them when considering learning and behaving. Teachers should start learning the best ways of rewarding their pupils which benefits more than punishing.

subject: HW1001
content: For my own opinion, I think rewarding students is the best way for learning. Teacher punish students can quickly present on their grades but in long tern this is not the better way. It may let students misunderstand that viloence can force someone listen whether he like it or not. When students grow up maybe he will use the same style to those who disobey him. On the other hand, rewarding students can let them feel like the are important. They notice that when they study hard something good may happen to them. This teaching style may let them learn things not for the teachers but for themselves. For examples, when students is well-behaved teachers may treat snacks or little stuff to make them maintain this kind of behavior. We may see elementary school teacher often use this to let students focus on learning. When students one day grow up they will also reward their children as their teaching style. Therefore, rewarding students is the best way for learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are many ways to teach students to have a better performance in school either in their test scores or their behavior. Some might agree to use punishment to motivate the students, others might prefer to encourage students by rewarding them. In my opinion, rewarding students for learning will lead a better result.
Due to the fact that confidence is built up through time, students need to be encouraged every time when they have done a better job. Once they receive a positive view of their own, their confidence will grow stronger. When a teacher always show a positive idea of how students' work, they influence the students' judge of themselves either now or in the future. On the contrary, if a teacher always uses punishment to warn students, some students might lose their chance to build up their confidence, and thus they might have a more negative personality. Moreoever, children and students tend to copy their adult friend's behavior. Accoring to that reason, we want to educate our future generation to treat the world and the people in a polite way. If they have been influenced by using violence to solve problems, we might create more people who are violent; on the other hand, if students recognize that being positive to motivate their learning could actually make things better, they wouldn't need anybody to motivate them through punishment but become self-motivated.
I used to teach young children and I always encouraged my students when they did a better work. The result was that they all loved coming to class and never neglected their study. If a kid comes from a strict family, they might either be very quiet but without creativity or be quite naughty without self-dicipline.
My experience told me that when encounter students with problems, it's better to reward the students rather than punish them.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, more and more people against teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn. Some people are making efforts to urge the government to make a law which can forbid those punishment. Others hold many parades to tell the country people how awful do teachers punish students. Although no teacher had punished me in my grown-up process, I'm still opposed teachers to punish students.
If the teacher rewards students and often praises them, I am sure that students rewarded by teachers will learn better than those who are punished by teachers. Moreover, students who often be rewarded may have positive attitude. For instance, my sister is a diligent student but she always gets bad grades. Her parents always punish her and scold her. On the contrary, her teacher treats her kindly and patiently. He encourages her, rewards her and builds her confidence. Gradually, she does well on the tests and she contributes the good grades to her teacher's patience, not her parents' punishment. In a conclusion, rewarding students is more effective than punishing them. Why not just reward them, praise them and encourage them?

subject: HW1001
content:
Well goes the proverb "Do not do to others what you don't want them to do to you". If I were a teacher, I firmly believe that I would reward students to make them learn better. Students would put efforts in being obident or scoring high on tests. This will encourage them and that they'll also give gratitude to teachers. On the contrary, if we use punishment to motivate them. They would not work harder but would be overwhelmed with the feelings of disappointed, rejected, and denied. At last, they would even abandon studying and dislike the teachers.
My friend, Jane, is my classmate in elementary school. She was late for school almost every day. At first, our teacher punished her to do the cleaning works for all the classmates. But it was in vain. Then the teacher rewarded her a candy instead of punishing her. This time it makes great effect on her. She tried hard to get to school on time. Obviously, rewarding students for learning is a better manner. It can not only lead them to better results but also raise their confidence. Why not choose this method and lead both of the teacher and students a happier life.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the past, most of the teachers in Taiwan were supported to punish students when their performance didn't meet the teachers' expectations. But now, the rights of the students are considered more important.
In my own opinion, I think teachers should reward the students when they perform well, and encourage them if they didn't, instead of punishing or scolding at them.
To support the idea, take me as an example. I don't really perform well on math at school, and every time I get bad grades, my math teacher scolds at me and makes me stand for the whole class. At first, I really tried to spend more time on studying math to please him, but everytime I fail, his insults just made me feel less confident. So gradually I found myself being afraid of math, and I started to avoid studying it. When teachers reward or encourage students, students feel more respected and are more willing to try to have better performances. But when students get scolded, they just feel uncomfortable and their fear of the subject will be increased.

subject: HW1001
content:
Every teacher has his or her own methods to teach students. By using punishments, students will try to study harder and perform better on tests in order to prevent themselves from being punished. By using rewards, students will be attracted to the prize they will get when they do great on schoolwork, and then they become delligent as well.
However, in my opinion, rewarding students for learning is more effective. Studying harder, some students still can't do better on tests, and still have to be punished. If staying up late to 3 a.m. and relaxing himself or herself all night both will lead to the same result, why should they work so hard? Consequently, they become frustated with schoolwork and loose the willing to study hard. And we won't see these phenomenon on by rewarding students.
Chinese style education tends to punishing students, and the foreign style education is just on the contrary. But foreign students seem to be more creative and have more ability to solve problems than Chinese students. The fact is that the current society needs the quality which foreign students have. Therefore, I think it's time to change Chinese's education style.
Some people might not agree with what I mentioned above; After all, how to train up the best students is the most important thing. What's your opinion? t will be increased.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I think rewarding students for learning is more effective and can lead to better results. Because nowadays students are more volunerable and obelious, they tend to against things, subjects, or teachers at school if they don't like. Students don't appreciate the kind of learning which has to do all about examinations, but once you fail, you get the punishment.

subject: HW1001
content: That whether using the punishments to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior is appropriate has been an controversial issue these days. As far as I am concerned, I personally stand on the pro side in this matter. And the reasons can be stated as follows. First of all, some students are more likely to behave astray if the teacher don't do something strict with them. For the students might think that doing wrong thing is anything but a big matter. Secondly, setting up punishment is more reasonable and convincing for a teacher regulates his or her class because students are able to do things with discipline; hence, there is nothing to be worried about preventing them from making mistakes. Last but not the least, take myself for example, I've been growing up in a strict family. Though it's difficult for me to obey all the rules my father's set up, I'm utterly grateful to what those rules have done to me today for I now know that something is definitely conducive to do or is going to be disastrous once it happens. There is a proverb goes, "spare the rod, spoil the child." I'm completely in favor of it.

subject: HW1001
content:
