Learning in the school is a process that make people to adjust themselves to the environment. I stand with the opinion that using punishment to movtivate student to learn and to control their behavior would be much more effective than rewarding students.
Because it is easier to make a standard for students to follow when the characters of students are not always equal. Especially, when students had broken the rules, you can't use rewards to teach them what they should do.
So, when it comes to which is much more effective, I'm with the opinion.

subject: HW1001
content:
I firmly believe that teachers should use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behaviors in a moderate way. At the stage of adolescence, teenagers are physically well-grown but mentally unmatured, they tend to do things on impulse regardless of the consequences. Some people may say it's better to "teach" them to come back to the right path instead of punishing them, for research says that it does good to teenagers' mental growing. In my opinion, punishment is an necessary evil.
Everybody makes mistakes, especially teenagers at the periods of rebellion. Moderate punishments make them understand what consequences their wrongdoing may lead to, and prevent them from going astray. But excessive punishments won't reach this effect. Teenagers may talk back and the gap between students and teachers will end up making matters worse. In short, only with moderate punishments can make students turn over a new leaf and learn from mistakes.
I would not say punishment is the best way to increase students' motivations of learning, but it's no denying that it is an effective way. The abilities of learning vary from person to person, and I think teachers should find a balance and choose different teaching styles which apply to different students. Take me for example, I am a go-getter, which makes me eagers to take challenges and experience new things. Those things always spark my interest and participation. My teacher encourages me to take part in school activities and competitions, for she say I'll learn more through defeat and glory. There are times that I make mistakes, she tells me to take responsibilities for my own actions instead of yelling on me and punishing me. She makes me realize that I am the person who can control my life, and she wants me to pursue my dreams. As with Oprah's famous saying, "The biggest adventure you can take is to live the life of your dreams." I always keep that in mind because it always gives me the strength to move on. In conclusion, I believe that students can learn and behaves well with moderate punishment and teachers' encourgement. After all, it is ourselves that can decide and change our lives.

subject: HW1001
content:
When it comes to the definition of education, it varies from person to person apparently. The followings are the most common-seen teaching methods. Firstly, as some social problems we can see on TV or newspapers, there are still many teachers, or school rules use punishments to control students' behavior. As far as I am concerned, it is brutal and it shows that Taiwan isn't a full civilized society yet. Students avoid schools and hate teachers, but to be frank, punishments work in some way. Take me for example, not until I grow up did I realized the purposes of those strict teachers, who punished me. I finally came to the realization that what they've done to me were for my own good. Students may understand more when they grow up and find that they've become more self-motivated, owing to the punishments they have suffered.
Secondly, on the other hand, many people nowadays prefer rewarding students to punishing them. It results in students being more willing to learn. However, to put it differently, while teachers show love and concern to students, it is very easy for some students to take it for granted. This way, the education system would be no longer efficient and useful, what is even worse, the education might work backwards. To conclude, neither of the two teaching methods shows predominance over the other. Well goes the proverb, "As you sow, so shall you reap." No matter which way you are given when you learn, always remember that working hard and looking forward will lead you to the end of success.

subject: HW1001
content:
From my viewpoint, I prefer rewarding students for learning to punishing them. The following reasons are why I choose that rather than this.
First and foremost, students will be more willing to study hard. Most students regard their studies as top priority. If they do well on tests and teachers reward them, they will definately make more efforts. However, if teachers punish them when they have a bad performance on tests, they will not only feel depressed but lack of self-confidence from then on. Punishments will have the opposite effects. Next, I think that harmonious relationships between teachers and students are also crucial. If one considers his teacher a stern person, he will be frightened to ask him questions and he can never get his questions solved. For the above-mentioned reasons, I think rewarding students for learning is more efficient.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, parents are more and more taking seriously on children's education On account of the birth rate decreasing. However, the parents are not willing that teachers punish their children. In my opinion, I think use punishment is the best way to motivate students to learn and control their behavior.
When I was a fifteen year old student, I went to cram schools. The first one's teacher was so mean and she would ask as to hand in the homework. She'd gonna check our homeworks respectly. What's more was that she make standard of each of us. Unless your scores only one point beneath of your standard, you would be punished by one hit. That was so hurt. On the other hand, the second one was just like a paradise. We enjoyed chatting on this class and the teacher didn't even stop us. The class was just like a party. That's not so exaggrate. One day I found the margin between the first class and second one was larger and larger. Althought the first class was in a hell, I really learned a lot from this. Also I totally didn't like those punishment, but I really can be motivated to get better during next test.
I believe that no one wants to be punished, but we can improve while we're hurt. The punishment is a name and inner things are that you can work hard, take responsibility on your behavior and gets better and better.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, learning, to me, should be delightful and self-disciplined. Rewarding students for learning is a more effective way to them.
When I was eight years old, my mother once sent me to a small English cram school. At first I was very nauseous at the prospect of a three-hours course to face every Friday night. The teacher in the cram school had gradually charged my mind. He was a very friendly teacher, with peacful smile on his face. Whenever I made a wrong answer, he would wait patiently for me to find the correct one. Sometimes students in his class got high scores in exams, he would give precious little gifts to the hard-working students. As time pass by, I was more and more willing to study English by myself, not only for the praise in class, but also for the high expectations I had myself.
In contrast of rewarding students for their good learning, some teachers tend to punish students just for one little mistaks. In the process of our life, learning can sometimes be difficult and overwhelming. Punishing students can make students feel unconfidence about their abilities though they might have great talents.
Rewarding students while learning, is a less painful way to help them get through the toughs that they encounter in learning. And thay will make students learn more willingly, and on top of all, pleasantly.

subject: HW1001
content:
How to motiavt students to learn and control their behavior was an old problem for teachers since that job exist. Some of them use punishment others prefer reward. Both of them had some good example, eventhrough there were some failure, too.
If a teacher only use punishment to teach his/her students, they will become more passive in their mind. They will not do anything untill someone ask them to do it. In other word they will lake of selfmotivation, because they did get reward want they do things right. If they do something that was not been told, they will end up in two situation: I. They do the right thing and get nothing. 2. They do the wrong thing and get punishment. That's what happen when you only use punishment.
What will happen when you only use rewarding to teach children? If they do right things, you give them rewards. When they do the wrong things, you still give them reward for not do that again. Finally, you will find out that you shoud give them reward no matter what they do, and you will never satified their desire. When you stop reward them, they will stop listen to you and do anything they want. Then you fail to teach those kids.
In my opinion, reward and punishment are both needed in teaching. When students do the right things, you reward them. When they do what they shouldn't do, you punish them. That will be the ideal way to teach child.

subject: HW1001
content:
I believe rewarding students for learning is a more effective way to motivate them to learn. First, I think that punishing students isn't good for students because that may lead to the frustration and fright of students. Sometimes when students don't want to learn or don't have good performance in learning, they could get even more frustrated and scared of studying after receiving punishment. They will think, "What if I can't do well next time? Will I be punished again?" Having a mood of frighten, they can't pay full attention on their study. For the students that don't like to learn, being afraid of punishment may force them to learn, but it will also increase their reluctance and hatred toward studying. Instead of keeping studying, they may choose to escape from it. For instance, when I was at the eighth grade, I didn't have a good performance on my study. At that time, my teacher just kept punishing me because she thought I didn't want to learn. And I became increasingly desperate and scared of school and studying and almost gave up on myself. Second, people would like to obtain something after doing well. They enjoy the sense of achievement and the things they get. Rewarding students can make them eager to behave and perform well. The rewards for students are like the real thing of their sense of achievement. Besides, seeing others get the rewards will also drive themselves to do better.
Final, we all should have fun in our study. Punishment brings disappointment and fright to us, but on the other hand, rewards bring hope and happiness to us. When we get the happiness after doing well many times, we may gradually find some fun in studying. And when we enjoy what we do, that's the best way to bring efficiency to our works.
As a result, I think rewarding students is a better way to motivate them.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, maybe sometimes the punishment can motivate students to learn, but if teachers did not to puish students, student would read by themselves? That is an important part of this question. In punishment, students learn and study hard, because they just don't want to get punishment. I believe that rewarding is the more apporiate choice than punishment. It is believed that everyone like to be praised. Hence, they will have confidence to do something better, they would try their best on getting good grades, studing hard, etc. They just want to be praised by the others.
For example, when I was senior high school student. I didn't liked to study English, and I alway failed the test. But my teacher didn't punish me or said how stupd you are or something like that, he just encouraged me, and gave me some suggestions in reading skill. And then, I made up my mind to improve my English ability from now on. I never gave up, because I thought my teacher had expection on me. So, I appreciate my teacher he didn't puish me, and he encouraged me to improve my English ability which let me have a achievement on English.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays it is hard to be a proper teacher because teachers need to learn a lot of things. They have to not only learn their professional knowledge in different filed but also learn some class managements. Some teacher use punishment to let their students to learn and to control their behavior. Others use reward to let their students to have better results. According to some teaching theories, I think it is good to use the reward to motivate your students. Based on some educational theories, it is more useful to expect some good behaviors by giving rewards. If teachers use reward to enforce their students to have good results, students will keep having good behaviors. But if teachers use punishment to change students' behaviors, students would not keep the good behaviors longer. For example, I have read some some books about behavior modication. Some professors point out that if you wish students to have good results, the best way is to let their feel comfortable and trust you in the classroom. Rewarding gives these merits I have visited some school, I noticed that one teacher rewards students for learning, students do their best on learning. The environment of the teaching is good and harmony. It leads all students feel good while they are learning. But I also noticed that next to the classroom, a teacher uses punishment, students are scared to speak out the answer and the teacher punish them and expect the right answers. It caused bad cycling.
In conculsions, teachers need to give students good expectations and they will do that for you. Punishment let students feel sad and scared but rewarding let students feel good and happy. So what kind of methods will you use? Of course, rewarding students and have good expectations is the best way for teachers and students.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think punishment is not the best policy to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. The responsibilites of the teachers are to lead students to new fields and help them find their interests. Experiments show that children whose teachers encourage them to learn by rewarding them can lead to better results. Students will be willing to learn if they want to be rewarded by their teachers. Those who learn with reluctance can't have good performances. They don't have real motivations to fulfill their goals. What they do is just for living up to their teachers and parents' expectations and avoiding punishment.
My little cousin can be a good example. She is not a straight A student. She loves drawing instead of learning professional knowledge. Whenever she fails the tests, my aunt will hit her with a wooden rod. After the punishment, she will walk to her desk with a terrible expression and begin to study. With a bad mood, it's hard to concentrate on what she's studying. Instead, I always buy some delicious snacks as her gifts if her academic performance improves. She tells me that she will study hard to get those sweets.
As we can see, rewarding students for learning is the best policy. With this approach, students will be willing to study on their own, instead of being forced by others.

subject: HW1001
content:
Since the issues about punishment or rewarding is pervasive among students, it's not surprising the critics or TV shows are discussing this buzz.
To tell the truth, things like this have pros and cons. There isn't a definite right or wrong answer. As far as I am concerned, I consider rewarding students to be the better choice. I think despite punishment urge students to learn, students would rather prefer no pressure than the anxiety of not meeting teachers or parents' expectation.
Take me for example. When I was in the elementary school, math was hard to me What I remembered was that I was told to stand on the stage because of the low grade. To my surprice, the teacher gave me a bag of candies. I was flattered and didn't know why my heart was pulsing very fast at that time. What really motivated me to work hard is this unforgettable experience.
Next time when I was once again on the stage, swelling with pride, is the time I got the highest score in class. People certainly like to get compliment instead of being blamed. No one is exception. Next time, instead of punishment, why bother to raise your thumb to your students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Recently, when I read the newspaper, there was some news about the problems of education. Parents argued with their children's teacher because the teacher punmshed or scalled their children. Avoiding punishment is the social tendency of Taiwan. However, I think that the proper punishment is important.
Encouraging children to do right things is good, but it should not be normal. When we start to work, it is difficult that whenever we did a right thing or did our job well, our boss would reward us or enhance our salary. On the other hand, when we did something wrong, there was almost a punishment. If we educated the children only by encouraging. I think that in the future, they might have difficulty to facing the reality of society.
According to some researches of the U. S., there is a big trouble between their parents and children. American educated their children by encouraging, not by punishment. They think that it is better. Now something is different. The confidency of these children is weak, small failures can knock down them so that their parents have no chioce but to encourage their children again and again. It is a cycle! I don't think it is a good thing. Therefore, to let our children face the failure, I think the proper punishment is important.

subject: HW1001
content:
As far as I am concerned, reward is the better method then punishment when teachers try to motivate or control their students' behavior. There are several reasons that make me draw this conclusion.
First, reward helps students maintain their interests about the learning materials. When they are interested in learning something, they learn quickly and happily. That's what a teacher really wants, right? Second, reward gives students less fear of failure when they come into obstacles. Because of the positive and guiding nature of reward, students may want to give it a try again and again even after several failures. Third, reward creates better learning atmosphere in any learning environment than punishment. How can a teacher expect his/her students learn well in a bad learning atmosphere? Students will have good mood and emotion under a rewarding atmosphere, and in this kind of mental state they will have higher learning efficiency, too. Moreover, reward gives students much more successful experiences. These precious experiences may further strengthen their self-confidence and later generalize to other aspects of other courses or part of their life.
To sum up, reward has so many advantages and if a teacher really wants to use it, it is quite easy to carry out. Give contingent rewards to our children and help them learn quickly and happily and even love learning things. If I were a teacher, I would give it a try.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the first place, I agree with using awarding students for learning. When I was a junior high students, I was naughty. I didn't like to study. I just wanted to play all day long. However, my English teacher started to praise me when I had good behavior. Moreover, she taught me basic English in her private time. Under her teaching, I became better and better in English field. Even now, I still like to read English managazines, English newspapers, and listen to ICRT and English songs.
When I was twenty years old, my niece got very low score in English class. When I saw her confused face, I knew that I could help her. I used my old teacher's way to encourage her by a beautiful hair band. That's the gift I could think all girls might like it. I started it by a simple sentence, she smiled and told me English seemed not so difficult. I taught her the basic grammar that all students hate it. After one month, I found her smiling. She told me she got high score and all classmates ask her how she could do it. She used my simple theory to teach other classmates. Then, most of their classmates advaced in English.
At the end, I think a good teacher is to use right method to inspire students. And the awarding is my favorite way to encourage students.

subject: HW1001
content:
The method which is rewarding students for learning is more effective than the other one. According to my experience and my peers', we are tend to have good performance in learning and behavior, when we are rewarded. Because there are something attracting to encourage us to study hard and behave well, we will enjoy the process of hard work. Once we have good behavior and are rewarded, will we know that our satisfiction and hard work are seen and worthy. We will try hard to behave well next time to get this kind of thought and happy emotion. Little by little, we will be more confident than before, and will be well-behaved people.
On the contrary, when we are motivated by punishment, we just correct our bad behavior for short period, not forever. We are just scared by punishment and are made to study hard and not behave badly. It doesn't cheer up our mind to be good, but horrifies us not to do wrong and not to have poor result of academy. Under a learning situation which is nervous and having to be affraid to be punished, we won't learn well and control our behavior from the deep mind. Because all we do is avoid the fault, we just try our best to not been punished. We never care about what we learn but care about how not to be punished. As a result, we might to cheat on the exam to get high grade to avoid the punishment. We might to care how good performane on the test, but not put any emphasis on the real result of what we've learned. Concequencely, we wont study well and behave well. The effectiviy is not good.
In a brief, I think rewarding students for learning is more effective than punishing them.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, rewarding students for learning is more effective than using punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. I am a junior students, and some of my classmate's are really bad. They pay no attention to the teacher and just keep talking in the back of the classroom. They often fight with other classmate, break the window just for fun, and even smoke in the school. Of course, our teachers get angry about them, and punish them all the time. But they don't care at all, they are still playing when the teachers have them clean the classroom. They think the punishments are fun! So, I think our teachers should change a way, they should find out what they really like or want to be in the future, and encourage them to get on the good ways. Then, they won't do those bad things. In conclusion, I think rewarding students is better than punishing them.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers punish students to correct their actions and behaviors. I believe that rewarding students can lead to better results. Punishing students may reach the teachers' goals to change their behavior. However, it might as well make the relationship between teachers and students worse. Rewarding students encourage them to work harder, which leads to a better result. It may be more effective. I believe all teachers prefer reaching their goals without causing a worse relationship to reaching their goals but cause a conflict between teachers and students. Students may also dislike teachers if they're too strict, serious, bad tempered and unthoughtful. Most teachers hope to shorten the distance between their students. They hope to gain a good social relationship. I suggest to reward students as the main method. Punishments may be used if the students are against the school rules. According to research results, students seem to do better on the subjects who the teachers they like teach. To reach that goal, rewards and punishments should be used together.
In elementary school, our homeroom teacher was our mathematics teacher. He was strict and had a bad temper. He considered drinking water in class was disrespectful. On the other hand, our English teacher was thoughtful and rewarded students often. The classes she teaches had an average of at least ninety-five. Our math average was only about eighty-five. Most important of all, teachers may consider another way to treat students following two rules. The first is to lead to better academic results. The second is to shorten the distances between the teachers and the students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Learning is one of the most important things we did in life. To learn properly and patiently are the basic rules of studying. I think it depands on how would a student like to learn. Teachers should know more about the students in addition to choose the right way to improve the students' skills or behavior.
I prefer to reward students when they do an impressing job. It will make them study harder if they have a destination and they will express more interest on it. Think about the last time when you won a prize or some other rewards, how did you feel when holding a trophy in front of everyone? By getting rewards and encouragment, students can find a place for themself in this world.
My class is an example. We were not really studying with all might in seventh grade. But since we are getting closer and closer to the ninth grade, everyone becomes nervous. Our math teacher had thought of a method to lighten our spirits. That is to compete in groups for a cup of milk tea. That works! I can feel the atmosphere changing and classmates started to enjoy the working and discussing in our study groups. We gave our thanks by being more focus on the quizzes, tests, and exams. It's amazing how much we improved in just two or three months!
Everyone should be patient on learning, either students or teachers. Don't think of learning as if you are going to be writing and writing. There are many ways to learn. Plan a learning schedule and a reward after you complete it. Or maybe you can also give advises to teachers about how you really want to study. It will surely change your life!

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, teachers have two methods to motivate students to learn and to obey the rules. One is to punish students, and the other is to reward. From my point of view, teachers should reward students.
Rewarding students can make students do better in school. Although it may cost much money, students will have the will to behave better and to get better grades in order to get prizes.
On the contrary, if teachers use punishment, the situation is worsen. Students may be more likely to rebel. They wouldn't be able to abide by the strict rules. Take my classmate for example, he is tired of the saying "You can't do this, or you will get punishment", so he decided not to behave well. He not only took his iPod to school, but he also read novels and comic books in class. Things changed when my teacher started to reward. Now he doesn't take things which are banned in order to get prizes. He behaves like a good student from then on.
From this example, I understand that rewarding students is more effective than punishing students, and that students can learn and behave better when their teachers reward them.

subject: HW1001
content:
If a teacher always punishes students when they are wrong, the students may hate the teacher. But if a teacher always rewards them without letting them know what is the right behavior, it may not be effective. In my opinion, a teacher should reward the good students, and punish the bad students. This sounds easy, but actaully it is not easy at all.
Some students are called "teacher's pet", just because their grades are better then others. Some of these students act like an angel in front of the teacher, but when the teacher leaves, they are like little monsters jumping around, shouting and throwing food in the air. I hope teachers can watch these students carefully, and warn them or punish them when they have gone too wild.
Using only one way to treat students will not be as effective as using both ways - "rewarding" and "punishing". For example, a little boy is running in the hallway and stopped by the teacher. The teacher punishes him without saying a word, and the little boy gets mad, doesn't want to come back to school anymore. But if the teacher stopped him, tell him "you cannot run in the hallway" in a nice way, the little boy may listen. Next time when the little boy walks through the hallway, the teacher can give him a piece of candy, because he has learned a new lesson and remembered it.

subject: HW1001
content:
When it comes to the which way is more effective to teach children some disipline, I think that the rewarding is a way that can work out better for children. For punish what they did and make they afraid of sticks on your hands will surpress their motives to learn, and day by day, they would become depressed and are reluctant to take in anything new to them, or by chance, they followed the rules you give them, but they just do it in careless way and hand it to you to get away from the punishment they may face if they didn't do their part, they would someday become indifferent to learning, too.
On the other hand, if you reward a child when he/she has good performance, they would remember the sense of achievement and the glowery of victory, he would want to experience it over and over again by trying to do his best part and impress you as much as he can, in that way, he would be accustomed to pursue the best without you giving him anything.

subject: HW1001
content:
As far as I am concerned, rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Since students would be willing to study hard with a view to getting the presents, instead of just avoiding the punishment. Another reason, many students may be more hatrive to learn after being punished. Last but not the least, the students may do their best to figure out any kind of methods to learn because they regard the rewards as their goals.
Take myself for example. When I was in elemantary school, my teacher alway rewarded the student who answered the questions positively. At the first, I was still shy to raise my hand in that I was afraid of saying the wrong answer. Nevertheless, gradually I found that it is so honored to receive the rewards that the teacher would compliment me. Therefore, I was encouraged to try. By doing so, I would like to reach my goal positively now.
Hence, I consider that punishment will only make the students more frightened to do everything, but rewarding can cultivate us to be positive.

subject: HW1001
content:
I am of the opinion that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. When we learn something new, we are often inconfident of ourselves. If teachers use punishment to control our intersts in subjects, we may be afraid of moving forward.
Take me for example, I have had a nice and wonderful English teacher. She was so kind that she seldom punished us although we got low scores. After the monthly exam, my English exam scores were very low. She was shocked and then had a conversation with me. My teacher encouraged me and promised me if I got higher scores, I could have the latest English novel. Therefore, I studied more diligently than before and anticipated the next monthly exam. On that day, though I was still nervous about the exam, I talked to myself that I could do it well. Most improtant of all, I want the latest English novel! Surprisingly, I got the highest scores in my class. Not only my English teacher was amazed but also my parents felt proud of me. It was so amazing that my dream came true, and I got the latest novel. What's more, my parents gave me two thousand dollars to buy what I want! It all credited to my teacher's encouragement and her appealing award.
For one thing, giving students positive attitude toward learning is so improtant. For another, rewards let students be more active and make more efferts to do the subjects. Last but not least, I think that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content: Some teachers always scold and punish their students when they did something wrong, while others reward their students and encourage them to do better. Which way is more effective? To me, I prefer the second choice, Why? If a teacher only punishs students for they did something bad, students might be scared and dare not do it in front of you, but they might still do it again when you can't see them do so. Because they just don't know what is the right thing or good thing to do. Instead, if a teacher tells the students what they should do and encourages them to do so by rewarding them, students will be more willing and happy to do the good thing. It is effective especially to kids. When I was in elementry school, our Chinese teacher often scolded us in a very loud voice when we forgot our homework. However, our math teacher was more kind to us, when we handed in our homework on time, he always smiled and gave us candy and cookies. So, in the end of the semaster, we not only got good math grades but also interested in it. On the other hand, most of us hate Chinese and the teacher very much. By rewarding the students, teachers can not only teach them more efficiently but also make a good relationship between you and the students. If you are a teacher, why not try this way? It can kill two birds with one stone.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students is better than punishment. Because people all like presents and that can be a positive reinforcement for them to do well. Otherwise, hitting students or blaming them may harm their mind.
According to researches, hitting children on bottoms before three years old for more than twice would make them more aggressive than others when they grow up. I think long-term effect is more important so we should replace punishment for rewards.
I believe that the most important thing is students can really learn and know why their behavior is wrong. If we just use punishment, they will just be scary but not reailize what is right and what is wrong. So, I think that use rewards to motivate students is more effective and better. Of course, not a lot of gifts for them.

subject: HW1001
content:
I believe that rewarding students for learning is more effective. In my opinion, the meaning of education is to motivate the students to search for their own interests and to pursue their goals or dreams. In order to reach the true meaning of education, teachers should play the role as the one who gives students courage and confidence. Yet some people may think that by punishing students, they can also be motivated. However, I believe that this can somehow affect students' confidence and also give them additional pressure. Therefore, in comparison, I think rewarding brings more benefits than punishing.
There are some examples of the disadvantages after punishing students. Some students will feel shameful when being punished by teachers in public, and this will lead to many negative consequenses. One part of them will lose their confidence and become afraid to behave themselves, another part will feel like being looked down by their classmates, the other part might become violent or have harmful behaviors. Therefore, I agree that by rewarding students to study is essential.

subject: HW1001
content:
I was strongly against punishment when being a junior high student few years ago. Now, after graduating from high school, I have got more deep insights into the students' mind and would consider punishment, if properly used, the most effective way to inspire, and encourage students on their schoolwork.
Take my junior high life for example. I went to a cram school for math course once a week, and the teacher there set up his own rule for punishment. That was, hit the student on the hands with a bamboo stick if he/she didn't meet the "goal score", which had been agreed with by both the teacher and student. I was really scared when asked by the teacher for the first time to discuss my own goal score. However, after hit by him several times, I made up my mind to study much harder, in order to show him I'm a potential student. Finally, with the unbelievable top math score, I aced into my ideal high school.
That example proves my opinion correct. Laziness and procrastination are naturally rooted in every students' mind. If it hadn't been for punishment, they might have been led to the wrong way during their early learning trip. It is punishment, even better if combined with some rewards, that can help students cut off all the bad habits and head for success.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think using punishment is more effective than rewarding students.
Rewarding students can make them confident and lead them to love learning. But it will also let them keep bad hahit. If they don't recieve rewards, they won't do what you ask them to do.
In contrast, punishment seems to have a bad effect and make them afraid of learning. But it can control their behavior easily and let them know what is right and what is wrong. Today, we can see that some children do things which are not allowed because they are the only child in their family. Their parents show their love by not punishing them, letting them do what they want to do, and giving what they like to them.
Due to the above reasons, I prefer using punishment to rewarding students.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, teachers punishing students can motivate students to learn and to control their behavior more effective than rewarding students. For the purpose of making students better, some teachers may reward students when they have excellent score in the test. Nevertheless, to study hard and get good grade is what a student have to do. And every students have different favorite things, the "reward" for the students can not really fit what every students want. The same reward maybe can't make each student cherish.
I am of the opinion that only punishment can motivate every student to learn. The reason is that everyone, not only students, don't like to be punished. For example, the teacher say that the students have to hand in the report tomorrow or the students have to be hitten by the teacher. People don't want to get hurt and fright to be blamed, then they will hand in the report on time! If the teacher said who hand in the homework tomorrow on time can get a hamburger to moviate the student, but someone don't like to eat the hamburger, and the student probably reluctantly to hand in the homework on time.
Owing to these reasons, I am convinced that punishment is the most effective way to motivate students!

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, teachers try to make their students learn harder and behave better by either punishment or reward. The results of both methods are from person to person. In my opinion, rewarding students is more effective in motivating students to learn than the other.
Students recieve reward when they behave well, and get punishment when they do something wrong. The students who get reward will keep working hard so that they can get another benefit next time. However, the latter may not do so. They will be in a bad mood when getting punishment. This mental condition may lessen their passion for doing better. I suggest that teachers can cheer their students up to inspire them instead of punishing them.
When I was young, I played basketball and joined the competitions for the school team. I used to do my best to win glory back for our team but I failed in a important game. However, my teammates and coach didn't blame each other but cheered everyone in the team up. By doing so, we united together and won the championship next time. So I think rewarding students is more effective.

subject: HW1001
content:
Education is critial to a nation. The places where implement education are important and should be tooken more attention. And the teachers are exactly the peopel who teach children and will affect children's behavior indirectly. Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Although using punishment will change students behavior instanly, I think the students who are rewarded by teacher will change their behavior for a long term. I think rewarding is more effective for one reason.
The reason is that rewarding will let the students know they are doing things right and good. If the teachers use punishment to motivate students, students will always think they are doing things in the wrong way and they never have done a right thing. As a result, students who used to be punishment may never know the feeling of being good and may underestimat the abilities of themselves. On the other hand, students who are rewarded will know that they were just doing the right think and know they did it very well. Students will feel better when someone praise their work and will think they are useful. More important, rewarding helps students build up their confidences. Took myself for example, I used to be a student who didn't like to study when I was eight-year-old. I didn't think education is important for me; thus, I usually got low grades on exam. However, I studied for the exam then because my teacher said, "The person who get 100 points in every field will be given present whatever he or she want." I just wanted the present the teacher would give, so I studied hard. Surprisely, I happened to be the only person who got 100 points in every field and I got a CD of one famous computer game. I was so happy and knew that studying is a right thing to do. Although I didn't study in the past, I felt great when I tried hard to get the prize and also enjoyed the study. Now, I am the student of National Taiwan University.

subject: HW1001
content:
Until ten years ago, it had been acceptable for teachers to use punishment to control the behavior of students. Nowadays, educaters are trying to change it into rewarding instead of punishment. In my opnion, I think rewarding students for learning is more effective.
There are two major reasons that I agree with the "rewarding" idea. First, it is crucial for students to communicate with teachers. If students are afraid of being punished, they are in no way talking to teachers. That will broden the gap between them. Second, it is important to make learners remember what they have done right instead of what they have done wrong. If a student is praised or rewarded because he or she does something good, that will be much more inspring to him or her. In addition, it will impress the students and encourage them very much.
There is an example to support my opinion. When I was an elementary school student, I was poor at math. My first math teacher always punished me when I got bad grades. That did not help me to be improved at all but make me be scared of math. However, everything changed when I met my second math teacher. She rewarded me and gave me compliment everytime I got improved. That really twists my scary impression of math.
In education, it is hard to tell which way is the best one. However, teachers have to have students learn happily, at least not scary. Rewarding and compliments will be an effective way for students to be confident and learn better.

subject: HW1001
content: How to motivate students to learn or to control their behavior is two different questions. Controlling their behaviors is the base of their life. They must learn how to treat other in a good way. For example, don't punch others after they hit you, or laugh at someone by some words in public. This is the most important rule of their life. If they obey it, they may get themselves and even some innocent people into trouble. To protect them from these kind of situations, we must treatened them by some punishments to avoid them obeying it. On the other hand, the level of grade depend on not only learning attitude but their natural intellegence. Maybe one tried hard to memorize the whole of homework, he got F because his intellegence worse than other, and he got a punishment. It is unfair that he was punished because a thing he can't change. Therefore it is best way to reward student to motivate them to study harder rather than punish student who try hard but get the worst grade.

subject: HW1001
content:
In now socialty, I think punishment is more effective then rewarding, though rewarding is also works. Nowaday, parents have one child only is normal, and they will spend all their time on this kid. They will do anything for their only child. This make the child think that they can have anything they want, and they really have. So when teacher use reward, they might think that they can get the same reward from their parents without following teacher's rule, then why they have to follow? So although the reward is good, few students would follow. In this kind of siduation, punishment is much better then rewarding. For example, when I was studying in elementory school, my teacher used to have reward if we follow the rules, but soon she found out that no one listened to her, so after few monthes, she change her rule to punish the students who didn't follow the rules. It worked immediatily.
I think rewarding can also be a good way, but only when our environment change, when parents stop bowling their kids and start to teach them the thing children should learn. Teaching is not just only teachers thing but everyones. If we don't realize that, then no matter punishment or rewarding will become useless.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some parents are willing to send their children to a private school because the teachers in there use punishment to control their students' behavior and the myth in the parents' hearts is that kids should be taught by using punishment, then they will have not only good behavior but also good scores on their subjects. However, is this kind of method really suitable for every kid? It's worthy thinking about.
In my opinion, maybe teaching children by punishment has its progress, but I think the other method is more effective. Take my friend for an example. Her parents give her lots of high pressure, such as getting high scores and big prize on every test and competition. They even send her to a cram school in which teachers are very serious and punish the students if they didn't reach the goal. What my friend's parents want is really effective, but she becomes unhappy gradually. To be her best friend, I know she has passion to learn everything and she is very smart. Therefore, because of this wrong method, she doesn't like to study and learn anymore. According to this example, I find that motivating students by rewarding them may be more effictive than punishing them. After all, it's happy and grateful to learn, isn't it? If their parents knew it eariler, their daughter might be different.

subject: HW1001
content:
In recent time, there are news talking about teachers taught students unappropriately by using punishment which would do harm to the physical development of students. Some teachers said that it is unreasonable for asking them to make students well-behaved and to teach without punishment at the same time. It seems that punishment is an essencial method for some teachers to teach.
However, not all the teachers have the same attitude towards this issue. My mother has been an elemetary school teacher for about twenty years. She used to be a stern teacher who requested her class to behave second to none no matter in behavior or in other activities. She used a stick to punish students who fell short of her requirement. And, she also educated my younger brother, younger sister and me in the same way. Things went well until my younger brother enter junior high school. He started to beat his classmates when they did things ignoring him. Although most of the time my brother had just reasons to be angry when his classmates play tricks on some inecent classmates, my brother always chose the wrong way, however, seemed to be similar to the way my mother had chosen, to express his anger. Gradually, my mother realized that punishment can not help his son to choose correctly. After reading a book called "Love Words for kids", my mother decided to love her children by who they are first instead of punishing them to force them into the shapes she had expected. Now, my brother can control himself very well. What's more, he knows what he wants and can, at the same time, think for others.
From the living example, I believe that rewarding the child with love and acceptance but not money or things can help the child enjoy who he is and what he is doing, including learning. Punishment seeds fear and anger in a child's heart field, but love and compromise not.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, the best way to motivate students to learn more is by rewarding them and also comliments. I think punishing students for what they had done wrong is a very negative behavior. The reasons why I think teachers should reward students are listed below.
First of all, as a student, I like to be rewarded and encouraged. I'll gain confidence in myself and make efforts for higher achievements.
Second, punishments can lead to serious damage on students. They may start to think that they are useless and just give up on themselves. It is going to be very hard to rebuild their confidence.
Third, everyone have self-respects, however, some teachers punish students in front of many people. The student who is punished might get angry and the anger can cause even more serious troubles.
In conclusion, I think rewarding students for learning is the better way to motivate students because students relying on encouragements and compliments to keep on going and achieve higher goals.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, students are too naughty to control. They are always talking, laughing or even screaming during the class. In order to solve this big problem, some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, punishment is much more useful than rewarding students and following are my several reasons.
First, students remember the punishment easily. If a student doesn't respect his teacher and affect his classmates studying, the teacher can punish him. By doing this, other students would know that they should not do things bad because the teacher might punish them and the punishment is very scary. Second, use punishment can teach the students what things we should do quickly. When a student do something wrong, he might get punished. However, if he do nothing wrong, he would not get any punished. Thus, this student would know what thing he can do and what thing he can't do. Though we can tell students by our tongnes, punishment is more powerful.
Punishment and rewarding students are both the ways to teach and control students. Since punishment is more powerful and unforgettable. I think the punishment is better.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. The reasons are as follows: First, if teachers use punishment to motivate students, the students may afraid to go to school, and the pressure of not being punished could let them toss and turn at night. Instead, if teaching students by rewarding them, They are more willing to go to school. Second, when students get rewards, they can feel that learning is fun, but if students work hard just to prevent themselves from punishing, they can hardly feel the joy of digging out the knowledge. Last but not least, teachers cannot always be with students, but life is not complete without learning. We should learn lots of things until the day we die, so if there are no teacher and punishment, students may feel relief and stop learning. Instead, rewarding students for learning can make student easily find the joy of learning and cannot stop learning even if there is no teacher. In my student life, I've met the strict teacher, he used punishment to make me learning, although I was doing well at that subject, now I still afraid of learning about any knowledge about that subject. So, honestly I think rewarding students can really lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students is much more effective than using punishment. Punishment is not a possitive motivation, but just the pressure. The pressure will make the students so afraid of making mistakes, so that they will turn out refusing to answer questions or even asking questions. It's bad for learning when students lose the eagerness of gaining knowledge.
I remember that when I was a universtity student, I held an astronomy camp in an elementary school. At first, most students were so shy and some of them even could not concentrate on what we tried to tell them. But, when the first little brave got his candy as a reward of answering our question, everything changed. They all raised their hands with shining eyes and buzzed "Teacher, choose me! choose me!". Through those little rewards, we could have much better interactions with these students. They might not really know all the answer, but they all tried hard to figure it out. By this way, we could teach them more from their responses. Isn't that the best and the happiest way to learning?

subject: HW1001
content:
Punishing or rewarding, which is more effective? Some people consider punishment is better for motivating students and controlling their behavior. However, I think rewarding students can have better results. There are three points of view to support my opinion.
First, it is rewarding that encourages students to learn. For example, teachers in elementary schools always rewards students by snack and prize. Students have more motivation on learning because of prize. On the other hand, punishment makes students fear the things their learn.
Second, it is rewarding that is better for students' mind and health. Rewarding may have more positive effects on student's mind, while punishment may be harmful on students. For instance, some teachers are accused because of inappropriate punishments that hurt students' body or mind. Rewarding, on the countary, releases students' positive feelings and make them happy, which is more effective on learning.
Third, it is rewarding that effects on one's behavior more. By rewarding, students may be more willing to break bad habits and behave well. On the other hand, students may forget the punishments on them once they get over it.
To sum up, I consider rewarding being more effective for some resons, among them encouraging students to learn, being better for student's mind and health and effecting on students' behavior more.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some people believe that punishment can be the most effective way to teach students because students would feel afraid and would do the jobs you asked for as soon and perfectly as you wish. However, in my opinion, I think of it cruel and useless. When I was an elementary school student, I just knew that I hate people punish me, make me stand in front of the class, yell at me or even hit me with a stick. Those punishment for me were really shames. And I think, for most of the students, they have the same opinions as mine. Punishments make students not only feel shame on them, but also lose their interests in learning. However, rewarding is totally different. It makes students willing to learn and, if the teacher uses it properly, it can also inspire and encourage students. They can learn in a happy atmosphere.
Take myself as an example. When I was in my junior high, I met a teacher who totally changed my attitude toward mathmetics. Although he was a teacher full of teaching experiences, he still could not make me love math more but even thought of the subject scary. He always punished students when they fail their tests. He shouted at them and did his best to make them feel shame, or even guity. On the contrary, my English teacher, who always tought us with a smile and rewarded us, wholly won my heart. She's the greatest English teacher I've ever met. I think the reason why I love English and enjoying learning it is all because of her. Therefore, for me, the rewarding is more effective than punishing.

subject: HW1001
content:
It has been an issue whether punishment is more effective than rewarding. Some people think that punishment can force students to concentrate on their studying. Beside, it makes students to obey the rules in shorter time; however, other people have different oppinions. They think it is not right to punishment kids because punishment left scar in children mind. In my opinion I prefer the former.
My brother is a rather rebelious boy. He drink, play PC games when studying and even steal money from my grandfather. At first, my families forgived him with all these behaviors. We promise to pay him 300 NT per week for being a good boy; nevertheless, things do not go better. To our disappointment, my father decided to punish him for what he had done. He told my brother that he couldn't go out and played basketball unless he made up his mind to avoid all these bad behaviors. The rule was simple, however, it worked and that is the reason why I think punishment is more effective than rewarding.

subject: HW1001
content:
From my point of view, I would rather reward than punish students for learning because teachers can not only teach what the students need to learn but also help students solve their problems. Take problems for example, it may be associated with their homework mental and so on ....... But if you punish the students and make them feel afraid, they may not ask you for a help, then it will be a bad situation.
Take the teacher in my senior high school for instance, he is such a kind of man which I mentioned above, the relationship between he and I is not only teacher and student but also friends. The range of topic for us to talk is very broad, and we usually played basketball together after school and our spare time. Most important of all, he always rewarded us instead of punishing when we had a bad performance.
Brief speaking, rewarding instead of punishing students is the best way for a teacher to follow.

subject: HW1001
content:
When we are at school, we can have a teacher that either use punishment to motivate us, to learn and control our behavior or reward us for learning. Most people would think both of which are effective. In my opinion, this is more effective to that.
In the first place, A good teacher has to do their best to think of methods to motivate students to learn. Nothing is more effective than to reward them. Take me for example, when I was little, I had a teacher named Lisa, she aways had a smile face and never scolded us when I did things worng, and what's more; I told us, we would get somethig as long as we did the good job on our test, and thus whoever got one hundred percent corretly on our test always won a gift from her.
That's why all the students in our class are make any effors to study hard in order to got the prises. on the other hand, whoever didn't follow tle instrustions never got rewords.
Finally, I think a teacher should reward students wheather they do the good job or not.

subject: HW1001
content:
In one school, we can see different kinds of teacher. Some teachers try to use the punishments to control the students' behaviors, because they think that the students must be afraid and think twice before doing something bad. However, some teachers think that giving students some rewards as an encouragement is a good way to urge students to try their best. In my opinion, I prefer the latter one, and I think it's more effective.
In my opinion, I think if a teacher just use punishments all the time, maybe the students who have poor performances will have pressures to study, even go to school. And probably, the students may skip the classes to avoid being punished by their teachers. Sometimes it will cause more problems. Conversely, if a teacher can give his/her students some encouragements, such as giving them some scholarships or offering a delicious meal as an award, the students will have the motivation to complete something or strive for a good grade. I had a teacher who used the way to encourage us, and therefore I did better and better on the exams.
It's not because that the students want to eat just a meal or get these rewards. Instead, it shows a teacher's expectations to students. Many students will try their best to let the teachers see the efforts they had made. Though some people say that the students won't behave well without punishments, I think rewarding students is a better way to teach students, too. And it can make a win-win result between teachers and students.

subject: HW1001
content:
The issue of teaching methods has been a controversial arguement for a long time. Some people believe that punishments make students learn faster and more, while others think it is better to reward student. In my opinion, I definately think it is better to teach students without punishments.
The drawbacks of teaching with punishments are way more than the advantages it brings. Not knowing the meaning of studying, students become a learning machine under the pressure of being punished. On the other hand, students learn to use the violence to force others to do whatever others do not want to do.
Rewarding students for learning can lead to better results for some reasons. Firstly, students learn in a better atmosphere, so they can absorb more. Secondly, they are encouraged to learn, so they know what they are studying for and why they should study. Finally, students are more willing to help others, so they all can have better performances.
Learning without punishment makes students know more about the meaning of studying, for they are not forced to do so. For example, a student who had received the certificate of medical degree killed himself because he had been learning under the pressure of being punished by his parents and teachers. As we can see, if students are forced to do what they do not want to do, they will fight back one day. If they are encouraged, they will know the meaning of the thing they are seeking for. Undoubtedly, I will support the idea of rewarding students for learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
As far as I am concerned, I prefer rewarding to punishing to motivate students to learn. First, when students are rewarded at the first time, they will realize that as long as they learn much hard, they will be given something good. Chances are that they will try more hard to win the better rewarding. Second, rewarding can be considered a present. Students learn so hard that it is reasonable they are given gift. They will also get more confidence, courage and motivation by that present. Last but not least, it is unwise to punish students for they don't learn hard. It is likely that after they are punished, they will be more unwilling to learn and thus have some negative results.
Take me as an example. When I was in the first grade in elementary school, I always got bad grades and thus hated to learning. However, instead of punishing, my teacher still rewarded me and encouraged me to learn. She gave me a pencil as a present and told me that as long as I learned and studied hard, I must get good grades one day. Taking her advice and attracted by the bigger rewarding, I decided to try again and learn as hard as I can. Eventually, the miracle really happenened. I was the number one in my class when I was in the second grade. I did really succeed due to the encouragement and rewarding by my teacher. Therefore, after this experience, I become much firmly believe that rewarding is more powerful to motivate students to learn than punishing. After all, rewarding can give students confidence, courage and encouragement while punishing gives students nothing but tears.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I think the rewarding method is more effective. I truly believe every individual in the world needs love, respect and encouragement throughout any stage of their lives. Whether they are in the childhood, young adulthood or even when they are old. People might be stronger when they got older, but they still need all the positive input from the people around them. This will do the same to students. It's also the human nature that no one likes to be punished. When one is being punished, most likely, he or she will not realize that he or she probably does something awfully wrong to induce the punishment. All the person see is the punishment they get and the pain they suffer. This mentality is immature. Unfortunately, this is the mentality that most students have today. If the students cannot see the true meaning of punishment, why not try a different way - the rewarding method. As a teacher, my experience told me most of the students do not take scolds or any form of harsh treatment. They like to be told calmly when they do something wrong. If I punish them, I will only make things worse because they will be more repellent and disobedient. In addition, learning should be a pleasant experience. To make the learning enjoyable, a good relationship with the teacher and rewarding are the keys. Sometimes, students do not do well is simply because they have no interest or they do not have the ability to comprehend or understand the course With punishment, students will just lose interest on that subject more and will never learn. All they remember is the teacher make me hate the subject. My student, Amy, has hard times memorizing most of her studies, but her school teacher always punish her by making her rewrite the questions fifty times. In the end, she hates most her subjects except English. It is because I always reward her and care for her even when she only gets "15" on her test. In a long run, she did not find English enjoying and her grades start to improve. This is the best example to show the effectiveness of a rewarding teaching method.

subject: HW1001
content:
As far as I am concerned, using punishment is more effective in controlling students' behavior. Though we all know everyone likes to be praised or rewarded, rewarding students would make them more self-confident, rather than letting them understand their behavior and control themselves. Especially in Taiwan, we have a big class from elementary school to senior high. If the teacher is going to control their students' behavior, punishment will definately be the fastest way.
I remember when I was in junior high school, I have two homeroom teachers. One was in charge of our first year, and the other the rest two years The first one was just like our mother. She never scolded us. She was always kind to us. Everytime When anyone did something good, she would said, "you are the best!" and sometimes even bought some drinks for us as rewards we all loved her and we were very happy at that time. But our class was always in a mess. Other teacher didn't like to come into our classroom because we were always noisy. They said we were creative and out-going and we had our own voices. Sometimes we were too independent to obey our teachers' instructions. When we did something wrong, we would find excuses for ourselves. We were not the ones to blame.
Things changed when we entered our second year in junior high. Our new homeroom teacher was a strict, hard and demanding teacher. He seldom smiled. He was never kind to us. When we did something wrong. He would tell us what was wrong and punished us. Sometimes he would ask us to copy our chinese or English reading in our textbook. Sometimes he would ask us to do sit-ups or run for ten miles. We were all afraid of him. We were not that happy, but we were not that noisy, either. Our smiles disappeared, and we became less energetic. However, strange to say, other teachers loved our class better than before. As time went by, we gradually picked up our confidence and our smiles. Though at first we dared not to do anything bad because we didn't want to be punished, we found that we learned to control ourselves when we wanted to do something bad. When we graduated, we loved him and we knew we learned from him, "Think before you leap."
Because of my own experience in junior high, I realize punishment is not that bad. No one wants to be punished. If you want to avoid being punished, you'd better watch your own behavior. That's why I think punishment is more effective in controlling students' behavior.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I believe that rewarding students for learning can motivate them to learn better. The teachers should realize that the purpose of learning is to become a better person, but not to get a good grade.
Rewarding students for learning not only can make them enjoy going to school, but also help them learn effectively. The reason is that once the students enjoy learning, they will be eager to learn more. Besides, students can be concentrated on learning new knowledge without being afraid of being punished by the teachers. For example, if the teacher promises to give the first student, who finish his or her assignment correctly, three candies, the second student two candies, and the third student one candy, those students will be actively finish their assignment. In this case, the teacher can easily make the class learn effectively.
On the other hand, using the punishment to make students learn might cause them not willing to go to school. Since the students are afraid of being punished, they may even try to cheat to get a good score. In this case, students only study for passing the tests but actually learn nothing.
To make a conclusion, I think the teachers should use the method of rewarding students instead of punishing them.

subject: HW1001
content:
The most important thing of teaching students is how to encourage students to do something good but they don't want to do. I think that rewarding students is better than punishing them, because the punishment means to make people scared for doing something, once that they leave the environment, there is nothing making them feel scared. On the other hand, rewarding can make people interested in doing something good for them. Even if they no longer gain rewardment, they may still think that it is worth it.
I began to be interested in study because a teacher in my elementary school gave many different praises to us.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are a lot of methods to motivate students to learn. Some think punishing students is more effective than rewarding them, but others have the different opinions. To me, I believe punishing student is definitly more effective than the other.
First, there are more and more parents only having one child in Taiwan. Those parents usually treat their children very well, so their children easily are spoiled at home. In the case, the teachers have to motivate them to learn and to control their behavior by punishing them.
Second, those children who are spoiled take the reward as natural at their house. Rewarding them for learning is useless. However, the suitable punishment is more useful than serious punishment.
In summary, I think punishing student is more effective than rewarding students if the punishment is suitable and good for the student's learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
Recently, teachers have been banned from punishing students. Before the law was enforced, we can see news about teachers punishing their students inappropriately. Though sometimes we cas still see this kind of incident be reported, but it has decreased in the cases.
Many teachers or parents think that punishing is a good way to teach. They think if there's punishments, it will put stress on students, and this stress can not only deter them from doing something bad but also be a good student. But as far as I am concerned, punishing in case of making students to learn hard is not a effective way. Because punishments may hurt students' self-esteem and it may put negative influences on one's personality, too. Even if students are under good controling because of punishments, it won't work forever. Once students understand the influences lied behind what they have done, they will play a good role in what they should do.
We can see many movies telling stories about how teachers changed their students. Most of the cases, they lectured them but not punished them. My mom has told me that when she was in junior high school, there was a classmate who was too naughty for every teachers to teach. When every teachers all had no idea about how to deal it, my mom's music teacher made him a big change. It took the teacher a long time to understand the student's thoughts. The teacher finally found that all he wanted was just other people's friendship. When the teacher found true meaning behind the student's performance, she owned the student's trust.
I was informed from this case that sometimes what we get used to is not always correct. Maybe there still are many good ways that not only are effective but also won't hurt others.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are two main ways for teachers to teach students are by punishment and reward. In my opinion, rewarding students is more effective than punishing them in learning and controling their behavior.
First, using punishment may be useful to some degree. However, it can damage students mentally and physically. It also makes students hard to get through the horror the punishment brings and have difficulties recovering from it. Second, urging students to study hard by rewarding them not only makes them feel more confident when receiving the gifts or encouragement from teachers, but also have fullfillment so that they will keep studying to strike for excellence.
To most of the students, they are more glad to earn reward than being hurt on their bodies. It seems that there are more merits to motivate students than to give them punishment. For these reasons, I think rewarding students is more effective between both of them.

subject: HW1001
content:
As far as I am concerned, the second method, "Rewarding students for learning can lead to be better results," is more effective. Generally speaking, when it comes to studying, students in Taiwan often have plenty of pressure from their teachers, parents or even students themselves. To make students learn happily and confidently, I would rather instruct them in an encouraging and rewarding way than punish them just because of the bad behaviors or poor grades. Maybe the way I choose might take a longer time to get the result; however, I think it's worth awaiting.
I am going to share two cases with you; they are in the following, Sam and Howard. Both of them ever had some problems in the learning and behavior. In the beginning, I would punish them for their mistakes by forcing them to some to school for studying on weekends or asked them to be volunteers for cleaning the house. However, the punishment didn't work well. Sam and Howard still made the same mistakes. One day, I changed my mind and had a talk with them. After Sam shared his feeling with me, I provided him certain flexibility and adjustment on learning. Whenever Sam met with the standard, I would give him an award. Gradually, Sam made improvements on his learning and life. On the other hand, Howard was seldom late for school again. I tried to analyze what he had now and told him directly about how to improve the terrible situation. Anyway, I firmly believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
Different teachers take different beliefs toward teaching students. Some teachers believe that students can learn well by punishments. However, some teachers are convinced that rewarding is the best way to motivate students to learn. In my opinion, I prefer rewarding students to punishing them. Although, students could learn better by punishments, it may reduce their interest about learning. Some students may take passive and negative attitudes toward study. On the other hand, rewarding students could keep their motivation in learning, particularly for young children. Though, rewarding can not ensure students get high grades in the exams, it is one way to enhance students' learning motivation.
For example, if teacher tell students they could get rewards by getting high grades in English test, some students may set the goals in order to get teachers' positive responses. In fact, setting goal is one of beneficial ways which could motivate students' interesting and inspire them to learn well. In short, there are some advantages and disadvantages about teaching students by punishments and rewarding. The important point is that teachers should not extinguish students' learning motivation, they must help them to find the happiness of learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think some appropriate punishment to students is needed, because all students do not want to be punished, it will remind students that you still have something to do.
Appropriate punishment sometimes can become a way to educate students. When students heared "You will be punished if you do not ... ...", it can form some stress in their mind. Stress of punishment can motivate students to finish their job on time, for example, it can let students pay more attention on their studying, so they can finish their homework on time or get better grades in the test.
If educate students just with rewarding without punishment, it will let the students become lazy. Because they will think that if I perform will in school, I will get rewards, otherwise, I will lose nothing. It is not a good attitude that a studying - hard students should have.
I think the punishment is necessary in our education, appropriate punishment can make students become more concentrate on their studying and more regular in their lives.

subject: HW1001
content:
"No pain, no gain," is an old saying that almost everyone has heard of it, but is punishment always work when it comes to education?
Punishment does help students to tell right from wrong, but rewarding students seems to make more sense as students growing up, and personally I prefer the latter. In my opinion, the motivation created by punishment is not even useful. If you are force to do something you really don't care, what will you react? You will put things off, being hesitating and distractive, or rush to finish your work. These reactions are just the oppesite things we want students to do. As far as I concered, rewarding students is more effective. You will be surprised what students can do when they trying their best.
Recalling my high school recollection, I can easily remembe that my classmates and chatting about our teachers. We talked about which teacher is better. Now, when I think about it, I find that the teachers we liked are those who reward students and respect students, and it's clearly that you will learn better from a teacher you like in spite of one you afraid of. When there's no one force you or tell you what to do, then you are on your own, and you have to force yourself to make the right choice.

subject: HW1001
content:
