To regulate students is one inentable responsibility for teachers at school. However, in my opinion, rewarding students for learning is more effective than giving punishments. When being punished, students feel not only scared but also more reluctant to learn. The results of punishment can probably demonstrate a better learning behavior, but students are not learning of their own will and just being forced to. On the other side, rewarding students for learning may not be the best way to urge student, but it can boost students' creativity and the ability to imagine, which are lacked under Taiwan's education system.
Take my friend, Bill, for example. Since Bill is in his childhood, he had passion and talent for math but did really bad on the other subjects. Nevertheless, his teacher patiently tought and advised him about other subjects while praising him of his good math comprehension, and so did their parents. They not only did not give him pressure but also encouraged him to be a math teacher. In fact, he really did it several years ago. He told me how he is grateful for his teacher and parents and wishes to be the one like his parents and teachers.
Another opinion of mine is that punishments may prevent children from enhancing their own interests, which might harm the future development. Teacher should link whatever they teach to the students' daily life and future careers, rather than tell students to reach teachers' standards on everything. Thus, when students have bad deeds, teachers should patiently advise him and discuss with students, instead of giving direct ponishments. Also, teachers should always encourage students and boost their professions.
In conclusion, teachers' influence is lifelong and profound for students. Students are learning and absorbing directly from teachers. Teachers should always be patient and kind when students make mistakes and lead them to the correct way, and never use punishments just for regulating unless necessarily needed.

subject: HW1001
content:
To motivate students to learn and to get ideal results of schoolwork or personal behavior, some teachers employ punishment, however, others reward students who perform well on schoolwork. In my opinion, I tend to support the way of rewarding students is more effective.
To encourage students to learn, the positive reinformancement, such as adding grades, giving presents, or even verbal encouragement, like "Well done." or "I'm so proud of you." could reinforce students' learning motivation from the affective perspective. Taking my own experience of learning English for example, when I was in the seventh grader, I was always afraid of speaking English in public. However, my English teacher often enouraged me and rewarded me when I made progress in speaking English. Gradually, I am more confident in speaking English and highly motivated to learn English well. Besides, I used to be always punished when I didn't perform well on the subject of math. After that I always escape to learn more or better on math.
Thus, if teachers could use rewarding appropriately when students make progress or perform ideal results, it is much more effective for students to learn spontaneously because of their high learning motivation.

subject: HW1001
content:
I would like to say that in these days, teachers reward students more than punish them. In my opinion, I think that most of the time, rewarding is much more effective than punishment. Because noone would like to be scolded and shouted by the teacher! With this thought in mind, sometimes it just won't work on some students. In order to solve this problem, "Punishment should be used as well as rewards." has become my motto.
At school, all the teachers try to be really nice to all the students, but my home room teacher, Mrs. Ho, record all the wrong thing we have done in her own notebook. If you're the first time to make a little mistake in one week, such as being late to the school, it would come out fine. But if you have make three "X" on the notebook a week, than you would receive your punishment, for example, washing the ground or helping the school to keep the campus clean, etc. To the one who have never get "X" in a pirod of time, she would give you the provity in choosing the seat in the classroom or have some tasks that is easy to finish, etc. that's why my motto comes.
In conclusion, having punishment without rewards or having rewards without punishment would not be the bet stragity in teaching. The best thing to know is that your teacher gives you both punishment and rewards. Thus, the students obey the regulation could become more and more than before and the one who don't would be less, even none in your class. Cheers to punishment and rewards balance!

subject: HW1001
content:
Punishments was one of the most useful way for teachers and parents to force students to match up to their expectations. But nowadys, using punishments to control students is no longer a good idea. In the past, people's thoughts were more conservative, students spared no efforts to live up to adults' standards for fear that they would be punished. However, young people think differently and more open-minded, they believe everyone got human rights that shouldn't be invaded by being punished. And there are also many people who launch compaigns in order to fight for students rights.
In my opinion, rewarding students for learning can lead to better results, which is more effective than punishing. Take myself, a student, for example, whenever my teachers ask us to do something, they never threaten us; instead, they encourage us by awarding those who achieve the goal. It's more acceptable for students to conform to what they said. As the proverb goes, "to err is human, and to forgive devine." We should motivate students by telling them what is alright to do and what's not proper to do in place of making them become upset by punishment. Although sometimes punishment and blaming is needed, for those who are really notorious, we should put more emphasis on urging students than warning them, because do it with delight is much more better and efficient than do it with an unwilling heart. Last but not least, awarding is always priorivr to punishing.

subject: HW1001
content:
Punishment and reward are totally opposite ways to educate students, although the main purpose is the same, which is to help students behave well. In my opinion, the two methods are both necessary for educating students. When students do something wrong or think things in astray ways, teachers must use punishment to control their behavior. On the other hand, when students have good performance in school, teachers should take rewarding method and it will motivate them to do more effort next time.
For example, I have taken one thousand dollars from my mother's pocket when I was ten years old, just for a new toy robot. When my mother knew it, she was very angry, and I had not got any allowance in the whole year. However, she told me, "if you have good performance in school, you will get allowance back." And then, I studied hard and got good grades in final exams. I learned how to do things good and control my behavior.
All in all, punishment and reward are both important to educate students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Recently the punishment at school has become a popular topic. Parents have different opinions, some think it's necessary to keep evacuating, but some consider it brings great shadow for children's future. In fact, many psychologists and experts agree that instead of using punishment at school, students would rather speak to someone, who are willing to listen to them and treat them as a friend.
Most of students are in puberty; therefore, their personalities and thoughts are usually unstable. They love to share secrets with friends but parents, because they consider friends are the only one, who compeletly realize them, so parents can consider to give more concern to children's life. For instance, figuring out their situations of friendship. This way can also be used, when teachers want to get closer with his or her students. Then, it's more easy to shorten the distance between teacher and students or parents and children. Children can modify their behavior by building resonable communication instead of impulsive punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
Punishment and rewarding are both a way to motivate or to control students' behavior. As far as I am concerned, I'll choose rewarding to encourage students if I were a teacher.
Rewarding students bring out better effect than punishing them because I think punishment is a method that makes students fear of what results from behavioring badly. Punishment might be a stimulating method, but it doesn't have students act well at heart. Once the punishments are canceled, all the misbehavioring will come back again.
And rewarding is not like punishment. Though it's like alluring them with rewards, it is much better than making them fear of punishments. I believe rewarding could lead students to act well by nature one day. By using a positive way to motivate and to control them, I think it will result in a postive outcome much better than using a negative way.
For example, my little two-years-old cousin, Andrew, is a naughty boy who used to pick up his neighbor's flower often, which really is a big problem to my uncle and aunt. At first, they tried to stop Andrew by hitting on his bottoms as a punishment. Andrew stopped picking neighbors flower and we soon found out that he turns to pick flowers from the road side. Then, my uncle and aunt changed the way, they told Andrew if he doesn't pick flowers randomly and behavior well, he would get a reward, and if he is always acting like a good boy, he'll get a big reward. Now Andrew is a kid well-manered and is always be claimed "What a good boy, he is very polite!"
Acording the reasons above, I support that rewarding does have better effect on motivating and controlling students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Currently, some people believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results, but others hold a different attitude. In my opinion, I think it is better to reward students when teachers want their students to have better perfermances. The following are my arguments.
First of all, I think the most significant reason is that rewarding students can help students to be confident and then have better perfermances. For example, I were not good at math at the elementary school. But no matter how many mistakes I made on the math tests, my math teacher didn't blame me or punish me. On the contrary, he continued to teach me and tell me that I were doing well on the other part of the exams. Therefore, I had built confidences and studied harder, and then I got the highest grade on the next math exam. From my own experience, I believe it will lead to better results if teacher can reward students for their advantages.
Furthermore, another reason of mine is that using punishments to students will worsen their study situations. If students are punished by their teachers, they might not like the teachers anymore. The students might not concentrate on the class lessons because they do not want to learn from the annoying teachers. It not only makes them have lower grades but also let the teachers to decrease their teach passions. I think the teacher should not punish the students in order to motivate students' learning willings.
In conclusion, if I were a teacher, I won't punish my students. I will be patient and friendly to teach them because I think that many students are too young to understand the importance of studying and learning, I need to reward them to make them having the interest in studying. Therefore, I strongly believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
From where I stand, teachers using punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior is more effective. There is no denying that from time to time, rewarding students for learning can lead to better results, but according to my experiences, this way will be effective only when the students are able to control themselves. On the contrary, if teachers use punishment to motivate students, many of them will behave well so that they won't be punished. Therefore, though this may not be a good way, I still think of punishment as a more effective way.
When I was a senior high school student, my English teacher used punishment to motivate us to study every day. If we failed to live up to his expectations, he would punish us. In the long run, we passed the College Entrance Exam with flying colors. On the contrary, one of the teachers rewarded us for learning. This way led some of my classmates to think that they could do whatever they want during the class. Therefore, they asked questions that were not related to the lessons. In the end, we were behind schedule and spent more time catching up with others. Due to these two examples, I think that teachers should use punishment to motivate students to do well though it's not a good way.

subject: HW1001
content:
Every student is unique and different. The best way to teach this student may not be the best way to teach the others. In the past, parents and teachers believed that using punishment would motivate students to study harder. However, more people support teaching with love is better nowadays.
I was the one who experienced this changing period in that my parents were under the front teaching way and I was the later one. Therefore, in my opion, the most effective way is rewarding students for learning but with some appropriate punishment. The followings are my reasons: First, proper punishment is okay for students. It can let students understand what is allowed to do and what isn't especially when they are little. However, students are willing to learn from their hearts through rewarding them. Last but not the least, students can build up their confidence by being rewarded and become more interested in learning. That's why I think rewarding students for learning is more effective.
The teaching ways can influence students a lot. And the teachers should consider more and be careful when teaching every student.

subject: HW1001
content:
At first, I don't think each of both methods is good enough to be used on so many different characteristics of students. Although for who believe in, "Spare the rod, and spoil the children" and those making students better by rewarding, they all have their counts, the key point is depend on situations, rather than on methods.
Hence, the best policy is to apply them at the same time. For the students who need rewarding more than punishment, providing attractive rewarding will be better than the later. On the contrary, for those who are not aware of their bad situations, proper corporal punishment is necessary. Take my classmate Tom for example, he was once a lazy student, but after punishment, he knew his fault and study hard. Now he enjoys the rewarding from our teacher.
In conclusion, both methods are good in some respect, but students may need to treated in a way that can combine the advantages of both. That is why I think the best method is not each of them.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. And the reasons are below. First of all, nobody likes to be punished rather than being praised. Students like to be rewarded so that they will have an urge to pursue a better behavior. Besides, human beings need encouragement to motivate them to keep on the good work.
Secondly, I think criticisms and punishments will lead to pessimistic preservative. If a person is always punished for what he had done and heard no reward for his good behaviors, all he sees will be the part that he had not done well. Sooner or later, he will be a pessimistic person without any self-confidence.
On the contrary, if a person is alway rewarded for the good behavior or things he did, he maybe more self-confident. And he will not always sees the dark sides in life, so when he experienced obstacles, he will definitely be the one who overcome them. I think this kind of people are more likely to succeed than the ones mensioned before.
In sum, I think that teachers should reward their students instead of punishing or criticizing them all day long. Besides, rewarding students does not only have good effects on the students but also on the teachers. When the teachers see their students have the motivation to break their bad habits and change their bad behaviors, they will sure to be happy.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I believe using punishment is usually more effective than rewarding. First, students are always naughty. They do not know the rule and like to do whatever they want, for example, fooling around, fighting with each other ... etc. They won't realize how serious will it be until they do it and taking the conceqence. So, punishing them can let them know it is not right and never do it again. That is why punishment is neccessary to them. Second, rewarding them may not help because student do not scare "not being rewarded". They can do the same stupid thing next time if they want, without punishment. Above all, I think only by punishing students can make them control their behavior effective.
My cousin is three years old. He always likes to eat everything he saw, concluding paper, eraser ... etc. My aunt always takes a candy to her baby and takes the strange things out of his mouth. My cousin loves candy, but he still eats everything he saw. Until my mom once yelling at him, who was eating my mom's credit card, he stopped eating it and never ate thing for a while. From this example, I find rewarding might let my cousin think eating strange things is not a big deal, but a game. Yelling at him will make him behave well.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are many ways to teach students. Some teacher may punish their students because they are out of control. Others usually reward their students because they behave well. In my opinion, both ways of teaching are important. When it comes to student who needs more encouragment, the rewarding way is a good choice. But if the student doesn't listen to the teacher at all, the other choice seems better.
Take me for example. When I was in elementary school, I was a very shy girl in the class. I didn't talk much during conversation class. In this situation, my homeroom teacher encouraged me very often. She rewarded me if I did something good, but if I made mistakes, she didn't punish me at all and told me how I can make it better. There was a boy in our class. He always played tricks on other classmates. At first, our teacher didn't punish him and asked him say sorry to the victims as well. But he did it all the time, and many classmates complained about it. Finally, the teacher used punishment to motivate him to control his behavior. And it seems a good way when facing the students who is out of control like him.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Why do I say that? Because people all like rewards. It can motivate everyone to work. Though punishments also can motivate people to work, it is much worse than rewards. People are scared of the punishment, so they go to work. They don't want to do it. They would make a very bad products, because they don't really want to do it. Rewarding them can make them really want to work, then, they would make a better products. They would work happier because they will get rewards. When I was a child, I had a example of that rewarding students is better than punishing them. One day, one of my chassmates got punishment from his mother because he got a zero on the test. When his mother promised that she would use rewards to exchange the punishments, he had a better grades than before I was suprised of that thing. From then on, I always believe that rewarding students is better than punishing them.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. I sincerely doubt it. Punishment might be effective for a short while, because the threat coming with the punishment might scare students to stop bad behavior or force them to learn. However, the threat won't last long and it won't inspire any students while they are learning.
In my opinion, rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. The reward could be anything from a warm hug to a very simple compliment. The progress may be slow, but in the long run the reward would become the power to support the students to change. It will be the courage they need.
One little boy in my third grade class never did homework since the first semester. Punishment was always the solution I could come up with. Until one day, I held his hand and called him 'my little baby'. He changed the way he used to look at me and he showed an unbelievable smile to me. The very next day, his little notebook lied on my desk. That was the day I believe rewarding is a better way.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. It is the best method for teachers to teach their students. If a teacher give his or her students compliments for their doing well, they will connect learning well to good behavior and the road to success. Students will do really like to study not for exams but for ability-fostering. It is more effective when it comes to motivating students to learn.
I have read a biography written by a famous piano player. He said that he was lucky enough to have a kind-hearted and passionate piano teacher since he was a kid. And she encouraged him to play well by rewading him. When he was a teenager, he had an another teacher. This one shouted at him and controlled him to play the piano in a difficult way. After several weeks, he could not but leave this one. Because he didn't learn anything from the hot-tempered teacher. Afterwards, he found the former one back instead. And he is well-known all over the world now!
Punishment and control won't make a student motivated. It may disminish one's curiosity in learning. So I think rewarding students for learning is much better.

subject: HW1001
content:
Strictly speaking, punishment used by teachers to motivate and to control students is an old-fashioned, out-of-date and even barbaric way. This method leads to more damage than its goods. Compared to punishment, rewarding students for learning is undoubtedly the better alteruative.
First of all, we should take the drawbacks of punishment seriously. Indeed, this way is effective in the relatively short time. Nonetheless, students who have been punished by their teachers are easy to hate the teacher and even the whole society. As a consequence, they often turn into a more aggressive and hatred-filled people. Besides, as is often the case, in a punishment-prevailing atmosphere, people tend to care much about avoiding it rather than doing better.
On the contrary, rewarding students for learning serves as the better choice for several reasons. To begin with, not only does this fashion help establish the proper attitude toward life, but also bridge the divide between the two sides. In fact, it is of great importance that students learn to cherish and appreciate for what they have and what they gain. Additionally, a good relation between teachers and students may a help the students after they leave schools and seek work oppurtunities. Therefore, it is safe to say that the latter method can make a difference in the long run.
Even though the latter method I certainly the better, we shouldn't neglect the advantages of punishment. My opinion is that we ought to take the two ways alternatively, however, rewarding accounts for the bulk of the process. Nevertheless, in comparton, rewarding students for learning can contribute to better results definitely.

subject: HW1001
content: I'm the opponent of the teaching of punishment. First, I am convinced that lazziness is the nature of human. Only through endless blame and punishment can we remember the mistake we have made. Second, we should cultivate correct behavior and perspect toward life as young as possible. So the severe education must come to existence to inspire the children from their childhood. Most of all, our society is established on the foundation of laws. We should let our children know if they break laws, there are many mean punishment and public wouldn't treat them again and give them new possibility. So I think the teaching of punishment is the adaptation of the society for a student. Many decades ago, the education system in Taiwan is severe. The students under this system grow up to be the generation of our parents. They shoulder the duty of the thriving of Taiwan. Their uncompromising determination brings about the economy improvement of Taiwan. All the ability they have is coming from the severe education the receive. The teacher's punishment result in their ability to stand failures, which is the characteristic our generation lack of.

subject: HW1001
content:
At the first, my opinion is NO teacher should punished the students, neither for motivate them to learn nor to control their behavior. Maybe some of the teachers will say they love the studonts, so they have to teach them the right and wrong, for that purpose, punishment is necessary. But, when the teacher did that, they were teaching the student that you can control or get what you want by violants and by the power you have. I do not think it is right. Recently, the goverment try to make New law to stop teachers use punishment to hurt the students Many reports tell us encourage is much better than punishment.
There for. We should understand that, if you don't like be punished by others, We should not agree that teache could use punishment to control students.
The good teacher we know always is kind and gentel. They will do the right thing by themself then the student will know how to lern and understand the teacher is their model. If you are parents, do you like your child be punished by the teacher. Do you want your chid study at a violant place.
If the answer is yes, then we should stop the punishment at school Now.

subject: HW1001
content:
Carrots or sticks? That has been a deboting issuce since teaching was in its existence. Some teachers insist that the punishment is the only way to motivate students' behaviors mentally and physically, while others confront that it couldn't be better to encourge students by giving some incentive as a reward. If I have a say on this topic, I would be leaning toward the latter one.
During their formative years, even the well-behaved teenagers probably turn out to be rebels. As their mentors to lead them to the right track, teachers or parents should be more careful about adapting the most appropriate way to guide them. Punishment can definitely call the shot and constraint their behaviors temporarily, but it also creates hidden conflicts at the same time. Eventually, when these young people grow to be adults, they will not learn the virtues of forgiving and correction. What could be worse, they might become violent persons who are apt to threatening other people. When I was little, there was a little boy who came from a low-income family. His parent punished him with sticks from time to time. He gradually became a gangster, hanging around with some delinquencies. Luckily, he met a good teacher who never gave up on him. He voluntarily tutored him after school, asked him to stay at his home so he would not be bothed by his bad friends. He finally grew to be a scholar with good virtures.
To wrap up my arguments and the above example, I would suggest everyone, no matter you are a teacher, or a parent, even if you only have one chance to teach somebody, do not us punishment. It might become a scourge in your whole life.

subject: HW1001
content:
I don't think punishment is an effective method to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. The first method, I make some cards which have scores on them. Whenever I start my class, I always ask questions to know if they review or preview the lesson. I encourge them to answer my questions, and I give them cards as rewards. They can get from one to three points according to the question is easy or tough.
I also like to divide the class into groups which are included high to low efficiency students. I'll leave some time for them to discuss the questions. They may need to answer individually or have someone to report in class.
In addition, I'll ask them to find the answers by surfing the Net or looking up some reference books. One time, I asked students to find the kinds of music. They needed to collect information, such as the background music, the representative musicians, and which place is famous for. Students in groups reported in class by giving the music they found, posters they drew, and the information they searched for. Each one of the students cooperated with his peer classmates. I could see how excited they were. Although I don't teach music, students can learn more from the other field. From this, I can also understand their talented abilities. Some students may behave better in drawing or role playing; others may like to write or speak. I'll let them find their own efficiecy, promote them to express themselves, and build their own abilities by rewards.

subject: HW1001
content:
Have you ever woke up and thought about the first thing was: "I don't want to go to school!" or "I want to pretend I have a headache today. So I can get rid of school!! ?" I did. And that was the fifth grade of my elementary school.
My teacher believed she could make us focusing in the class by using all kinds of punishment. Yes, it worked. But temporately, she made most of my classmates hated to go to school, hated to learn knowledge from her classes. In the end, No one wins.
I am a father now. I still can not forget all those horrible memories. Every time I think of those days in her class, I still feel anger. So now, while I am teaching my 8-year-old son, I will use the rewarding way. Sometimes it was not easy to make him focus on the things that I am trying to teach him. And it might take longer time to have him remember. I still believe the punishment can only make him unhappy in learning things. Just like I could never forgive my fifth grade teacher. She took away a lot of joy in learning which should not happen in anyone's school life.

subject: HW1001
content:
School teachers are playing an important role to education their students to be a useful person in the future. To make this goal to come true, teachers have to work hard to the education, and they want their students to performan great grades on their studies. Some teachers will strict with their students, taking some punishment on them. But for me, I don't like it. I would like to the teacher encourage their students instead.
First of all, everyone likes to get respect from others, if your student do not doing good job in their studies, and the teacher just punish them, not finding the problems behind them. As you know, most students are teenages, which mean they are in rebellion stage, if you put too much stress to them, they will rebounce it. So you can get what you want to.
In another words, if we can encourge them to do something they wan to do, and compliment them when they get a little progress in their performance. I think they will like to study hard. Taking me as an example, when I was in high school, I falled behind in studies. But my teacher of high school had encouraged me and said you have a talent in book if you could study more hard? Then, I had enrolled a college.
I have to say that they who have a good environment to grow will be a good people in the future. If you grew up friendly, you are to be a good behavior peroson. So rewarding students for learning can be a good choice.

subject: HW1001
content:
This is a long-term question that is never solved. In my opinion, I would believe that punishment is the most effective method to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. I am 50 years old now. I still clearly remember when I was in the primary school and junior high school, I was punished by some teachers owing to certain inappropriate doings such as cheating, playing truant, fighting with classmates, and the like. With the severe punishments, I realized what was right and what was wrong, which helped me a lot toward several fields like studying, making friends, doing right things, and so on. After my graduation from junior high school I entered the best senior high school and university in Taiwan, and furthemore I have been working in some international and famous companies since I finished the army service.
Neverthelessly, the so-called punishment should be given appropriately. Teachers should hold the though in mind that they punish those who have a bad behavior or have a low score mark as so to correct their wrong behaviors, or to motivate students to study hard. In addition, teachers have to use punishment in a right way and at a right time. In this current education system in Taiwan, teachers dare not punish students because they don't want to bring about any trouble as well as complaints from students' parents, especially when the students have a better background in social or political status.
Although love education is also not so bad, yet I still believe only by giving students certain suitable punishments can students realize the right and the wrong. I am the good example as mentioned above. Without the punishments given by teachers, I am still a nobody now; I am convinced.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding is always better than punishing when it comes to educating students. I do consider appropriate punishment sometimes an effective way to modify some behavior, especially for those who are too naughty to abide by any regulation. However, I think that teachers should come up with more creative ideas to educate and motivate students rather than to punish them.
My personal experience is the most convincing evidence for example. I was one of the most troublesome students when I was 11 years old. Sometimes, I did something bad only to show my rebellion against my strict teacher. He tried every possible ways to control our behavior such as kicking students or slapping students on their faces in public. But I found that the stricter he was, the more we defended. I only learned negative emotion at the time. After several years I met another teacher with a totally different attitude in educating students. She believed that all students are born with good nature and what we have done was just because we got lost. She tried to teach me about responsibility through assigning me as her assistant, instead hitting me. I found that I no longer had those negative emotion but even were eager to do more for everybody. Although it's not really a rewarding, the result is much more valuable than any rewarding. By comparison of the above example, it proves again my opinion that rewarding is better than punishing.

subject: HW1001
content:
To my opinion, I think that rewarding students for learning is the more effective method. First, I believe that mankind were born in kindness. Because of this kind of personality, students who do the wrong things has two different factors. One is that the chid hasn't been educated enough to think of what is defenitly mistaken. In order to deal with this situation, the student originally didn't know what is right what is wrong, the teacher used punishment to control the student's behavior might cause side effects. The better way is that tell him what is right and teach him how to face the events. If he or she does the correct way when another similar situation bump up, the teacher should have to reward the student. Additionally, the student should strongly remember what is right and what is wrong. They will pursuit the correct way to solve any problem they will meet.
Second, as the teacher try to teach the student the correct behavior, using punishment at first may make the student feel awful and uncomfertable. To make the student think of the optomistic way in their childhood, the teacher should be positive not negative. When I think of my elementary school life, there were both happiness and unhappiness. The unhappiness most likely is that something I didn't wrong and then I got strickly punishment. At that time I might totally remember next time I won't do this again. when I grew up and are able to criticize the wrong and the right, I think there will be another peace way can teach me the truth. After all, no one wants to be punished and take the teacher as a harmful devil. Give me a candy is better than punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
As we know that students are the most valued potential for the State's future. The growing of students can be affected by two mainly environment including family and school. Family undoubtly should provide deeply love and warm bed for children. On the other hands, school should provide achademic knowledge and making students learn better is teachers' responsibility.
But the ways which teachers use in teaching students are very controversial at some degree. Some teachers use punishments to motivate students to learn and control their behavior. Others use rewarding students for learning. In my eyes, using punishment definitely brings more disadvantages than advantages. And they can be stated as follows. First, it could make bad effect on students such as misunderstanding that the only way to achieve one thing is using punishment. Second, it might remain an awful experience in students' memory which can make their behavior change badly. What's worst, students might use the same way on teaching their children in the future.
Hence, I believe that rewarding students can lead to better result. Take my experience for example, my high school teacher promised me that as long as I got a good grade on Chinese subject, she took me to a theater watching a movie. That's very encouraging. So I worked very hard to achieve it. Finally, I did it and I felt the sense of achievement which I had never had.
In Sum, if I were a teacher, I would give reward to my students to learn because it is the best way to brighten their way for future developing.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, there are many arguments about whether teachers should punish their students or not. Some people support this point of view because they consider this is the fastest way to correct these students' behavior and motivate them to study. Some people reject this method because they think punishment would discourage students and make them refuse to learn.
In my opinion, I think teachers should reward their students instead of punishments. Students always make mistakes during learning. A good teacher should try to figure out why the students encounter so many learning difficulties and try to help them. Rewarding students doesn't mean you have to give them gifts or something valuable. If your students do their homework well or always have good reaction in the class, you can praise them verbally and give them a big smile.
I have a part-time job in the cram school. My responsibility is teaching children English and help them to improve their skills as soon as possible. However, some of the students are pretty slow and naughty. They can't pay attention to me in the class at all. At first, I would become very angry and scolded them seriously. Nevertheless, this method didn't resolve the problem. It only made these students scared and they were afraid to ask me questions. As a result, I decided to change my attitude. I try to be patient when the students face some learning problems. When they answer my questions right, I will praise them and give them stamps. After a period of time, I find out these slow students has improved their skills a lot. It's really inspiring.
Everything has pros and cons. We can't say that rewarding students is the only way to help students become better. Nevertheless, by my own experience, I consider this is a good method to encourage kids to learn. They need teachers' supports to become strong and confident during their learning process.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my point of view, I think rewarding students is better than punishing them if teachers want to motivate them to learn. Though punishment can make student behave in the way teachers expect them to do in a short time, this kind of change will not last long. Once students leave both school and the control of teachers, they will behave in the way they used to be. On the other hand, if teacher reward students by complimenting them instead of punishing them, then students will be happier and more willing to learn and quit their bad habbits. After graduating, students will keep learning and behaving in a good way because doing so can bring them happiness which is the same as the pleasure and compliments they get from their teachers while studying in school.
I still remembered when I was a little girl, I went to an English cram school. Teachers in that cram school was not only harsh but also scaring. They punished student if they didn't do well in the exam. And I was the one who always failed in every exam and received many punishment after the teachers found my low grades. At that time, I really hated to learn English. No sooner had I entered that cram school then I started trembling. Fortunately, my mom noticed this and decided to teach me by herself. She encouraged me to learn English. Even if I didn't do well in the English exam, she still complimented me for making a little bit progress in the exam. Thanks to my mom's "rewarding teaching skills", I fell in love with English gradually finally.

subject: HW1001
content: Teaching style is a topic people usually mention in modern society. Some insist students must be under severe discipline, or neither will they have good grade, nor will they obey any regulations. The others believe that offering compliment and reward is the best way to inspire students. In my opinion, the latter is better than the former. A positive treatment may not be the most effective in short term, but it lead students to realize their capability in studying and discover their own interest in different subject. Oppositely, negative punishment forces students to learn. Results might be shown quickly, but students always take too much stress and lose interest in learning. Hence, they will possibly deny any chance to learn advance and even forsake themselves. When I was in junior high school, my teach use corporal punishment to make students abide the rule and study hard. I didn't see any outstanding achievement was made, all I knew is that some of my classmates were full of fury and pain.

subject: HW1001
content:
During my school time, this problem also confused my teachers. I think rewarding students is more effective and more good and can last longer. Why punishment is useful? Because students affride teachers. But if teachers use the second method to encourge their students, students will change their behaviors by they wanted, not because the fear. So I think rewarding students is more effective way to learn and to control their behavior.
Like my school time, I remember that was my second year of junior high school. And my classmates very like to talk on class, and first teacher said if somebody had talk on class seem by me. I will punish he or she. And a mouth later our class still very noise, because when our "punish teacher" go away, we started talking as fast as possible. Finally, our teacher decided to try another ways to control our "talk on class". This time he used rewarding, he said if no teacher talk to me say you are noise then we went to somewhere to play. Because everyone in my class is very want to go out, so they stoped talking on class. And if someone talked on class, they would "adviced" he or her talk later. Now, I still had the pictures we went to Yang-Me moutain. This method not only achieve what teacher wants but also improve the relationship between my classmates and my teacher.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students for learning is much better than using punishment to motivate students.
In most of my experiences indicated that if you used punishment to motivate students, the result can only be a failure. In fact, students will be afraid of even hate to study because their teachers use punishments for their academic performances.
On the contrary, if teachers reward students for their academic performances, students will have their ambition to get good grades. Students will be willing to study if there is a rewarding they can get.
For example, when I was in my junior high school, my teacher punished me because I got a 80 in my Chinese test. Since then, my Chinese grades went lower and lower. Few weeks after, my father discovered my grades were worse than before. He told me that as long as I got 90 in my Chinese exam, he would buy an mp3 player for me. Finally, I got 95 in my Chinese exam.
As far as I am concerd, rewarding students is more effective than punishing students.

subject: HW1001
content:
There is no denying that both punishment and rewarding are important to help students learn better. It's almost impossible just to use one access to lead to good education. If given one choice, I would choose rewarding studens for learning can lead to better results.
Since I am an elementary school teacher I have experienced too many times that when you use punishment to control students' behavior, they would stop bad behavior right now. However, after a period of time, the bad behavior shows again. Punishment can control students' behavior only for a while.
If teachers set up rules clearly, most students will follow them. When students have good performance, teachers encourage them or give them prize at proper time, students will keep the honor in mind. Such positive attitude will lead students to make progress.
I almost forgot what I was punished for in my elementary school when I was a little girl. But I alway keep the words "You are good at Art." that my teacher told me in a class. When I feel discouraged at schoolwork, I would think the encouraging words my teacher told me. Now, I am an Art teacher. I try my best to encourage students.
In conclusion, I firmly believe that rewarding students for learning is better than punishing them for it.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Students will have better relationships with teachers and they will be eager to learn.
Learning should be something enjoyable and happy. If teachers use punishments to motivate students to learn, those students won't be happy while learning. Instead, they don't like to go to school. because they're scared of their teachers. They will have a lot of pressure while learning. In classes, they can't express their own opinions, because everything that they do might provoke the teachers. In this condition, students lose the opportunities to think. All they have to do is to follow what the teachers say.
I saw news on TV one day. It was about a teacher use punishment to motivate students. Those students were so scared that they cried and begged their parents that they didn't want to go to school. This was a real example that showed the bad impact of punishment. Students refused to learn because of the scary teachers and punishment.
To sum up, rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. With encouragements and happiness, students can enjoy learning. With better relationships between students and teachers, students can discuss their learning problems or teenage confusions, they can grow up in a heathier environment. With this happy and healthy environment, they will have the ability to think, express their own thoughts and be more creative.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are a variety of ways to motivate students to learn harder. In general, those ways can be divided into two categories: punishnent and rewarding. However, in my opinion, rewarding students for learning is more effective than punishment due to the following reasons.
First, no one likes to be punished, and students are no exception. When students are forced to study harder for fear of being severely punished, it's unlikely for them to love what they are learning. On the contrary, everyone likes to be rewarded after he or she is doing something right. The more positive enforcements one receive, the better they like what they are doing. Even a simple but continual praise can work a lot.
In addition, students who study just to avoid punishment tend to achieve merely a little bit higher than the teacher's expectations. However, students who are often rewarded will usually do their best to excel the goal. They want to prove they are worthy of being rewarded. In other words, triggered by such sense of achievement or satisfaction, they will try to reach excellence instead of meeting the basic requirements.
Therefore, teachers should encourage students more by rewarding. When students are intrinsically motivated gradually and develop their interest in the targeted subject, far better results will definitely be seen naturally.

subject: HW1001
content:
This issue has been talked about by lots of people since education became important. I think that the rewarding way is more effective.
I think almost all the people like to be accomplished and treated in a good way. No one would like to be punished in the classrooms, especially there are many classmates in the same place. Maybe the student who is punished would hate to learn and go to school forever. Therefore, I think punishment is a bad way. Moreover, this way may make the results become worse.
I have been a tutor since I became an university student. Everytime I use the punishments, such as memorizing more contents, solving more mathematical problems, my student become upset and unhappy. Subsequently, his grades on school tests don't improve. However, if I use a rewarding way like giving a present when he gets a good performance, my student will study more and become hard-working. Based on my own experience, I think the rewarding way will lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I would rather prefer rewarding students than punishing because rewarding them can build up their self-belief which can back up theirselves in their lives, and punishment often destroy students' self-esteem that is quite important for them to face any kinds of problems in their following long lives. Therefore I would consider rewarding students for learning is more effective.
About this issue, I would like to take my parents as examples for they are both excellent teachers in my hometown. I often saw many students of my father or mother visiting their teachers in my house when I was a child. Some of them even were bad students, regarded by other teachers, my parents, especially my father, would be very patient to them, gradually rewarding them to adapt their behavior, and step by step they became good students finally!
From my self experience, I would strongly consider that rewarding students would be more effective than punishing them!

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students may be my answer. There are three reasons to support my opinion. First, by rewarding students, teachers can construct their self-confidence. The students would think that they can accomplish the work by themselves, making their utmost efforts to try to do better next time. Therefore, without the punishment, students can demonstrate their best as well.
Second, by rewarding students, teachers don't have to worry about the students' emotion. On account of punishment, students would always bear the disappointment in mind, and that would be the most vital reason why students become more discouraged and absent-minded. Nevertheless, as long as teachers reward students, they would strive on what they want, such as another reward or appreciation from others.
Last but not least, by rewarding students, teachers can possess a blissing mood as well. What teachers get after the punishment to students are anger and regret. Teachers may be mad at what the students did and be regretful after seeing the long faces of the students. If the punishment makes not only teachers but also students have a bad time, why don't the teachers who used to punish students change their way to rewarding the students? What teachers get after rewarding students is neither their better behavior nor excellent grades but the most adorable smiles on their faces.
Take me for an instance. Once I had a chance to be a teacher for one day. My students are scores of first grades students. They laughed loudly, running around the classroom, and even picking their nose without a piece of tissue. In the meanwhile, I was driven crazy by the scene I saw; however, I calmed myself down, trying to talk to them. The kids followed what I said and got back to their seats with a candy I gave to them in their hands. What I learned from being an one-day-teacher was the most cherish thing. Without a severe way to control students, I could still win the hearts from students by the most effective way -- rewarding.

subject: HW1001
content: Every student will be encouraged if other people praise him or her, especially the teacher. However, perhaps there would be some students who have never been rewarded for learning because of their bad behavior. As a result, contrary to the rewarding, I think that appropriate punishment is going to be better. While our society is getting more critical and worse, the only thing we have to do is do our best to make the next generation better. Using punishment at school may appeals to some criticism, but students under that pressure will behave well. Instead of rewarding only some parts of students, punishment is used for each student. There was an example: When I was in junior high school, there were two kinds of classes, one is filled with well-behaved students, and the other is filled with bad ones. The well-behaved students were not born to be good. Self-dicipline of them was cultivated with punishment. In contrast, those bad students were seldom controlled by their teachers who rewarded for learning. Eventually, those good students got into great senior high schools in the entrance exams, while the bad ones didn't.

subject: HW1001
content:
If you know that you will be punished in school, are you still willing to go to school? Most people would say no. Then why some teachers still use this kind of method to make students behaved. Here are few reasons about why they still use this punishment and why I strongly object it.
First, those teachers using punishment may make those unbehaved students under those teachers' control. However, it may also cause mentally or physically hurts in their hearts and bodies. The wounds on body will be recovered but the scars in heart will never be. Second, the teachers using punishment believe that a student being educated through a strict way will have a better future. I don't think that can work on everyone. Some people who can not stand the pressure may skip classes and even worse be suspended. When those teachers realize that, it is too late to fix it.
On the other hand, if teachers often rewarding students may make students want to study and have a sense of accomplishment. Studying become an enjoyment, not a scary thing. That is what a teacher should teach students.
To sum up, it is difficult to change some teachers' teaching methods. As long as more and more people express their objection of punishment, those teachers will change someday in the future.

subject: HW1001
content:
No one in this world knows what is the best way of teaching. However, in my opinion, I believe that rewarding students for learning is much better than punishing them for not performing well.
Let's take me for example. When I was an elementary school student, one of my teachers used to punish students who didn't perform well on the test. I hated her at that time. I couldn't understand why she punished me after I had tried so hard. Gradually, I started to dislike studying.
Nevertheless, when I became a 5th grader, I had a new homeroom teacher. The new teacher was kind and nice to all of us. She gave us candy as a gift if we made progress on our grades, and when we behaved ourselves well. I loved the feeling when I got rewards after I did something great, so I improved myself in many aspects.
To sum up, punishment is not a good motivation for students to make progress. Sometimes rewarding students can make them become better.

subject: HW1001
content:
As a high school student, I think the first method will be more effective to high school students.
In my experience, most high school students won't care about what the teacher said if that teacher doesn't punish. I think every teacher knows they have to set a punishment or the student won't do what she said. For example, my history teacher told us to hand out a homework next week, but some students didn't want to do it. Next week, when the history teacher was collecting the homework, those students started to find all kinds of excuses to avoid handing in the homework. My history teacher said "Give me the homework tomorrow or you'll fail my class". None of them didn't hand in the homework in the next day.
From this example, we can know that threaten or punishment always work on all kinds of students. You have to tell them what will happen if they don't finish what you said. Then, they will try their best to finish it, not avoid it.

subject: HW1001
content:
We can see lots of news about punishing students on TVs and newspapers. Is punishment the best way to let students control their behavior? It's an important question to think about.
Actually, I don't really agree with using punishment to students. As a student, I will feel very sad and angry if the teacher hits my hand with a stick or tells me to stand outside. And it is very embarassing if the teacher does this in front of all the classmates. Punishment makes students very sad and doesn't let them learn too much.
I think giving rewards is better for students. It doesn't have to be a gift, it can also be a sentence which makes a student happy. When I was learning swimming many years ago, I met two teachers that are very different. When I didn't swim well, the first teacher hit my hand because of doing the wrong gesture, but the second teacher always said that I was doing better than last time. I improved much faster when the second teacher taught me.
Concluding my experience, I think rewarding students is better than punishment. Students feel better and learn more.

subject: HW1001
content:
Both methods are effective, but they have good and bad in their own way. Punishing the students can make them obey you right away! Even though they listen to you for now, but how long can this keep up. They will learn to fight back sooner or later. You might also get tired of the yelling and screaming, too. Rewarding them is another way. Maybe they do learn well, but what if you don't give the reward, will they listen, can they concentrate on learning, can they behave. All of these are questions, you can try and find out the unknown answers, but is it worth trying. They can not except some to give them reward for their whole life, can they? I say why not use both of them, it is better than to just use one.
Give them the reward when they are not being punished. Punish them when they are not rewarded. For example, my family is one that are using both of the methods. Three children have been through it. The process is tough, but once you make it through the rest of it is easy. Combine both methods can make us concentrate on learning and the behavior can be controled well. Two of the children does lead to better result. Their future are bright. The third children is coming to an end of the process. His grade was not the best, but it is still good. I wonder if my family did not use both method on him, will he still have good grades, or the opposite.

subject: HW1001
content:
In traditional Chinese teaching method, students should be punished in order to motivate them to study harder. However, I don't think this is the best to teach students. Rewarding students can make them learn happily and willingly.
Students can learn happily by praising them. When they get high grades or do not fall asleep while class, they should have some rewards. This behavior help them to judge whether they do right or wrong. If a student does not study hard and not get any reward, then he or she would know this behavior should be changed.
Rewarding students can also strengthen students' willing to learn. For example, when I was a junior high student, I have met an English teacher who used punishment to force us to study. If we could not attach her standard at test, she would punish us by verbal abuse or hitting at our butt. At that time, we did not like her and sometimes got a bad grade on purpose. Plenty of the classmates hated to go to school and study. After a year, she left and another teacher became our English teacher. She was a kind person and always wore smile. She didn't punish us when we did not study but told us why we should study. She gave us candy or praised us when we had good grades. Gradually, more and more student liked learning and after a year, we all entered good senior high schools.
Punishing students cannot change their behaviors deeply. The only way is to praise them and give them reward to make them learn happily and willingly.

subject: HW1001
content:
To me, as the teacher in the university, I believe that rewarding students for learning is better way to teach than punishing them.
There are two reasons to explain my point of view. First, it goes without saying that god help those who help themselves. Once you give the students more oppertunities, they will return you as you expected. Teachers should teach students how to help themslves by helping them to build more confidence rather than giving them punishment. Second, only if the students have more confidence, they are willing to try things on their own. If teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn or to control their behavior, they will be afraid of trying many thing. It's because they will be afraid of making mistakes.
Moreover, here are some ways to reward students for learning. Besides the rewarding from teachers, teachers also can encourage students to help each other. Through this way, students can learn how to cooperate with others and learn how to control their behaviors.
To sum up, dream is the power to move on, don't destory students' dreams by punishing them. On the other hand, teachers should help them to put their dreams come true and build their confidence for their better future.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Every student might face difficulties in their study, and they will feel frustrated at the same time. When they don't do well on their tests or fail in few subjest, what they really need is some comfort and couragement. Everyone wants to do their best to do anything, and achieve their goals; therefore, teachers should give students appropriate and effective suggestions to solve their problems instead of punishing and blame on them only.
My English was poor when I was a first-grade student in senior high school. I studied very hard in order to get high scores on every English test. However, all my effort was in vain, I felt depressed and cried in the classroom. My English teacher came and told me that I should give myself more confidence, and my English will be improved one day if I could keep practicing it. After the class dismissed, she gave me a pat on my shoulder, and asked me to remember the old saying "Practice makes perfect."
After that time, I studied English harder and harder, and my English became better in the end. My English teacher praised me in the class and assigned me to be her little assistant. It was an unforgettable thing in my life, and I do really enjoy English from then on.
According to my own experience, I believe rewarding students for learning is the best way in teaching. When students get rewarding, they will have more motivation to try again and will not give up easily.

subject: HW1001
content:
In traditional chinese culture, we often think that punishment is best policy to learning. My thoughts were the same before, but nowadays, I change.
Punishment will be the direct and time-saving method to learn, but it also reflects that the teacher doesn't put much time and mind on teaching.
Reward seems like time-consuming, and you can't see the results immediately. However, the students will feel warm, and love to learn although their performances are not so adventage. The teacher delights their interests in learning, and they'll work hard afterward. I think it's the most important.
To take myself as an example, I didn't get a good grade on organic chemistry this sememster, and I needed to learn it for one more year. I was depressed, but my porfesser doesn't blame on me. Besides, he made me see another chance, a hopeful future, and I know I'll try it one more time and never give up.
As a result, I don't think punishment is a good method to teaching. In my opinion, I prefer the rewarding method. After all, delighting the students' interest in the root to education, but not the scores.

subject: HW1001
content: Punishment is more effective than rewarding. Some students are lazy and slack to a degree and some have a weak determination to carry out what they have decided. For example some students regard studying as a painstaking job, so they would rather fool around with their friends and play online games. They need a person to stimulate them in a strict way such as punishment. By doing so, if they want to idle their time away, they will remember the punishment they have gotten. Punishment can also control the students' behavior. In most schools, some students bully their peers and say some insulting words. If we only verbally discourage them from doing the same things, they can not fully realize the feelings of the students who are bullied. The students who bully other peers should be punished, so that they can reflect and understand other people's feelings. Punishment is an effective way to put the students right. Although some people think it is too cruel, punishment is still the best way to discipline the students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Now at the opening socialty, through our education system, it is not hard to see that teacher's teaching style have become a serious problem. First, some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior, in the other hand, others teacher believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, I think that rewarding students is the effective way, never use punishment when it really needs.
In few days, it is not hard to see that teacher punish naughty student with stick, and let the student hurt seriously on every media. To tell the truth, using punishment can't even save the problem, it might cause more serious issue. Students will not change if teachers don't talk properly, if teacher use punishment, it will cause the oppsite effect and that will be show on students. As far as I concerned, the education and the way teachers teach have become an important issue these days. We can't say that using punishment is always the wrong way, it depands on both teacher's and student's situation.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opnion, rewarding students for learning is a better way. I always think punishment is not a good way to motivate students, espically the physical punishment. I have to compromise, it is useful in a little time. But in the long run, it will cause huge problem. Using punishment will let students think it's really a solution to many problem. So there are barling in the school is not strange at all, we can even say it was learned from the teachers who use physical punishment. What education really is? I think it is absoutly not to avoid punishment. It is more close to motivating students to teach themselves by a rewarding way.
When I was a junior high freshman, my teacher is a man who puts really high pressure on my class. If we didn't get scores we should get we had been beated by him with a paddle. Our class grade is really excellent on those days, but all of us are unhappy. However, on the third year, our teacher was substituted by a young teacher who just graduated from National Taiwan Normal University. She let us know what is education of love, and our grade maintains. So I really think rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
As far as I am concerned, I suppose that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. That is the best method to let students study hard and improve their poor grades. For instance, I am a true and terrific example of acceping this kind of education way.
I still remember that when I was a freshman in the senior high school. My math grades was so poor that lots of my classmates always laught at me because of it. At that time, I felt very annoyed with math. Every time I saw the math book, I really wanted to put it into the trashcan. Nevertheless, when I was going to give up of my math grade, there was a good teacher appeared to help me. She is like an angel. She taught me math patiently and encouraged me to get good grades by rewarding me delicious chocolates. Then, because her rewards were so wonderful, I tried to study math harder than before. Afterwards, my grades really improved better.
Hence, after that experience, I really think rewarding students to get good grades is the best policy of education. It will provide students much power to study hard and then get a beautiful grade.

subject: HW1001
content:
In order to make the students learn better, some teachers think punishment is more effective to motivate students, while others think rewarding students will be a better method. As for me, I prefer rewarding students, and the following points may account for my opinions.
First of all, comparing with rewarding, punishment arouse unnecessary pressure in students. Nobody like to be punished, so students may be reluctant to go to school when they know that they will be punished if they don't do well, especially for those who always do poorly on their school work. Second, people like to compare themselves with others, including the students. As a result, rewarding can arouse the motivation between peers, for everyone wants to surpass others. Also, students will be happier with the method of rewarding. When one does something great, one will prefer to gain more rewards rather than cease punishment. Students will be happier if they get something in return when they do well.
To sum up, I think rewarding can make students feel a great sense of achivement, which can arouse their own motivation to learn. To make students to have interest in what they are learning is more essential. As a consequence, I think rewarding students is a better way to teach students.

subject: HW1001
content:
I reckon that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In most cases, we doing a good job in a certain field, we are rewarded. The interest and confidence follow by. In contrast, it is impossible to get any award when we act badly. As a student, it is probable to be punished or criticized. After that, there is little desire for that field.
To illustrate, a friend of mine studies science. We may think him good at math. Nevertheless, he does better research on history than math. The reason can be traced back to his teachers in junior high. Once, his math teacher scolds him with irony due to his bad grades. This behavior equals to sentence him to death because he had done well in math. Since then, he is not interested at all in this subject. As for his history teacher, there was one time he unexpectedly scored high and received teacher's praise. Until now, he has studies articles or papers related to history.
As what I mentioned above, one prefer praises to blame. It applies to students learning any subject. On being rewarded, students' confidence is built.

subject: HW1001
content:
I consider that rewarding students for learning is a more effective approach than punishing them. Punishment isn't the best way to teach students and it may hurt students' mind even their bodies. It will give students hegative influences on their thoughts. Students will learn passively and reluctantly since they always be punished and they feel frustrated. On the contrary, rewarding can have a positive impact on them. Being rewarded, they will have a sense of achievement and willing to have further study.
Take myself for instance, when I was in junior high school, my teacher always wanted us to have good grades. If we didn't realize the target, my teacher would punish us seriously. I had a terrible and stressful life in my junior high school. I was forced to study, in fact, I didn't want to study at that time. But when I entered the senior high school, everything changed drastically. There were no punishment any longer and if I did a good job in any competition, I would get a prize. I felt happy and I loved the feeling of being rewarded. I always did my best to be rewarded.

subject: HW1001
content:
Students of my age must have this common experience -- students would be punished if they don't obey the rules. In my opinion, I strongly disagree to motivate students in this cruel way.
Maybe when teachers use punishment, most of the students would behave themselves and study harder in order not to get punished. However, students would feel nervous and stressed every moment in class; as a result, they don't feel like go to school and even lose the interests in learning. Pushed and limited by rules and teacher's requests, they can't learn what they really want to learn. Consequently, some students behave against the teachers on purpose while others obey the rules.
When I was at grade 3 in elementary school, my English teacher always inspire us and say "good job", "fine", "great" ... to us. Moreover, she let us speak loudly in class, telling us not to be afraid. Every student in class liked English class because it wasn't as dull as Chinese class. We could speak, play games and read English books full of illustrators. Although we often used wrong words and dare not speak, she always encouraged us to speak more. Things chaged after I entered junior high school. My English gived us piles of test sheets. We didn't speak much in class and always looked at the text books. When getting a bad score, the teacher shout at us and punish us to write English word many times. Most of students hated the teacher and some of them even gave up learning English. They skipped or slept in class.
To sum up, if teachers resward student instead of punishing them, they will be willing to lean. Besides, they will have a happy memory of their school life!

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, punishment and rewarding are both effictive in some aspects. Punishment can make children realize what they will need to pay after doing something wrong, I think that's part of the reason why we need law aganist those bad guy. But before or after punishment we should communicate with our children with patience, knowing what they think and whether they have tried their best or not. It is espically important when it comes to study. Asking children to fullfill goals that are too high for them to reach will make them loss the motivation to learn.
Sometimes, giving them some reward can encourage children to maintain their passion and find satisification in learning. But too much reward and compliment will make distort their motivation, their will no longer take study as their own resiponsibility.
My uncle never scold his child, always rewards him something after he finishs his homework. As time gose by; his child unwilling to do his homework unless his father promises some reward. It's a tragedy for both my uncle and my cusin. Treating children is alway not easy. We should choose the right time to punish or reward. If we want to do things well, we need to keep trying and knowing our children.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teacher use punishment to motivate students. However, some would motivate students by rewarding. In my opinion, I suggest that punishment would be a better way to teach students than rewarding. First of all, nowadays, most children are too pampered by their parents because they may be the only child in their family. Hence, children live comfortabily without anxiety and preasure. If teachers don't use punishment during the lesson or in school, students will take all things for granted. Secondly, using punishment can make students know what is right or wrong and keep them from the wrong way. Last but not least, using punishment can spur students mind and stimulate them to reach their goals.
To my knowledge, I'm the best example to support my opinion. During primary school's life, my teacher was so serious to me. I had to do more homework than any other students. Therefore, I was so unhappy that I usually did bad things. Everytime, my teacher punished me but also taught me what I did were wrong and told me the reason why she was always serious to me - to make me better. Eventually, I gradually realized what my teacher meant but still punished by her occasionally. In the graduation, I was rewarded the first prize. So touched was I that I couldn't help but drop tears. Everything my teacher told me came true.
All in all, according to the trend and my experience, I think that using punishment is the better and effective way to teach students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Everybody has their own views and their views may be different from each other. In my opinion, I prefer rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. And by using this teaching method is more effective than punishing students to make them become better.
Take my younger brother for example, when he was at his first year in junior high school. His teacher used the punishment to improve their grades. However, my brother's grades didn't improve at all. What's more was that he was afraid of going to school. Not only my brother but also his classmates hated this kind of teaching way. Luckily, they had a new teacher at their second year, their new teacher was totally different from their first one, he used the rewarding way to motivate students to stuy hard. By using this way, my brother and his classmates all gained their confidence back and studied hard. In this case, I do really think if you want to make someone become better or improve other, you shouldn't force them or even punish them. The results are usually bad. By using rewarding and love, I firmly believe that they would become better.

subject: HW1001
content:
Should punishment be used to motivate students to learn or we should use reward to encourage students to learn is a dilema issue. In my opinion, I think both of the methods are worth to use when teachers educate thier students. Which means should be use is count on the situation.
