Adapt the method of rewarding students in the first to increase their intersts in learning and encourage them to do something is correct. However, if giving prize doesn't get use, I think it's time for teachers to use another method, punishment, to urge students to study. Students might study more hard to get rid of being punished. In these way, I think it's the most effective way to motivate students to learn.
To support my opinion, we would like to take a boy as an examlp. The boy was my classmate when I was in junior high school. His grade was not good, in fact, it was very terrible, so my teacher, who wanted to help all her students as much as she could, told him that he might get a cup of pearl milk tea if he progressed at the next exam. At first, it was work, and my classmate studied hard to win the milk tea. But soon, he got tired of always learned and started to fool around to find something more intersting. Then my teacher told him if his grade getting worth, he might get physical punishment. This time, my classmate study harder then ever before to avoid being punished.

subject: HW1001
content:
Whether teachers should punish students has been a hot issue these days. In my opinion, I think rewarding students can be more effective. As far as I am concerned, education is a process to help students gain healthy personality and the ability of telling what is right and what is wrong. Rewarding students can make students think positively and they will encourage themselves to reach the goals. If the teachers use punishment instead, students follow the teachers just because they want to avoid any possible punishment. They don't have much strong motivation to make themselves "better" people.
Take my junior high teacher for example, she usually rewarded us when she thought we had done a great job such as in some contests. Everyone in my class therefore had great will to show the best of us at every moment. We didn't need the teacher to force us. We would ask ourselves to have good behavior. To sum up, I think rewarding students is nuch better than punishing them.

subject: HW1001
content:
Students nowadays are much different than before. They become smarter and more mature in their early ages. Therefore, it makes teaching and educating students more and more difficult to teachers.
In my opinion, teachers need to use both punishment and rewarding to help students learn better. But the principle is, "Rewarding students more, and punishment only if necessary." Rewarding students helps them build more confidence in themselves and interests them in learning. Punishment, on the other hand, could make them realize what kinds of behavior are not allowed. I think all the teachers should truly pick up the skills of how to use both methods right.
Take myself for example, as an elementary school teacher, I always discuss class rules with my students at the first begining of my class. Usually, I let them tell themselves what are good manners and behavior, and what are bad ones as well. In this way, students will easily understand what they should do in order to win gifts or compliments from me.
It's never easy to teach, and I'll keep trying to adjust myself to do a better job in the future.

subject: HW1001
content:
The education system varies from place to place. Some teachers use punishment to force their students to study, while others have a penchant for rewarding students for learning. The way I prefer is to reward instead of punishment.
As a student, I want to keep away from the punishment. Everytime I saw my friends scolded or hit by the teacher, I felt so bad and had no more energy on studying. However, when I was 13 years old, I met Mrs. Lin, who never use punishment. At that time, I felt so happy everyday and my scores were keeping rising and rising. That was such an amazing experience to me! After I was taught by Mrs. Lin, I can definitly say that teaching with love is always better than teaching with punishment and scolding. If I had not been taught by Mrs. Lin, I couldn't comes off with flying colors on the performance in my school. Though I graduated from the school, I'll keep the words Mrs. Lin told me in my mind forever.
If I have a chance to be a teacher in the future, I'll do my efforts to become a teacher who never use punishment to treat her student and always encourage them to study by rewarding. Due to the experiences with different kinds of teachers, I am sure that a teacher without using punishment is beneficial to the students.

subject: HW1001
content: Recenly, people argue about using punishment on student. I think the teachers shouldn't use it to motivate students and make them behavior well. Although punishment may seem effective at first, students won't follow the rules once they are out of sight of teachers. They did well just for escaping punishment. However, if you always encourage students, say they do things well and reward them, you'll find they become eager to do their best. For example, when I was in elementary school, my Chinese teacher always told us we were the best. When I got bad grades, she didn't punish me but said she beheved I'll do better next time. Then I'll work hard for not to let her down. On the other hand, my math teacher was mean. She usually used a ruler to punish people who failed. Some students even cheated to pass the tests and other classmates also helped them and promised not tell a word to the teacher. How to teach students well is a serious question, many scholars have their own opinion. However, there is one thing I know for sure, rewarding is alway more effective than punishment, and the reward can be a beautiful pensil, some candy or even an encouraging smile.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think that use punishment is a more effective method than reward students. Students will not know that is wrong if you don't tell them, we can not always live in a beautiful and peaceful life. Actually, face the reality and adjust ourself to the right way can lead to better results.
My mom is a primary school teacher. When I was little, I studyed in the same school as her, and she drove me to the school every morning at that time. Then, I went to classroom; and she went to work. However, I had a very bad habbit that was I would not prepare things or even finish my homework at night. As a result, I was always doing all the stuff in a hurry in the next day morning. That made my mom extremely angry. She told me either got up early to prepare my own stuff or finished them the last night, but I didn't keep it in my mind. I thought that my mom would drive me to school as usual, and she would wait for me every time, but I was wrong.
On one day morning, I got up at 7 am as usual and started to package my belongings. After fifteen minutes, I started to leave from school. I found my mom and her car disapearing. I got a shock and stood there for almost ten minutes. Then, I knew, that was a punishment for me to remind of time controling. Although I still could not imagine that my mom would leave a nine-year-old girl alone at hom, but she did, and I got to know package things last night.
What a huge punishment for a elementary school student to be left at home. However, I know I wouldn't change myself to be better if this inciden't hadn't happened.
There are many different kinds of children in our society. Though punishments are not the best way to educate them, I think it's still a very effective method to know the right and wrong. What a parents should do is make their own chid better and better.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are all kinds of people in the world, and everybody has their own favor and annoyance. If I were a teacher, I will try not to use only one way to teach students, and help them to find the most efficient learning way to get more knowledge. Then, "It is important to make every student find the suitable way to learn" will be my teaching principle. According to this teaching principle, I won't support to use heavy-stressed ways, such as punishment at the student. To teachers, it's easy to make students follow their commands with this way while not consuming lots of energy or mind. In the other side to students, it's stressful to learn new knowledge and norms in such kind of surrounding. As a result, I opposite teachers to use punishment to motivate students or control students' behavior.
As the first teacher in Chinese said, teacher should use all kinds of ways to teach students, and the students will get the best learning effect. I agree with him, and that's also why he can be the best teacher in the Chinese history.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, there are more and more controversies about whether the teachers use punishments to students or not. In my perspective, I disapprove teachers punish students instead of rewarding students. There are some causes:
For one thing, teachers are the symbols of educated ambassaders. If they always impose their pressure and punishments on their students, the students might feel frightened and get lose of their interests in learning. Furthermore, students are innocent, because some students really have barriers or difficulities on their school performances. Sometimes they burn the midnight oil to study, but also get the poor grades. In this situation, if teachers still put stress on them, as a student, I think I would jump to death.
For another, teacher should encourage students. It's the unbelievable power that teachers give rewards or suggestions to students. Owning to the fact that students are learners, they know what obstacles they confront, so teachers could try to consel them and set a goal for them. If they attain, teachers may give them some rewards and set a higher aim to progress their learning interests and abilities.
Take me for example. When I studied in the elementary school, my math was terrible. Even if I endeavored to learn it well, however, it was in vain. At that time, my teacher taught me during the nap time every day, and gradually I knew the problems I faced. At last, I succeed. Teachers can't punish students but use their mercy and time to grow their students.

subject: HW1001
content:
As a experienced teacher, I deeply believe that punishment is a necessary evil. Generally speaking, teachers can give advices to well-mannered, hard-studying and friendly students. However, there are always a small part of students that refuse to accept any rules. If teachers can't correct and control their behaviors first, these children may become bad samples for other students. While all students go wild, effective teaching will turn into a impossible mission! Of course, any rules or laws won't work, too.
While I was still a new teacher last Setember, I encountered the worst class that I have ever met. No one followed my direction, and fights sometimes happened. As a result, In one hand I use strict punishments to surpress several "leaders", and gave them some advantages for obdying my instructions. On the other hand, I continued to communicate with parents and the school administration. After half of the year, I rarely heard about arugements and fights in the class. I thought that punishment can adjust children's behaviors on occasion. However, it can't always work.

subject: HW1001
content:
Wherevor you live arould this planet, every parent and the education experts are always debating if we should punish or reward our children or students. As far as I'm concerned, education can't be splited frm punishment and rewarding.
When I was a teenager, my parents stop punishing me, including calling my name and physical punishment. All they did was to guide me to the right direction or lead me to the way they thought it's better. But the prerequisite is I was not the hind of children who may be against their parents. So under this condition, I prefer rewarding studnts/son.
Another point of view to discuss this issue is "the age". In my openion, we can't discuss with studnts/children who are younger than eight or six. What they have in their mind is following the instinct and not to breah the laws their teachers or paents set. Just like pets, the owers have to mahe some rules for their pets to follow and abide wth. If they are doing well, the owners will give them some candy or meat as a reward. Thereafter, the pets would be goody goody and can reach the owers' expectation.
Since the world is changing, most parents don't like teachers hitting their children, especially the only child in a family. I don't want to criticize these parerts are spoiling their kid (In fact, it may be true!). What I wart to say is maybe ue can switch the punishment from physical to mental or other social service activities, such as sueeping the floors, helping parents do chans, and whatnots. Besides that, the parents and the teachers should work together not just for punishment or ban but also try to do something make them feel honored or something uhich may give them more motivation, such as pochet money, tahing them to the movies, tahing them to for a journey, declear their accomplishnat at school, etc.
Simply put, thu is no right and wrong for the two methods, punishment and rewarding. The most important is how the parents and teachers decide to use. Each way has its awn effectiveness but if we can combine two of them, the motimation and spur would be countless. Just like for the donkeys, we must hold larnt in one hand and sticks in the other, so that we can make our decision which method we should use at this time.

subject: HW1001
content:
Teachers have many different ways to educate their students, but it usually comes down to whether they should use punishment to motivate and teach students or not. Some say punishment is the best and only way to educate students, while others believe that rewarding students will lead to better results. My perspective as a student is as long as the punishment is acceptable, punishing students is more effective. The students in a class can be roughly seperated into two groups: The obedient group and the naughty group. Students in the first group are usually hard working and would do anything teachers tell them to do. Students in the second group on the other hand, never study and rebel against their teachers any chance they get. So I believe that the students that cause all the trouble are the ones that need to be punished, and rewarding them won't do them any good.
An expirience I have is when I was in junior high school, our teacher tried to motivate us, so she said that anyone who did well on tests or haven't fooled around in class will recieve a gift. The obedient students in my class got many gifts and awards, but the naughty students remained the same. So she said that if a student improves a lot on tests or behaviors will recieve a gift to try and change them but in vain. In the end, she punished the naughty students and everyone behaved themselves from then on.
Good students will behave and study regardless of any prizes or rewards, so punishment for the bad students is what we really need.

subject: HW1001
content: What kind of education should a good teacher take? What way of expression can really make the students understand the meaning of learning? When I am junior high, I am bad at Math, because I hate it. Why I hate Math? Althought I am not good at Math since I was a kid. But I never give up the hope of learning Math well. I didn't hate Math at that time, but after I met my junior Math teacher, everything changed. She is famous in the school for her stick. She always bring a long stick to the class, and test all the time. She use test to let us get used to the Math questions. After the test, if you didn't get one hundred, then show your hand, wait for her stick to "kiss" your hand. Three years ...... I have stand it for three years. I hate it! My Math didn't became well under her stick, but worse! The really thing should a teacher do is not punishment but to reward students or urge students. Show your patient and love to them. This is what students really need.

subject: HW1001
content: Does punishment really motivates students to learn and behave better? Or it just makes students lose their interests in studying? In my opinion, rewarding students is much more effective than punishments. First, nobody is perfect, we all make some mistakes. The teachers should give students chances to improve and learn instead of giving punishments only. Second, nobody likes to be punished. The students might want to rebel against the teachers because of the awful treatments. On the other hand, if teachers encourage or reward students for the good behaviors, the students would be more confident. Moreover, they would behave better to get the praise. When I was in elementary school, my home-room teacher was strict. She punished us for every little mistakes! Nevertheless, nobody wanted to listen to her. After several months, she found that she needed to change her attitude. She no longer punished us for naughty behaviors. Instead, she gave us candies for rewarding. From then on, we became more hard-working. In sum, I think rewarding students is a more effetive and useful way to motivate students.

subject: HW1001
content:
From long ago to nowadays, which method of teaching students is the best is always a popular issue. Some teacher use punishments to motivate students, others use compliments and rewards to make students learn better. In my opinion, rewarding students and encouraging them when they improve is a more effective way for teachers.
First of all, rewarding students can improve the relationships between teachers and students. If students like teachers and like the learning atmosphere at school, they are more willing to study hard. On the other hand, if theachers always punish students, no only will they feel sad, but also give up on the subjects. Second to be metioned, self-confidence is the most important factor of effective learning; when students have self-confidence and positive attitude, they can learn much better; rewarding and encouraging them is just the righ way which leads to the result. In contrast, if students are always punished when making small mistakes, they'll probably lose interests in learning, as a result, they may even lose the chance to understand the pleasure of learning new knowledge.
To sum up, rewarding but not punishing students not only makes school a joyful learning place which is full of laughter, but also gives numerous students self-confidence on learning. After all above, I think rewarding students is the more effective way to motivate them.

subject: HW1001
content:
Have you ever been infuriated by punishments? I bet you have. From the beginning of history, students have been punished for their lapses in learning. In some cases, the punished will work harder, driven by their fear of further punishments. However, once they escaped from the leash of teachers, they rebel by doing exactly what they have been punished for, simply for the thrill of it. I, for one, am such a case. By forbidding me to read novels in class, my teacher caused me to zealously read when they turned around, even if I'm tired of reading and want to stop. So, it totally defeats the original purpose.
Then, how do you motivate students to do stuff? Some psychiatrists and I agree on this theory! instead of using punishments, encouragments better serves the purpose. Like a slow but steady wind, it slowly wears down the students' reluctance to obey. At first, nothing changes. As time flows by, the student will likely want to obey, driven on by trust, confidence and gratefulness. In addition to actually making students wanting to learn, the teacher might "earn" a loyal future-friend.
Thus, one can conclude that if the teachers have the wisdom to use rewards rather than punishments to achieve the near-impossible goal of motivating students to learn, they have a greater chance of seeing the fruitition of his or her normally hard and futile job.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I support that rewarding students is a better method to encourage learning. Confucius said that if a kind rules his people with punishment, people would just try to avoid from being punished; but if he teaches them what are good behaviors, people would natually being good. Therefore, I believe that rewarding is better than punishment. In my experiences, I have tried both methods to my little cousin, rewarding is also a effective way. I once took care of my little cousin for a few months. I asked him to study for his math test, and I told him if he didn't get good grades, I would give him less allowance. However, he didn't care about what I told him, and he thought that he could ask money once he run out of it. After a few weeks, I change my mind. I decided to reward him if did well on his tests. After that, he started to study math. What an amazing thing! I was astonished when he took his test paper to me. I was happy that he did that and I finally found that rewarding is a better way to encourage learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think rewarding students for learning is more effective. Take me for example, my father always rewards me as I got high grades and that he is proud of me. I think study is our business, we should not get rid of it, but if we get more motivations, we will do our best to get the rewarding. So, I think rewarding students for learning is more effective.
On the other hand, I think using punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior is not wise. Punishment is no use to those rebel teenagers. The more punishments are, the more rebels the become.
All in all, the way to motivate students is rewarding, but be careful, too more rewarding will spoied students. Think twice before you reward them, think what is appropiate and what the gate they should arrive to get the rewarding.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. The way to motivate students usually lead to a good response. The students may be grateful for the prize and think that they should do better to reward teacher's compliment. They are likely to feel more repectful, and they have stronger willing to learn at school.
Nowadays, we can always hear or see some teachers punish their students too overly to cause thier physical and mental hurt on televisions. At first, these teachers don't mean to hurt students but their want them to revise students' flauts from their good will. However, they use the wrong way so that it cause the error that can't be complemented. It leaves great side effect for those students. They afraid of schools. As a result, it is better that reward students when they behave well, and teach them in soft way when they make mistake.
If teachers use voilence to teach a student, and the student perhaps teach his/her children in the same way. If teachers use prizes to guide him/her to true way, he/she may have better way to get along with people. That why the western people always advocate "education of loveness."

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers may prefer to use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. But I think the better way is to reward students for learning.
Take myself for example. I always try my best to do every schoolwork. If the teacher give me some praise, I'll feel encouragement and pay more effort next time. However, if the teacher just think that all I do is nonsense, I'll feel being humiliated and even hate the teacher and that class.
There is a learning English system in my school. That is if we read English novel or do anything that is good for learning English, then we can get a stamp. My friends and I are crazy about collecting the stamps. We think they can represent the improvement of our English. We also enjoy the activity and think that learning English is fun.
Due to my experience, I believe that rewarding students for learing can encourage them and lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
It goes without saying that there are many methods to motivate students. Some are good to students, but others do harm to them. In my opinion, the most effective way to improve students' learning is trying to reward them from their studying, for everyone will meet lots of problems from learning. Only the person who face those problems straightly could solve them. Using punishments could only enhace students learning and control their behavior for a short time. Many reports show that lots of students give up studying after graduate from school due to bad memories which teachers gave them in school. As a result, we must use the right way to improve our students' learning.
There is a teacher which affects me a lot. When I was studying in high school. Due to play online games all day long, my grades were getting from bad to worse. I only studied ten minutes a day. However, my teacher found out that there are some problems on me. She told me that playing game is just a way to relax. Only knowledge could accompay to me all life long. She helped me to ride out that terrible time. Therefore, using a right way can lead a student to a bright road. Perhapes the method of motivating students differs from person to person. However, I'm convinced that rewarding students is the best way for them.

subject: HW1001
content:
I strongly believe that rewarding students can lead to better results. Using punishment to motivate students can lead to even worse. I think rewarding students is much more effective.
Take myself as an example, while I was in the seventh grade, I hated English. I always got poor grades on English. One day, as my English teacher noticed, she tried to persuade me to study hard like I had never before. She even promised me to give me two hundred dollars as a reward if I got the highest score in class! After that talk with my English teacher, I studied really hard. As a result, not only did I got the highest score in class, but also the whole seventh grade! I'm quite thankful for what she had done. Even now, being a high school student, English is my strongest subject. What's more, I always got first place in any English competitions.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think reward is better than punishment. When you use punishment, the students just remember the hate about this subject in his mind. He will have little interest about keeping learning or even he will never touch the relating courses again for good.
When I studied math at school, the teacher usually said that if you lose one point, you will get a hit. I tried my best on every tests, but I still get hit most of the time. I don't know why I should be punished even when I do well. I was very depressed. Now I will never try math agin.
When the reward is applied, everything is changed. The students know that the better they do, the better reward they will recieve, so everyone is happy to learn more. If you learning something happily, you will learn it well. It's a famous experiment result.
I remember when I'm learning how to play basketball. My coach bringed lots of candy everytime. He said that he will give me a candy if I make a good shot. At first, I was not a good shooter. Being so willing to get the candy, I practice shooting everyday. Now I can shoot the ball accurately and I love basketball. I really thank this coach. He is nice coach who knows how to motivate someone.

subject: HW1001
content:
The purpose of teaching is to help students learn knowledge and instruct them to behave well. In order to reach the goal, teachers use different ways, for example, punishing students or rewarding students. Each side has their perspective to do so. However, I'm of the idea that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Here are two reasons listed below.
First of all, everyone has self-esteem. Nobody wants to be blamed in the public, and that will cause that the person are afraid of doing the thing again. For example, when I was in junior high school, I was hit by my math teacher in front of the class because of the bad grades on the test. After being hit, all of the things I remembered were the pain in my hands and tears, not how to get better next time. Therefore, punishment brings terrible feelings to students rather than encouragement which students really need during learning.
Second, rewarding students is much more optimistic and effective. The reason why I say this is that telling students their good things not backwards makes them feel comfortable instead be nervous. Encouragement gives student more engery to overcome the difficulties of learning. Learning is not a easy thing, so teachers should help them. For instance, English teacher can teach students the tips for memorizing vocabulary, such as using sound to memorizing it on some rules of making a work. I still can remember that the roots, "er" or "or", are for the people who do that action. So I can know "writer", "singer", "actor", etc. are reffered to people's job. Teaching students how to learn effectively and efficiently is much more important than punishing them and forcing them to recite something they don't know.
To sum up, teaching is to help learning instead force learning. Students have their self-esteem and need teachers' careness and encouragement. I believe there is no doubt that rewarding students for learing can help student learn effectively and efficiently.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the past, not only teachers but also parents thought that punishments could make students or children move forward fast; however, was that true?
Though punishments are the most efficient way to teach students because they will be afraid of being punished and force themselves to have a prograss. But they may have the bad influence on students. In my opinion, rewarding students is a better way to motivate students to move forward because human can accept compliments more easily than being scolded. If you tell them they did very well but they can still do much better, the students may feel happy and believe that they are not bad, so they will be brave to go on.
In my life, I've encountered many situations about this problem. For instance, when we were preparing for the musical performance, there was a teacher would scold us if we did not well, we would feel uncomfortable and nervous, so we couldn't show our best performance to her. On the other hand, there was another teacher alway encouraged us and rewarded us even we did not really good. But we felt well and was willing to enhance our skills, and then, we finally did an obvious prograss. That's why I think rewarding students can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to control their behavior and to learn better. While others think that rewarding is the best way. I think that which of the method is effective depends on what kind of personality the students is and the age of mind they have.
For students who is very little like the age of five or six, they are just curious about every thing. If we punish them for their unsuitable behavior may kill their curiousity of new things and may cause them have mentally demage. When they grow up they may have fear to do it even if time is right. So I think rewarding is better than punishment when students were young. In contrast to elementery students, high school students have a kind of attitude to against their parents and teachers. Thus you have to show your authority through punishment. Even if they hates now, they would appriciate what you've done in the future.
For example, my best friend Jack who always have a hard time to eat tomato. It is due to the kindergarden teacher who wants all the student to eat things in their bow clearly. He just to full to eat, but teacher force him to finish eating the tomato soup. From that time on, he began to hate eating tomato. So I think teacher should rewarding kids rather than punishment.
To sum up, either punishment or rewarding are good way to teach students, it is effective or not depends on who you going to use.

subject: HW1001
content:
Punishment is not a good way to motivate students to learn or to control them. Compared with rewarding, punishment is less efficient and harmful. In my opinion, although punishment seems easier for teachers to control students' behavior, there are many bad effects caused by punishment, namely, students' antisocial behavior, less attention on the lesson and morbid perspectives on the society. As a result, rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.
First, punishment may cause students' antisocial behavior. I have been teaching in the junior high school. I find out that some students need encouragement not punishment. I remember one day a student came to me and complained, "although I get good grades, I hate this world." I was shocked then because of his words.
Second, students may pay less attention on the lesson because of punishment. One day, I found my students talkative during the class, and some of them even cheated. I was angry then and punished them by depriving their break. However, after that, students didn't pay attention in the class.
Third, students may have morbid perspectives on the society. One day my students complained to me that why the adults always beat them. They feel the world is not friendly.
All in all, punishment is not an effective way to motivate students. Rewarding is better. I remember a low-motivated student got one hundred after I encouraged her. As a result, in my opinion, students can understand teachers' expectations if teachers use rewarding, not punishment.

subject: HW1001
content: To my opinion, I consider rewarding students for learning a better method to lead students to success. Of course, the way that using punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior is also an effective way to teach students. However, this method has a drawback that may bring an upset experience to students, causing mental problems in students' minds, especially for children in elementary school. In addtion, teachers may get plenty of problems if they only use punishment to restrict students. For example, while watching television or reading newspaper, we can see many cases that teachers become the spotlight because of the punishment toward students. And these may make not only students parents angry but also embarrass the school. On the other hand, if we reward students for learning then students can also learn whether he did was right. What's more, students can enjoy lessons a lot during the class, and this may get more achievement than we've ever though. To sum up, I tend to use the method that use praising more that blamming while teaching the students.

subject: HW1001
content:
As far as I'm considered, I think rewarding students is more effective. Through punishment, teachers could teach students nothing but not to do the wrong things. It was just tell them "no" and they wouldn't learn anything from it. Maybe for some rebellious student who prefer not to obey the rules would try not to follow it and see what will happen next. Fortunately, those students are usually more creative, having their own thoughts and opinions.
For instance, I'm the example. Since entering elementary school, teachers always try to let students listen to them or study hard. After growing up, I found that I behaved better when the teacher rewarded us. The teacher may give us points as we behaved well by groups or individuals. When we collected enough points, we could changed the points into presents. That's really attempting for elementary students. Because I have always tried to behave the best, not okay, to strive for more gifts and rewards. For me, it was honored when teacher and classmates accomplished me. That motivated me to do everything as excellent as I could.
In the contrast, if the teacher use the method of punishment. I wouldn't want to respect him. I would live up to the lowest level, sometimes accrossed it. That's are my indivisual examples. As a result, I think that rewarding students can really lead to better outcomings.

subject: HW1001
content: Although it is more efficient to motivate the students to learn by punishment, I think the best method to guide the students to learn is rewarding. Punishment may lead the students to study, to take practices for examinations, but the students will not like to learn by heart. On the other hand, to guide the students to learn by rewarding makes a positive motivation to the students to let them like to not only study but also explore the world. For example, during the invetion of the light bulb, Edison tried thousands kinds of materials. The driving force of it is not punishment but the reward of bringing the light to people. Punishment may drive people for a short period of time, but only the motivation by heart can let people devote into something. And the best way to guide the motivation is rewarding. Edison is the best example.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are two ways to teach students, one is to punish them when they did something wrong, another is to reward students. For me, I think the second one is more effective. I consider punishing students may result in bad effects in the future.
When I'm in Junior High, Mrs. Wang, my English teacher, was a strict teacher. She gave us a lot of handwriting homework and reports and asked us to hand in to her in a short time. The one who did not hand in on time would be punished in different ways, such as hit the palm, mop the floor with hands and so on. These unreasonable punishment made everyone in our class really angry, because no one was able to finish the big amount of homework. After that, everyone hate her and phone calls asking the school to change the teacher rings everyday. Finally, we had a nice teacher, Mr. Li.
He is the kind of teachers that encouraged students more than yelling at students. We all like him and would do what he had ask us to do. We got good grades with out being punished.
As a result, I think that rewarding students can lead to better results, and students would like the teacher, too.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are two major ways to teach students, using punishment or rewarding students. It's hard to say which one is better, but I think the latter one is more effective. Because the students are not as free as the adults, they always can't get something they want. So when you set a goal for them to get the things, they will work hard to attain it. Gradually, the students work harder and harder and lead them to better results. If you just use punishment to motivate them, they don't really want to learn. Day by day they will get tired of it and want to avoid. So it can't lead to happy ending and students may lose the enthusium for studying.
I go to teach the junior high school students every thursday. At first, they don't want to learn anymore and they just want to chat with each other. But after rewarding them for learning or studying, they just sit on their desk writing homework and preparing tests now!
Although I may spend extra money in this way, it is worth.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the essay, I will express my opinion about the more effective method for learning and give out the example.
It's better for teachers to reward students for their learning. Rewarding students is like to build up their confidence in learning. With encouragement, students will tend to keep learning no matter they'll succeed or not. Besides, education is not about limiting the possibility of children's behavior, but about opening up a new world for them. Thus, through rewarding them, they can always have the motivation to learn and keep working on delightly.
Take myself for example. I was not good at math since I was little. What's worse, I met a teacher who always yelled and punished me when I made mistakes on quiz. Gradually, I lost my confidence and interests in math. "Why I have to learn something that would bring me suffers?" I thought then. Fortunately, a new math teacher came to my life as soon as I got in high school. He liked to encourage students and always said "Well-done, well-done, you got it!". Also, he would give little gift for students who progress on tests. This kind of teaching style made me more confortable when learning, and be more willing to ask him math questions. With his encouragement, I found the satisfiction in my mind and were no longer fear to learn math. I even got the highest grade in my class on the college entrence exam.
Since most people tend to learn happily, it's quite effective to reward students for learning. All punishment no rewarding makes students stocked and passive to learn!

subject: HW1001
content:
Being a student for so many years, in my opinion, I believe that rewarding students for learning is more effective. Because of nature, people usually like to be praised, and compliment can make students more self-esteem and want to prove themself.
Take my sister as an example, she used to be a permistic girl and thought that studying was noththing but wasting time. Under the pressure and punishment from her teacher and my father; What's worse, she was sick and dare to talk with most people. After this lesson, we realize that punishment is just a tool, only rewarding and encouragement can change a person's attitude or even all his personality. Now, my sister has been turn into a aggressive girl with a dream.
All in All, sometimes we win, sometimes we lose, that's life, so everyone might have a setback. So, if we hope to motivate other people, try to help them think the bright side and make them be themself.

subject: HW1001
content:
In Taiwan, few decades ago, teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and also make them behave well. This method did work and also made it easier for teachers to teach. However, I prefer teachers to teach their students by rewarding students for learning.
Students in these years are much more different than before. They have their individual aspect of view and many of them are even independent from their parents. In my opinion, teachers have to know each students clearly and take more care about them. They have to respect their students so that students will respect them from the bottom of their heart. If possible, they can also try to be friends with students. In this way, students would like to share their problems and tell what is really on their minds so that teachers can help them. For instance, I had problems on English learning before. My teacher took much care of me and always solve my problems. I trusted him so much and no sooner we became friends. We talked about all the problems that I were facing when learning English and he always listen to me patiently and reward me by encouragement. After few months of hard-working, I had overcome the problems.
In summary, to educate with punishment might work, but teachers can do better by rewarding students by encouragement and their care. I believe this can help students learn more from their teachers than before.

subject: HW1001
content: I think that punishment is the most effective method to control students. Students may be very lazy to do their homeworks or they may play with classmates outdoors too late to do them. So teachers must be play the role to motivate students to do their homeworks or learn what teachers have teached by punishment. In that way, students are afraid of being punished, and their homeworks can be finished on time. But the relationship between teachers and students must be worse and worse. When that students become adult, they consider their school day to be their poor memory. So I think rewarding students for learning is the right way. Althought it looks like not a effective method, and must be taken a lot of time. Students must be happy to learn what they study and do homework. They are not forced to do, but volunteer to do by themselves. Now this is not a period that after graduate you don't learn anymore, so I think that it is important to build up their learning hobby from school. In summary, instead of controlling the students, we should encourge them and reward their excellent behavior in study.

subject: HW1001
content:
There is no denying that the mothods of teaching become various; however, my standpoint toward it is to reward students for learning from time to time.
Undoubtedly, advantages fill this approach. To begin with, by rewarding students for learning, no student would love to be the last person to gain the prize. What's more, in no way will punishment be a part of school life so that students may as well exert their efforts to fairly be awarded. Last but not the least, students whose intelligence is instinctly inferior to others will be inspired with this sort of incentive. Take myself as an example. I am now a volunteer teaching English for those living in remote areas. Due to a freshman in this part, firstly I used a common way to teach them -- just teaching without making them answer questons or show themselves. They seemed bored with the lesson. Not until a learned English teacher told me to reward students for learning did I realize that there was still a lot I didn't understand. Receiving the marvelous way, I did my best to try it. Now, much to my surprise, students in my class have a great passion for learning English, and also they cooperate to show their powers and to get the decent rewards. In short, having an appropriate method to motivate students to learn is really a mainpoint.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are two perspectives toward motivating students to learn. One is making use of punishment, yet the other is rewarding students. As my opinion, the second one is more effective.
Take my brother for example, he is a playful junior high school student. To push him studying, my mom tried every means wholeheartly, but there seemed useless and ineffective. Coincidently, all of her methods were punishment without any rewards. Later, my mom came up with a new plan. She gave my brother one hundred dollars every time when he did well on his tests. Hardly had the policy been implemented before my brother's improvement showed up. We were stunning with his improvement and his efforts on his studies. My mom is satisfied with my brother's grades and gives him more free time. She had not been upset with my brother's attitude toward studies since she made good use of the rewards. Now my brother is interested in studying without any punishment.
Punishment and rewards are both methods to motivate students to learn. I strongly suggest parents and teachers try the second one. Everyone likes to be respected instead of being humiliated. Why not attempt to respect your kids? You would find the unbelievable results beyond your expectation.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, I believe teaching students by punishment is much more effective than rewarding them.
I think that teacher should punish students when they do something wrong in order to make them totally understanding that what they have done is not right. I remember of my senior high school teacher, who was very strict to his students. He took a special method as punishment to teache us. Whenever we were late for school, skipped class or got a lousy score in exams, he would make us to run the field for five times. It wasn't a touch punishment, but we were lazy and we didn't like running in a hot summer day. Therefore, we would try our best to get up earlier and study harder. With my teacher's help, I now set up a concept that I should never be late for class or work in the future. I am really appreciate for it.
I believe that rewarding students is also a useful method, but punishing them is much more effective. People need to learn from the mistake they have done and they will have the chance to change their behavior.

subject: HW1001
content:
How to promote students' willingness of learning is the main question to teachers except for teaching. Some teachers prefer using punishment to stimulate naughty students while others like to use rewarding to encourage students. As far as I am concerned, rewarding is the batter way to make students work hard, and it makes students to learn spontaneously. By rewarding students, they are aware of how good it is to acquire knowledges, and they will study by themselves without stress. On the contrary, students who encounter punishment will lack the interest to learn new things, and they will be afraid of textbooks as a result. Even worst, the more punishment they suffer, the more they want to escape from classes and do something bad. So punishment will neither motivate students to learn nor control their behavior.
When I was studying in junior high school, I was addicted to online game, and I spent much time in the Internet Cafe'. As a result, my grades dropped sharply, and I almost spent all the money I saved before. As soon as my teacher noticed that, she shouted at me and warned me not to go to Internet Cafe' again. However, I didn't learn at first, and I spent even more time on online games. But when my parents was informed of my behavior, they didn't punish me. Instead, they encourage me to study more, and they said if I have a progress for the next monthly exam, I would get some money for reward. After that, I made my best to study hard, and my grades gradually increased. As a result, I got a good grade even better than the grades before I addicted to games.

subject: HW1001
content:
Ten years ago, when I was still a little boy. I don't know what is punishment, and I lived very happy then. My study at school was also great at that time. And then, when I was a junior high school student. I still remembered my teacher always hit me. So, at that age I knew what is punishment and I don't like it. And then, when I was senior high. My teacher didn't hit me. Actually, she didn't hit anybody, because she told us it didn't work at all. So, although my senior high didn't get any punishment, my senior high still got some bad record.
So, in my opinion, I don't think punishment is a good way to motivate students, because lots of students are not willing to get hit. But, in my mom's opinion, she is very willing to let children getting punishment. So, everytime I got hit by my teacher at junior high school time. My mom was very happy to see it. But I still don't think punishment is a good way to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior.

subject: HW1001
content:
As we can see in the daily newspapers, many teachers were accused due to inappropriate physical punishments. Though some teachers think that they can motivate students to learn by using strict punishments, while other teachers believe that giving rewards can lead to better consequences. In my opinion, I think giving rewards is more effective than punishing the students.
There are two main reasons why I think giving rewards is more effective than punishing. First, I think the rewards can be the factor that propels the students to learn harder. Take my classmate as an example, he was once a very naughty student that didn't even read books. After our homeroom teacher bought a baseball cap that was the one my classmate really wanted and set it as the goal for the next first place. My classmate then worked very hard to try to win the baseball cap. To his effort, he finally won the baseball cap and became very hard-working. Furthermore, I think if the physical punishments is too strict, then it might cause some body injuries. Take my chemistry teacher as an example, he was accused by student's parents due to the punishments he made. My chemistry teacher was so angry about the student who was so naughty in class, so he grabbed a wood stick and beated him on the bottom. My chemistry teacher was so angry and beated the student's bottom almost one hundred times. As a result, the student was too hurt to sit on a chair.
In conclusion, I think that rewarding the students is much more effective than punishing the students. Because inappropriate punishments may cause unexpected injuries to students and leave regret to the teacher.

subject: HW1001
content:
Recently, there have been several pieces of news about how the teachers punished the students in improper manners. Though sometimes punishment do make its purpose to motivate students, it still do not always work, or even makes the situation worse. As a reult, I prefer the method by rewarding students.
Speaking of rewardness, encouragement comes to the first. When there is a student feel down & depressed, try to understand the reasons. If the reason are something related to poor grades, tell him not to be defeated by such a small failure & encourage him to keep on moving. Things will go better. If they were scolded because of bad behaviors, try to realize the purpose lying behind. Encourge them to quit those bad behaviors & reward them when there is a progress. If they're tired of the condition where they're in, encourage them to find something that can colors their lives, something that can relieve their tenses, like playing ball or doing art works.
It is easier & cleater to convey your love and care by rewardness than punishment. Encouragement can also prevent students from feeling-hurt occasion. Consequently this kind of teaching & leading work the most successful.

subject: HW1001
content:
The issue of whether teachers should use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior has aroused much attention in Taiwan nowadays. Since the education is the foundation of one's growth, the schooling plays an indispansable role in the worldwide society. In my opinion, rewarding students for learning can give rise to better results. For one thing, the children's motivation to learn is more vital than their real grades. For another, the more self-confidence a student establish, the more effective he or she will learn. In view of this, teachers and parents should enhance children's self-confidence by rewarding them from time to time. Therefore, if I were a teacher, I would give children reward instead of punishing them.
On the other hand, every coin has two sides. The same issue may bring about other opinions. Some teachers may think if they don't enforce the punishment severely, it will goes with bad impact. In this way, students may so fear that they don't want to go to school and thus decline their motivation to learn.
In a word, the schooling is so essential since it is schooling that broaden children's horizons, enrich their knowledge and thus cultivate their self-displine.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers regard punishment as the best way to control their students. However, the other take rewarding them to be the best method. Two ways have pros and cons, but I prefer punishing to rewarding them. With the rate of birth getting lower and lower, most family has only one child, and this situation causes parents to put all their time and effort on the child. Therefore, the students are getting harder to be controled, and the arguements between teachers and students happen really often.
In view of this, I think teachers should try to do something to make the situation changed. Take my homeroom teacher in the senior high school as example. There were a lot of students from extremly rich family, so they were arrogant and thought that they could manipulate everything. After thinking carefully, my homeroom teacher set up forbidment on the classroom and punished students who made the same mistake twice strictly. Five weeks later, our class became the best among our school, and everybody felt really confident and took class honor as priority. Nobody didn't appreciate our teacher and we are still in touch with him now.
There is no denying that punishment isn't the best way. However, I think the relation between teachers and students starts from respect. If there is no respect, rewarding would be useless. All in all, I think students should obey their teacher. Only when this has been reached, teacher can take rewarding on students.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, it is more effective for teachers using punishment than rewarding when they want to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. To begin with, by using punishment, students will probably obey the teachers commands immediately. They don't want to get hurt. The punishment is such as the law in our society. For fear of being punished, people comply with the laws. As a result, fewer accidents happened and the criminal rates got lower than before. I don't think our society will become more peaceful if government change their strategy into rewarding instead of punishing others. Some may think that they can commit the crime because no one will be punished.
Additionally, students know the clear boundary between what can do and what can't do by punishment. If teachers reward students to control their behavior, their thought may be twisted because they correct their bad behavior, and get the rewards. How about others who never do bad things? They shouldn't be rewarded?
In conclusion, punishment should always exist anytime, anywhere. Otherwise, our society or classes may turn into chaos.

subject: HW1001
content:
From my perspective, instead of using punishment to motivate the students, we should give them courage and faith on the path of learning. Due to the media, the public have been more aware of the influence on students who are punished and scolded all the time. Many of them choose to be cynical, not being accepted by other students, and turned out to be the dropouts or crimminals in the near future. In this case, I suggest that the teachers change their methods of teaching. Students nowadays need to be praised more so that they will have faith when learning the unknown. In regard of this, we should give them compliments even though they're just doing their jobs.
Take one of my classmates in elementary school for example. He was exactly the kind of boy who would never be popular among the class. He was impolite, rude, and even outraged the teachers as much as he could. But there's one thing he was proud of, fixing. He could fix anything that was broken, chairs, windows, toy cars, you name it. At first our teacher thought the student was a trouble, but after she noticed the fixing labor made him delighted and confident, she started to praise him for that. Gradually he become nicer to the other classmates, and also he treated the girls better. Sometimes he even stood up and answered questions during class. I think that's how the compliment works, making people want to be better and better, giving people a chance to see what they're good at.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students for learning instead of using punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior is more effective that can lead to better results.
So many teachers punish their students after they do something wrong. I think that the punishment might be useful for the teachers to contral students by keep them from bad behavior, but the students may not totally understand why they are wrong, and they stop doing those things just because they afraid of the punishments. Moreover, if teachers or parents alway force their children to study through punishment, even if the student gets good grades, it might not last long. They need to understand why they have to study.
When I was in the elementary school, my mother avoided me to watch TV in order to let me study more consentrate and gets good grades at school. Accordingly, I always watched TV without telling her when she was out for work. That means my mother's policy didn't work at all! But when I grow up, I finally know the true reasons for us to study is only for our own good. So without the punishment of watching TV, I

subject: HW1001
content:
In recent years, we have seen some over aggressive teacher used corporal punishment to motivate students to learn in social news. They consider the punishment is deserved to those who have bad behavior at school. However, in my opinion, it's quite inappropriate and less effective that students might be frustrated by the punishment just because they had done bad on tests or made some little mistake. Instead, rewarding students for learning is more effective. As a teacher, encouraging students to learn is the most important job. A little praise or reward never fails to make students more confident and inspire them to make more progress. But teachers should reward students moderately.
It was in junior high school time that my teacher often bought some stationaries, such as pencils, erasers, rulers, and notebooks to encourage us to keep on learning. When she sent them to me, she always said "Good job boy, you're the best, but it's not the end, you have to keep moving forward." All of my classmates wore smiles on face and continued to study hard to face the entrance test of senior high school. After the test, our class performed better than the other class using punishment. Our teacher gave us a sense of satisfication and achievement by rewarding us. And I know that rewarding students prevails over the corporal punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
The issue of whether to use punishment or to reward students so as to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior has been controversy for a long period of time. In my opinion, rewarding students will be the best solution to this situation. In this way, students have to be careful on their bad behaviors in order not to lose the rewards also be glad to behave well because of wishing to receive compliments from their teacher.
I remember once my classmate -- Jeff had been a headache of teachers who had taught him. He tended to break the rules and showed no respect to teachers. Even his parents decide to give him up. The situation hadn't turned well until he met our Chinese teacher who changed his entire life. She often asked quetions and told him to answer. If he answered the right answer, the teacher had everyone give him a big hand. From then on, Jeff raised his to answer every questions the teacher asked in class. He sure was eager to listen and answer what the teacher asked. However, Jeff still attempted to bully classmate after school. The teacher thought of a perfect way to deal with this problem: everyone was asked to do ten good things for classmates every day. Surprisingly, it did work! The relationship between Jeff and his classmates became closer and closer.
It turns out that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Giving too much restrictions and using cruel punishment only make things worse. What they really need is love and courage, not punishment. As a student, I can proof this.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, I think that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. There are two reasons to support my thoughts.
Firstly, in the modern society, a lot of educationers believe it is important to offer a safe and comfortable teaching and learning environment for teachers and learners. For example, when I was studying at a college. My teachers respected the students that learning experiences were different from my junior/senior high school's. So, I think teachers should create a confortable learning community to encourage students to get involved in the class instead of scared and frightened surroundings
Secondly, because the rate of population is reducing, a lot of parents cherish their children very much. Therefore, they care their children and are not willing their kids should be punished by teachers. When their kids make mistakes, they hope teachers use verbal advice or other ways to improve their kids' wrong behavior instead of body punishment. Actually, body punishment is not allowed to do in Taiwan anymore. If a teacher punishes hir/her student, he/she may be charged by cash or goes into the jail.
In conclusion, I think teachers should adjust their minds and thoughts because those kids are different from the generations. No one likes to be controlled. When teachers treat their students at a respected way. I think students also can learn how to respect other people at the same way. You may ask me if students really make mistakes and how teachers can do? Don't forget there still are other departments or offices deal the problems. Teachers don't have to have conflicts with students. They can pass the problems to the supporing substitutes at school. Teachers only need to do is to let students know they will understand, give love and always encourage students for good.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are many ways to stimulate students' motivation in learning. To my opinion, punishment is more effective than rewarding students although I don't agree you always use this way to make them learn.
Rewarding is a positive way to let students learn, but unfortunately, this is usually useful to good students. The people who don't like studying sometimes think that the limitation of gifts is too multiple, and they may think this way is only beneficial for good students. It ends up making a situation that good students' score is better and better, while bad students' score is worse and worse.
Punishment is a much more effective way. First, it is useful to all students. If you don't want to be punished, then you should try your best to improve your score whether you are a good students or bad one. Also, punishment is a fair way. Teachers cannot punish only bad students. It is just like law, you will be punished if you don't obey rules. On top of the list, it is indeed a fast way to make students improve their score. You must hear this sentence "you will thank me punishing you, and if I don't do this today, you will hate me in the future."
Although I think punishment is more effective, punishment can't change the truth that it is a negative way. Hence, I think we should use both ways in the same time.

subject: HW1001
content:
Many people believe that rewarding students for learning is preferable to punishing them when they make mistakes. These people tend to feel that motivating students to learn by encouragement can somewhat help them search for their genuine goal instead of just catering to their parents' or teachers' expectations. Although it needs time to change students' mind by mild methods, I believe there are some positive aspects.
Take my cousin for example. He was a little boy who never obeyed his teacher's rules when he was at first grade. His teacher at first grade always punished students when they made mistakes. The more strict the teacher was, the more impolite my cousin behaved. However, he had a different teacher at second grade who always took care about students' feelings. The teacher taught him to behavior as a good student by telling him a lot of stories about successful celebrities, and also encouraged him by rewarding him some toys or candy when he did nice job. He really had an apparent change between first grade and second grade.
More and more research is suggesting that those who grow up with considerate methods of learning are more self-confident and can have positive thoughts when suffering difficulties. With the encouragement they receive before, they would realize how to express their care and affections to others. It is vital to be a considerate person.
In conclusion, the decision to which methods are better may depend on different parents. However, based on the important factors discussed earlier in this essay, it is clear that rewarding students instead of punishment is certainly beneficial to them.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I think rewarding is more effective. Although punishment is a good way to control students' behavior, sometimes too much punishments will make them more afraid of learning or even hate learning. If we can reward them when they perform well, they can build more confidence and they will be more willing to learn. Nowadays, lots of students are punished by teachers very often because they don't follow what their teachers expect them to do. Some teachers even give them up. These students behave worse and worse. However, these students don't want to give up learning. They don't like learning because their teachers don't think they can do well. If we can give these students more rewards, I believe they can be more confident on learning. In this way, they can perform well at school.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, after people get married, they often choose not to have a child. Therefore, there are less and less children. It is also the reason why parents always view their children as treasures. They can't stand others, including teachers, punish their children. One coin has two sides, and the topic we discuss is not an exception.
In my opinion, I think that rewarding students for learning is more effective than punishing them. First of all, students will study hard and concentrate on their studies in order to win the prizes. Once they win the prizes, they will be honored, and it really motivate them to pay more attention on studies.
For example, when I was a junior high school student, my teacher is strict. If we didn't bring textbooks or forget to do our homework, the only ending is to be punished. Though we all understood that the teacher just hoped we could enter a good senior high school, the punishment resulted in many bad influences. Many people finally chose to cheat on exams in order not to be punished by our teacher. In addition, the fear of being punished by the teacher dipped into my mind, and I was reluctant to go to school.
Because I have experienced such terrible things, I don't want to let it happen again. As a result, I think rewarding students is the best way for teachers to use. I think the students who are rewarded must have a happy memory in their school lives.

subject: HW1001
content:
Laziness is the most quintessential feature of students, so students need may as well punishment as reward. Punishment is the most effective method of reining students. Students are fear of getting punch or other punishments, so they'll control their behavior lest they'll be punished. Rewarding students is a good method, but students won't lose anything if they do something wrong, so they may take rewarding for granted and ignore the meaning of rewardness. I think punishment is the better way to stimulate students to work hard.
When I graduated from junior high school and got into the new school, I have great fantasy of the high school live. Our homeroom teacher set a regulation: if we behave well, he'll give everyone beverage every week. At first, everyone talked politely and behave deliberately. After knowing each other, the class began to be a noisy and dirty environments. Our homeroom teacher noticed the bad situation of our class, he stipulated that the reward is cancled and he was going to punish those who make the classroom ugly. The new regulation affect our classmates behavior profoundly, every became a good student.
Setting regulation of punishing students just like setting laws to prevent crime. For fear of being punished, students will be careful on their behaviors and what they said, so punishment is the best method of teaching students.

subject: HW1001
content:
As far as I am concerned, I believe that rewarding students for learning shall lead to better results for two crucial reasons. For one thing, rewarding them shall help them build on their confidence. Confidence is extremely important when learning. For the other, I believe by doing so, the students won't feel as stressed or as agitated when learning. Students need to know that somebody believes in them and is rooting for them in order to learn well and efficiently. In a word, rewarding students for learning shall only motivate them further onto their path of education.
On the one hand, a lot of students doubt themselves when learning in modern society now. If we reward them for learning, I'm positive that it will have great impact on their confidence when seeking education and knowledge in a fantastic way. Take myself as a telling example. I used to be the poorest student in pratically the whole grade. I was about to give up when an "angel" stepped into my life, Ms. Chang, her name was. She was my sixth grade teacher, she coached me after school until seven. She never gave up on me. She kept teaching me until I understood. She never ceased to hand out touching compliments to me when doing so, too. As a seventh grader now, I have so much more confidence in myself, and I really owe it all to Ms. Chang for rewarding me and complimenting me along the rocky path. On the other, being in stress and under pressure aren't good for learning at all. It only further damages the relationship between teachers and students, and even the students' confidence shall be shattered. By rewarding them, the teachers and students would get along in harmony. Nobody would have to feel hurt or agitated. Take my sister, Sally, as a fine example. Her former teacher used to beat her up whenever she got a low score or even misbehaved a little in class. Then, Sally got a new teacher who encouraged her and rewarded her. Now, I can assure you she is the top student in her class. In short, rewarding students is the best method teachers can use when teaching.
Although some might argue that "the cane" might be more efficient, we don't' want to damage anyone's confidence, do we? And some might even argue that punishment would scare the students into learning and behaving well. Yet, in consideration for all the benefits rewarding students provides us, I shall raise both my hands to "rewarding students" as it leads to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
Punishment has been playing an important role in our education. Most people had an experience of being punished wherever at school or home. As far as I know, some teachers in Taiwan love to punish students. They believe by doing this, students can be motivated to learn and control their behavior. However, some other teachers don't think so. They think that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, rewarding is much more effective than punishing. Here are some reasons why I think so.
Firstly, some students tend to be out of control when they are punished. Take my friend, Daniel for example, he enjoys being punished. He thinks getting caught and doing bad things are fun. He always breaks the school rules just for getting punishments. Second, punishments can totally down a person. Students might feel depressed or sad after being punished. Making students upset is not the right way that teachers should do. Additionally, most students tend to feel the happiness when they get rewards. Take myself for example, I always feel good after getting rewards. That really motivates me to do well on tests and studies.
In conclusion, rewarding is always better than punishing. Therefore, I think rewarding is more effective.

subject: HW1001
content:
Increasing number of teacher believe rewarding students for learning is preferable to using punishment. They think "educate with love" can somewhat help the students in the future. Although rewarding students for learning may take teachers more time and spirits, I think there are some aspects worth mentioning.
Take my cousin for example. He was a naughty boy. His parents were worried about what would happen after he entered elementary school. He met a really kind teacher, she never scolded, or punished students. Initially, my cousin acted like childhood. However, his teacher didn't give him any punishment because of his behavior. Instead, she encouraged him to play some sports to release his energy. Gradually, he could concentrate on what teacher said. He worked hard in class. During break time, he played ballgames full of passion. After graduating from elementary school, he became a changed person. Now he can separate working from playing clearly, and become a manager in a big company.
More and more research is pointing out that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. It may makes the students carry on more responsibilities and burdens. Also, students may be more self-confident in the future. In conclusion, only educate kids without severe punishment such as shouting at them, or hitting them with sticks can let the students have a proper developement.

subject: HW1001
content:
Teachers use many ways to motivate students to learn or to adjust their behavior. I think that to encourage students is the more effective way than the punishment. In fact, giving punishments to students is really inappropriate. It might ruin their passion to study or make them resist toughly.
For example, my sister had been poor in math. Her school math teacher always scolded the student who had bad performances on math tests. My sister was one of the victims. She said that she had no confidence on math forever. My mom found a tutor for her in order to save her grades. Surprisingly, her math grades improved rapidly. I wondered why and asked the tutor. He said he always encouraged my sister when she got stuck in a math problem. If she finally solved the problem, the tutor would give her a candy for rewarding. And, if she couldn't answer the question, he would tell her the right solution patiently and make a similar problem to check whether she was understand or not. The tutor was great!
Teachers should make themselves learn the way the tutor tought my sister. There is no student who can't be tought in the world. Passion and patience are required for a good teacher. If teachers were as wonderful as the tutor, all the students should love learning new things.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teacher prefer punishing students than rewarding them. It is because punishments scare students. However, students may get hurt mentally and phisically through punishing which may lead to the decreasing of the will of learning. Further more, it may let students think that violence is the best way to solve problems. And that's the result we are not willing to see. Therefore, I think rewarding students for learning will be more effective.
When I was in elemantery school, teacher usually punished me because I didn't do my homework or because I didn't get a good grade. However, I didn't really care about the punishments I deserved. When I reached junior high school, my teacher didn't use punishments. Instead, she taught us that learning is one of the many ways which leads us to becoming a better person. And she told me that I'm smart so I'm likely to learn faster than others. With her encouragement, I studind harder and harder and found that it is fun to study. It was her rewarding instead of punishing that let me became willing to study.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the old times, teachers were used to punish students to motivate them to learn. For the time passing by, some teachers start believing that to reward students to learn will be more effective.
As a teacher, I think it's not the time for punishing students but rewarding. If we can encourage our students more often, the students will be more willing to accomplish what we expect for.
I have a student who wasn't interested in English. I found out that if I encourage her, she will try her best to learn, and of course, she got improved and she is more confident now.
