Punishing won't be the best way to teach students and to control their behavior, instead, rewarding and encouraging will lead students to be a better person.

subject: HW1001
content:
Many people of the old generation think that, nowadays, children are more difficult to control because they have more freedom to express their opinions. Therefore, they suggest teachers motivate student by punishing. However, in my opinion, rewarding students for learning can be more effective. The reason why I support the latter one is that the positive way is more likely to encourage students and even increase their confidence in learning and improving their mistakes.
The result has been proven by some psychologists as well. They make an experiment which includes a teacher and two groups of students. One of them receive severe punishments after making some mistakes or ill-behavior. Yet, the other get more gentle punishments like forcing to write one more diary. As a result, the latter one shows that children who receive milder punishments are more dare to improve and admit their mistakes. Some of them even can learn more things from their mistakes. Hence, I approve that students had better be rewarded instead of severe punishment.

subject: HW1001
content: Nowadays, the government has practiced the love education for decades. However, the terrible physical punishments are still hitting the newspapers' headlines. Some teachers deeply believe that physical punishments can avoid students making the same mistakes. Therefore, they use punishments to let teenagers learn the correct behaviors. In my opinion, the serious physical punishments have caused severe mental hurts to these growing children. On top of the mental and physical hurts, they start to afraid to go the school and get low intersting in learning the acdamic knowledge. Compared to the punishments, I would support the way of rewarding students. By rewarding them presents or candy, the students would not only be happy but also be more intersted in learning. For example, my little brother, now is a ten-year-old boy in elementary school. When he was in grade two, he began to struggle to go to school. Besides, he cried after school almost every day. Feeling strange, my mother and I noticed that my little bother's teacher disliked him. Nearly everyday, she commanded my brother angrily that he should stand outside the classroom. My brother was afraid of the teacher's terrible face, and had nightmares. The pressure had made him get sick for a long time. Therefore, my mother determined to change school for my brother. Now, my little brother is in grade three, living a happy time. Knowing my little brother's miserable past, his new teacher always takes more care of him. In addition to noticing him more, his new teacher as well as gives my little brother many presents, such as pencil box, candy and so on, when he does well on his exams or class learning. If my little brother had met the new teacher earlier, he would have not suffered the severe memories. I think rewarding students is the more effective way to lead to better results. Because of the rewarding and the love education, my little brother get his beautiful sweet smile again every day.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some believe that the best way to raise students' motivation is punishment, while others hold a different point of view by saying that "positive reinforcement" is more effective than "negative reinforcement". In my opinion, moderate rewards for students can lead students to be confident and highly motivated. With the aids of rewards, students are encouraged and willing to learn. Thus, students will become active learners. On the contrary, if teachers use punishment more than rewards, students are unlikely to gain self-confidence and willingness to learn. And this would lead students to be passive learners or even not learners at all.
Take myself as an example. When a teacher encourages me to answer questions and rewards me whenever I have the right answer, I gain confidence and willingness to learn that subject. However, when a teacher punishes me whenever I do a bad job on my exams, I am frustrated and reluctant to work on it. Although the two approaches would raise students' motivation, the purpose of the students is extremely different. With punishment in mind, students study to prevent from being punished; with award in mind, student study to gain knowledge. Therefore, rewarding students is a better way to help students learn and lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
Different teachers have different teaching ways. Some teachers think punishment can motivate students to learn and control their behavior. However, in my opinion, I believe that giving reward to students can lead them to learn better.
Nowadays, students like to be admired and be rewarded. When teachers admire them in class or give them some presents as reward, student will think they do a great job and have more confidence. For example, I have student who is in sixth grade. He is not a smart student. When he gets good grade on the tests, I give him some presents as reward in order to motivate him to learn. Gradually, he does better and better on the tests.
I think rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Students are willing to learn. They will not be afraid to go to school; in contrast, they will think going to school is happay.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion I perfer to rewarding students for learning is more effective way. The reasons why I perfer this way is that when students get compliments from teacher they will feel more confident. And when teacher giving them candy or chocolate as rewarding they will feel much happier. So I perfer rewarding students not punishment.
When I was young I clearly remember I had a great teacher. She never punish or try to control students. She always told us moral story let us learned moral leasson from it. And she taugh us we needed to praised everyone everyday. She came up an idea anyone who followed this rule can got rewarding. So everyone in class behaved well and try our best to got the rewarding. My teacher didn't punish us but she let us became a well-behave student and have great manner. She used her own special way let us leared many things. This is why I think rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students for learning is more effective than using punishment to correct their behavior. In other word, sugar is better than a bar. By using punishment to control students behavior, some may be well-mannered, but others may be not. However, if we reward them for learning, they will be cheered up, and they are willing to do well next time. Besides, punishment is not always effective, but rewarding can be useful for a long time. People like to get presents, and hate to be punished. According to psycologists, if you hit someone frequently, he or she may do harm to you. In terms of these facts, I think rewarding students is better than punishment.
Take my friend Tom as an example. He is a teacher teaching high school students. He doesn't punish his students but reward them. All of his students like him and are willing to behave well. Moreover, his students do well on any undertaking, including studying and activities. Therefore, it makes me believe that rewarding is better than punishment. It is true that students will behave well when they are punished. However, if we want to shape up students, we should reward them instead of punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my views, the second methods is much better than the first methods. First, recording to reports, students will enhance their academic performace if they are encouraged. Second, teachers will get closer relationship with their students by praising their students. Futhermore, students will feel betters when they get poor performace if their teacher encourage them rather than punish them. Hence, I think the second method is better to motivate the students.
When I was in my third grade in elementary school, my math was pretty poor. One of the reasons is that my teach would beat my hands with the steals when I got bad scores, which made me affraid of my teacher and hate math very much. In this way, my math got more poor and poor. However, when I was sixth grade, I had new math teacher. She looked very beautiful and treated me very well. Besides, She would be very paitient to teach me how to solve the problems. Moreover, she never beated me. Instead, she even encouraged me when I got bad grade. Hence, I made a dratical progress in math and through her help, I loved. From then on, I was firmly convinced that encourage and rewarding is the best way for teachers to motivate their students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, people have different opinions toward how to make students' learning more efficient. Some prefer to use punishment, but others think rewarding may be more efficient. To me, I prefer rewarding to punishing.
First of all, rewarding makes students want to learn! Rewarding is a more positive way to tell students the advantages of studying. By rewarding, students not only gain knowledge from studying, but also they get some benefits. When they get some advantages, they may become more willing to learn because they know there are always benefits in studying.
In addition, rewarding helps students get to know the fun of learning. Learning is an interesting process, but it may not be easily understood, unless you really enjoy it. To reach this goal, rewarding may be a good method. Take myself for example, when I was small I always hated to learn because I thought the textbooks were so boring. Therefore I usually get grades that weren't really good. One day, I learned a lesson at school that I was quite interested in. After school, I reviewed the lesson on my book and did some research on the Internet. A few days later, I had an exam on that subject. To my suprise, I got the best grade in my class and my teacher and parents were so happy that they praised me and gave me a lot of gift. It was that day that I finally found out that learning could also be fun. Since then I am always willing to learn and I always hope I could absorb knowledge in my everyday life.
Although some people may argue that punishing can make students study immediately and get good grades, I think the real reason why we ask students to study is not for the grades. We hope that they can truely understand that learning can always do them good. In conclusion, I believe the advantages of rewarding students to learn outweigh its disadvantages. Therefore, I think rewarding is better method than punishing.

subject: HW1001
content:
According to a survey done by the social department of NCCU, 75% people consider using punishment to motivate students to learn a bad method, and 85% of them claimed that it is the government's responsibility to forbide physical punishment by making a new law. Although there are still some people support using punishment, as we can see, most people rather peffer rewarding students for learning.
Most teachers have the experiences of blaming students and punishing them. However, most teachers have been trying their best to change this habit, due to the fact that their students have become even more rebelious after the punishment. Chief amoung the causes of this problem is that both physical and mental punishment can result in the damage of stundents' self-esteem and confident.
On the other side, rewarding students turns out to have better effects. For example, if a student is pariased by his or her teachers and parents because of getting a better score, he or she will difinitely try harder next time.
The positive thoughts and enmotions students received are undoubtedly the most contributing factor of a student's improvement. With the determination of not letting teachers down, students will surely have a huge progress.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my point of view, I think that it is better to reward students rather than punish them in order to motivate them to study or behave well.
Compared to punishment, rewarding is more acceptable for students simply because no one wants to be punished. Besides, it may hurt student's self-respect when punishing them. Furthermore, the point is to let them know why he is being punished, not the punishment itself.
Rewarding students is more effective than punishing. Take the scores for example, it is better to say, "It is great that you score 50 in math test. I think that you can get 60 next time.". When students hearing these words, he will have more confidences in himself and try his best to study. However, if you say, "I feel very disappointed at you." and hit him because his scores, it doesn't solve any problems but destroy relationship between teacher and students.
In sum, I think that you can always find other methods to teach students rather punish them. It is important to use love and passion to educate them rather to let them suffer physical and mental pain. Only by love can truly make students become better, and that is what our education should be.

subject: HW1001
content:
Punishment is often used to force the students to behave well and some of the teachers also believe that it's a good way for them to frighten those who don't really work hard. But in my opinion, punishment is completely illegal for teachers to do so, and it will lead a negative result which may cause students' depression or self-doubtness. Therefore, I totally disagree with punishment.
Conversely, Being rewarded, students will get more confidence and they will learn better because their motivation will be positive. I still remember clearly that when I was a junior high student, one of my teachers was extremely strict and mean. He always punished me if I didn't get good grades on the subject he taught. I got more and more nervous and stressed. Eventually, I didn't make any progressive. Worst of all, I became scared every time when he just came into the classroom. From then on, I have hated history.
All in all, punishing is obviously not a proper way. Students will perform better and more only when they are encourged or rewarded. Pep talk really works.

subject: HW1001
content:
Recently, corporal punishment is an widely disscussed issue. You could heard the news that a teacher is sued by parents because of the inapporate punishment. As a result, teachers are more careful about how to discipline students. Should teachers punish stduents to behave them or should teachers reward the students for learning?
In my opinion, I think rewarding students is the best way to motivate students. Instead of punishing the students, teachers should reward students for learning. If teachers always punish their students, the students will loose their interests in learning. Students are forced to learn, they may study for test. They will think that they study for their teachers. However, rewarding students can increase students' intersts in learning. They will learn well. Students will work hard in order to get the reward. In addition to the reward they get, they learn better. Students will think they learn for themselves.
When I was a senior high school students, the teacher always punished me for bad grade. I was afrid of punishment, so I studied the part that teacher asked me to. Even though my grade was better, I wasn't insterested in learning. When I learn, all I think about is that I should learn or else I will get some punishments. I'm forced to learn. On the other hand, one of the teachers rewarded me instead of punishing me. I found out that I learned better and harder. I had fun in learning when the teachers rewared me.
To sum up, instead of punishing students, rewarding students could lead to better result. Students will not only learning for the reward but also learning for themselves. It could increase their interests in learning. They're not forced to learn. Students will have fun in learning.

subject: HW1001
content: Both punishment and reward are used to make students learn better. In my personal opinion, rewarding students for learning can lead better results. Everyone refers to be rewarded than be punished. It can motivate student to pay more effors on studies. It is not only more positive but also more effective than using punishment. For example, I have taught a student during my senior-high. She was about fifteen years old and was cute but a little shy. When I used some punishment because of her mistakes for test, I found that she lost interest in studying. As result, I started to encourage and rewarded her for good learning. Then, she learned more and more with more interest. We both enjoyed the happy learning-time together. So I support the second method. Using punishment maybe can motivate students to pay more attention to studies; however, giving positive encouragement can make students learn more on their own willings.

subject: HW1001
content:
Many people argue either punishment or reward is the most effective method to motive students. Therefore, I agree with using punishment. In this society, many students lead a comfortable life and they even do not lack any reward. Reward is like Mc Donald if students do not get it, they will not feel disappointed because it is not necessary and important. On the contrary, nobody wants to be hit so it makes punishment have a potential strength to force students to study and improve.
My younger brother is the best example to prove my opinion. My mother always tells him if he can get ninety on his English test and then my mom will buy a pair of NIKE shoes for him. Nevertheless, my brother still do not get this prize. I think perhaps he always has an idea that he has many opportunities to get this prize. On the contrary, if my mother says if he does not get ninety she will punish him and my brother tries his best to get good grades.
It shows that reward is not as effective as punishment and it just like that the government declares people will be fined if they smoke in closed space. Therefore, this regulation actuelly reduces the rate of smoking. Every people's mind is the same and we all want to escape from punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
Severe punishment may achieve the immediate effects to control students but I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. You can prevent your students from behavioring badly for a while by physical punishment because they get hurt and are afraid of what you treat them. On the contrary, they hate you from the bottom of their mind and make the same mistakes or even more criminal behaviors in future because they don't be educated what's going wrong with them and the benefits of learning in school. However every one wants to be respected, treated tender, understood well. Surely love can lead a person to the better world. Teacher's love would motivate students to learn happily and have a better future in stead of getting high scores in tests. The most important thing of being a teacher is to guide his or her students to explore the wonderful world and do something good for their society.
One of my classmates hates to learn English when he was a freshman. Fortunately, we meet a nice teacher who always keeps smile while he got poor scores in English. Furthermore, whenever he gave a correct answer to what the English teacher asked, the teacher would request all classmates the big hands loudly. Day after day my classmate began to love English and at last he passed the entrance examination of junior high school.
Believe or not, even animals can appreciate your love if you respect them and treat them good. Therefore, I am convinced that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Love can make you smarter.

subject: HW1001
content:
Being a teacher is always a difficult job. Teachers have the sacred job to educate and even influence a person's life. The teaching method they use will effect their students learning. Some people say punishment can make students learn how to behave properly; still another people say rewarding them will be more effective. In my opinion, I think rewarding students will be a better way in teaching.
Rewarding method can help student cultivate their confidence and stimilate their learing egerness. I think being confidence in what we are doing will make us become outstanding in the specific field. For example, I am a tutor and I have a student that at first really hated EngTind. However, I think he was just afraid of it. In order to help him, I reward him everytime when he finished his work. Gragually his grade improved and his teacher also impressed by his improving. Now, he like English very much, because he knows that he is good at it.
Punishing method will hurt student's heart and may cause other bad influence. Students are mostly teenagers. In that time, they will get angry easily and have a strong personal opioion. Punishment will make them feel embarrased and then unwilling to learn or do what teacher whan them to do.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I believe that rewarding students for learning leads to better results. With the devolpment of modern education, punishment is out of date and counterproductive. I think teachers should reward and encourage students for learning because it has positive effects on students and teachers should play their roles right in order to educate students.
First, rewarding and encouraging students to learn has positive effects on them. No one wants to be punished and as a human being, he or she has rights to refuse any unproper punishment. I think by rewarding and encouraging students, they can gradually get interests in learning rather than feel scared about it.
Second, teachers are models to their students and they should play roles positively by rewarding and encouraging students. Teachers have to show their patience to students and how they concern about their students instead of punishing them. If teachers are kind and nice, students are willing to accept their suggestions. If students like the way teachers teach them, then they will enjoy learning little by little.
From my point of view, I believe that rewarding students for learning leads to better results because it has positive effects not only on students but also on their learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
I believe that rewarding is better than punishment. It has long been a controversy that a teacher should take physical punishment or education by love to teach their students. I think the former may have effect immediately and will also make students pay attention to their own behaviors. However, it is not a good way because sometimes it may hurts the feeling of students' and they may also be afraid to express what they thought. In addition, it have little influence to the bully students. As a result, I believe that teachers should take the latter approach.
It is inescapable for a teacher to get along and communicate with students. Therefore, it is essential to provide some incentives to motivate and encourage them, such as giving them praise in public for doing good deeds, giving them some gifts worth cherishing or taking them for a trip and so on. Students might be grateful and confident in mind and perform more outstanding in learning and behaving. On the contrary, using punishment may function right away, perhaps, but the students may not be satisfied and identified with in their mind.
Finally, I consider that all students possess good heart but only go astray easily. If only teachers could encourage and motivate ther students by expressing their affection. By doing so, the students would make their way to better future!

subject: HW1001
content:
Both using punishments and rewarding are good ways to make students become better and better. However, I regard teachers using punishments is the more effective way. Most of the children in my generation are often spoiled by their parents. They don't respect their teachers and they even make fun of them. So using serious meterials to control students behavior is the fastest method. Moreover, students usually do things better when there are some punishments waiting for them if they didn't do well.
One boy in my class can be a suitable example. Our homeroom teacher asked him to give her a hand to send some papers to her office, and after that she's going to give him a small reward. But the boy didn't want the reward at all, so he didn't help the teacher. Helping our teachers is the thing we students should do. Our teacher got mad and punished the boy. Still, the boy had to send the papers.
In my opinion, lazy or naughty students should use the punishing method for they don't even care about the reward or something about respect. In the other hand, students who are behaving well don't have to worry about the punishments. They can do their best to avoid to get punish. In short, using punishments is the more effective and direct way to make students behave well.

subject: HW1001
content:
As far as I am concerned, motivate students to study harder and behave themselves by rewarding them is much more effective than scolding or punishing them.
Take myself for example, when I was in elementary school, my teacher insisted that those who got one hundred on any tests get an elaborate toy selected by herself. Out of desire, I tried my best on every tests; therefore, these lovely collections belong to me. I am still appreciate for this affectionate teacher, I might not discover the innate intelligence in studying if I had not taught by her. What she had done was simply giving a small gift; nevertheless, it turned out to be a enormous blessing for me.
Therefore, the influence of rewarding students is significant. If a teacher praises a student improving even five scores on the test, he will definitely feel delighted. As a result, he is more willing to prepare for the next test, managing to shine again. I love to be recognized, and so do others. We all need others to identify with during the span of learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers teach their students by giving them punishment, but others choose to give their students rewards and encourages. These two ways are totally different. And I prefer to choose the second method. I would like to share my opinions.
To begin with, punishing students is not a good method. Once the student get punishment from teachers they will feel panic to do the work again simply because they gradually lose their confidence. Then, they have no any motivation on works or assignments.
Moreover, that teachers control their students behavior is not appropriate at all. They might limit students' developments of interest. Life will be boring if a person has no interest in everything.
However, giving rewards instead of blaming are the best way to teach students. As the students make an achievement and receive a reward, they believe the efforts they make can change into big prizes. Needless to say, the students will make any effort to achieve and complete the work.
If the students make a big trouble, he or she may be upset. I believe encouraging is the best way for them. When they learn the disadvantage, they will avoid to make the same problem again.
In conclusion, even if the students achieve or not, they will try hard the next time when they get the rewards. They will have more motivations on assignments. "No pain, no gain."

subject: HW1001
content: To some teachers, using punishment is the best way to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. In contrast, others believe that rewarding students for learning is the best method to teach students. For me, reward is more effective than punishment. Due to lots of rewards which teachers give, a student will become more confident of himself. Thus, learning will be a happy thing to him. On the other hand, no one likes to be punished. The more punishments are performed, the more dislike emerge in a student's heart. As a result, learning would be the last thing a student wants to do. Rewarding students for learning truly can lead to better results. For instance, when I was in the elementary school, I once did bad in a speech contest. I was so frustrated that I didn't want to deliver speech any more. For me, delivering a speech was a horrible nightmare. However, my teacher didn't punish me for the bad performance, but encouraged me to give myself another chance. She said that she would be willing to teach my, as long as I wanted to try again. Finally, I tried again and fortunately won the first prize. Now, I am no longer the slave of a speech, but its owner. I awed my success to my teacher, who didn't use punishment but rewarding to teach me. From the experience, I realized that the best way to teach students is rewarding them instead of punishing them.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, corporal punishment should be abolished. I think education is a process of work-and-reward system. Teachers and students is like a partnership. Teachers help students learning either from academically or personally to get the rewards -- grades, and student, on the other hand, gain teacher the feeling of self-acomplishment.
Take one of my elementry school classmates for example. His name is Tobby, and was the stupidest boy of the class. Almost evey teacher had given up on him except my science teacher. She found that Tobby is not a bad kid, he just can't concentrate in learning. So my science teacher decided to spend three hours everyday after school in helping Tobby.

subject: HW1001
content: In Taiwan, taking exams is common to every students. Having a terrific grade, means you are supposed to enter good university, and it will lead you to a bright life from then on. As a result, many parents and teachers in taiwan will do their utmost to make their children or students do well on the exam. Some of them use punishment to motivate students, on the other hands, others reward students for learning better. In my opinion, I consider rewarding is better then punishment, and is more effective. For example, if a student usually get poor great in the class, he most feel upset, unhappy or something bad, should we still use punishment rather than encouragement? Punishment will hurt the student's dignity, making the situation worse. Maybe the student have made effort to study but still no use. By insping him, even he only has little process, the rewarding will let him realize if he keeps being perserverent, he can reach his goal. By the reason, I prefer rewading students rather than punishing students.

subject: HW1001
content:
When it comes to the best way of teaching students, I will vote for rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. I consider this method is more effective than using punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavir.
First of all, the best thing is students can have good behavior and have the willing to learn from the deep of their mind. Rewarding can make students love to do the right thing. However, punishment may only let students not to do the wrong thing. Second, students teached through punishment think of fear. While students teached through reward think of love. The more positive conscious students have, the more willing of having good behavior they may enhance.
In short, in my view, more love and less defindent make the world much more lovily so as to students' behavior. I think the method of reward is more effective.

subject: HW1001
content:
This is an issue that concerns us today -- is using punishment to motivate students to learn a good method? Some support the statement that controlling students' behavior by punlishment is the best way to their prospets. Others, including me, believe othewise. In my opinion, a large proportion of punished students don't rectify their misbehaviors; in the depths of their hearts, they are not satisfied with the outcome. It stands in a glaring contrast to rewarding them. When students behave, rewarding them is the effective way to make them realize what they have done are right. By doing so, such a good behavior will be deeply rooted in their bosom.
From my experience, my parents' method of education occupies a siginificant role in my life. Everytime I misbehave, they never punlish me. They use their way to make me understand what I have behaved was wrong. If I rectified my misbehavior, they rewarded me. In summary, punlishment is not an appropriate method to motivate students to learn.

subject: HW1001
content:
It goes without saying that some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn well. In the past, using punishment to students might be quite common. As far as I am concerned, it is a little inappropriate in the society which calls for human rights nowadays. It seems that there are certainly some reasons why teachers choose to punish students. The reasons why the condition has such a great influence are as follows:
First and foremost, some students may spend too much time indulging themselves in some computer games, chat rooms, or even inappropriate web sites. Consequently, their teachers want to prevent them from wasting their time, thus punishing them for their poor performances. Despite the fact that it is somewhat effective, I personally believe this is definitely not a best way to teach students.
On the other hand, rewarding students for learning can probably lead to better results. After all, no student wants to get punishment. With love and care, teachers can express their concerns to their students, offering a tender and enjoyable learning environment. I believe students may pay more attention to such a good learning place.
To sum up, there are a wild variety of ways to teach students. There is no need to blame or punish them all the time. From my perspective, teachers should be aware of their teaching styles and use punishment in a reasonable way. In this way, punishment can be more positive to the students.

subject: HW1001
content:
People are willing to achieve the goals which can get repay. Because of the salary, people make efforts to work hard. As the same, students will try to have a good behavior as long as they can get the things what they like. As far as I am concern, rewarding students for learning is the proper way to get better results.
Students should own a pleasant mood to study instead of learning in frustration and unhappiness. Study shows that the students in northern Europe are the happiest children of the whole world because of their education. With the encouraging thinking, the teachers in northern Europe follow the concept of rewarding students. Therefore, their children are looking forward to going to school, and actually, teachers get a good relationship between students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Due to the law, more and more teachers stop to punish students while they make mistakes. I think this is a good result because punishment isn't a good way to teach students.
I have once read a report said that if there were two plants A and B infront you, and you say different words to them, they will grow different. For example you say "I love you." or "You're the best plant." to plant A everyday. It will become a beautiful plant. On the other hand, you say "I hate you." or "You're the most ugly plant I ever seen." to plant B. It will grow to be dry and small. As far as students are concerned, this result works too. Students need encouragement rather than punishment. Students will work harder if they can have a reward after reaching the goal.
In my opinion, rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Because, everybody likes to be encourage.

subject: HW1001
content: As far as I am concerned, I agree with the point that appropriate punishment is more effective motivating students to learn and to control their behavior. In addition, students will remember clearly that they were punished by teacher due to do mistakes. When I was a senior high students, not only my English teacher but also my Chinese teacher punished us in interesting ways, if we did mistakes, we should do our level best to find a similar experience which was happened on another people, and shared with my classmates the way they solved the mistake. After graduating from my senior high school, I remembered these special experiences so clearly that I have never done the same mistakes again. What's better, my classmates could learn a lesson from my punishment. There is no denying that some punishment make people feel scared and shamful, but use interesting punishment not only doesn't have these problems, but also makes us progress.

subject: HW1001
content:
Teachers in Taiwan not only teach their students useful knowledges, but also had the responsibility to teach students how to control their behavior. In order to reach both of these goals, many teachers tend to punish their students in class because it seems to be the best way to stop kids from doing the same mistake again and again. However, in my opinion, these terrible punishments only do harm to students.
I consider rewarding is a much better than just punishing students when they fell to control their own behavior. If you only tell a person what he can not do, it will cause a lot of trouble! He or she will have no idea about what is wrong, and what is right, all be or she realize is that if they do it, they will be punished. It won't do any help to the society. Everyone behave himself well, but they do not want to help others because there's no rewards or even encouragements from their friends and family members after spending a lot of time doing things like that!
Take my cousin for example. He was a good student when he was in junior-high. He liked to help his friends with their homework and never argued with his teachers. However, the teachers just ignored his good behavior because they thought being a good student is the basic responsibility to every kid. My cousin gradually felt tired about behaving himself well and began to do tricks on classmates. He did not want to be a good student, so his teachers yelled at him and smacked him on the face. All these made him felt disappointment, and he no longer wanted to go to school till then.
I've lost contact with him after he got expelled from high school, but I'm quite sure that he still don't know why teachers just ignored him when he was a good student. This story really gave me a chance to think again the educational system in Taiwan and how teachers treated their students at school. To me, rewarding is more effective than punishing.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results is more effective. Because I think if teachers use punishment on students too much can make students feel more stressful and can have a negative impact on themselves. They'll know if they don't do their best on the tests, they'll be punished. So when they do anything their teacher ordered, they'll be so nervous that they can't do things well. Also, when they grow up, they seem to be less confident than others. On the contrary, rewarding to students is much better. Because I think if students do their best, and know they'll have rewards, they can be more confident when they're trying to do much more difficult tasks. And I think giving them encouragements is important. Also, here is a special example I want to talk about. We can tell ouselves if we do things well, we give rewards by ourselves, that can also give us more confidence and more courages when next time we do something challengeable.

subject: HW1001
content:
I thing teachers should not punish their students. If you are a teacher, you must take care of your students. School is a place to learn, not a prison. Sutents are not prisoner, so don't punish them.
My brother is a elementary school student. One day, he didn't get good grades in class, so his teacher scolded at him. He was very sad, and he didn't want to go to school because he was afraid of seeing that teacher. It was the first that I perceived that punishment is the most terrible way to students.
My sister, a junior high school student, is a diligent student. Every morning, she would listen to Let's Talk in English before she goes to school. She could get one thousand from my parents after she studies that magazine for a month. As a result, her English skills become better and better, and she are happy to learn English.
In my opion, I thing there are many ways to control student's behavior, but using punishment is the last way I would choose.

subject: HW1001
content:
Although punishment can make child pay more attention to what they are doing, it can also be toxin that spread over their mind.
Rewarding students can make them feel more confident and even inspire their motive to do things to their best. On the other hand, punishment can stimulate them to have serious attitude while tickling things. Nowadays, more and more events about physical punishment are unveiled, and it seems to bring shadow on those students.
It's essential for the teachers or parents to have the balance between compliment and punishement. More compliments and rewards seem to impact whether having a positive attitude or not. However, proper punishment are also important. Adults should make their child know if the behaviors are correct in a proper way. That is, it's important for the adults to find a compromise between rewards and punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
I believe that approprietly adding punishment toward students is a more effective way to benefit both side of teachers and students on their study path. Giving rewards means telling students what's the right thing to do, but does not tell them what's correct from wrong. On the other hand, students from the twenty first century are tend to be more and more "independent". They started to develop their own thoughts and try to complete things in their own way. It is when punishment can show it's motivation.
"What do we do if students refuse to hand in their assignments?" I believe that many teachers or tutors have considered this problem for millions of years. "Should I give some rewards to the students who do obey? Or should I lecture the kids who refuse to?" This is actually a very simple issue. For example, there were a bunch of annoying boys sitting next to me in elementry school. They're so naughty that they never put the teacher's word behind their head. There was a week that the teacher started giving extra points to the kids who did great on their tests, or folded their blanket neatly after nap time. However, this method did not work out quite well. The naughty boys still did not respond to it. But when the teacher announced that amount of punishment will be added if they don't obey the rules, they started to show some respect.
How did these happened? The answer is dignity. Students love being under spot lights and shinning the best part of them. And punishing them in the crowds or letting their "fans" know what they're done can always make them collapse. However, using punishment to motivate students doesn't mean to crush them. We punish because we want them to improve, we punish because we train them to control their behavior, we punish because we hope they can have better results on learning. Above all, I believe that appropriete punishment is a more effective and smarter way to do.

subject: HW1001
content:
The issue of people's views about motivating students to learn and to control their behavior deserves careful consideration because it is such a complex one. Some people seem to think that using punishment is very effective while other people tend to think that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, I think both using punishment and rewarding students are effective. There are two reasons why I think both ways are effective.
One reason for my position is that when students are badly behaved, teachers should give them some punishment, or they'll think that it's okay to behave that way. For example, when the class is getting really noisy, teachers should tell them to be quiet and maybe have them to stay in class for the recess. If teachers just let them keep talking, it's likely that teachers will find them playing around in class next time. The other reason is that when students are doing good on their test and behaving well, teachers should reward them, so they'll know what's the right thing to do, or they'll just think why should they do those meaningless things. For instance, my English teacher always give honor cards to students who did well on exams, so next time more and more students will want to study hard for good grades.
of course their are arguments to be made for other answers as well. Nevertheless, for the reasons that I have presented above, I believe that my opinion is a valid one.

subject: HW1001
content:
I am of the opinion that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Punishment is the worst way to motivate students to learn, and it can't control their behavior either. In other words, I believe that rewarding is more effective and positive than punishment.
When I was in junior high school, many teachers used punishment to force students to learn or to prevent students from making mistakes. But those who were punished didn't perform well, either. Punishment just let my classmates start to hate the teachers and they spoke ill of those teachers, too. My classmates all hoped they could get rid of the bad teachers as soon as possibile. On the other hand, those who performed well were not motivated by avoiding punishment, either. They were motivated by rewarding. Teachers usually tended to reward those who performed well not those who needed most.
In sum, I believe that not only good students but also those who fail to perform well need to be rewarded. Only teachers encourage or reward students for learning, can students feel the teachers' love and passion. Therefore, I believe that teachers should reward rather than use punishment to motivate students to learn or to control their behavior.

subject: HW1001
content:
In Asian society, we tend to use punishment to push students perform well on academic; however, in the west, rewarding is their best policy to make children better.
As my concerning, punishment puts pressure on students' mind, making them lose their concerntration on study. On the other hand, rewarding is more suitable to students, because that make them desire to get both good grades and prizes. If parents and teachers always punish children to control or to force them learning something, then this would press their own studying will in the long term. Giving rewards to students lead them to learn by their hearts, motivating the happiness of learning.
Take my little brother for example. He didn't like to study math, so his teacher came up a good idea to make him willing to learn. My brother's teacher found my brother's hobby is reading, so the teacher lend a book to him. After that my brother wants to read the next series, and asked his teacher for borrowing the book. However, the teacher said: "Only after you pass the math exam, then I'll lend it to you." Out of my imagination, my younger brother studied really hard and got a high grade on the exam. In the end, my brother got the whole series of book from his teacher, and after that he fell in love with math.
Everyone loves prizes instead of punishment. I think rewarding students can be the best policy to lead a better result on their performance.

subject: HW1001
content:
The methods to control and correct students' behavior has been discussed many years. However, by no means can someone reach a wonderful conclution. As far as I am concerned, I consider rewarding students for learning a better way compared with punishment. It is through the reward that students can behave well whenver they encounter difficulties because the method can make students think that what they have done will pay off some day. Therefore they may learn to set up a goal and spare no effort to fulfill it.
Take one of my experiences as an example. When I was a junior high school student, I hated studying on account of my teacher. Instead of any encouragement, he always punished me whenever I had made a mistake. Never had I received any reward when I was in the junior high school. Fortunately, I gradually did well on the schoolwork when I entered the senior high school. My teacher always took his students to see a movie when they reached the goal set up by him. With the goal, I paid more attention on my schoolwork and thus improved a lot. Finally, I achieved the goal and went to the movies happily with my classmates. Never can I forget that happy day.
To sum up, only through rewarding students can help them build up the confidence and thus perform well on the schoolwork.

subject: HW1001
content:
With the idea of respecting students' right being more and more prevalent. Some teachers gradually believe that rewarding the students for learning can lead to better results, while the others still regard the punishment as the best tools to motivate students to learn. In my opinion, rewarding students would be a better alternative for following reasons.
First, as a learner, students might feel fustrated or disappointed if they run into the challenges which they can't go through. In this situation, what students need most are encouragements instead of punishments. Second, sometimes over punishments will result in not only physical injuries but also the severe hurts of the heart. Those hurts will discourage students from learning.
To sum up, punishments would lead to some side effects. Therefore, it's my belief that rewarding students will be more useful and effective.

subject: HW1001
content:
Every teacher has different types of teaching. Some teachers may punish their students in order to make them behave well. While others believe to reward students and encourage them, which can lead to a better result.
In my opinion, I would choose the second one, which is more effective and efficient. A teacher should give complimentary to students when they behave well. Not to scold them when they have bad score but to encourage them. Teachers should treat students nicely so that they would want to listen to what teachers said and make friends with their teachers.
On the contrary, if a teacher always punish students for making mistakes, this would lead to a bad relationship between them. Because students would be reluctant to learn and do the opposite way what teachers said on purpose. For these reasons, they would become enemies rather than friends.
If teacher want to make teaching easier, they should spend more time and mind on students to make students feel like getting along with their teachers.

subject: HW1001
content:
At my school, there are lots of different teachers, and they use many different ways to help their students learn. Some teachers punish students to make them learn harder, but other teachers use rewards to help students. In my opinion, I prefer to use rewards to encourage students.
For example, my friend's teacher is always shouting in his own class, the teacher punishes those who made him upset. Because of this, all the students kept quiet in class, but the students grades did not improve, this made the teacher more disapointed. One day, my friend went to see the teacher, he explained why their grades are always so bad.
He said because a class living in fear cannot learn in peece, they are always scared of the teacher, instead of getting better, the whole class's grades went down. A class can not learn in an enviroment of fear and punishment, my brother's teacher is a funny old man, it's said that he never punishes his students, instead of using punishment, he use words to talk to his students. He often tells stories to make his students control their behavior. using rewards to lead students work hard is one of the best way my brother's teacher does to help his class.
I think teachers can't use punishment to motivat students, these students will only fear punishment and they don't understand why they should work hard. To make students understand why they should work harder is better than using punishment to make them work hard.

subject: HW1001
content:
When we were still young, the teachers always told us that the student most realize the saying "Spear the rod, spoil the child." It meaned that the punishment is the "perfect" way to let us control our behavior. But, I'm not agree this conception.
The first reason is quite simple but powful, and I dare say that everyone must have the same expierence. Punishment not only cause the pain outside of children's body, but also inside of their heart and soul. The other, if punishment really works, the teachers just need to punish a student only one time, but the fact is that the punishment may absolutely not appear just one time.
Therefore, I think that rewarding is the perfect way to encourage to student. Punishment and rewarding are the two sides of a coin; they may have the same effection, but I would rather to choose the "rewarding side."

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, many people say that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results; however, I think using punishment to motivate students are better than rewarding. Here are two reasons.
First of all, students are more impressive on punishments than rewards. For example, when I was a junior high school student, I had cheated on the exam once. When teacher saw me cheating, she tore my test paper angrily and hit my hands. I won't forget how painful when I was hit, thus I never cheat again. What's more, some students are just so rebelious, they won't listen to your advice, so use rewarding ways to teach them is impossible. Therefore, I think punishments will be more suitable for them, they will know what's fault they had done immediately and directly.
However, some parents say that because teachers punish their kids, their kids don't want to go to school anymore. In my opinion, some punishments are fine to children, parents shouldn't too protect the kids.
In conclusion, I support teachers use punishment to motivate students to control their behavior, in this way, students won't do the same mistakes again. Otherwise, our students won't find out their drawback.

subject: HW1001
content:
It has been discussed frequently that what the proper way to teach the students is. Some teachers use punishments while others believe that rewarding is better. What a controversal issue. In my opinion, it is not a best way to teach the students without care and love. Take myself for example, I was poor at math when I was in the elementary school. Every time, when I didn't do well on math test, my father would punish me, which made me hate math deeply. Although I tried hard to get myself improved, it was in vain. To my disappointment, it even got worse when I entered the junior high school.
However, something changed when I met my math teacher of senior high school. She was fifty-something years old, with a cute red glasses on her face. She taught me math step by step. If I didn't understand, she would explain it for me again and again. Due to her, my math became better and better and even got the number one when I was in the third year. Therefore, I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
I prefer to reward students for learning and teach them in friendy ways Through these methods, students can build their confidence and enjoy learning.
In my opinion, the fundational reason for students to study is develop their interests in learning. Education provides people with tools to enrich their knowledge, but not putting pressures on students. Teachers should encourage and reward students instead of punishing them. With teachers' encouragement, students would try to reach their goals and find answers happily. If students enjoy learning, they would learn in high efficiency. In addition, if teachers reward students properly, students would try to get the rewards.
When I was in the third and fourth grade of elementary school. I had two different English teachers. The first one was strict. She demanded us to memorize ten new words every day. We had tests every week. However, some students rejected to memorize those words, and everyone hated English class. After I went to fourth grade, things totally changed. The new teacher taught us interactively. We played games and had competitions in the class. The winners would get some gifts. Sometimes she devided students into two groups and we should compete with each other. We had to write down words that we had learned in that week. Who memorized more words would win the prize. Thanks to the games, all the students enjoyed English class and loved to memorize new words.
Nobody wants to get punishments. They would just make students dislike learning. It's more effective to reward students for learning since students want to get rewards. They would surely enjoy learning and gain knowledge happily.

subject: HW1001
content:
"How to motivate the students to work hard?" is always a big problem for the teachers and their parents. Some people believe that punishing the students is a great idea. They think it can make them fear, so they will work hard to avoid being punished.
Others believe that making them study by themselves is a better idea. If you reward them, they will work harder and harder to get the rewards which they want. Unlike punishments to make them fear, and forced them to work. The second idea is more effective. Students are willing to learn and control their behavior. Finally, they know that what they have doned is good for them. Therefore, they will keep an eye on themselves and work better even if they don't have any rewards.
When I was ten years old, I got bad grades twice on my math exams. My father punished me and forced me to do hard. However, it didn't get better even worse. Therefore, my father changed the way. He told me that if I got good grades, he would sent me a puzzle as a reward. Thus, I did my best to learn, and loved to go to the math class which I hated before. Finally, I got 100.
Rewarding the students is a great way to motivate them to learn and maintain their good behaviors. I think most of the teachears should try this way. Then, you will surprise that it is more effective than you think before.

subject: HW1001
content:
In our modern society, more and more people advocate that we should teach students by encouraging them. In contrast, some people insist that students should be taught by punishment. In my opinion, I prefer to reward students for learning. Rewarding as well as encouraging can make students have more confidence, more interests and more happinies.
First, having more confidence in learning can lead students to learn better. Students need encouragement and a good advice when they make a big mistake, then they will have confidence to keep learning. They will realize what to do when facing the same situation next time.
Second, rewarding helps them be more enjoyable to learn. When they get a good grade or do a great job, we can buy something they want to them as a reward. In this way, they will do a good job next time. And they will be more enjoyable to lear.
Last but not least, some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. I consider that students are afraid of them, they will give up learning at last.
In conclusion, teachers should teach students by rewarding and giving them encouragement, so that they will have more confidence to try new things and be more interest in learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are many daliy news about teachers punish their students and do the students harm. I think that use punishment to motivate students to learn is inappropriate. In my opinion, rewarding students is a better way to motivate students to learn.
Take my little sister for example. When she does something good, her teacher will give her some candy, and tells her she did it well. In order to gain the candy and teachers compliment, she makes effort to study and does her work better and better.
Another example is my cousin, he is the one who is always punished by his teacher, but he doesn't try to make effort; instead, he always fails his test and his teacher keep punishing him. That is why I think rewarding is a better method to motivate students to learn.
Although there are many ways to motivate students, not all the methods are useful. We need to find the way that students can accept, then it will be the best way to motivate students.

subject: HW1001
content:
If one day God gave you extra one hour, what will you choose to use it? To do whatever you like, or to study hard? I think most of people will have the first choice. People are passive. This is why I think appropriate punishments are good for students.
As the above saying, people are passive. When there is nothing to push or motivate them, they will be lazy. Take myself as an example, when I was a child, I always needed my mom to ask me to do homework, or I would just "forget" about it. And so did my brother.
The second reason is for teachers to control the whole class easily. When someone get punished, others will have a mirror and know what should they do. Through this, teachers can control students easily and create a good enviroment to study.
However, this doesn't mean that you have to punish students very hard. Too many punishments will cause oppsive effects. Only appropriate punishment is the best way to teach.

subject: HW1001
content:
Education is always the topic people concerned about. Still now, some experts are discussing whether we should use punishment or rewarding to motivate students. In my opinion: use both.
Use both, but use it appropriately. Anything in the world be too much or too little can do harm. If you just punish and punish, students may lose their passion about study. And if they just recite what on the books, how could they make good use of them? I am a student so I am very clear that it is impossible. On the other hand, only rewarding is not the best way, either. Every time, pupils might want things which are better than the previous time. Or, they may feel dreary at the same trick. Even, some don't care about the prize because they think they can buy it by themselves, if the prize is an object. So, use both can give students less pressure and be not that dull.
Education is important because not only you had experienced it, your children may have to, too. No wonder it is always the hot issue. Although the way your teacher treats you may be not that well, how you think about your future is more essential.

subject: HW1001
content:
The punishment in education become a hot problem from several years ago. The main reason is the decreasing of the children number, so the parents usually put more love to their children and always give them all the best they can. But the children not always think they should study hard that they could repay the giving of their parents in the future, and some of them become more grrogant and selfish than ever. So the teachers must use some methods to encourage their students to study and control their behavior.
Some teachers use punishment in physical or mental to motivate students, and some of them use rewarding. In my opinion, these two methods have their use in different situations, so I would say use them both. And which method should use more depends on students' behavior.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I think the Second method, rewarding students for learning, is more effective. As we know, no one likes to be punished. Punishment maybe can stop the students from doing bad things this time, but next time they will still do the same. However, when it comes to rewarding, it can be very diffrent. When I was in elementary school, our teacher gave us secret gifts if we got high grades on the exam. I still remembered clearly that everyone studied very hard to get good grades on the exam. After the exam, many people received the teacher's secret gifts. There were candies, books, pencils and so on. Everyon was very happy and decided to study hard for the next exam. Gift can be just a little thing but it can encourage students to study happily. To sum up, I think rewarding students is better than punishing them.

subject: HW1001
content:
For years, educators have different methods to educate students: one is use punishments to help to learn what's right from wrong; another is rewarding students for their good work in order to get better results. In this essay I will argue in favor of using punishments to educate students.
In my opinion, punishment can help students to know what is wrong when they made a mistake, moreover, prevent them from doing it again. Say when a student cheat in an exam and got punished by the teacher, this student will definitly think twice before cheating in an exam. On the other hand, rewarding makes it harder to educate a student. This method can be use only when a student has done an excellent work, but what happens when he made a mistake? It can only motivate a student to do a better work, but it will be hard for them to learn what's wrong.
I suppor punishment as a method to educate students, because it is more useful to help a student to learn well and to behave better.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, how to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior play an important role in the education. Not only diligent teachers and parents but hard-working students should pay attention to. As far as I am concerned, I support to take rewarding measures to encourage students to learn diverse subjects and even expolre themselves. According to some research, punishment would have the possibility to leave behind bad influence on students and even make them escape from learning. However, by the method of rewarding, students are happy and willing to learn and can get better grades on their academic performances.
Take me for an example, since I was a senior high school student, my parents always encourage me when I faced difficulty and depression on tests instead of punishing me. In addition, they always solved my problems by taking to me sincerely. Moreover, I was so fortunate that I had a good teacher who always rewarded students to study. Hence, I successfully acheived my goal to enter my ideal college. So I think rewarding students is the best way for education.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, the answer of "Which way is more effective, punishment or rewarding?" can't be devided into two option. I think both are effective if we use them simutaneously and properly.
In the past, teachers punished their students very often just wanted to shape their students into what they thought. Besides, a variety of punishment didn't make sense. Such as some teachers might ask students to get full points, and if you don't reach that, the teacher would hit you as more as the points you lose. In addition, still some other teachers like to punish student by making them copy the text for fifty times or even one hundred times. These punishments really make no sense!
Nowadays, more teachers are sensible. They wouldn't ask students to do "something imposible". Instead, the ask students to reach goal step by step. Eevy time they reach a small goal, teachers will reward and encouraging them to study harder. This seems great and effect, but still some students hehave inappropriately.
I think we should paralell with punishment and rewarding. Take my class for example. In ten grade, my teacher used the method "rewarding". But some classmates didn't satisfied with those rewarding and began to brake the class rule. Aften ten grade, my teacher decided to change her strategy. She claim that anyone who brake the class rule would be punished and anyone behave well still can get rewarded. After a period of time, my class really improved! To sum up, I think we really should paralell with punishment and rewarding!

subject: HW1001
content:
Children are blank paper when they are born and they learn right and wrong as they grow up. It is the teachers' responsibility to install the correct point of view into the children's mind. As the result, teachers use either punishment or reward to tell kids right from wrong. In my opinion, punishment and rewards are complemantry and neirther one is superior to the other. In other words, punishment and reward are used in different situation.
The spirit of setting punishment is to dissuade people from doing wrong things such as stealing. However, rewards are use to encourage people do some kind things which might make our world better such as reaching out to those who are in need. In conclusion, punishment are used to stop people from doing wrong things while rewards are used to encourage people to do right things. Therefore, both punishment and rewards are essential to form a person with judgement.

subject: HW1001
content:
How to let students study effectively has bothered teachers for a long time. Some people say that using punishment can motivate students to learn their behavior while the others believe that rewarding students at appropriate time can lead to better results. As to me, I prefer the second one.
Take me for example, I met those two kind of teachers before, and the effect of studying was very different. My first teacher was always harsh on everything on everything, such as attitude, study and so on. If I did something wrong, she would scold and punish me. At that time, whole class were so scared that we felt studying wasn't so fun. However, my second teacher was totally different to the first one. She always used the truest mind to get along with me. If I did something wrong, she wouldn't scold me angrily, but having a conversation to understand the reason. Also, she would praise me at the appropriate time.
I think most of students prefer the second kind of teacher. After all, what we need is the help from teachers not the punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
Teaching is a lesson which needs a lifetime to learn. For the improvement of students, some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and control their behavior; others reward students for learning to have better results. Which one is more effective?
For me, both methods are necessary to lead to better results. However, teachers should use these two ways properly. When students are in first grade, teachers need to set up rules for keeping students well-behaved. Once they break up these rules, they deserved punishment as a reminder of being careful of their wrong doing. In addition, as long as students are obedient to the rules, teachers reward and praise them immediately for keeping good deeds going. When students received teachers' approval, they are more eager to well behave.
My student Johny, who is a naughty boy, has been punished by me for littering paper on the ground. But one day, I saw him throw a paper into paper-recycled box, and I praised him right away. Since then, he has thrown gabage into correct trash cans. I am so proud of him. I know that punishment and reward are two important ways to shape students' behavior and mind.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. If teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior, students will live in fear. In this generation everything is competitive so people should not just work on paper writing. we should try to find out what we want to do during the years learning at school. If you have to worry about be punished all the time, you will lose yourself and follow the rules that may not fit you.
I think rewarding students is a better way. The students will learn and behavior well by themselves. When you are doing things what you want, every hard works you devote in won't be painful. For examples, my parents never told me what to do. Because of their support, I become more confident. I think the most important thing is be happy. Learning should bring us happiness. so I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
It is indisputable that "interesting learning" is the key for efficient learning. Therefore, instructors should stir up their students' interest in learning. By means of that, students can not only obtain the knowledge they need but also indulge themseves in learning.
Yet, some teachers neglect the fact and use punishment to motivate students to learn and control their behavior. Sitting through the classes without any fun, students definitely feel bored and have no desire in learning.
On the contrary, if the lectures are versatile and full of fun, students are willing to be involved in learning. Furthermore, after the class, if they feel the learning is interesting and rewarding, they will become more active in advanced studying.
As we can see many extinguished students devote their effective learning to "motivation" and "interest". Therefore, instructors should make their teaching more interesting and practical, which will help to stir up students' interest and motivation in learning and exploring the world. To sum up, "interesting learning" motivate students to learn, and the rewarding encourage them to expands their knowledge.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, the more effective way is to reward students. Because love and care are the two most important things in the world, no one can live without them. In fact, love and care are gifts from God. And, the more we choose to reward students, the better results we will see. Therefore, I will like to use them to correct students through thick and thin. Like a friend, rewarding students makes them feel confident, regarding them as indispensible ones, which is so supportive that they will forget the difficulties they encounter. No wonder, many students are obliged to their teachers for their kindness. Takes my friend, Tom, for example. He used to be a pessimistic guy. Because Tom was not as smart as other students in the class, he often fell a victim to some students' rudness. However, no sooner had he met his teacher, Mr. Lin than he changed since then. Rewarding Tom with care and love, Mr. Lin devoted himself to rebuilding his self-confidence. In consequence, Tom has become more optimistic, and more popular in my class. In a nutshell, rewarding students has so many advantages that we should cherish it forever.

subject: HW1001
content:
With the rights of the students have increased degree by degree, punishments are no longer the only manner to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Therefore, I prefer to reward the students rather than punishing them. First of all, punishments to students can cause injuries physically as well as trumas mentally. As we all known that injuries are easily to heal but trumas don't, they can last for many years even last for the whole lifespan. Moreover, student who was punished might gained hatred toward that specfic teacher. The last but not the least, punishments can cause barriers between teachers and students.
I had a classmate whose name is Jay. He was a very friendly person and always spared no efforts to do his assignments. Hard working though he was, his grades still was very low. One day, our math teacher was announcing the monthly exam score. When he announced to the Jay's score, he slammed Jay's cheeks and said something insulted words to him. He can't standed such a great humiliation and ran out of the classroom. From then on, I have not seen him in school and I have lost touch with him. This painful reminder always reminds me that punishments toward students is unfair and they should be abolished.

subject: HW1001
content:
Six years ago, I was a junior high student. At that time, I was afraid to go to school. I also could not sleep well if I had math class next day. My serious math teacher cared students' learning a lot, so she always tested us in the end of each class. Whenever someone did not achieve 90 points, she would hit them in the class, in the front of others students. I was one of the students often punished. I knew I was bad at math, so I spent more and more time on math. However, I still could not get her standard and was hit again and again. At last, I gave up.
In the senior high, I met a teacher. My grades were not high, though he kept encouraging me, helping me have interests in math again, and asking me that not to give up. He was also the first one who ensured my hard-working in math. Sometimes he praised about my improvement, which made me more confident. In my study experience, I learned to teach a student, teacher should not use punishment. Rewarding or encouraging students will be the better way in education.

subject: HW1001
content: People always talk about what's the better way to control students' behavior. Some say using punishment is important, while others prefer rewarding students. I think rewarding students would be a better idea. There are three reasons. First, students will do better after they are rewarded. For example, in our childhood, we got candies for good behaviors, and we would behave better to get more candies next time. However, if students are punished for their bad behaviors, they might be mentally hurt and stressed. Second, rewards can help students gain self-confidence. They feel happy when they're praised and would consider themselves important. On the other hand, punishment, especially physical ones, might effects the personalities of students, which leads to even more serious problems. Most importantly, other students can learn from the rewarded students. For example, many companies rewarded hard-working employees with more salary, which make others work hard to get the extra pay. Nevertheless, sometimes when students are punished, they would want to take revenge on the teacher, which, would cause even more problems. In conclusion, though some people think punishing students is significant, I think rewarding them would be a more effective idea.

subject: HW1001
content:
Does a teacher have the right to punish his students? Some people agree that moderate punishment will motivate students' studies and keep them from doing some improper things once again. However, others think that punishment will not correct one's behavior nor will it prevent students from doing such bad deeds once and for all. Instead, they consider rewards to be a much better choice. As for me, I think the latter teaching method is more effective. First of all, I do believe that most students will eager to receive some encouraging and praising words from their teacher when they do good deeds. Moreover, if a teacher always smile to his students rather than be serious all the time, his students will desire for learning more. In addition, teachers should generously praise their students even though they merely progress a little, in this way, students will definitely be uplifted and be more willing to study.
In my personal experience, my piano teacher is the kind of teacher who never blames on her students or punishes them. Whenever I make a mistake, she won't be furious about me; instead, she teaches me patiently until I can understand. Despite the fact that I failed my tests, she would say some encouraging words to me and give me concrete suggestions to improve my skills.
