Because of her, I could have confidence again and be brave to face my challenges. Had it not been for her, I might have given up myself and considered myself to be an useless person. As a result, I always tend to think that a considerate teacher will absolutely motivate one's learning attitude.

subject: HW1001
content:
While considering the ways to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior, there are two common ways that teachers will use: one is punishment and the other is reward. In my opinion, I believe the two methods are effective in some way to motivate students in learning. When teachers encounter a student who is afraid of punishment, a punishment may arouse the fear of the student and therefore he/she will try their best to avoid any possibilities of punishment. However, as a teacher, I believe that education should not be based on fear. If students' learning is built on their fear of punishment, their learning motivation is negative. One day, when the punishment is disappeared, they may stop their learning as well. Therefore, even punishment may be a convenient way for teachers to motivate students' learning; I would rather use encouragement and reward, to arouse students' motivation, I believe that it is a very possitive way for students' learning.
Most of the time, students' learning difficulties will frustrate teachers, so, sometimes, teachers will bring their emotion to their teaching. They may become impatient and moody and want to punish their students for stopping their improper behavior in a very short time. However, it is not a good way to improve the relationship between teachers and students. Hence, try to use praise and reward to increase students confidence. Everytime, when students do sometime great, teachers can give them praise or some little rewards. Then, students will become willing in learning because they have faith in themselves and believe that they are welcome in class. One day, even when they leave school, their learning process will not cease. They know that they learn for themselves, not for others or for the fear of punishment. The reasons above explain why I support rewarding is the best way to motivate student's learning.

subject: HW1001
content: I don't agree the punishment which the teachers motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. It doesn't make sense because the pushnishment can't make students realize why they're being punished but make them shameful, confused or even angry. To make me an example, I have been punished when I was ten just because of my poor grades in the math tests. If you asked the teacher the reason why he did that to me, you could hear him answered carelessly, "Because she didn't make efforts on the tests". Didn't I? I did math excercises every night, but in the test, I just failed because of being careless in answering the questions The most important thing I want to express is that to be a good teacher, you should try to realize what the students really need instead of punishing them in a non-sense way.

subject: HW1001
content: There are always two sides of view to every question. Some people may think the first method is more effective, others may think otherwise. As far as I am concerned, using punishment to motivate students to learn seems to be more effective. The reasons are as follows. To begin with, I think the power which comes from one afraid of being punished is a lot stronger than that from being rewarded. The more one is afraid of being punished, the better he or she can work on his or her studies. On the other hand, once the students are rewarded because of their making progress in their studies, their desire for better rewards will become stronger and stronger. Finally, teachers can no longer come up with a good way to control their students. In view of this, we can easily realize that using punishment is really more effective than rewarding students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Using punishment to motivate students to learn and rewarding students while learning have been put into a debate for a long time. Some strongly believe that punishing students is the most efficient way to prevent them from stopping learning. However, in my opinion, I considered rewarding students from learning can lead to better results.
First of all, punishment such as scolding or grounding can easily do harm to students' emotion or confident temporarily or permanently. Scolding students might make them consider themselves to be worthless and unvaluable, while grounding them will definitely destroy their enthusiasm and interests to almost everything, regardless of learning and playing.
Moreover, while suffering from punishment, by no means will the students come up with terrible ideas in order to avoid or escape from being punished. They may lie to teachers or parents or even try to escape to illegal organizations. That makes the problem even worse to deal with.
Rewarding students; however, can simplily motivate and inspire them to devote themselves to being rewarded. That causes rather positive influence on students. Furthermore, students might feel positive and optimistic toward everything including learning.
In conclusion, we can precisely draw a result that rewarding students from learning have better and more effective impacts on students than using punishment to force students to learn due to the factors that are mentioned above.

subject: HW1001
content:
Philosophers have long been debating on the essence of human nature. Some believe that human nature, in essence, is evil and lazy, so people must be controlled by punishment and disciplines. On the other hand, some consider human nature to be kind and full of potential, so people must be praised and encouraged.
Modern psychologists have done many experiments on animals, and they call it "conditioning" in training animals. Animals will respond to stimulus and learn new skills. But human are more complicated when it comes to learning. Bandura developed so-called "social learning theory" in describing human learning processes, and the theory is applied by management theorists.
There is an old saying goes like this, "Spare the rod, spoil the child." But I disagree with such a notion. If a student obey the rules just because of fear of punishment, then he or she might not keep behaving like this once entering a new environment. On the contrary, if a student is self-motivated, he or she will incorporate a certain traits into his or her own personality, which won't change easily overtime.
For example, we all know that there were two famous city-state in ancient Greece -- Athens and Sparta. People in Athens were encouraged to express their ideas, while people in Sparta were trained as woriors. History textbooks tell us Athens had very splendid achievement in many aspects, whereas Sparta had not so bountiful attainment. Even in today's world, artists from a liberal contry usually perform better than artists from a communist contry.
To sum up, as far as I am concerned, a good teacher should praise and encourage students instead of scorning and blaming them. Likewise, a manager should use positive methods to enhance workers' efficiency instead of using negative methods. You may well just spare the rod!

subject: HW1001
content:
There are different ways to motivate students to learn and behave themselves. Rewarding students for learning is better than punishing students. It is important for students to receive rewards from teachers so that they can get confidence. With a confident heart, learning becomes interesting and not difficult. On contrary, punishments can lead to negative results. If students get punishments every time they fail in test, they will be afraid of making mistakes and then lose the passion for learning.
Take my own experience for example. My English teacher always encouraged me when I failed in test, so I never gave up learning it. Whenever I made improvements, the teacher rewarded me, so I got a sense of fulfillment in learning English. To my surprise, I even found myself enjoying learning English. If the teacher had punished me at that time, I would have given up English right away. I was so lucky to gain rewards from the teacher that made my English ability improved so much.
To conclude, rewarding students for learning car surely lead to better results. It not only encourages students but also makes students enjoy learning. Therefore, the most effective way to motivate students is to reward them and encourage them.

subject: HW1001
content:
Physical punishment has been a controversial issue for a long time in Taiwan. While the tradition notion "punishments polish the children" backs up those who in favor of using violation to stimulate the children, I prefer to rewarding kids more. In school, most of the teachers would like to punish those who violate the rule because they believe the way can tackle the misbehavior efficiently. Nevertheless, from the prospective of mine, rewarding, in the long run, is the better way. Besides, when teachers are struck in how to boost students' interest in studying, some praise, few gifts, or packets of candies can work.
Take my experience for example. My teachers in elementary school tended to commend their students. Though a few troubles those naughty boys made was inevitable, most of the student are eager to behave well. What's more the average scores of our class were the top all the time. Almost every students in our class were fond of studying. Thus, in my opinion, without a doubt, rewarding is superior to punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
Since I was a little boy, no matter in elementary school or junior high school, most teachers in school have always used punishment to spur his or her students to study hard or to control their behavior. Although using punishment may sometimes be effective and cultivate students to do better, I think rewarding students can lead to better results. Unlike punishment may probably lower the students' tendency to study; rewarding can set a goal for students to achieve and by doing so, inspires their passions for learning. Besides, rewarding is able to be the bridge between the teachers and students, thus hardening their relationship.
Taking my own experience for example, when I was in my freshman year in junior high, one of my best friends, John, was always late for school. Therefore, everytime when John was late, our teacher punished him by hitting his hand. However, this method still couldn't avoid John getting up late because the more the teacher hit John, the more frequency of John's late. In order to solve this problem, our teacher came up with an idea. He told John that if he could come to school on time for lasting two weeks, he would rewarding him to enjoy a big meal. At first, all of our classmates thought that our teacher may fail up again, but to our surprise, John really went to school on time for not only two weeks but for everyday until we were graduated. This experience told me that if I could be a teacher, I would reward my students instead of punishing them.

subject: HW1001
content:
How to educate is a crucial issue people are always discussing. In Easten countries, physical punishment is ubiquitous and even has been done in morden cities. However, in Western world, love education is commonly implemented. As I am concered, I support the latter.
First, it provides motives for students to learning. In a study, with prizes waiting for winners, students studied harder and got higher scores than the counterpart. When I was a child, I also advented in this way. If my mother hadn't rewarded me when I did well, I wouldn't have learned so much. More importantly, students will not be frustrated so much when failing. Students build their confidence by being awarded but if they are not winners, they will reflect on themselves and reset a goal. Love education can cultivate optmistic and confident student.
On the contrary, some may say that only will punishment give students strong minds. However, I disagree with it. Punishment makes students lack confience and it hurts them a lot. My mother, for example, who suffered from physical punishment, said the bad memory spoiled her childhood. Teacher is the latest career she would choose.
To conclude, rewarding well-done students is a good way to push them. It will inspire their potential ability. As Randy Paush said, "The wall here is to show how you desire one thing," students deserve sweet apples after crossing a high wall. Education is a two-edged sword, so it's crucial for teachers and parents to choose the right way.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are lots of method for teachers to control students' behavior. Most of them punish students if the students don't behave well or do something wrong. Some reward students if they behave themselves. Still some use both punishment and rewarding. As I see it, the last one is the best method for several reasons.
The first reason is that some students are not good at studying no matter how hard they try. If a teacher use punishment, they might be discourage to study. On the contrary, if a teacher give them something attractive, such as secret presents or desserts, they may become more interested in studying.
Another reason is that rewarding is not desirable to some students. Some students need teachers to punish them. For instance, laborous punishment, such as cleaning toilet, is a proper and beneficial punishment for students. This kind of punishment not only makes students think of their fault, but can also clean up the classroom or school. After that, students who have this punishment might be exhausted so that they cannot do something bad.
To sum up, various students should use different methods to teach. Thus, I think both rewarding and punishment are practicable.

subject: HW1001
content:
It is indispensable that teachers use punishment to motivate and control students' learnig. But I prefer rewarding to punishing.
My opinion is, if you always punish students, they might lose their interest in the subject. Just take my brother for example. His Math teacher always gives him lots of homework as a punishment for getting poor grade. So my brother hate math. And he doesn't want to deal with it, because he is scared of his teacher. However, different from his Math teacher, his English teacher usually rewards him by writting some inspiring words on his workbooks or giving him some stamps, Thanks to the English teacher, my brother learns English happily and it is his favorite subject.
Teacher, is one who broadens our horizons and enrichs our knowledges. Every teacher might has different way in teaching. No matter punishing or rewarding, I think the most important thing is to lead to a better result than before.

subject: HW1001
content: Nowadays there are many people arguing about the issue of whether to punish students or to respect their rights. There are even laws that forbid teachers to lecsture and beat students because students have human rights and the rights to stop others from doing harm to them, even it's for education and is good for them. So they argue about whether punishing students or rewarding students would be better. But I think it depends on what kind of person the student is. Some students can behave themselves and study aggressively without the teachers asking them to do so, but some students never want to study and always fool around whenever they get a chance, they wouldn't want to meet any of the teachers expectations if the teachers don't punish them or act strickly. So I think there wouldn't be an absolute answer of which is more effective. When I was in junior high school, I had a classmate who hates punishments. She has an extreme personality and she always did things if she wanted to, no one could force her to do anything, if she felt like studying, she would did really great on an exam, but if a teacher asked her to get good grades, she would fail the exam puposely because she didn't want to do what she didn't felt like doing. So it's better to reward her than to punish her. However, My another junior high school Classmate is totally different. He always slept during classes and never handed out his homeworks on time, he never studies because his parents never forced him to do so. But when the teacher started to punish him whenever he's late to school or kept forcing him to study, he turned out to be more aggressive on everything in case the teacher punishes him, so he's the one that needs punishment instead of rewardness. The two examples can prove that it depends on the students' personality than for just an absolute answer.

subject: HW1001
content:
Which method is better? Rewarding or punishing students? In my opinion, I think the later is better and more effective. Rewarding, which means treating excellent students with some good things, is used to aspire students to improve their behavior and studies. But what about the others who don't care about the honer of being a good student? Rewarding seems to be meaningless to them, and they just do anything which can make them happy but sometimes hurt other people as if there're no decipline and rules to limit them. In this way, students who are behave well would be affected by those who put entertainment first, and the whole class may be a messy environment for studying and learning. Is it good? Absolutely not!
For example, students should arrive school on time, but for the procrastinators who are forced to go to school, they think it isn't a matter to attend classroom after the bell rings, even if it's an hour late already! To solve this problem, the means of punishing students emerge. For those who always late for school, I think to punish them with some labor or copying down the texts on the book and etc. , are all good methods to motirate students to learn from doing these things and to control and improve their behavior. By means of giving these punishments, students may become behaving well and twice thinking before they do anything. I think it's good to improve the whole learing environment.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the past, students who behaved poorly might be scolded or even be hit by their teachers or parents. They thought that being strict and stern helped them to improve their attitude. But in my opinion, punishing is not the only way to this goal, students also need some rewards to arise their self-confidence.
Punishments may be a fast way to make students control their behaviors, but sometimes they hurt their self-esteems. By giving them proper rewards and praises which they really long for, I think it is the way that leads them to the positive thoughts.
Furthermore, there were lots of tests show that students who were rewarded had better accomplishments than those who weren't. by puting them into a same room, scolding the half and praising the rests, the latter ones seemed to have more cofidence in themselves, and were more willing to finish their work.
Eventhough there still are people who believe that it's necessarry to be strict to the students, it is love and encouragements that make them behave positively. In this way, students may have easier routes to their success, and they may also do this to their own students and children.

subject: HW1001
content:
Personally I think both the punishment and rewarding system are a mechanism that is helpful in the process of students' learning. Each of them will only serve its best if the other one is carried out properly to balance with each other. None of the ways would be effective, if any of them is one-sided emphasied.
For like a day is made up by day and night, the mechanism of punishing and rewarding system works in this way. The punishment alerts the students of the things or behavior they need to be aware of, or rules that should be followed. Under this suitable confinement, the order and displines is cared for, and becomes an ad in the learning process.
After the basic and organized learning situation is created, the rewards system will work its way to promote students learning enthusiasm and interest. People's motivation to become better is being much encouraged through the rewards that are promised.
A classroom example is -- if children are only being given rewards, the atomosphere and emotions could get too excited and therefore influence the going-on curriculum or activities. With the assistance of punishments, students tend to act in a modest way that can go along with their interest of learing and determination to achieve certain goals. In this way, students learn better without losing the balance from missing any aspects from these two pole.
Therefore, I would say, the punishment and rewarding system are good friends hand-in-hand in students' learning process.

subject: HW1001
content:
Imagine this picture: students in the class are talking to each other, and the teacher asks them to be quiet. However, no one listens to the teacher, and the class becomes noisy. Therefore, I totally agree that teachers should use some punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior.
To begin with, class rules are like the law of our society, and students should obey these rules to make the class better. For example, my friend, John, who always talks in class. Some teacher would punish him, so that he would become quiet in their class. Other teachers would not punish him; thus, he talks more in class.
In addition, there are a variety of punishment that teacher can use in class to motivate students to learn. Take me for instance. I'm always lazy to memorize English vocabulary, so my English teacher would make me write Some vocabulary when I got poor grade. As a result, my English is getting better and better. In sum, from I mentioned above, I believe that teachers should use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior.

subject: HW1001
content:
Using punishment to motivate students to learn and control their behavior is more effective. In my opinion, most of the people have to be forced to do something by means of punishment. Although it isn't a good way to educate students, it usually puts into effect in the schools. Lazyness is the inherent character. Parents usually want to lead a comfortable and pleasant life, let alone the students. But the punishment is just a method to force the students to focus on their lessons. They will get used to the atmosphere and then study automatically and behave themselves.
When I was eight years old, I didn't like going to school at all. At that time, my father always scolded at me with a rod. I was afraid of being beaten by my father. So I reluctantly went to school every day. Gradually, I didn't hate going to school. I was thinking that my father's rod was the most influential thing in my life. It is a good example to support my opinion.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers prefer punishing students while some don't. As a student, I think it is better for teachers to reward students for their well behavior or hardwork. First of all, rewarding students can make them have a desire do better on the next time while punishment can only make students angry and even give up learning. Serious punishments can even harm the students not only physically but also mentally. Moreover, it is believed that giving rewards to students can also make others who aren't behave very well have a desire to get the reward. As a result, the whole class will be more hard-working than before.
Taking myself for an example, when I was in junior high school, I was addicted to playing computer games. Therefore, my grades were poor and I was not really concentrated on my homework. But one day, our teacher decided to give gift to the most hard-working person in class. And the gifts were one of the things that I wanted to get. In order to get the gift, I studied and studied every day and sometime even studied until twelve o'clock in the midnight. As a result, my grades were gradually going to the top of the whole class. After the exam, my teacher rewarded me the gift for my hard work. I feel very pround and thankful of getting the reward. In conclusion, I think rewarding students for learning is better them to punish them.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the recent years, so called "love education" is more and more popular in teachers and parents. However, there are also more and more teachers have conflict opnion with parent on education, because the teachers don't believe rewarding students for better result.
In my opinion, using punishment to motivate students is a better way. When using reward to motivate student, some student may think rewards are no big deal any more. And some student may think unfair when you gifted something to a student no matter how well the student does, which will lead to some troubles.
On the other side, when using punishment to motive students. I don't think there are anyone who like to be shamed or beat. In order to avoid it, student will doing well in afraid of punishment.
When I was a kid, I didn't like to study anymore. But my parents and teacher forced me to do that, And now. I go to the better university have a better future than the other young man. I am appreciate to what they do for me.
In all, I think punishment is a better way for education. Just like the old chinese folk said if you don't blame or beat your child, they may not be a good man, and the "love education" will bring some child being protect too much can't stand for the stress of life.

subject: HW1001
content: There are all sorts of students in the world. From my perspective, I think rewarding is for those who are not so obedient to the teacher. If we keep punishing them, in their hearts, they will gradually regard it as a normal thing. Moreover, they will not reflect themselves for what they have done. In addition, they probably hate the teacher and behave inproperly. On the other hand, in my opinion, I think slightly scolding is for those who are obedient to the teacher. Take me for example, if I do something wrong, I will hope someone to scold me but it should be "slightly". Parents or teachers may think they are good students so scolding is not proper for them. However, good students still need to be taught, if there is no slightly scolding, they will not find the correct direction in life. In conclusion, I think every student has its own personality, teachers should take it into consideration and find the best way to teach them.

subject: HW1001
content:
From the best of my knowledge, I deem that rewarding students for learning tends to be more effective than using punishment to spur students to learn and to control their behavior. There is one major reason why I think so as follows.
With no doubt, everyone wants to be either praised or given prizes for his or her good performance. Therefore, if teachers set awards for those who make progress and fulfill their goals in learning, these awards will make it possible that students will spare no effort to learn as well as possible. However, if teachers motivate students to learn, students may think learning is terrible but never find that learning can bring endless joy.
If I were a teacher in an elementary school, I would reward students who make a great advance or get good grades on the exams by giving them special gifts. These special gifts are from snacks to an iPod. I think, in this way, students will develop a good habit of learning. Little by little, they will show much more interest in learning and find that learning can not only obtain a great deal of valuable knowledge but also have a sense of achievement and pleasure when they acquire the gifts.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Every student is an individual and he or she will be upset when receiving punishment. Also, students will lose their motivation and patience on learning. It is very important to hold the interests when students learn new things; however, punishment will make students lose their interests in learning, and won't really control their behavior.
When I was a junior high student, I always got bad grades in my math tests, and I lost the confidence in learning math. Moreover I was afraid of going to school. My parents encourage me a lot instead of punishing me. Everytime I had little progress, they rewarded me. In the long run, I found the interests in learning math again. Thanks to my parents, I finally became a college student in Math Department.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I think rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. There's no one who likes to be punished. Students neither. Their grade might improve by punishing them. But students might gripe behind your back and they don't really want to study hard. They are just afraid of the punishment. Once you don't punish them, their grade will drop. In contrast, you can courage students by giving them reward. Giving students reward can lead students to the right way of learning. While the students studying, they are really want to, but not afraid of being punished. And they might find the fun of learning things. My senior high teacher never punish us, and she always gave a small gift to the person whose grade improved most compared to the last time. Our class' average grade improve time after time. It is a good example that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results than by punishing them.

subject: HW1001
content:
Every teacher wants their students to be the best. I believe that rewarding students for learning new knowledge can lead to better results because rewarding students can make students not only get happiness but also earn more confindence. When students feel confident and happy, they will learn better and quicker.
Sometimes, a little punishment is en easy and quick way to make students to be taught which kind of behavior is prohibited or isn't prohibits. But punishment isn't suitable for every kinds of students such as shy students and students who have been punished all the time at home. When teachers try to punish students, they have to know clearly which kind of students they have.
One of my experience is a good example. I always give students some stamps or stickers when they do a good job or good behavior. They always want to get a good gift from me, so they have to be good and study hard to get a good grade. When they have more than ten stamps or stickers, I will get them a present to choose. When they get the gift, they are very satisfied about their good grade and my cute gift. And I think that teachers should think about how to make students learn in a happy way because they are kids and they are not robots.

subject: HW1001
content:
Recently, the teaching ways teachers enact have changed extremely. With conservative notions in the past, many teachers would exploit some methods violating the humanitarian to motivate students to learn and control their behavior. However, as the perspective changes, many teachers convert their idea and adopt positive ways to civilize their students.
In my opinion, I prefer to positive ways rather than negative ways to stimulate students to study. Students would perform better because they receive positive treatments. They'll become more confident of their teachers, schools, and their studies. In this way, they are capable of breaking down their barrier they meet in their studies. For instance, if a student behave well and meet your requirements or expectation, you would give them a big applause or some practical encouragements, such as money or candies. After receiving your rewards, they'll feel that it is worth executing the same thing next time. Little by little, not only do they have more confidence in their learning or studies, but they also overcome the difficulties by your stimulus and assistance. In addition to providing practical substances, you are also able to provide some advantages. You can tell them that studying hard in the school enables you to apply for more favorable jobs in the future. With this advantageous incentive, they will have more positive attitude toward their behaviors or learnings. Because they realize these significant and imperative factors would help them in the future society containing innumerable competitors, they would devote themselves to working on their studies much harder. With their strong eagerness and motivation, they would become much more hopeful in their studies.
Last but not least, compared with the negative teaching ways, positive teaching ways are bound to be more efficient, effective, and useful than them. Although mere teachers insist that exerting punishments would enable students to motivate their potential, I believe that the punishments would lead students to disadvantageous circumstances in the last. After all, many teachers and students are fond of good, useful, and encouraging ways, aren't they?

subject: HW1001
content:
Some people think that using punishment to motivate student to learn and to control their behavior is necessary. However, others think that giving a praise to childrens is more effective.
In my opinion, I prefer the later to the former. There are some reasons why praising is on top of a punishment. First of all, a courage or a satisfiction smile can alway encourage a person to keep doing the good deeds. As a courage is to the mind, so food is to the body. Besides, a punishment may well make a student depress and make things worse. I vividly remembered such kind of circumstances happened to me when I was in the first year of the junior high. I was so shy to introduce myself at the stage. Yet, my homeroom teacher demanded me speak or she would make me clean the whole classroom. However, things go worse, I couldn't even talk to my classmate at the end of the semester. It is the experience that me realize how a punishment can make me a heartfainted. Last but not the least, when a teacher tries to praise a student, both of them can get into a good mood, while when the teacher starts punishing a student they may both get into a anger atmosphere and other students in class will be a fraid of the teachers, too.
As the purpose of punishment is to make student well behave and improve their attitude. Why not give a courage and tell them your expectation more smoothly to let them know the way they can pursue. That may be much more effective.
In conclusion, not only getting rid of punishment is important for teachers, but being self-controled and performing good deeds is also necessary for the students. As long as we all do the best to make ourselves good, the relationship between students and teachers will get better.

subject: HW1001
content:
Studying and having good behavior are essential in today's world. The paramount reason is that they are the cornerstones to make it possible for people to live well. However, if not for learning, all the people wouldn't be equipped with these abilities. Therefore, it's necessary for teachers to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior.
There are two main methods to use. One is punishment, and the other is rewarding students for leaning. From my perspective, the second method is better. This is because everyone likes to be praised. Besides, if they know that they'll be given gifts as long as they learn well, the strong motivation, along with happiness, will come out in their minds. If they learn new things just because they are afraid of punishment, they will have bad emotions while studying and think that they just study for their teachers rather than themselves. What's worse, after graduating from school, they'll think that they are out of teachers' control and gradually go bad because they don't know how to treat others with love and kindness instead of punishment.
One of my teachers in my elementary school likes to use punishment very much. I vividly remember that even if I could do well on the tests, I hated studying and going to school. Because I couldn't find pleasure from them and I didn't know why I had to study. During that time, I lived a miserable and unhappy life. But after entering high school, I found the hope of life again just because I used some different ways to deal with all the things in the world. Thanks to the optimistic way of teaching the teacher in high school gave me!

subject: HW1001
content:
A hot topic for debate is whether teachers should punish students or not. Some teachers use punishment to motivate students, while others believe rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. From my point of view, I approve of rewarding students.
Chief among the reasons is that everyone likes to be praised or get presents by others. Take myself for example, when I was a little girl, I always felt upset about learning how to write correct Chinese words. My teacher taught me without blaming. After I finished practicing, she would give me a lovely pen as a gift. I recall this good memory and do the same thing to my students. I think that's why I become a teacher and teach students well.
Another reason is that physical punishment can be harmful to students' bodies. If the teacher didn't hurt him or her intentionally, but the student still felt painful and told his or her parents, the teacher would get into a big trould no matter the efforts he has done before. My best co-worker has one terrible experience. It happened during recess, two boys were fighting when the teacher went to the bathroom. She did nothing but knocked on their heads. Parents came to the cram school and asked for payments. It was a tragedy.
Of course, there's an argument to be made for the opposing position. However, the reasons I have provided are much stronger and in favor of my opinion.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I support that teachers should encourage students to learn by rewarding them except punishing them. Take me for example, I was taught by a strict math teacher when I was in junior high school. His teaching guideline is to set the standard of each student, if any student did not achieve the goal he set, then the student will be punished. In this way, each student will spend more time on studying math because they are afraid of being punished. However, I think this teaching method is not perfect at all; because students will lose the passion of learning soon. I still remember that I was afraid of math classes at that time and I totally lost the ambiton of learning math. On the contrary, the other teacher of mine is good at praising every student in her class. I was not good at English when I was a senior high school student, but she told me that the level of my English is not that bad and encouraged me to spend more time on listening English. Gradually, my English ability became better because of her patience. To sum up, each teacher has their own teaching style, but I maintain that teachers shouldn't make students lose their confidence and motivation of learning. Therefore, I think teachers might take the strategy of rewarding students and abandon the way of punishing students.

subject: HW1001
content:
When I was in the senior high school, my grade was poor. Unfortunately, my teacher was serious, so, as you can guess, I was punished everytime after the damn test. Because of his punishment, I felt sick of him, and hate to study. I knew that he wanted me to be good, but he used the absolutely wrong way.
Teachers usually think that punishment can motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. However, a student like me never think it's right. All we need is reward and respect. When students do good in the class, teachers should reward them. Therefore, students will have more confidence facing their challenges. If teachers just know how to punish students, students will hate you and not willing to learn any more because teachers hurt their heart. So I think reward is a better way to treat students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Without a doubt, I agree with the second one -- rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Why? In this society, on TV news, newspapers and so forth, we see lots of teenagers go astray, most of which fight, steal or take drugs. According to renowned experts, ten out of nine these people's anti-society behaviors are caused by their school experiences.
Human beings grow up with education, the way the grown-ups educate kids has a enormous impact on these children's mentality. Sometimes teachers entertain punishment, which is somewhat negative, may hurt the students and keep their minds in a bad situation. Potentially, they would become bulky in the future. However, if these teachers choose to teach, or specifically, "correct" students with compliment and encouragement, there's no denying that they would be turned into more excellent learner on their path of being educated. Such people as my sister, she used to be hate going to school when she was in elementary school. Strikingly, her teacher always scolded her at shool and treated the class cynically. But when my sister got into junior high school, her attitude toward learning changed. Instead of disliking to go to school, my sister even went to school on Saturdays. That was because her teacher was always encouraging and friendly. After my sister's junior high life, she got into the best high school in the area we live. It's a great result, isn't it?

subject: HW1001
content:
In the news reports every day, we can find that several child abusements happen at schools or cram schools. On the contrary, I have met some teachers reward their students instead of punishing them. Punish or reward? Which one is better?
As for me, I am a student, and of course I prefer rewarding rather than punishing. None of us would like to be punished under the banner of motivating students or on the spur of teacher's moment. However, there were still some punishment happened which resulted in students' taking offense at school. Though some teachers use punishment to control students' behavior, my home-room teacher does not. She always owns a positive attitude and encourage us by rewarding us with delicious foods and drinks. What's more, she never makes a fuss at our wrong behaviors. For the sake of her encourging and rewards, we all make efforts to study hard.
Punish or reward? I think the conclusion is obvious, that is, rewarding students can contribute to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
As far as I am concerned, whether teachers should use punishment to let their students learn well or behavior well is a very crucial issue nowadays. I hold that teachers should not punish their students; instead, they can come up with other better methods to treat their pupils. My idea can be described as follow.
For one thing, I don't agree that teachers use punishment to their students because students may not like their teachers, and afterwards, they won't listen to their teachers' lecture any more in that they think their instructors hate them. Take one of my cousins as a telling example. She liked to play with her classmates in class, and her teachers scolded and punished her all the time. However, she didn't improve her behavior; instead, she always skipped all her classes almost every day. From the example, we can learn that punishment is a toxic thing for students.
For the other, I'm of the opinion that teachers should teach their students patiently when they can't learn well or when they don't show a good behavior. Then, if students really improve their problems or make a little progress, teachers should praise them. I think that few people dislike praise, so when students receive praise from their teachers, they will feel very hilarious and happy. Gradually, they will like to do right things, and they will also like to listen to what their teachers instruct in class. In short, praising students can lead to a number of good advantages.
All in all, when teachers want to punish or reproach their cute students, in my opinion, they should think twice, since I hold that punishment isn't good for their students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, some teacher still use punishment in order to let students learn a lesson and change their behavior. However, other teachers rather choose to reward students if they have done lots of improvement in learning. In my opinion, I think that rewarding students is more effective. Here are my reasons and examples.
Take myself as an example. When I was in junior high school, our Grade one English teacher was very strict to our classmates. He usually punished students that didn't behave and those who didn't have good grades. Then, our classmates started to hate having his English class and our grades became worse and worse because we didn't want to listen to his classes. One year later, we changed another English teacher and his English class was very interesting. He also usually rewards the students that improved a lot in behaviors or grades. He often gave us discount cards of bookstores in order to let us read more outside reading in a cheaper price. In the end, we became the first in English in all Grade two classes and we all thanked him a lot.
This is the reason why I think rewarding leads to better results. Students can be motivated and try to work hard to change their behaviors or grades. In this way, students learn things by themselves which can give them more interests to learn them. In addition, students can have a better friendship with classmates and teachers.
Although using punishment may also have the same effects to students because they will remember that they should behave, but I think that in this way, students will have a bad mood when having his class. In conclusion, I think that rewarding students can both let them have good grades and also have a good friendship.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. This method is more effective than the other.
Students are more willing to learn if they really want to learn somethings. Many research reports show that students are end up a bad grade or performance in a long term if they were forced to learn or study by punishment and controlling.
Students' behavior are better when they are in a pleasing environment. When students get prize or compliment from teachers or their parents, they are encouraged to study harder and try to make other people proud of them.
Everyone like to be respected and treasured. No one likes to be teased or blamed. It will make one lose confidence and dislike oneself. Only when students feel confident and are willing to improve themselves, then their grade can become better and better. So, as far as I am concerned, the method of rewarding students for learning is more effective.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are more teachers in Taiwan that prefer using punishment than rewarding to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. But, for myself, I think that rewarding would be much better when teaching children.
The education now in Taiwan seems to become that grade and scores are everything. If the students do not pass or reach the standards of the teachers, they may get punishment like doing more works than others. But this kind of rule, I think, is a negative way to motivate students. Students won't study much harder as they are not afraid of the punishment. Some students may even think that taking punishment is the way to get rid of those textures and scores. The better way to motivate them would be rewarding. The way of rewarding students is important, too. The right way may encourage them to study and work harder. Getting a good grade or having a good behavior, the students can be rewarded what they want. One good example of this point of view could be my own little brother. He used to be punished not watching TV and not going outside with his friends because of his terrible behaviors. At that time, my brother still went out with his friends without telling my parents. He was so bad that he even did not attending the class. When my mom and the teacher talked and choosed to change the way from "rule" to "rewarding", my brother became more polite and good in his behavior. It would be really hard to believe that my brother used to be a bad guy.

subject: HW1001
content:
There is no doubt that every student was once motivated by his/her teachers via two methods; one is punishment, and the other is reward. However, there is no one can tell which is the more effective one. The issue is still on debate.
In my opinion, punishment certainly works. Nevertheless, it may do damage to students' bodies as well as their minds sometimes. The reason that several don't like to go to school is physical punishment, leading to their poor academic performances.
Reward, on the other hand, is more effective. Once students know that they will get reward if the behave well, they will strive to earn the prize. Take me for example. My history was not good, especially when facing our managers' tests. One day, he said that he would give one thousand dollars to those who could get eighty on his test. I buried myself into textbooks in order to get the money. Finally, my hard work got repay. Since then, I still couldn't deny that this method is better than punishment.
Everything has its advantage and disadvantage. Whether the two methods work, it all depend on the person who use them.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior commonly in the past. However, today some people view it as a fault, they consider it better rewarding students instead of punishing them.
In my opinion, I think of the first method as an more effective one. In today's Taiwan social, the ethic inside people's heart is decreasing, even the students are growing strange thought due to the outside changeable environment. Only rewarding them may not receive positive effect, but induce them think it's ok not to study. Punishing them can not only give them pressure, but also make them active to learn. In addition, this can help teachers manage their students' behavior and discline more easily. It's important to cultivate a good habit of not doing bad things at an early age.
Take a real occasion for example. My junior high school teacher, Mrs. Fu, tends to punishing her students if they do something wrong or study with a lazy attitude. Though it was tough under her management, the effect was fantastic. Most of my classmates attained a high score in the high school entrance exam then attend TCFSH or TCGS, and I was no except. We also have a great attitude toward ethic.

subject: HW1001
content: I think that rewarding the students is a more effective way in education rather than punishing them. Rewarding students when they do a good job on something not only establish themselves in a higher spiritual status, but also is a spirit-lifter that can help them more forward without any difficulties. Despite just rewarding them all the time, I think it is also a necessity to give them some punishments in special occasions. Because once they are indulging in the rewards that come after the accomplishments, they might forget what's their goals for life and thus lost themselves in the darkness. Therefore, punishments is required when these misfortunes truly happen, and all of us should take measures to bring the one back to the real world. For examples, my brother, John, was a successful businessman who gain an abundance of wealth and fame when he was young. And all of these magnificent fortunes didn't come at a glimpse. He earned it by his bared hands and determination. Afterwards, he got what he should receive and take the lead in our family. However, he became proud of his great fortune and lost his way in the reality. He started abusing drogs and wines, which lead to his failures and bank-ruptcy. It was really sad that me and my family didn't notice how strange and rediculous his behaviros was then. And we missed the chance to punish him and warn him of the consequences that might come after his injustice. This experience give me a deep lesson that none of us are perfect, and thus no one can be rewarded all the time or punished in his entire life.

subject: HW1001
content:
As far as I am concerned, rewarding students for learning can definitely be more effective. On one hand, encouragement given by teachers and parents can heighten students' interest in studying. On the other hand, punishment often brings about pressure; students will instead act poorly when they are under tremendous stress.
Take myself as an example. I had learned painting for five years. My first art teacher was very strict. I felt like staying at home whenever it was time for me to go to the art classroom. She would scold at me if I used the wrong tint, and she even asked me to stay at the classroom and practice it until ten o'clock at night. I felt extremely tense, it seemed like all the punishment had killed my inspiration. I couldn't draw any satisfactory pictures. Under massive pressure, I thought that I was going to be smothered.
However, she resigned no long after. My art teacher became a gracious senior woman. She never blamed me. She told me that the meaning of painting was the craving for the display of our own creavity. Without taking any pressure, I started to find the hidden beauty in my every stroke, and how fantastic it could be to exhibit my talent without punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
Since encouraged-education has been used in Taiwan for a long time and evoluated more and more people who cannot be survive under a high pressure caree enviroment, it is time for us to rethinking the way we educate our next generations.
Offering benefits for people doing the right things is the basic idea of building up positive personalities. However, if the motivation is removed, people seem have no reasons to stop themselves from doing something wrong. In my opinion, to limit someone's behavior by punishment can not only help oneself learn the border-line of what they can do, but shape their characters into one which can suit to the society in which there is no one to give you prizes.
I am the best example to explain why I support the punishment should be used in our education. When I was young, I was not eager to getting any reward from teachers. I don't need them. Nevertheless, I followed teachers' rules because I needed a peaceful life which was without punishment.
Although someone doesn't agree with the effection of punishment by physical and pcysical reasons, to tell children there would be something bad happened if they make mistakes on purpose, punishment is one of the best choices.

subject: HW1001
content:
In past times, teachers in school used to use physical punishment to manage their students. I was also one of the victims. Personally, I am not in favor of this kind of method to educate children.
In my opinion, punishment hurt students' feeling very much. Some of them propably get depressed after being punished. They might therefore lose their self-confidence or interest in that respect. As previously mentioned, if a child has lost his zeal on learning, we hardly can educate him to achieve our educational goal. Take my experience for example, when I was a young student, I always tried my best to behavior myself as the adolt wanted. However sometimes I still should be punished because of neglecting or not understanding. It really made me flustrated. Moreover, the bad feeling still remains now.
I would like to call upon all of teachers to pay attention to this issue. The importance of education for a society will never be overemphasized. In the long term, it is the most important thing for every country, even for the whole world.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the past, teachers used to punish students a lot, while it is forbidden to conduct physical punishment nowadays. From my perspective, I think the recent change benefits teachers as well as students because of several following reasons.
First of all, I regard the obedience students show under the strict law is fake. What they respect is not teachers' dignity, but the harsh regulations. This phenomenon can be observed from my junior high school. My school conducted heavy punishments. As I saw then, teachers were all nasty. As soon as my teacher left, our class would be in chaos. However, we pretended good students in front of teachers. Therefore, I oppose punish students.
I believe if a teacher wants to manage a class thoroughly, what they need instead is the respective from students. Teachers should always praise those students who behave well so that others would be influenced by good students. All of them may follow suit and are willing to be rewarded. By doing so, both teachers and students gain dignity and they will get along together, too.
In conclusion, I am quite convinced that we should stop punishing students immediately. Neither teachers nor students will gain any benefits. What students need is being respected. Rewarding students can really lead to better results. It is the most effective method. We should implement it as soon as possible.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think rewarding students for learning can be more effective. The reason why I choose this idea is because if you punish someone maybe you can't get what you want.
Some students accept this program whereas others don't. Sometimes, punishment will just get the things worse. They might refuse to study or finish their homework. On the other hand, if you conduct the program of rewarding, it will motivate students to study hard in order to get some notice from their parents or teachers.
When I was in elementary school, my dad had told me, if I could get number one in my class, he would buy me a notebook. With such a reward, I studied hard. After the test, I was number one. That night, my dad bought me a notebook. I was happy. So was he. So, I think it is a good way to commit our effort no matter on education or on work. It will encourage us to try our best. Even though students did not do well on study or test, we still need to pay attention to how they feel, not just blame on them. Whether you agree or not, I think love is the most important key to motivate students to learn.

subject: HW1001
content:
In these days, people pay more attention on children's education. Parents not only notice their children's grades in school, but also notice the way of teachers' teaching.
In the school, some teachers use punishment to motivate students to study and to control their daily behavior. However, others believe that rewarding students for studying can encourage them to do things better. In my opinion, I agree that teachers should reward students instead of punishing students. For example, my high school teacher was a very strict person. He made lots of rules to control our behavior. In those days, I felt like I was a solider because I couldn't make any mistake or I would be punished. The memory of my high school life was miserable. I also remembered that my teacher wanted us to win every competition in the school or he would punish us. To my friends, the school competitions were games. However, those competition were tests to us. Therefore, I didn't have any happy memory in my high school life and I also felt a lot of pressure during those days.
Because of my experience, I believe that punishment is not a good way to motivate sudents to learn. In other words, it may give them a lot of pressure and refuse to learn. That's why I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
During the past, teacher used the punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. In the meanwhile, the parents were saying "thank you" to the teacher. Because, they thought it's a good way to teach the children. But now it changes. They will no longer think it's good for their children. Maybe, it's just because they only have one child and they want to treat their child as a treasure. They don't want their child to be punished.
Therefore, due to the change of parent's mind, you can see many news about this issue on television So, is the punishment good for children or not? In my opinion, it worths to use when children have bad behavior. I think there is no teacher want to use it to hurt their student. They just want to tell them which behavior is correct and which is incorrect. For example, when students cheat on the exam or steal other student's object. If they don't get the punishment, they will never know their behavior isn't correct. I think the teacher has the duty to teach student.
In the end, I will say that apropriate punishment is good for student. It really can let students know what they are doing.

subject: HW1001
content: As far as I know, physical punishment has aroused much attention of the public. So it is difficult for teachers to motivate students. Most people think rewarding is the best method, however, I think otherwise. I regard punishment as the best way to inspire students. If a teacher often rewards students, it may let students just want to get the prizes and forget it is their duties to learn and to control their behavior. On the other hand, if a teacher can use adequate punishments, students will know that it is wrong and the lessons will engrave their mind. Looking back on my past, I cheated in class when I was ten. Knowing this, my teacher used a ruler to hit my hands. Although it was painful and let me cry loudly, this experience indeed craved in my memory. Now, the lesson still reminds me. In view of this, only does a teacher punish students, they dare not do it again.

subject: HW1001
content:
In western countries, teachers prefer giving rewardings than punishment. On the contrary, teachers in eastern countries are more willing to moltivate the students by punishment. My view is that using punishments is more effective and more powerful than rewarding the students.
According to my opinion, there are three instances. First, it is a good remedy to the students who are not willing to study due to their laziness. People push themselves when they know the consequences if they don't study. Second, many students may gradually take the rewardings for granted. They start to become lazy, because the teacher doesn't give them any warnings. The final reasons is that students remind themselves whem teachers give them punishments. They start to think where they are wrong and give improvement.
To sum up, the punishments are not the sollutions to everything. The best way to solve the problems always depends on yourself.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students for learning is more effective than punishing them. There are several reasons. First, I think punishing or blaming on students may make them lose their confident. I still remember my best friend in my childhood. She used to be blamed on doing everythings. Now, she lose all her confident and is even unable to believe in herself.
Second, I consider that students will feel warm and happy if teachers encourage them. I am a good example. As far as I am concerned, I will feel appreciate and work hard if teachers praise of me. My grade wasn't very well until I met my junior high school's teacher. He always encouraged me and solved the questions I asked patiently. He inspired me studying harder and harder. Therefore, my grade has become much better from then on.
Besides, none will like to be blamed. Based on the above reasons, I suggest teachers rewarding their students instead of punishing them. I think that will make students more happy and willing to learn.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students for learning is more effective. Students like me prefer to be rewarded if we have a good grade, and also hope that teachers can be nice or friendly if we sometimes cannot control our behavior or have good grades. Including teachers, everyone may make mistakes. If someone don't try to give one chance to let us turn over into a new leaf, no one is willing to improve himself and being a good child. As a teacher, you should use all your ability to applause students. Although I agree sometimes teachers can use some punishment to correct students, the punishment is just a little, not the main way to teach students.
For example, if one student was crashed down by other students when they play basketball together, what would you do?
Can you punish the student who hurt someone?
If you asked me, I would like to answer you "No!". She was not willing to hurt other student, and it was just an accident. On the contrary, you should stabilized both students' mood. This is my own experience. At that time, teacher punished me, and really let me heartbroken. And then, this experience let me unbelieve every teachers, because she didn't try to understand me.
So, I don't agree to use punishment to motivate students. Love is the most effective way to teach students. Just let students know you are willing to reward them by all means if they do well, and I consider that teachers can quickly know the advantage of this teaching way.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I believe that peope will learn better when they are willing to learn, and aren't forced by their parents or teachers. Though some people may regard the punishment as a good way to motivate students to learn, the punishment may do harm to students' minds. I think that we should make learning an amusing thing. When we are willing to learn, we will regard learning as a game (When we learn, we are playing a game. ) For example, my mom always tells me that you could learn from everything and I will always give you a big hand when you achieve your goal. I'm glad that my mom is a woman of wisdom. Now, I learn everything, like cooking, dancing and playing the piano and I am really happy about learning.
Because of my mom's educational method, I suggest that everyone should learn and shouldn't be forced by any punishment but the support and applause from your family and teachers.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the past, teachers used to punish students when they did something wrong. However, in these years, more and more teachers try to teach their students by rewarding them.
In my opinion, I think that rewarding is more effective. There are several reasons. One reason is that students get confidence from being rewarded, especially those who can't do well on tests. Take one of my junior high school classmates, Jack, for example. He can't do well on tests and always gets poor grades; nevertheless, he can draw very well. Once he was praised by our teacher for his good painting and from then on, he has become more and more confident.
Another reason is that rewarding can give students passion. Take Jack for example again. After being rewarded, he fell in love with arts immediately, and he's now studying in art school. He wants to realize his dream of becoming an artist. I admire him.
Teachers can also benefit from rewarding students. They can get happiness and be proud of their students. For these reasons, I believe that rewarding is more effective than punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to punish students who do not behave well. Althrough there are many studies saying that it is not healthy to children mentally, I still stand by the side of teaching with punishment.
Firstly, punishment is a very useful tool. Everyone hates punishment. In order to prevent being hit or staying behind after school, of cause, students would behave themselves.
Secondly, the method of rewarding does not work for most of the naughty students. It is just a way of pushing students to be more demanding and aggressive, especially those whom are given physical prizes as award. This time you give him $1, next time he would ask for $10. Everyone has endless desires.
To conclude, I personally believe that pressure is powerful tool to encourage us to be good and to have better performence in all way round. So, I think punishment would works better than reward during eductation. But, of cause, punishment must not be too over. Otherwise, it would bring opposite effect.

subject: HW1001
content:
There is no denying that teachers spare no efforts to motivate students to pay attention in class and to control their behavior. However, as a matter of fact, some students fooling around in class. As a consequence, teachers either punish or reward students to reach the fulfillment.
Take my cousin for instance. Initially, he interrupted the teacher in class all the time. At first, the teacher punished him in order to control him. However, this method did not work. My cousin still distracted the teacher in class. Gradually, the teacher use another way. The teacher told my cousin that if he concentrated in class, she would prepare a mysterious reward for him. To her surprise, it worked, my cousin was curious about the reward so that he paid attention in class. My cousin always expected the reward, hence, he no longer disturbed the teacher in class.
Increasingly, research is suggesting that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Instead of punishment, students expect rewards. With this method, children would pay more attention and show more interest in class in order to gain the reward, such as my cousin. Consequently, the method of rewarding students for learning is tend to be more effective than punishment. By using this method, teachers can not only teach students without distraction, but can also attain a better learning quality in class.
In conclusion, no matter what methods teachers finally decide to use, only when students willing to pay attention in class can they truly grab the knowledge which teachers want to convey to them.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students is more effective than using punishment to motivate students to learn. Take myself for example, when I got the first prize in the class, my parents used to give me some money as the bonus. If I didn't do well in the test, my parents shouldn't blame me at all. They would tell me that "You can do better next time. Just try it." In this way, I often had the hope to each test. Because I knew that however well or badly I did, I wouldn't be blamed. I would have the motive to try to do better in the next test.
In the other method, punishing students when they are bad is not the right way to motive them. Students should be cultivated by their personality. They will be happy when they are doing what they are fond of. Not every student is suitable for studying books. They have their own gift. If you make them do what they are not good at, they would be hate it, and avoid it on purpose. To sum up, rewarding students for learning is a good way for teaching students.

subject: HW1001
content:
It is difficult to discuss which method to teach is more effective because it is such a multifaceted topic. Some people seem to prefer to use punishment while others tend to reward students. From my point of view, I think the latter is better.
Some teachers seem to prefer to punish their students severely when they make mistakes. By doing so, students may make progress soon. However, they won't study hard by themselves once they leave their stern teacher. What's worse, these students may hate to study forever. Thus, in my opinion, using punishment to motivate students to learn is the last thing that a good teacher should do.
On the other hand, some teachers believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. And the reasons are as follows. First of all, in this way, a harmony learning atmosphere will be developed among students and teacher which is absolutely essential in learning. Besides, by rewarding, students will have incentives to study hard, and therefore learn everything effectively. Last but not least, by doing so, students will acquire a habit of studying voluntarily, which is imperative in the course of life. Take me for example, most of my teacher reward me when I score high, and it really spurs me to study harder. Thus, I think the latter position is comparatively much more effectively.
Of course, there are arguments to be made for the opposing position. However, I think the reasons I have presented in favor of my point of view are beyond reproach.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my humble opinion, I would like to believe that rewarding students is more effective. Using punishment will not only hurt students' body but also their hearts. What the worst is it makes students refuse to learning and even refuse to going school. Therefore, I consider that rewarding students is the better method. For example, I remember that I really hated English when I was a freshman of junior high school. At that time, my English teacher always forced me to spell vocaburary. If I made a mistake, he would hit my hands. Even though he gave me such serious punishment, my English grade did not improve at all. Because this punishment let me hate English, I did not want to spend time on studying it. However, my English teacher had changed to another person in the next year. It was her who made me be interested in English. She always encouraged me and told me not to be afraid of speaking English. When I had a mistake, she just smiled to me; when I was improved, she would give me candy as reward. Until now, I still remember her face and voice.
Because of the above example, instead of punishment, I believe rewarding students is more effective.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, using punishment to motivate to learn and to control their behavior. But now the goverment said that we can not use punishment because it may hurt these students that were punished. Using it, as for me, is the most effective way to make me study or work hard. Punishment makes pressures. If we want to prove ourselves, punishment has its necessary to be exist.
But some people believe that awarding students for learning can lead to better results. This is the truth that I must accept, but this is not a good way for the majority of the students. For example, a friend of mine, once was a student who's score on tests were only 10 or 20 sometimes he got an 0 in the exams. But after we changed a teacher who made us study everyday, it also changed my friend's behavior. If he didn't do well on tests he had to go to the teacher's office to study for the whole semester. From then on, the score he got became higher and higher and now he is in Taiwan university.
As far as I'm concerned, it is essential to use punishment if there is a need. Most people may want to live in a comfortable life. But this would not come by doing nothing. What we have to do is to do our best, no matter how hard it is, and punishments can makes most of us have more motives to do it.

subject: HW1001
content:
To teachers, there are so many ways to motivate their students in both learning and behaviors in their classrooms. In my opinion, I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. I have two reasons to support my point.
First, rewarding students can motivate students to learn more automatically even though they are not really interested in that subject. I, myself is an English teacher in an elementary school. I usually reward my students in the class. I prefer to interact with my students in learning English. I set up a rewarding system. I put students in groups and they can raise their hands to answer my questions. If the answer is correct, I add one point to their group. When they reach a certain goal, I have them pick their prize in a bag randomly. The result of this rewarding system really works in my classroom. My students always want to learn more even though some of them are not really interested in the subject of English. I am glad the all the students can partisepate in my class when I teach.
The second reason is that punishments can bring negative consequences in learning and behaviors. I can see lots of news reporting how teachers use corporal punishments to students and bring up serious issues. Lots of students refuse to go to school or learn just because they are afraid of overuse punishments in their daily lives.
In short, I think that rewarding is the better strategie to students in their learning. Making them learn knowledge passively. Why not make them to learn automatically.

subject: HW1001
content:
Low profiency in learning is a major problem in most students in Taiwan. To work the matter out, teachers oftentimes seek two main solution; one is punishment, and the other is rewarding. Each has its benefits and drawbacks.
Punishment, a way lots of educators seek to, is a negative but efficent way of handing problems. Take myself for example. I would work much harder to avoid being slapped or writing a word ten more times for answering wrong. However, punishment could lose its power, especially to those who perform badly in almost every field. The punishment doesn't seem to work on those students, who seem to be immued to those punishments, and make no progress on their academic works. In contrast, rewarding works well in both high and low achievers. The only disadvantage of rewarding could happen when students receive no reward; hence, they lose the motive to learning.
On the whole, rewarding is better than punishment. Students favor compliments to scolding. When one is being flattered, he/she is to show all what he/she got and do good on every aspect. On this point of view, I favor rewarding students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers think of punishment as the best way to teach students. Others firmly believe that rewarding students can contribute to better results. As far as I am concerned, I' am in favor of rewarding students. My opinions can be described as follows. First of all, nowadays, using punishment often leads to some conflicts between parents and teachers. Besides, once students are punished by teachers, they will start to hate the teacher and do more rebellious behavior. In this way, it is totally impossible to help control students' behavior, but do harm to them. Nevertheless, if teachers reward students for learning, they will be more willing to study. Furthermore, once teachers reward and compliment them, it will leave a good impression on students. Then, it stands to reason that students will respect teachers and be more willing to take advice from teachers. In view of this, I think that rewarding students is more effective.
Looking back, I vividly remember how my friend, Jack, becomes a bad guy. He has been a very naughty boy since elementary school. However, our teacher always punished him because he never handed in homework. During the six years, our teacher kept scolding him and even beating him. Finally, on graduation ceremony, Jack even fought with our teacher. He even joins gangster now, which makes me deeply unstand that punishment is definitely not the best way to teach students.

subject: HW1001
content:
I believe that rewarding students is more effective than using punishment. When I was in elementary school, I had a strict math teacher who was known for his bad temper and punishment. If the students didn't hand in the homework on time, the math teacher would shout at them and make them to stand whole class. Gradually, students began to avoid him and hated math as well. Some students who were good at math then lost the interest on it. Later, I found some classmates cheating on the test in order not to be punished by the math teacher. I was shocked to see that but didn't dare to tell the teacher because he would definitely erupt like a volcano.
