For another example in contrast, students always love the teacher who rewards them and encourages them. I was very poor at English before, but it had totally changed since I met a patient English teacher. The teacher told me not to give up on English because it was getting more and more important in this global village and taught me English from basic level again. She always helped the students to build up the confidence instead of using punishment. As a result, I'm no longer afraid of English.
From these examples, it's obvious that using punishment may lead to a worse result. That's because we all want to learn happily and without fear or great stress.

subject: HW1001
content:
Everyone believes that education plays an important role in nowadays society. However, methods of educating varies from person to person. Some teachers think that punishments can make students work harder, while others say giving encourages can make the best effect to their students. As for me, I think giving rewards is better than punishments, and the reasons are as followed.
First, it is good for students developing their potential in every area except for schoolwork. Perhaps students who are poor in schoolworks have a great talence in other place like sports, arts, and so many more. Second, punishment will give student terendous pressure in learning, and may make them feel depressed, anxious, and sleepless in night, thus may lead to social problems. Last but not least, giving students encouragements can give them confidence and make them have courage facing with problems in school, family, or even among their friends. They will not afraid of the task confronted because of the appropriate rewardings from their teachers.
To sum up, under the great pressure of schoolwork in nowadays society, what students need is encouragments and concerns instead of blames and punishments. And giving them cheerup can make them more opptimistic in the future.

subject: HW1001
content:
Teaching students is not a kind of easy job. All the teachers try their best to give as much information as they can. However, not every students can achieve the goals which set by their teachers. That's really a difficult choice for teacher that which is better, to punish or to reward students?
In my opinion, I think it is more effective that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. This kind of teaching way is wonderful for those who didn't have enough self-confident, especially the little kids. Moderate encouagement can inspire them very much. We can easily discover that the children who are encouraged or rewarded by their teacher do better on their school studies than those students who are punished. In addition, to reward students can also change the atmosphere in the classroom. The classroom will be filled with happiness. I believed that rewarding is benifit to both students and teacher!
There's an example to support my point of view. My younger brother used to study in a school which is famous for the strictness of the teachers there. If my brother didn't do well on the test, he will get punished from his teacher. Unfortunately, his grade is not really good so that he almost be punished everday. He is unhappy then. And then he decided to go to another school to studies, the teacher there prefer to reward him instead punish him. Steps by steps, my brothers grade has improved a lot and he seems to know the correct and happy way for learning. Finally he got an excellent score on the big exam, and be able to go to study in the best high school. I'm proud of him.
How big change it is that a teacher use a right way to teach. All in all, rewarding students is always better than punishing them.

subject: HW1001
content: I think teachers who believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results is more effective. I prefer this because students want to have reward if they do something better than before, the relationship between students and teacher will be good, and it will give students energy to work hard. First, if students do something better than before, they may feel happier if they get rewards. For example, if I get good grades, I hope someone to tell me that I am good or give me some rewards so that I will work harder to get better grades next time. Second, the relationship between teacher and students will be better. To illustrate, when the teacher rewards student for their good behaviors, the student will think the teacher is good. Students will like to talk to the teacher. Last but not least, the rewards will give the student energy to work hard next time. To demonstrate, one of my classmates plays basketball better than before, our PE teacher tells him that he plays very well. After this, he plays basketball every day to make his skill much better. I prefer teachers reward their students for learning can lead to better results because they will work harder to become better next time.

subject: HW1001
content:
It is common belief that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. But currently, some teachers punish students instead of rewarding them. However, I consider that rewarding students can have positive aspects.
Take myself for example. When I was in elementary school, I got poor grades initially. However, my teacher kept inspiring me by giving me some toys, thus, I studied hard in order to get those toys. After a period of time, I became a changed person. I always ranked first in the class, and my parents were glad at me.
More and more research is indicating that motivate students by rewarding them can be more effective. If we punish students who don't do well on studies, they will probably lose their self-confidence as well as determination, and refuse to study. Hence, we should encourage them more and tell them if they get good grades, they can receive a toy, a gift, for instance.
In conclusion, due to the advantages discussed earlier in this essay, we can infer that rewarding students is a positive way to inspire them to study. Trying to control students' behavior and punish them are not a wisdom choice. Therefore, we should ban school punishment.

subject: HW1001
content: Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, rewarding is more effective. When students have tests, they will not always do well. At this time, if teacher reward those who get good grades, other students will know if you get good grades, you do the right thing and you are respected by other students. They'll work hard to reach the high grades. In the other hand, if teacher use punishment to let students do well, students will not do so well as teacher wants. They will gradually understand how should they do, that teacher will not punish them. They just do something like test in the average. All they want is just no punishment, not do the best. Students should study in a class fulled of pride and rewarding, not a place filled with punishment. You can go to a school and discover the differences between the two methods teachers do to students. Most of all, teachers should motivate students to love studying, to love learning new knowledge. If students have the ethusiasim to learn, they will always do well on the exam whether there is pride or not, whether there is punishment or not. To have more knowledge should not be motivate by pride or punishment. It is the deepest desire from one's heart.

subject: HW1001
content:
It is often said that teachers should use punishment to motivate students to learn well and teach them to distinguish right from wrong. However, as time changing, there are more and more people believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. As far as I am concerned, I believe that rewarding students is a better method than punishment.
For the reasons why I believe that rewarding is better for the students are as followed. To begin with, rewarding encourage students to work much harder to win the compliments or presents next time. In addition, through this method, students will have more confidence to face the exams or difficulties, and once they have confidence, they usually do well on their homework. Last but not least, I am a student, too; therefore, I know no one would like to be punished. For all these reasons, teachers shouldn't punish students but reward them.
With all these mentioned above, rewarding students have more advantages than punishment, so we should let all the teachers realize the benefits it brings. In this way, as long as the students do well on schoolwork, it also means the successful of our education.

subject: HW1001
content:
An increasing number of people nowadays are advocating the education by rewarding way. These people tend to feel that using punishment will reduce the willing of studying as well as decrease the efficiency of learning. However, I think the method that using punishment to control the students' behavior is more effective.
Take my cousin for example. Initially, their parents didn't give bad temper at him; instead, they always encouraged him to behave himself and buy him some toys in reward. However, my cousin always ignored them, and the relationship of their family even deteriorate. His parents thus send him to a private elemantory school. At first, he was reluctant to change his rebellious behavior. Gradually, with the strict rules and punishments, the school made him realize what he should do. Also, the school even inspired his motivation of learning. After he graduated, I found that he had a big change. Not only did he learn obeying, but also he had an excellent grade.
There are studies suggesting that punishment is still required. Most of the students in junior high school and elemantary school are lack of the ability to control themselves. Besides, they even don't have a corret concept of whether their behavior is right or wrong. By punishing the students, they would consider not to against the rules. After a period of time, they will follow the rules and they will cultivate the value of tackling things.
In sum, the students maybe hate the strict rules and punishments, but I consider that after these students learn it by heart, they will be well-educated and behave themselves. With the reasons above, I think using punishment will be beneficial to the students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn while others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, I have a tendency to feel that rewarding one is perferable to punishing one. Though students may think of teachers as "nice person" and lose their respects, I believe there are still many positive aspects.
Take my cousin for instance. Initially, his parents thought punishment could somewhat raise the grades; however, my cousin persuaded them that it would be in his best interest to study under the education of love. Gradually, he gained self-confidence and had great passions in studying. With the accumlation of the encouragements his teacher gave, he is now a changed person. He recommanded that the education of love is certainly beneficial.
More and more research is suggesting that students can hold positive attitude after being educated in a soft way. They can use a proper attitude when encountering obstacles either in their live and work. They can also build their own realm of confidence and shoulder more responsibilities under pressure. Therefore, they can not only train themselves but be mature and learn to be a "man".
In conclusion, living in this competitive society, we all should arm ourselves with as much confidence as possible. The education of love is certainly essential. Without a doubt, the education of love can provide us the key to the shining future.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are many methods to motivate students to learn and to be educated. In my opinion, using punishment to force students to do better is not appropriate, even if it seems much more effective right away. Recently, there are more and more news to be reported that children got hurts and refused to go to school because of being treated in a wrong way from their teachers. That is a crucial evidence that we need another method to educat our kids.
Many cases showed that rewarding students for learning can led to better results in a long run. What is so-called education? Education means to educat a person to be a person. Hence, teachers should teach kids who be treated well would do well too in the future. That is why we want our kids to be educated and what we are asking for.

subject: HW1001
content:
It is widely believed that the way teachers taught their students plays an important role in the students' behavior and study, especially to the young kids. Since the influential power affects the students deeply, it is extremely important to choose which way to influence them: You can force them by giving punishment, or persuade them by giving reward. As far as I'm concerned, the latter one will be more effective. Different from giving them pressure, you may established a goal for them to accomplish. As long as the reward sounds attractive to him, he will do his best to finish the work, no matter how difficult it might be, and get the reward. Your may also teach him the importance of setting a goal, which will sure benefits his attitude of studying and learning.
I'm glad I came from a family which taught me this way, which brings changes to me until now. No matter how hard the goal seems to be, after I decided to achieve it, never did I give up until I reached the goal, standing on the destination. This is the way that will bring changes to many children, I'm sure about that.

subject: HW1001
content:
When it comes to the education, I think rewarding is a better and effective way to students. Rewarding can not only stimulate students to study harder but also help them find happiness of the subject. When students find happiness, they will love the subject and want to learn more knowledge of the subject. If students want more, they will communicate with teacher, and that will make the atmosepher of the class more energetic and positive.
Here are two examples. First, my English teacher, Nelle Houng, she used punishment when we got bad grades. The way she used make us afraid of English class, we would study it but we would not love it. On the other hand, my Chinese teacher, Amy Chang, she rewarded us when we did well on tests, and we learned in a happy mod. After analyzing these two way, I think rewarding can make students become more joyful and learn better.

subject: HW1001
content:
Without hesitation, I will think of the second way as more effective. Punishments only work well at first. When students are gradually accustomed to such hurt, they become unafraid of it and the relationship between students and teachers will even worsen badly. It's absolutely a vicious cycle. Nevertheless, giving them reward makes great success. Once students receive a reward after behaving excellently, they will anticipate being rewarded again and thus they spur themselves to do better.
To support my perspective, I would give an example. A boy named Teddy was a trouble maker in his teachers' eye. He behaved badly in grade one to grade four until he met a amiable teacher. The teacher, unlike other punishment-oriented teachers, knew his background and decided to do something. She said "hello" and "good morning" actively to Teddy and rewarded him when he performed well. Finally, the naughty boy graduated from school and sent a card annually to the teacher. He wouldn't have been the greatest scientist had it not for his teacher's dedication.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think rewarding students for learning is a better way to motivate the students. Based on the behavior psychology, giving students rewards to arouse their interest of learning is a positive feedback. A good positive feedback can not only stop the unwanted behavior but also make the students have motivation to learn. Students are willing to learn and study if there were something appealing to them. On the other hand, students may do the study because they don't want to recieve the negative feedback, and the punishment may make students hate the task of study because punishment is not a good attraction for them.
For an example, I would study hard and learn more to do the practice of the math work, because the high score and the prize was appealing to me. But if the rule had been changed to "not doing homework would get punishment" would make me sick of the math, despite the interesting of studying it. Thus, giving students punishment to force they to learn is not a good idea.

subject: HW1001
content:
In our education, some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and control their behavior, but others believe punishment is not good for students. In my opinion, both ways are effective, but it depends on how to use them.
In my experience of teaching in the elementary school, I found the students are getting smart and smart. They get some information from TV more than the school. So they try to do something good and bad to know their teachers. If the teachers are serious, they have good behavior, otherwise they are out of control.
When I teach, I use both way to mange my students. I punish them because I want them to understand the rules and don't try to cross the line. Then I do reward students, too. They will know good learning and behavior earn some prizes and be good role models from other students. They like to do because kids always want to show how best they are.
In my opinion, both methods are useful and effective if teachers know how to apply them in good timing.

subject: HW1001
content:
During our school time, we will encounter different kinds of teachers. Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others use rewarding to encourage students to learn. To me, these two kinds of methods may all work but use rewarding is more effective.
Take myself as an example, during junior high school time, my math teacher always used punishment to punish those who failed the exam. I usually felt frustrated at that time because my math was not very well. Also, I felt discourage to learn. Thus, my math score always lower than average. On the contrary, my English teacher used rewarding to encourage those who did well in exam. I felt motivated because I wanted to get the rewarding. Therefore, I usually get good grades on English. To sum up, many parents may think punishment works well, but it depends. Different people have different favors. I think that parents should choose the one that works on their children. Thus, their children will do well.

subject: HW1001
content:
There're always some students who can't melt into the class and behave themselves. They may be full of energy and not being able to quiet down even for a minute. It indeed cause many problems and making teachers headache. Some teachers may use punishments such as forbidding children from activities or scolding them in front of their classmates to cause peer pressure. However, it would deprive of children's right for learning and casting a shadow on their mental developments. What's worse, there're rare teachers even use physical punishments when they lose their temper.
In fact, I saw a piece of news several months ago. There was a nauty boy in a cram school who refused to do his homework but keeping on playing and making loud noises. His teacher finally flied into a furry and beat the boy's ass. Though the teacher came out to apologize to this boy and his parents afterwards, the boy has been hurt both mentally and pysically.
Children are always full of energy and curiosity. It would be cruel to give them heavy punishments which may distort their personalities and kill their creativity. I vote for using patience and encouragements to guide children instead of punishment. Children are our hopes so they're worth to be treated well.

subject: HW1001
content: I think that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Punishment might bring positive effect, but it is a permanent way to prompt students to learn. You can punish naive children because sometimes punishmend can make them alert, but you can't push teenagers to study if they don't like to study. Punishment should be the last way in the process of learning. It may cause both student's mental and pysical problems if it is used in an inappropriate way. One of my friends shows the best example. He used to be a naughty boy in the elementary school. One day, his homeroom teacher shouted at him and punished on him because he didn't pay attention during the class; as a result, he became scared of coming school and refused to talk with his teacher. All teachers want to motivate their students to learn move; however, rewarding is the better way to use compare to punishment. Only when teachers stop to use punishment but to reward students for learning do the teaching quarrels disappear.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, rewarding is a better method than using punishment to motivate students to learn. According to my own experience, when I was a elementary school student, my teacher was serious to everyone. More often than not, she asked all of us to be perfect in every field, including Chinese, English, and math, and so on. Everyone in our class were afraid of her and could not help but follew her "rules." Under her instruction, although some of us performanced well in academic behaviour, none of us rejoiced at learning new things. We were trained to keep disciplined and wrote test paper every day. What's worse, it seemed to take me forever to get rid of this. Things did not change better until I graduated and became a high school student. This time, I met a friendly teacher, he never blamed us whenever we didn't do well in the exams. Instead, he encouraged us to parctice again and again. He said, "No one is perfect and everyone is likely to make mistakes once in a while. The only thing one can do is learn from lessons." It was his world that inspired me to acquire knowledge actively and refound the interest in learning. I was really thankful for him and his way of teaching. After all, moderation, not compulsion, is the secret to happiness.

subject: HW1001
content:
There is an old saying, "Spare the rod, spoil the child." I agree with the proper punishment. Teachers are responsible for teaching the right attitudes to the students. If the students do something wrong, they have to let students know that, and help them correct their behaviors.
According to my opinion, there are three examples to support my opinion. First, students can learn something from the lesson. Most people are forgetful, punishment can help them to remember. Second, teachers can ask students to do social service rather than to punish them. They not only learn the experience, but also help the other people. Third, the punishment is the way that teachers express their love to the students. If the teachers don't care about the students, they will not strictly ask their students and motivate them. According to the above opinions, I agree with using punishment.

subject: HW1001
content: When I was a junior high school student, my English teacher used punishment as a tool to motivate her students to learn English. But I am not the case, I still got not sign of improvement. In my senior high school, I met Mrs. Li, she used unique technique to teach, she punished students when they didnot do their best effort, but also reward they when they got a little advantage. Eventually, I came over the fear of learning of English. Therefore I beleive that punishment is the force push you from damage, but rewarding is the force pull you to goodness. They are both effective if you use they right.

subject: HW1001
content:
As far as my experience is concerned, I prefer the way to reward the students than the way to punish them. Because punishing students is a way to make them scared, woried, and horrified, so that they finish the assignments reluctantly. I used be punished, so I consider it as a less effective way. Quite the opposite, the way to reward the students is to stir the competition between them; eventually, to win the reward, they will spare no effort to do their best.
Take the students in a remote country, and the ones in a city for example. The former one prefers the way to punish students, and the students who didn't behave by the school rule, and were punished become less energetic, and lacks self-control. However, the later one holds a possitive attitude. They encourage the students, and inspire them to do something risky instead of restraining them. Besides, if the students do a good job, what they gain is a unbelievable amout of rewards. Therefore they are more willing to spend their time on their homeworks, books, challenges than those restrained all the time.
Punishing students might sometimes makes some effort; however, the students restrained too much are less spry, and lacks the interest in challenging something risky. In the contrast, students who are encouraged to challenge theirselves more will become the leaders someday. In a long run, I prefer the rewarding way.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to spur students to learn and to control their behavior. In the contrast, others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. As far as I am concerned, both of the methods are effective but the percent these account for should depend on students personalities.
For me, proper punishment can make me feel shame but motivate me to go forward. However, some teachers put to much emphasis on this which bring about many corporal penalty incidenties not only doing harm to the students but ruinning the teachers' goodness.
Rewarding studets for learning can lead to better results, and I am a vivid example. Although my academic performance is not in the top, I always have a positive attitude toward studying, and it can be attributed to my homeroom teachers of junior high. With a view to improving our grades, he prepared lot of gifts for us if our grades got better.
Both of these are good, but it varies from students.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the age of communication and information, teachers play a great role in giving their knowledge to students. Nevertheless some students are so lazy that teachers need to punish them in order to motivate them from learning.
In my course of schooling, I will never forget my homeroom teacher, Tina, when I was in junior high school, Tina is a beautiful women with black hair. She is also a strict women who expects all of her students to have great grade. She gave every of us a standard of score and if we didn't achieve the standard she would punish us. Hence we always worked very hard and tried our best on the test. When we got good grade on the test, she gave us candies and presents for rewards, therefore all of us repected Tina very much.
Nowadays we can sometime heard about the punishment that teachers gave to their students was so strict that some of them can't afford and even leaded some bad efforts. Yet as the instance that has been said from above, I strongly believe that proper punishment is necessary and effective. Nevertheless teachers can't just punish their student without rewarding. Well goes an old saying "To hit to birds with one stone" if teachers want to motivate student to learn and to control their behavior, they have to punish them and reward them at the same time as well.

subject: HW1001
content:
Hardly does any teacher not want their students can be the best, no matter in their studies, personality traits or daily behavior.
I prefer rewarding students rather than punish them. Because if teacher reward something that studuents are interested in when they do good, the relationship among the teacher and students would be hamonious. The students may not only be grateful for it but strengthen their confidence in their process of pursuing academic achievement. For example, the dolphins in the amusement park, got their food after performing each breath-taking actings, and they'll do better on the next show.
In my words, learn happily is more effective than learn under the great presure. After all, who want the bitter memory in their studenthood.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, more and more teachers start to sence their duty to teach their students not only the knowledge but also the morality. Moreover, they find that the most effective way is to reward students with applause and encourgement. In my point of view, this way is more considerable than punishment. In order to motivate students to learn by themselves, teachers should be helpers in their back, and push them when they are in need. Therefore, students can struggle from the way they find.
From my personal experience, I feel that rewarding is truly the best method for learning. In general speaking, people all like to be admired, and students are no exception. When I was an elementary students, I met a good teacher. The teacher was creative. She came up an idea to push us to learn by ourselves, and this idea was something like a sort of encourgement. For example, if we took higher grates than last exam or did a good action, we could take one point from her. Then, if we collected 5 points, we could have a meal with our teacher, and surely, it was a free meal. It was an interesting experience for me, and it was unforgetable, too.
Maybe somebody agree to punish students to push them to learn and control their behavior. However, do they really take students' mood into consideration? Do they believe the students are really willing to learn? When I watch the kind of news on TV, I always think about these problems.

subject: HW1001
content:
With the competition about academic performance more and more serious, teachers always try their best to courage their students to persue better grades. The way they use are various such as giving candies to well-behaved students, admiring students in front of their parents and using punishment. As far as I am concerned, I think that rewarding students for learning can trigger better results. Students, especially teenagers, are inclined to be admired in front of their peers because they can gain confidence from it. Moreover, teachers can't hit students and scold at them as the right of students urges.
When I am a junior high school student, my math teacher was keen to teaching. However, he always asked us to stand in front of the door of classroom if we couldn't live up to his expection to our test grades. In this way, there were more and more students didn't focus on what he taught in the class. Finally, he realized that rewarding student is a better policy than punishment. So, I think rewarding students for learning can lead to better consequence.

subject: HW1001
content: When I was little, my parents always said that their teachers usually taught them with the strict way. For example, writing the wrong things for one hundred times or standing outside the class. It seems very useful in the past. Such the punishment be used that the students can stay in the school for the whole day without making troubles. But some parents think that teachers have to teach their children with the lovely way recently. Do not use the punishment or shout in the class. In my opinion, some children are too naughty that teachers can't use the smooth way to let them calm down, they didn't know what would the other people feel when they played in the class, teachers also have trouble dealing the events without blaming them. Maybe use some punishment to make the bad children to study with good behavior, and give some reward to make the good children to keep up the good work.

subject: HW1001
content:
The question about how to teach a student has become a controversal issue since years ago. Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to study hard and control their behavior; while others think rewarding students as a best method to encourage them. In my opinion, I support the second point. Because teachers always give rewards to good-behavior students, and teachers put more attetion on these students. Same as other students, they also want to get the rewards, and even attract attetion from teachers. So, they will behave well or study harder to win the teacher's praise.
I still remember when I was in elementary school. My class teacher set up some principles, if you achieved one of these priciples, you would get one point. When you got ten points or more, you could change a gift. Eevery classmate tried their best to attain the goal, in order to get a point. At the period, our class was filled with energy and everyone studied hard just wanted to be the first in this class. Because of our teacher's unique method, our class always got the best grades in every tests or competitions.
However, I think there isn't a best method about how to teach a student and control their behavior. Teachers only have to find a balance between punishment and rewaring, and not every student can adapt every teacher's teaching method. After all, every student is unique and has their own thinking toward everything. And I also believe that there must be a moderate way to teach a student.

subject: HW1001
content:
Teaching is the only way to make a student independant. Many teachers are confused in whether punishing or rewarding students to teach them. In my opinion, teachers should punish students when they are wrong in order to motivate them.
Being lazy is everyone's nature. If people are in conditions that satisfy them, they have no reason to change, and therefore, they often choose to be the same. While teaching, teachers should punish students to let they know that they are not good enough and encourage them to do better. If we reward students before they succeed, they will consider that they are good enough and meet the command.
We should not give students sweat things before the final. The results after the hardships are rewards.

subject: HW1001
content: To motivate students to learn and to control their behavior, teachers should reward students instead of punishing them. Rewarding students is more effective because they will be more active. Punishing students will make them listen to you when you are around only. After school or after graduating from the school, students will not touch books. However, the students who are rewarded study in a good mood. Take myself as an example, the reason why I love English very much is that I have been encouraged by my parents since I was very little. Whenever I speak English, my parents will clap their hands or tell me how good I am. I am getting interested in English because I know my parents are proud of me. My parents told me that whenever you find some advantages from others, even though it is a tiny one, tell that person and encourage him or her. When people are rewarded, they will try harder to do right things and make themselves better. According to my experience, I think rewarding students is more effective.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think that rewarding students is more effective. Rewarding students can make them not only joyful but also confident. It goes without saying that children need courages. Therefore, if you give rewards to the students due to their outstanding performance, they will be happy and do their best to achieve another performance. They will be satasify with their doing and get the confidence. Besides, they can have more creativities on every projects owing to the confidence and courages. It will make them have better career in the future. In the contrast, if the teachers use punishment to control their students' behavior, it may not get so many benfits as rewarding students. Punishing students will make them scared and loose their imagine. They will have to worry about doing wrongs and punishment, so they made every efforts to live up to the teacher's standard. Needless to say, they won't perform as excellent as the students who got the reward in the childhood.
My experience is that my elementary teacher encouraged us to help one people a day. After doing that, she would give each of us a sticker. At that time, in order to get the stickers, I not only help the old lady cross the road, but also pick up the trash on the way home. I didn't notice the big change happened to me until I grow up. Today, although I don't get stickers any more, I have the habit of helpping others. I volunteered to help many old lonely people to give them my warm heart. To sum up, through my experience, I think it's better to reward students.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think it is useful to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior by punishment. I believe in an old saying that spare the rod, spoil the child. I think that students who are poor in studying or controling their behavior may because they don't want to do it and just want to win a status in the class that he or she doesn't afraid of teachers. In order to prevent this and make them walk on a right way of life, we should take punishments to achieve this goal.
One of my teachers in junior high school is such a person believe in punishment is useful to control students' behavior. Because of him, I don't go on a wrong way of life. On the contrast, my neighbors don't take punishment to control their children, so their children are not good in studying and have some strange behaviors like staying in a man's home over night. If they can take punishments to control their children's behavior, I think there will be a big difference. Spare the rod, spoil the child is an old saying, and it can't be known today if there were no examples. So only by punishment is an effective way to control students' behavior.

subject: HW1001
content:
Due to my knowledge and experiences, I would assert that it is more appropriate and effective to punish students when the mistake are made at the first time. Thus, they can immediately receive the awareness of danger and the ideas about harsh consequences. Frankly speaking, cheating can be the most common event happened in our school lives. This kind of behavior should be banned as we figure it out; otherwise, those cheating guys may continuously doing so and even make it prevelent. Therefore, most of the time I would secretly inform our teachers, because I deeply know that most of them would give cheaters an unforgettable punishment which would prevent them from doing so for second time. What's more teachers may also tell our class that there is no short-cut in the learning path, all you have to carry with you is diligence and tolerance. As to those black lambs, they are now feel guilty and regretful for their cheating behaviors. They even give promises to teachers that they would begin to learn well.
It seems that sometimes punishment is necessary and useful to control and restrict students' wrong behaviors, especially when they go into wrong ways. Hence, I would still be the supporters for keeping punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
Many people believe that rewarding students is preferable to punishing them. These people have a tendency to feel that students can learn better when they have positive motivations. Although punishments may be the useful way to control students behavior and force them to study, I still believe rewarding students has some positive aspects.
Take my cousin for example. He used to be a naughty boy and no matter how my aunt punished him, he still behaved as usual. One day my uncle could never endure it so he decided to send my cousin to the most famous elementrary school in the town which acquired students to live in the dome. Initially, my cousin was unwilling to leave his parents and cried all day long. Then, he found that if he behave good, the teachers would give him treats to encourage him. Gradually, he loved the live in the school and always got the first price in his class. After a year studying in the school, he came back a changed person.
More and more research is suggesting that those who get rewards while they are learning can shoulder more responsibilities and burdens. They usually build their self-confidence while they are learning. That's the reason why teachers loves encouraging students.
No matter which reasons bring you to the decision of rewarding kids and students, helping them while they are learning is certainly benefical to the sociaty.

subject: HW1001
content:
Everyone has different opinion on motivating students learning. Some of them think that if students behavior is not right, teachers have the right to punish them. On the other hand, some of them think that teachers shouldn't hit the students, because it might get some negative results. In my opinion, punishing and rewarding students have different function. Later I will divide it into three parts, first, the good and bad sides of punishment, seconed, the good and bad sides of reward, at the end I will make a conclusion for my essay.
When I was in the junior high school or even elementary school, if our scores were below the average of whole class, then the teacher would hit us. We all know that teacher's methods were helping us to get a better grades. Some of our classmates just don't have interest on learning. So, I think teacher shouldn't hit the studen't because of their grades. On the other hand, I think rewarding students for learning is a good way to motivate students on learning. Expecially little kids, because they'll pay much more attention on learning. Although rewarding them can motivate their study, I think it might come to a bad results. After one time or two times, student's study might because of the reward but not for themself. Maybe, if one day when the reward can't contract them anymore, they'll lost their study interest. In conclusion, I think that everything has two sides, good or bad. Teachers have to hold this line, because it's very important and also very hard.

subject: HW1001
content:
Most teachers in Taiwan used to take punishment as the most effective way to control students' behavior. Nevertheless, there're an increasing number of people maintaining that rewarding them for learning can lead to better results. There are several reasons which are as the follows.
First, rewarding students makes them fond of learning. Students would like to study in persuit of the prize. They study out of their minds. When students eventually manage to win the prize, not only are they delightful but learning has become a joyful thing. Also, keeping rewarding students will get them into the habbit of learning. They will be used to studying and take it for granted. That will definitely help them a lot in the future.
What's more, frequently rewarding students helps them cultivate a positive mind. They'll understand that they will harvest what they till. When they're disappointed, they know that the bad will go away and something good is waiting for them and that nothing can't be overcome as long as they try their best. They will face all the troubles and conquer them all in the way when they overcome the hardest assigments. What our students need is this optimistic and positive attitude.
In conclusion, rewarding students rather than punishing them can do good to both their academic performance and their mental heath. In my opinion, rewarding is such a beneficial way that every teacher must try it at once!

subject: HW1001
content:
In the past, many teachers liked to punish students and considered it the only way to make them learn better and have better manners. In my opinion, punishment only makes the things even worse. Students listen to the teachers who like to punish students in appearence, but hate them in the bottom of their hearts. We should change punishment into the reward. Students will motivate themselves to learn and control their behavior because they want to get the reward.
When I was a junior high school students, my teacher was very stern that he hit us when we didn't do well on our tests or dropped a little trash on the floor. The method he used wasn't work. Many classmates didn't listen to him. Then, we changed a new teacher in the next year. The new teacher was nice. She gave us gifts when we made process on our tests or we cleaned the classroom. Our class became better than before.
Reward is better than punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
Many people believe that using punishment is preferable to rewarding. These people tend to feel that using punishment can somewhat make the students pay more attention in class. Although using punishment do a little harm to students, I think their are some positive aspects.
Take my cousin for example, he lives in a rich family and was spoiled when he is little. No one could cease him when he wanted to do what he want. Moreover, his parents were not willing to punish him. When he entered elementary school, he was always naughty and influence the classmates sitting next to him in class. However, after his teacher using the punishment to him that no one had used to him before, he began to pay more attention in class.
Increasingly, people in our society are objecting to using punishment. I think using punisnment is a effective way to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. In conclusion, the decision for a teacher or parents to use punishment is difficult. Based on the factors discussed earlier in the essay, I think using punishment is beneficial to students when learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, more and more news is that teachers punish students just because they don't do well on the exam or forgot to hand in the homework. In my opinion, I think some teachers use punishment only to let the students know how to respect them. Nevertheless, it doesn't seem a good way. This ridiculous way usually makes students hate teacher or even hate themselves. Finally, they may get depressed. On the contrary, rewarding students is the way to go. Students can feel sense of achievement when they get complement. Teachers will be more adorable and lovely.
For example, when I was in fifth grade, I attented the speech contest. My teacher took all her strength to teach me. To her disappointment, I didn't do well. After the contest, I didn't dare to talk to my teacher as I was afraid of being scolded. My teacher, however, she smiled at me and said that she was proud of me. At that moment, I felt everything couldn't be too wonderful. After that, the relationship between my teacher and I was more like friends. Also, I took first place in the next contest.

subject: HW1001
content:
Judging by the advantages and disavantages of the punishment and rewarding, I approve of the former to be much more effective by several reasons as follows. To begin with, constant rewarding make students easily take it for granted that they were born to be rewarded. And as the passing of time, the more rewarding they are given, the more greedy they will be. Secondly, an environment with the punishment corresponds to the real society. Those who are lazy while working are more easily to be fired. As a result, if people can get accustomed to the punishment when they are students, it will be better for them after they grow up.
This issue reminds me that when I was an elementary student, my teacher prefer punishing us to rewarding us. Although we were scared at first, we gradually realized that we would not be punished if we made no mistake and our performence were better than ever. However, the other classes agreed rewarding policy to be useful. it might be effective at begining. Neverthless, they would no more feel satisfied afterwards and their behaviors were getting worse.

subject: HW1001
content:
As far as I know, the project that some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior has aroused much attention of the public. There are both pros and cons about it. In terms of advantages, physical punishment makes a deep impression on each of them. However, it is not the best way to do so. What teachers don't know is that when students were punished in front of the whole class, it not only hurt their bodies but also their hearts.
In my opinion, I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Looking back on my past, I vividly remember a pleasant experience. It has been engraved on my memory. When I was at my first year of junior high school, I took much time to prepare every subjects except math. I was proud of my math ability. However, much to my surprise, I got a goose zero. I thought my math teacher may punish me. Out of my expection, she came to asked me whether I have any difficulties on learning math. I was so shamed to face her. Since then, I have learned a lesson, pride goes before fall. After teacher's rewarding, I studied math more hard. In a word, rewarding is more effective than punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, punishment is more effective than rewarding students. Since punishment would give students who did something wrong some warnings, they would not dare to do the same mistakes again. Although giving students rewards would benefits students who are well-behavior, it will not affect those students who do not treat honor importantly.
Taking my brother for an example. My brother Jim would never be seen as a good boy before he was sixteen. The only thing he did everyday was not studing but playing online games. He was so addcted to it that made his academic perform badly. But now, he is an Math teacher in Junior high. And the changing point is the punishment my parents imposed on him; cut off the Internet, took back the pocket money, and physical punishment. That is why I think punishment is more effective, because my belief is that childrem will not become successful if you just give them love without punishing them.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are many ways to teach students. Some teachers think punishment is a good way, but in my opinion, I think rewarding students is a better way when I want to change the behavior of my students.
As a school teacher, I found that students would behave better when they know they would get candies or cookies after they do good jobs. For example, once I gave my students an assignment and said that anyone who could hand it out the next day he/she could get a little gift. The due day was three days after that day. But the next day, I got 80 percent of students' assignments.
Another example is that when I was a student, my father told me that if I got good grade, I could get a gift. So I studied harder than before.
To sum up, I think students can learn better when they know there would be good things waiting for them. So I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the past, I always thought that punishment is the best way to manage students and arouse their interest in learning. Because students are afraid of punishment, they would follow teachers' instruction just like tamed sheep. Additionally, they would urge themselves to study all the time so that they would not be punished because of low grades. However, I was wrong. Punishment is not suitable in teaching. Instead, rewarding is the best choice.
First, students who lack of confidence could feel a sense of achievement because of rewarding. Sometimes, learning a new thing is a big difficulty for some students. They tend to give up everything because they trust that they could never pick up. For example, one of my students, John, used to keep silent in class. Once he failed a subject, I would take out my "stick" to threat him, and he never expressed his opion. Until one day, he said he wanted to quit and leave this school forever with sobbing. All of a sudden, I realized that his fear and anxiety in learning are all caused by me. I never gave him a chance to develop what he desired. Instead, I killed his learning interest through punishment. Therefore, teachers are supposed to encourage their students as much as possible.
Second, students would easily become self-motivated because of teachers' encouragement. Managing a class is like leading a group in a company. The manager should win workers' heart so that they are willing to try their best with pleasure. When a teacher says something good in front of students, the teacher also conveys an active impact on students' learning emotion. For example, my another student, Lisa, is a very thoughtful student. She always turns in her homework or finishes her jobs on time. One time I was so curious that asked her the reason why she is so tender. She just told me that because teachers' complement would promote her interest in those jobs. Therefore, rewarding is also beneficial in cultivating students' motivation.
Using rewarding is more effective to manage students actually. When a teacher gives encouragement to students, they would become not only confident but also self-motivated. Much of the time, people always think encouragement is the best strategy for them to raise their interest and efficiency no matter in which area. So why we stand in others' shoes as well and treat others in an active way?

subject: HW1001
content:
When it comes to whether we should punish or reward student to motivate students' attitude toward learning or regulate their behavior, there would be many different thoughts in the society. In my opinion, I will definitly stand on the side of the latter. I believe that children who accept adults' encouragement will act better than those don't, which means rewarding students is more effective.
As a student in high school, I have a lot friends. Some of them get good grades while others don't. The main reason is how they are treated by the teachers. Tom, who studies hard, always fails to finish test sheets. Because teachers don't know his effort and blame him, He beomes faithless to himself. However, Mary, who always gets teachers' encouragement, acts even better than Tom although she doesn't work harder.
All things considered, rewarding students turn out to be the more effective way to treat every student.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I prefer to teach students by rewarding rather than teach them by punishing. Here are my two reasons and one example.
First, according to the research, almost every student wants to be rewarded at school. They say if teachers use the gifts to reward them, they are willing to study and dedicate themselves to studying because they are eager for the prize.
The other reason is as follows. If a teacher use strict punishment to motivate students they will follow the teacher at first because they are afraid of punishment. But as time goes on the result will become worse and worse because they hate the teacher. Then, they would rather lag behind their homework and receive the punishment than study. Moreover, students are likely to against the teachers because they don't like to be binded by punishment.
Take my younger sister for example. Her junior high school teachers are so strict that she receives punishment every day. However, she still continue hanging around with her friends and receive the punishment because she hates teachers at school and doesn't care about the punishment.
To sum up rewarding students seems to be more effective on motivating them to learn because nobody wants punishment. So we should promote this method to public and practice it more.

subject: HW1001
content:
As to the controversial discussion, some are in favor of it, while others are against it. In terms of me, I don't be partial about each other. Corporal punishment along with compliments in an adequate time are exceedingly imperative.
When we have a poor performance and get scolded or disciplined by our teachers, at that time, we may have a dislike for the one who punishes us. But, as time fleets away, the attitude of ours has changed. That is to say, we are grateful to him. However, provided that the teacher only gives us rewards no matter how our performance is good or poor. We may develop an attitude of having no care about everything. Worst of all, such originally good behavior will spoil us and we will lose the standard to distinguish right from wrong.
Take my younger brother for example, since his birth, everyone in my family has shown too much care and love for him. They don't let him do houseworks. Even he makes mistakes, they just blame themselves. Because they think they fail to take good care of him. Besides, despite the fact that the things he does is very simple, they tend to make compliments on him, so that he has become a self-conscious child and be indifferent about others.
As a consequence, physical punishment and rewards are both needed to teach children. None of them can't be overlooked. In this way, our society will move to a decent stage.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the society, bad guys are punished by the government; good guys are rewarded. Same things happen in schools. Students get their punishments or rewards according to their behavior.
I firmly believe that punishments are as important as rewards. Lacking of any of them can not lead to the best result. For example, if we never punish a student even when he or she is hurting others to get what he/she wants, the the student might feel that what he/she did was good, because no one stoped him/her and the student can get what ever they want. On the other hand, if a student never gets rewards when doing good deeds to others, he/she might one day feel tired of being good to others.
Rewards and punishments, I believe, are both important in school and society. With them, students will behave better and learn better.

subject: HW1001
content:
When teaching students, teachers will definitely encounter an important question; that is, which method is more effective, punishment or reward? If I had to choose one of them, I would give my students reward because of the following reasons.
The first one is the limit of time. When teachers use punishment to control students' behavior, they have to spend some time on it. However, if they praise students for learning, they just need a little time to say something good to their students. This method is good for the time control in the classroom.
Moreover, students can learn in a happy environment and happiness can cultivate their learning autonomy. This can enhance the learning effectiveness.
Therefore, I think rewarding students is better than punishing them.

subject: HW1001
content: I believe that rewarding is much more effective than punishing for students to learn because rewarding doesn't hurt students' feeling, is what people like to listen to and makes students be willing not to break the rules. Compared with rewarding students, punishing them may make them feel offended. Feeling offended, they will do what teachers ban rather than behave as good students. Robinson is an good example, he was the kind of student who drove teachers crazy when he was a junior in high school. His homeroom teacher punished him all the time. Because of these bothering punishments, Robinson even didn't go to school instead of becoming good students as his teacher's expectation. If students don't feel hurt, they will listen what teachers want to tell them. By the way, every person likes to listen to rewarding. The reason is that rewarding can strenthen their confidence. For instance, Robinson's coach started to find him after he was absent at school and basketball practices. His coach told him "What you did was not wrong, but I believe you can do much better." Because of the coach's encourgement, Robinson went back to school and became a good student that surprised every teacher. Last but not least, students likes to hear teacher's rewarding so that they will tend to behave well instead of breaking the rules. For me, I will try to do better if teachers rewarding me. To sum up, rewarding can motivate students to learn and control their behavior better than punishing because it is good to hear.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, it is better to reward students to learn than to pnnish them, and I believe this because of two reasons. First, by rewarding students with smiles and warm compliments can show that the teacher supports and cares for them. Such an act makes them confident to reach out for more knowledge or participate in more beneficial activites that help them learn. Second, pnnishing students for their poor grades or misbehavior is, in my opinion, not the best way to educate them. For example, some Taiwanese children dread one thing when they go home -- to see their parents holding a bamboo stick and reaching out a hand to get the report cards. Students that are psysically pnnished or scolded are often dispondent; they are nnder constant pressnre dne to their poor preformances and the disapproval of their parents and teachers. Under such circumstances, disconraged students can either become rebelions to their teachers, or simply neglect their stndies becanse they feel no support to motivate them. To sum up, it is better to reward students as they learn. When they gain confidence, it is more likely for them to dream for a brighter futnre, and to eagerly pursue their dreams.

subject: HW1001
content:
I agree that rewarding student for learning can lead to a better results. First of all, rewarding students for studying will lead the student to have a positive way of thinking. Student will think that they will be reward if they study hard. They will also think that it is an honor to study hard. Instead of being punished, student will have a positive way of thinking about studying. Further-more, student will study harder to get a reward, if they study hard to get a punishment, they will have less movation on studying and think they are useless. The most important, students will be encouraged to do and try new things, this is a good way to develop a student's creation. In school, students often make mistakes when trying a new thing, but they will be encouraged and reward when trying it, they won't be punished by having an creative or unique idea.
In my experience, I'd been to a training lesson of Dale Carnagie. Inside the lesson, there are no punishment, there are only encouragement and reward. Students in there will be encouraged and rewarded no matter what they do is right or wrong, but they will only be rewarded if they tried. During the lesson, I really learned a lot, we learn to encourage each other, and I can see not only myself but also others are improving. That's because we didn't get punish from making mistakes.
In conclusion, I agree that rewarding and encouraging students for studying will lead to a better results, I can see that from my own experience, and I hope teachers can try this method to teach their student.

subject: HW1001
content:
There has been a keen debate over how to educate students in recent days. In my opinion, rewarding students for learning might be the better method. Everybody yearns to be loved, eagers to have the sense of being dignified. In the result, if you rewarded the students for learning, they would keep it and even behave better next time.
There is a true example happens to fall on me. In my childhood, I was stupid and lazy. No matter how hard my parents pushed me, I didn't proceed even an inch. Eventually, they came up with an idea, which changed my whole life. They rewarded me for all the good things I had done. Gradually, I became positive because I couldn't forget the feeling of being rewarded and anticipated. So far, there is no rewarding anymore though, I still remain positive and hard-working.
A different fashion of education can change a lot. And, I am convinced that rewarding is much more better than punishing.

subject: HW1001
content:
To use punishment or not is a long-argued issue since the society as a whole began to sense the significance of education. Moreover, the problem is becoming more and more complicated as time went by.
In my point of view, using corporal punishment and verbal warnings appropriately at certain times is available because some naughty boy is just not the one that you can reason with. However, to make sure that the kids really understand what you're angry and care about is important, or it may not be a effective way for sure.
As a student who had a experience of tutoring an elementary school girl, I found it useful to give the girl compliment because it may encourage her to do the right things again as well as have interests in study, but the reward sometimes just couldn't work if she's in a bad mood or decided to be wayward that day. Then I will warn her to behave herself at the first time and hit her finger slightly if she got distracted again. It always turned out effective.
According to my personal experiences, I suggest that giving reward along with adequet punishment is an effective way.

subject: HW1001
content:
Whether punishment should be forbidden in school has been drastically debated over the recent years. While some teachers still insist that discipline is indispensible in motivating students toward better academic performances, most parents and education professionals urge to put a hault to this uneffective method of controlling students. In my own opinions, punishing students is certainly useless as to pushing them to work hard. Learning is supposed to be fun and oringinates from the thirst of getting more knowledge. Without the curiousity and will as the driving force, even if you were frightened by the punishment, you won't be able to get excellent grades.
Take myself as an instance, I had encountered a physic teacher that was extremely strict that he set standards for all the students. All scores under 80 percent in his test would end up as zero and those who flunked would not be able to have break times between the courses. Although my classmates were horrified by this insensible rule and worked extremely hard, they still failed to reach any improvements at all. According to this personal experience, I think it is evident that punishment has less influence on students rather than rewarding or encouraging them. Most importantly, the major conception of educating is to develop the interest and eager of learning and facing challenges. Punishment will only bring frustration to students and results in the lack of self-confidence and less will to learning. Since there's so many disadvantages of school punishment, why not urge to stop it and prepare the perfect way of learning for our students in the future.

subject: HW1001
content: There is no denying that rewarding students for learning is more effective method than using punishment. In my opinion, there are three important reasons why teachers shouldn't control students' behavior by punishing them. First, esteem. Every student deserves respect even though they made some mistakes. If a teacher just punishes a student everytime he makes mistakes instead of teaching him what is the right behavior and encourging him to have confidence to correct his behavior, the student will just feel that he go to school only to be punished and be derived of esteem. Second, confidence. Punishing students will definitely make their confidence in themselves decrease. It is reward that can make students optimistic and believe that they can make it next time. A person without confidence has no difference with one without spirit. If a student has no confidence, apparently, he won't have interests in the class, let alone learning how to behave well. Third, relationship. Relationship is the most vital element to manage a class. However, pushing students will absolutely worsen the relationship between teachers and students. A class without good relationship can never have good interaction in the class. If students don't listen to you, how come you can teach them the right concepts after they make mistakes? As far as I am concerned, there are no advantages of punishing students to control their behavior. It is a traditional and unreasonable way to educate students. We shoud use more positive methods, such as rewarding students for learning or praising them for their good behavior, to build their mind. After all, nobody would have a good feeling after being punished.

subject: HW1001
content:
It needless to say that the punishment has the vicious influence on students. There are many reasons as follows. To begin with, students must be in a overwhelming mood and have a sense of frustration and loss when they fail in the examination. If teachers punish them regardless of their emotion, it will definately deteriorate the circumstance. And the final result may be that the students will lose the confidence in themselves or the passion for learning. In my opinion, the teacher should take the initiative to show concern for frustrated students. That is to say, what the students need is encouragement and some affectionate words instead of punishment in the condition. In addition, there will be more serious impact on students if the physical punishment is permitted at school. It is equal to teach them using violence to solve the problem. Besides, it will do harm to students in physical and in mental.
If the students achieve their goals or perform well in their academic performance or contests, they should win compliments or rewarding from their teachers. In this way, they will have a sense of achievement and enthusiasm for learning.
In retrospect, I clearly remember I had poor performance when I was a elementary school student. Fortunately, I encountered a patient teacher. She gave me encouragement whenever I have bad performance. Her goal is "no student left behind". I made progress step by step. Finally, I caught up with my classmates.
In view of this, I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
I prefer to the idea of rewarding students for learning. If teachers pay more attention to encourage students and give them hope and chances, students will be touched eventually. No matter how hard to teach students to become well or to have good behaves, it is teachers job to let students realize the true meanings of education. Education is to make all students have the abilities to learn new things and to pursue knowledge by themselves. If using punishment to give students a fright, the effect won't be clear and knowing. I think that punishment will sometimes push students into the dark side and let them become depressed and frustrated. If a student can't behave well in a certain part that means she or he has problems handling it, we should help her or him. Before long, students will get used to the punishment and it won't be a motivation anymore.
Rewarding students not just means to give them prize or gifts. I think the most important is to make students who behave well be filled with courage and self-confidence. Teachers can plan to let students make teams and do the teamwork such as answering questions to get one point or the team which average grade is the highest one can get ten points. And when a team get 100 points, they can choose whatever they want to eat to be a reward.
Rewarding is to make students believe in themselves and don't lose the courage to learning. And as doing this, students' hearts can be full of happiness and light.

subject: HW1001
content:
In 21st centery, there are varies of occupations. Not only education but experience are important. In my point of view, there's thousands of ways to keep a living, so there's no need to punish studends to motivate them to learn. The curtain of reasons and details will be drawn in the following paraghs.
First of all, people have different talents. Take Edison as an example, he's not good at schoolworks, but he's curious about everything around him. If we ask, have Edison been punished? The answer is for sure. Thanks to Edison's mother, she chooses to reward than to punish, and lets him do what ever he likes. Today, Edison is well known as an inventor. So there's no need to limit students' talents, they are born for this.
The next to go would be, if we are punished when we fail, people will bear it as a bad experience, but the most important thing we have to remember is that "failure is the mother of succeed." Hoping on my memory journey of learning, I was frustrated when I fail, but the next thing I would do is to climb up and keep moving on. There's no need to be punish, because we've already learned from the experience.
The long and the short of it, rewarding is much worthy than punishments. Partly because people have different talent we shouldn't limit them, and partly because punishments can't gain our courage to improve.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, punishment is more effective than rewarding. Take myself as an example, although I hate being punished very much, when one teacher tell me that I can get extra score on my test by reciting some poem while another teacher tell me he will call my parents if I don't pass the math exam, I will choose to study math for whole day instead of spending a little bit more time on reciting the poem. Being lazy is a kind of human nature, and I think it's only when we are aware of some emergency events will we be diligent. Pushment does appearently better than rewarding in this aspect. However, punishment doesn't always help when it comes to becoming a better person. If the punishment is too cruel or unreasonable, it may hurt the person being punished and end up forming a wrong concept in his mind. I suggest that a reasonal punishment should involve conversation after the course of punishing. In this way, we can ensure that the one punished will definetly understand what he have done wrong and how he can avoid to make the same mistake again. To err is human, and it's important and valuable to learn a lesson from the mistake we made.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I agree with the rewarding students for learning can lead to better results and it is also more effective. Teacher could motivate the students' personal potential and triger out their learning strategies in learning with objects and spirit rewarding as feedback.
The students have lots of potential in different subjects because they all have different background knowledge in their life experience. When they learned with interests and they would like to try their best to achieve the learning goal. Teacher observe their learning style and teach them how to use their learning strategies to enhance learning. They would find learning is fun and interesting.
The feedback is the most important element in learning and teaching. People tend to prevent failure and pursue success in all kinds on situation. The student could know and tell the rewarding feedback is good and helpful for their learning and they would like to do and take it. The rewarding could be objects like gifts, food, trips and reward cards. The goal that they achieve then the students can get the feedback as feedback. The spirit rewarding could also be oral encouragment from the teacher, peer and parents, the words from someone important or famous and the school grades improved.
Therefore, the way to inhance and motivate teaching is a good teaching. In education, teachers have responsibility to demostrate opmistic attitude to treat their students in every ways. Be patient to wait for them to grow up gradually by encouraging their improvement. This is what we want to see our society is happy and progress without fear from punishment and feel free in learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
When I was in the lower grades in elementary school, I started to get used to the life at school. Since then, I have been concerned about whether punishment or rewarding is good to us, because things about this issue happen arround us every day.
In my opinion, I think a teacher who wants to teach his or her students must use both punishment and rewarding in the right time at the right situation. Appropriate punishment can make the students to know what they did is wrong or what they have to improve, while right rewarding can greatly motivate them to do things much more better.
Why do I think like this, maybe because of what I encountered when I was in elementary school. When I was at the third grade, I met a teacher who was young, energective, positive and kind. Though when she started to teach us, some classmates are very naughty. She taught them with patience, she rewarded them greatly when they behaved well, and punished them appropriately at the right time.
Soon, the classmates' behavior changed unexpectedly, and our teacher successfully made our class turn into a good class.

subject: HW1001
content:
As far as I'm concerned, I believe that rewarding students for learning is the better policy of education. Traditionally, students in our parents' generation are threatened by severe punishments when they are students. However, These kind of methods are unappropriate in this generation. The students at present are not as silent as the pasts. They would defy you if you give them stiff punishments.
It is often reported that some parents attempt to accuse their children's teachers because their teachers imposed strict physical punishments on their children. These news apparently show that punishments should not be used anymore. On the contrary, the instructers should teach their students with moderate ways. I believed that each individual is happly to be praised and encouraged. Hence, teachers are supposed to reward their students when they perform excellently on their schoolwork. If students made mistakes or got bad grades, teachers can scold them by language rather than punishment. In this way, students will not be afraid of learning and their moralities will automatically be cultivated from their mind. I believed that this is the best policy of education.

subject: HW1001
content:
Punishing and rewarding students are two things which are regarded as the methods to teach students. In my opinion, I think rewarding students is more effective than punishing students. For most of us, punishment isn't a good memory. Most of all, some may feel humiliated while being punished in front of the class. These students won't change their behavior against their teachers to get their minds balance. Rewarding students is a better way. Having rewarded, these students will be more glorious in their minds. The other students see this and will do their best to win these praises. Rewarding can be a great power to progress students not only learning but also their behavior.
When I was in elementary school, my teacher adopted rewarding instead of punishing. During the math class, teacher would ask some question to us. To show the answers, my classmates and I have to write it down on the small white boards. The more correct answers you wrote, the more candies you would get. By getting rewarded, students in class learned well. In conclusion, rewarding is more effective than punishing to students.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I think that teachers using punishment to motivate students is more effective. But I do not agree the way some teachers do to punish students. In today's newspaper, I can still read that teachers are using some terrible way to control students' behavior, for example, some teachers carry a stick to class in order to correct students' behavior "as soon as possible" or have them do many push ups in amout of time.
