To speak frankly, if students don't do what they should do during class or obey the class rules, they deserve punishment to tell them right from wrong. I'll take my chemistry teacher for example. When he tell us which equation you should memberize and which material you should pay attention to, then he will have a quiz in the day after. All of my classmates, including me, are afraid of not doing well on the quiz, because in his mind, if you didn't do well on the quiz that means you didn't pay attention during class and didn't review what he taught the day before, so you deserve punishment. His punishment is -- standing at the back of the classroom, maybe you think this isn't a effective method, when you stand in our classmates' shoes, this is quite "unique" that everyone else in class are sitting in their seats only you stand up just like the teacher does. I realize this is a good method to help students learn from themselves and do better next time. By the way, we also learn to be more active on our studies.

subject: HW1001
content: In recent years, I often heard of children in schools are punished strictly by teachers. It becomes a controversy problem and everyone has different thoughts. In my opinion, I prefer to rewarding students for learning or studying. Children in this generation are often called "strawberry generation". The main reason is children now are unable to stand too much pressure or frustration, they always tend to avoid the problems and difficulties which they can't get through. I think using punishment to motivate students is less effective than rewarding them. Take myself for example, I was the one who totally understand how different the ways are. Whenever I recalled my childhood, I remembered how my mother taught me and my siblings. My mother is a respectful but strict person, she used to make some specific rules for us to follow. Whenever I made some mistakes, she punished us and even hit us. Although it really made us to follow, it made me feel terrible and unhappy. When I was in junior high school, I met a teacher who is really considerate and kind. She encouraged us and never scolded at us. At that time, I studied harder than before and her way of teaching made every student feel comfortable and pleasant. As a result, I think teachers should encourage students more than punish them. Maybe in this way, students can increase their confidence or even lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I agree that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results and can be more effective, since students always like to be encouraged and complemented. I believe no one wants to be punished and blamed. Moreover, rewarding students for learning is a positive way while punishment to motivate students to learn is a negative way. As a teacher, his or she should give students confidence, not threat instead of pushing them to learn. Students will perform better if they can obtain big reward or present. On the other hand, using harsh way like punishment to control students' behavior is also the worst idea. Students have their feelings, and they are not soldier. Teachers need to use mature methods to communicate with students who don't behave themselves well. Teachers have to find the reason why students behave badly, and then try to find the appropriate way to solve each student's problem.
For example, when I studied in the universaty, I did my best to get the first place in the class each semester. That because I knew I could gain many scholarships if I was the first place in the class and had more opportunity to get other scholarships. So I studied very hard to get these rewards. The rewards and scholarships attracted me to keep learning well. So, during the school life, I was always the excellent students and the best graduate. I was so satisfied and thanked the school for encourage me to perform myself the best. That was my example.
Finally, I would like to say as my experience, I believe the rewarding students for learning does work. It is the best way for students to learn well. The better results is that students like to learn by themselves, not to be pused to learn.

subject: HW1001
content: The ways of punishment and rewarding can both lead students to better results. But in my opinion, punishment only can make temporary effect on students while rewarding them will impact on the future lives. To lead students to better results by rewarding can make them be fond of and willing to learn more. This way, they won't bear too much pressure from teachers but a little from themselves. It benefits learning. For example, when I was in junior high school, most of my classmates didn't like studying and always got bad grades on exams. Our Chinese teacher always punished them when they didn't write homework or did badly in tests. But no one became better. In other hand, our English teacher always treated everyone as the same. Nobody would be "bad student" in her eyes. She taught every student with patience and always praised on us. Everyone enjoyed her class and was willing to learn more after school. The way she used to encourage us has made large impact on my English studying till now. I don't go to cram school to learn English, but I often buy English magazines to read. It really becomes one of my interests.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishments to motivate students to learn, but others use rewarding to our students. In my opinion, I think that rewarding students for learning can cause to better results. I am an elementary teacher, and I discover that rewarding can empower students' confidence and increase their positive attitudes to learn and control their behavior.
A survey shows that punishment may have bad effects on our students. For instance, one of my students always punished by his ex-teacher; Hence, he becomes more coward and be afraid of making mistakes. On the contrary, I give him some chaces to do something. If he does a good job, I will give him rewardings. This way, he becomes more confident and pays lots of attentions to his schoolwork and behavior.
Besides, I always use the rewarding to motivate our students' inner motivations. A proverb says that "attitude determines altitude". Accordingly, we have to use some rewardings to help our students to set positive attitudes. If our students have positive attitudes to everything, they are will to have responsibilites of learning.
In sum, rewarding is a good method to progress our students to learn and to control their behavior. Therefore, they can have responsibilities and confidence on everything.

subject: HW1001
content:
According to these two methods, I believe that each has its prons and cons. However, I tend to agree with teachers who use rewarding as leading the students to better results.
I think students would be more likely to behave well if teachers reward them. In this way, it would constantly increase their confidence to themselves. The students will also believe that the teachers haven't give up to them, and they will try even harder in order to get another reward from the teacher. They will be satisfied whenever they heard a compliment from the teacher. While they gain more confidence, they will learn to perform responsibilities and obligations which will benefit them even more. Take my friend for instance, she feels disappointed to her life until she met an inspiring teacher who encourages her and gave her strength whenever she needs help. She was now a top student in our class, and she felt lucky to have met this teacher.
All in all, I believe that teachers who award students would be the best way to change students behavior.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think the way to rewarding students for learnining is more effective. Although some teachers think that punishment is the most efficient way to motivating students to learn, I don't think this is an appropriate method. Moreover, this can even do harm to some students.
As far as I am concerned, rewarding students when they have well performance can make them gain confidence. In addition, they will be willing to learn in the future. Last but no least, this way is good for their mental as well as physical development. As a consequence, I am in favor of rewarding students for learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
At school, I know that most of the teachers choose to use punishment to motivate students instead of rewarding students for learning. In my opinion, I think that using punishment to motivate students is more effective than rewarding. I believe that everyone is lazy, so we need someone to remind us to learn. Maybe that is why teachers choose to use punishment. If teachers reward students for learning, students might think that even though I don't do homeworks, I will not be punished.
There are two reasons to support my point of view. First, oneday, when I was at elementary school, I forgot to bring one of my book. Then, I was punished by my teacher during the class. I was so embarrassed that I never forgot to bring my books and studied hard now. Secondly, my teacher once tried to reward us for learning. She said who makes a big progress at the test, she would give him or her a big gift and no punishment to those who failed the test. However, after the test, teacher said that only one or two people make progress but most of people did worse than usual. Because the two reasons above, I think that punishment is more effective than rewarding for learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
With the decreasing birth rate, parents would like to pay more on their children's education to ensure that their children will learn happily, efficiently in a "friendly" learning environment. However, students from different family background might have different level of motivation toward learning. As a result, motivating students without punishment has become a big issue in education field.
In my opinion, rewarding should always be used before punishment considering showing respect to students. In other words, if we don't respect our students, how can we expect that they will learn to respect others? And also, rewarding is always the best way to inspire the beauty of one's soul. That's why people say that after physical satisfacation, people start to look for a high level of satisfacation -- self conscious.
Eric, a 1st grader in my class, has been a trouble maker in my class for almost one year. Being talkative, active, and irratating, he has got a very tough situation among friends. I reward him everytime he does something nice, even it is not worth mentioning. His eyes sparkle when rewarded. His smiles get bigger when praised. He now is a loving boy with better behavior. I guess that is the magic of rewarding.
Using punishment to stop bad behavior while using rewarding to inspire good thought, but rewarding shoud always be used for the first place. This is what I believe throughout my 10-year teaching carreer.

subject: HW1001
content:
In modern society, children in their families have become more precious. Since that, teachers had difficulties making their students listen to him or her. In my opinion, teachers reward students for earning can lead to better results. Because when I was in my elementary school, my English teacher always gives me some sweets when I had good grades. And of course, I would study hard in order to have the gifts from my English teacher.
I once heard that a student sneaked out of the classroom after the teacher punished him only because he didn't do well on test. And the story have deeply influenced my concepts on teaching others.
Students now have a lot of pressures on them just like lifting a big rock, and the pressures have almost taken their breath. As a teacher, we should help them, listen to them instead of punishing them.
Hope one day, all the teachers can show their love by rewarding students, not by punishing them and pushing them in the darkness of the society.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the education history, there is always an arguement about whether teachers should use punishment or rewards their students to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. In my opinion, rewarding is better than punishing. Actually, both two ways can reach the goal of education, but nowadays, using punishment to teach students is unappropriate. Also, if a student is under fears of punishment, he couldn't feel the happiness of getting new knowledge, instead, the reason why he studies is to avoid the punishment or pass the test. What's more, everyone's human rise should be respected, even if he is only a student.
Long times ago, I have read a book called "love education", it's about a teacher who never punish her students but lead them by encouragement and love instead. After I read the book, I was deeply touched and I considered "love education" the best way for teachers to teach their students.
If a teacher can lead the students by rewarding them instead of punish them, the students will consider learning a wonderful thing, and there will also be a better relationship between teachers and students.

subject: HW1001
content:
In this highly competitive society, most parents and teachers believe that having a good grade is the only way to success. So they choose to enforce their child and student to study harder, hence, they take two oppisite method: punishment and rewarding. You can also found that punishment is the most common one.
In my opinion, I think rewarding is more effective. Since most parents and teachers think that once have a poor grade or make a mistake, punishment can remind the fault of child. They can learn a lesson by being punished. But they didn't take the side effect into consideration, the condition might get worse, and go into a vicious circle. So I prefer rewarding because it can not only encourage them but also enhence their confidence.
But how to reward? Here are several suggestion. Once they have a good grade, you can complement them and say that you are really proud of them, hoping that they can keep working on. On the other side, once they accidentally made a mistake or got a poor grade, you can take encouragement instead of scorching their fault. Say something that can enhence their confidence, and you are looking forward to seeing their success next time. Besides that, you can also help them figure out the problems and assist them to overcome the difficulty. What's more, never show your dissapointment to your child. Rewarding and encourgement are the best choices.

subject: HW1001
content:
There have been many ways used by teachers to motivate or behave students. Two of them are punishment and rewarding students. The issue of "which one is better?" has received hot debate throghout the history by experienced teachers. In my point of view, I personaly believe that the way of rewarding students would bring better results.
There are two reasons come to my mind. Firstly, the rewarding will keep students working hard to get the prize which had been proved by studies that the reward actions outweight punishments when it comes to learning. Students may become tired whey they are forced to learn instead of learning by their own pleasures. Moreover, when students get used to the punishment and feel nothing about them, then there would be no motivation for learning.
Last but not least, the second reason is that the rewarding is helpful to develop students' characters. The students are motivated to learn new knowledge by their teachers by encouragment. Under the encouraging learning condition, students will develop positive characters and usually see things in the bright side. Furthermore, they may find interests in their learning and develop the sense of life-long learning.
Thus, for the reasons I have just mentioned before make me believed that rewarding outweights punishment when it comes to motivating students' learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
Sometimes I turn on the TV, the big title about the over punishment will suddenly in sight. At that time, I would be confused about what the teachers have done to the students. I would like to encourge students rather than punish them.
There will be plenty of problems when teachers facing their students. When students did something wrong, I think we should tell them right from wrong, not yelling at them and hurting them. For example, if a student always talk to others in the class and are not polite to teachers. The first thing we should do is not angry at him, but calm down his exciting heart. Next, tell them if they follow the class rules, they will get rewards.
I don't like the punishment toward students; instead, we should use something like rewards to improve their behavior.

subject: HW1001
content:
Living in this modern society, teachers have more ways to teach students. Some teachers think they should use punishment, while others belive that rewarding students for learning is the best policy. In my point of view, I think teacher should use both ways to teach their students. If they have some bad behavior or bad habbits, teachers should teach them to cultivate good ideas and reaction. By setting rules and disciplines, they would realize what can do and what they should avoid. Using some punishment, they would lead a good way of life. However, teachers also can compliment on or reward their students. By encouraging them, they might have a possitive attitude and more courage to move on. Here's a story about my opinion.
Years ago, it was a movie called "Jump, boys". The students were gymnasts. They should practice a lot doing gymnastic movements to win the championship. Their teaher was really strict. He would use punishment to correct the students' behavior and movement. However, sometimes he would reward the students doing the best. Through punishment and compliments, they have achieved their goals.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some kids hate to go to school because teachers will punish them whenever they do something wrong; while others go to school with hope and come back home with happiness because they learn more about this world.
In my opinion, encouraging kids instead of punishing them is much more effective. Once children are punished hard for the wrong thing they did, they might lose the passion to explore things, feeling scared and startled. However, if we encourage them and teach them why the things they do are wrong, they will know the reason and the consequences, so they won't do it again.
Several days ago, there was a piece of news, saying that in an elementary school, a nine-year-old boy rejected to go to school on account of the punishment he suffered. His teacher lashed out at him when he didn't do what she had expected. This shows that punishment isn't the right method to educate kids.
In many well-developing country, such as Norway, Finland, United Kingdom and Netherland, they seldom use punishment to teach children; instead, what they use are encouragement, motivations and game playing.
Everyone makes mistakes, so do children. We can't make physical or mental harm on them, and letting their curiosities about the knowledge and the world disappear. Helping them to learn is the educationers' biggest mission.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I prefer rewarding students for learning to using punishment to motivate students to learn. If we reward the students, they will enjoy learning. What's more, this may influence their behavior and thoughts in the future. As a student, I hope I can win something as I do something right. Therefore, rewarding is more effective than punishment, and students will not be hurt.
As far as my personal experience is concerned, I am fond of rewarding the children I taught in the swimming pool. The first day, they usually cried loudly. To make them swim happily and enjoy the fun of swimming, I gave them stickers to exchange the sweets they love, such as chocolate or ice cream. Day by day, they made progress step by step since they wanted my compliment and prizes. With the positive motivation to learn, they will not get tired of swimming absolutely. In addtion, they would love to encourge their family or friends to take part in such activities. After the students being enthusiastic for learning something, they don't need rewarding any longer. And this can be part of their lives.

subject: HW1001
content:
"Spare the rod and spoiled the child", a saying goes like this. But to my opinion, it is not the rod and punishment that makes the motivate students to learn, but the power of rewarding and love to trigger them to perform well.
Punishments might be effective, and most of the time it really works. Without punishments, motivate students may out of control. That will make them harder to aware and sense the rule of party living. But like the wisdom from the philosopher "Lao-Tzu" said: "Give a man a fish, you feed him for a day, teach a man to fish and you feed him for a life time." Education itself should not only be full of punishments, but also to teach a young soul from a motivate student to a mature and responsible adult. That is the origin and brilliant light of education that teachers should always carry with them.
I was a motivate student in my school life, too. So I realize the benefits and disadvantages to punishment and rewarding. We cannot be always be punished or be rewarded. Both of them are important to shape a brave heart and tender soul, knowing about devotion and responsibility well. Finally, I would like to make a conclusion to my opinion, that is: "Teach a man to punish, and you make him to learn about violance. Teach a man to love, and he knows about to love forever." Love is so beautiful, isn't it?

subject: HW1001
content:
In the past, the traditional way to control students is all about punishment. Teachers held the right to punish students without rebellion from parents. However, as time passing, the attitude towards teaching students is changing quite differently from the past. In my opinion, rewarding students for learning is a better way than punishment.
By rewarding students for learning, teachers could encourage them and further make students focusing more on learning. Take myself for an example, my English teacher of junior high offered great prizes for students who got high scores instead of punishing us for not doing well on exams. In that way, everyone would work harder to get the prizes. We later also found out that the greatest prize was actually the progress of our learning through the teacher's encouragement.
In short, punishment has never been the best way to control students. After all, what students need is definitely encouragement, not punishment.

subject: HW1001
content: I agree with the saying that the strict teachers have excellent students. The teachers have followed this rule for thousands of years, and it works. But somebody says that when a teacher punish their students, though the students may become great, the anger to the teacher appear at the same time. So, they suppose that we must throw away our ancient way to teach, replace the punishment with the reward. Usually, the method which reward students to courage them have a good effect. Unfortunately, there are always a few naughty students you have to punish them to make them be quiet and be good. For example, George Washinton, if his father wasn't strict, it would not have been an encouragement to Washinton the only time his father didn't beat him because of his honesty to tell the truth that he felled his father's tree. So, I think we can use appropriate punishment to make the students work hard. And maybe we can say, when we stop punishing, we are rewarding their good jobs.

subject: HW1001
content:
I don't agree with Spartan thinking, children are not machies. It is impossible to have them follow orders we give without any communication. Punishment would never works, when kids are pushed hardly, they tend to act in a rebel way.
Teachers can either punish students or reward them. As a matter of fact, in the school of leading countries, teachers are no longer use punishments, because this is considered bad. They tend to use other ways to solve problems, to let students realize their moves are inpropriate. So I strongly agree with rewarding students. It would be more effective than punishing students. In the movie of "Street Journal", the leading actress was a teacher, she has assined to teach the problematic class. This class is organized by a group of black people. Because of racism they are not treated well. The teacher gave them journals, asks them to write down their stories, she even uses her money to buy new books for those student. Gradually, because of her patience and love, those students accept her, and each of them achieve great success after graduation. This movies shows that patience is the best way, and it always work.
In conclusion, just try to be patient and give students more time, I believe there's nothing couldn't be solved.

subject: HW1001
content:
To motivate students to learn and to control students' behavior, some teachers choose to punish those who do not reach the standard while others believe that rewarding is much more positive in educating. In my opinion, the later one seems more effective. First of all, punishment definately hurt students' confidence. It may cause a student no longer confident in him or herself. Plus, punishment can probably make students to study harder, but they are not willing to get those information to their own will. However, rewarding a student when he or she has some improvement while studying does encourage the student to do better jobs.
Let me illustrate, my younger brothers grade and behavior become pleasing after his teachers' small gifts but turn worse in the result of punishing by his teachers. I feel that punishment to students make them feel awful and unrespected. Therefore, encourging them through regarding may benefit more while teachers want their students to improve.

subject: HW1001
content:
According to a survey done by the educational experts, about 70% of teachers in Taiwan admitted they once tried to force children to learn by punishments, yet the result of the method were totally failed. In the contratry, others using the way by rewarding had got the different outcomes. Then, why could this two methods results in such difference?
With my perspective, the most significent factor between this two approaches is the attitude of an educator. Take my friend Jenny for example, she was a talented but lazy student. Because of her laziness, Jenny often ignored her school work. Teachers considered Jenny as a rebellious girl and found her weakness to punish her regularly. Since the depression, Jenny has had tried to commit suscide for several times.
From the instance above, we can find that punishment is not an adapt way to a successful educator. In my oppinion, children would rather access the rewarding way than being punished. I am a really luck student who always meet good teachers using the rewarding strategy to educate me.
To sum up, motivating students by punishment is not an efficient educational approach to all the recivers and educators. We should really avoid using such vident way to educate our generations.

subject: HW1001
content:
When it comes to stimulating students' learning motivation, people always have different kind of views. In my opinion, I prefer to encourage students by rewarding their good behavior instead of teaching them by punishment. The reasons are obviously simple. First of all, when students are depressed by their poor school performance, they want someone to give them encouragements and useful advice. If teachers treat them with strict punishment, they may feel their every effort to learn is meaningless, so they will not do their best on learning. Secondly, the most imperative thing that students need is confidence on their own. With teachers and parents' assitance and encouragement, their learning confidence can be found back again, and with teacher's rewarding on their better performance, students can do better and better beyond teachers' expection.
For example, in my class during senior high, teachers rewarding classmates' good performance with gifts and snacks, and all of the students in my class are very eager to have such fantastic gift. Little by little, our class has better performance than before, and we always win the ball games by harder practice. By teachers' rewarding, all of us feel that we can do better and better than before.

subject: HW1001
content:
In many schools, some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. But others believe that rewarding students for leaving can lead to better results.
In my opinion, I prefer the sencond way to students, rewarding them. And I have couple of reasons why. The first is that this way would not hurt the little children. If a student did a wrong thing, and the teacher just gave him a huge punishment instead of telling him why he was wrong, then he will do the same thing next time because he didn't know why he can't do this. In contrast, if the teacher rewarded this student in a good mood and tell him what he have to do in the future, this students will not be so scared and he won't be hurt when the teacher punished him. Second, I think rewarding is better than punishing because the friendship between students and teachers will be close. For example, if a teacher punishes the students all the time, will the students still love their teacher? Of course not. But if that teacher gives his students rewards rather than punishment, these students will like their teacher very much and the friendship between them will be closer and closer.
In conclusion, those are two reasons why I choose the second one, rewarding students for learning can lead to better results instead of punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
There is no denying that all teachers want to do has beneficial influence on their beloved students. Even by punishing or rewarding, the teachers main idea is the same-to lead to better results. As far as I am concerned, motivating students with same punishments, like some teachers do, is the better methods in these two ways. There are two reasons that support this though, which I deeply believed in.
For one thing, it is not until the approaching-exams will students start preparing for their studies. Undoubtedly, there should be some motivations to have the students, who are lazy and usually absent-minded, make up their diciplines. If their teachers have some punishments to them, it's easy to see that students will follow the schedule table, leading them to promising future. For instance, take me for an example. Lazy and undiligent am I that I always be flunked in the present. However, after my students going mad and gave me a great punishment, which I would never forget, I became hardworking, controling my behavior is such an easy one for me now.
For the other, many students might cheat in the exam in order to get good grades for awards. And the soothe educational policy can't keep them from doing so, however, the mean one is definitely opposite. No sooner will those who want to cheat in the exam give up struggling than the punishment comes to their mind. Tae my good friend, Tom, a bad-habit student, for an example. Upon Tom was cheating in the test one day, our teacher came in. there are no words can decribe the terrifying situation that Tom was in. since then, to every classmates' surprise, Tom become a person that seldom make mistakes and be honest when taking the exams. Indeed, this can be credled to the right policy that the teacher made.
To sum up, it cannot be more emphasize about the importance of punishment. even though the soothe one is not bad, the mean one might be more appropriate to students, even more effective to them.

subject: HW1001
content: As far as we know, teaching methods of teachers has aroused much attention nowadays. Some teachers us punishment to motivate students, some rewards students. In my opinion, both of them have advantages. It depends on what kinds of students you teach. If the student is rude and selfish, regular punishment is more effective. On the other hand, if the student can do things right by rewarding, you have to use it. For instance, I played the piano when I was young. When I finished my practice, my mom would give me a new toy as a reward. Because of the reward, I would like to practice the piano again and again. But my brother is the exception. Although you give him something he likes, he doesn't follow your words. When facing these kinds of things, the best way to control my brother is give him a punishment. In this way, teaching students won't be a trouble for teachers anymore!

subject: HW1001
content:
To my opinon, I think that rewarding students for learning is more effective. Because make students to behave well by punishing them is not a method that can be used long. When students are in young ages, they may be afraid of being punished and behave themselves well, but when they grow up, they will no longer afraid of punishments and do what they want to do or ignore what the teachers say.
Rewarding students for learning is a better method to lead students to the right way, it because that they might feel couraging when receive presents or medals as a reward, and they will do their best to get rewards next time. Teaching students in this way, they will be glad to learn and gain more confidence. The good learning recycle will effect more and more students, and make them have love of learning and behaving well. Not only teachers but also the students' parents will be plesant to see so.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some people think that teacher use punishment can inspire students to work hard, but I don't think so. In this way, students might give up themselves, and even hate their teacher.
In contrast, rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Take my brother for example, he used to be a bad student, who just hung out with his friends all day and didn't study. One day, his teacher told him that if he got a 100 on exam, he would treat my brother to Fridays for dinner. My brother began trying to work hard, finally he made it! The relationship between he and his teacher became better and better, and he got confidence in study as well.
In my opinion, teachers who reward students for learning, such as scolarhsip or something, are useing the more effective method to teaching students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Rewarding students for learning is a better choice for me. People of all ages many encounter challenges. Most of us get afraid and wouldn't believe in our abilities. Encourgements from our parents, friends, and even teachers usually make us more confident and lead us to start to try getting across difficulties with different methods. When we start trying, we are improving.
I have met many kinds of people who face their students and friends in different ways and have learned a lot. Once, I met a classmate in elementary school. He was strange indeed. Wearing strange clothes, doing strange things, all that you can think of. My teacher couldn't bear this and often beat him with a stick. I found it that he never apologized with his heart but became sad and san. I started to talk to him and tried to be a friend to him. We spent a lot of time together doing homework and joining in activies. Always telling him he was great and encouraging him to improve really changed him. And I knew that this was the best way to lead a person to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the past, teachers beat up the students for bad behavior, they says its a leason of teaching the students how to control themselves.
But I think it was wrong, humans are not like animals, humans have more emotions than animals, because of that, punishment caused shadow in the students mind, even consquenced in suticide.
In Taiwan gang members in school is very usual, because of the shadow in the student's mind, the shadow turns into anger, the anger made them into a bitter man, and desire to revange, that why many thought convict of bully or violence can be find on most of the student's blog or diary.
It is twenty first centry, the world of freedom, freedom comes for revolution, revoluting is made of bloods and countless lifes, the price of freedom is so expensive, because it is our's true mind, so why would anyone wants to be punish in school for not obeying what the teacher said to do or not to do.
I think we should rewarding the students for good behavior, becaus of the reward, their thought of learning will be joyful, and turn into willing of studing by themself not by the methods outside.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers believe that using punishment is a effective way to motivate students to learn and control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding students for learning is a more effective way to lead the students to better results.
I believe that to reward the students who done well will be a more effective method for teachers to teach students. When you reward the students who done well, those who wasn't rewarded would like to have the same treatment. And they'll have to behave well to earn this treatment. By this way, you can lead your students onto the right way. But those who punish the students when they misbehave are setting an example of violence, and it may effects what the student will do when they grown up.
When I was in elementary school, there was a spelling bee contest every month in my class. At first, most of the students were not interested in memorizing the spelling words for the contest. But after the first contest, the winner got a box of ice-cream as a reward. Well, this reward really encouraged the class to work hard on memorizing the spelling words. I supposed that this is a great example for the method of rewarding those who done well. We seldom heard teacher punishing their students recently. I think that is because a lot of parents are against those punishment, and also, most teachers learned that rewarding the students are really a good and effective method to lead their students onto the right path.

subject: HW1001
content: I firmly believe that rewarding students for learning can undoubtedly lead to better results, because it is much more affective to make students behave themselves from the bottom of their hearts. Punishments can be good choices when you are in need of the instant changes of students, but they change for fear of the ashamement to be punished or scolded, not because they really change. As a result, once the students were out of the control of the teachers that would punish them, it is highly possible that they make the same mistakes. Take myself as an example. I used to be late for school when I was in junior high school. Somedays my teacher would warn me or even give me punishments, and I would not be late for a few days after that. But I continued my habit soon after I forgot the pain to be punished. Untill one day, my teacher talked to me and let me know that how this habit can harm me in the future, and also promised that if I never did it again she would reward me, and then I changed forever. That's why I consider rewarding and encouraging students in learning and their attitude toward life will be the method that is indeed useful.

subject: HW1001
content:
Education has always played a very important role in our life and the develop of our personality, high educated people enjoy higher social status and better treatment, and those who aren't well educated don't. The age of the "As long as you are good at something, you can get a well-payed job even if you aren't a great student." no longer exist, so, learning in a good way is very important in our modern life.
Nowadays, some teacher use punishment to motivate their students to learn and to control their behavior, while others believe that by rewarding the students for learning can lead to better result, in my state, I would say that they both work perfectly on diffrent students. Using punishment is most effective on students who are lazy and don't like to study or finish their assingment, by this way, for fear of the punishment these students tend to study hard and get good scores to stay away from it. On the other hand, rewarding these student won't work because for them, no reward seems to be attractive enough to drag them away from computers and televisions. However, this way works perfectly on those who have desire for honor and good comments, if these students recieved some gifts or being honored by the teacher, they tend to study harder in order to get more good comments or gifts. These are the things that motivate them to study harder and harder.
I've once report a news about a phycologist having a experiment on this, the students were devided into two groups, the lazy ones and the benefit pursuaing one. By using punishment and rewarding each for a week, the punishment week's average score was A+, the rewarding week's average score was B-, according to the students, punishing them can kill their laziness, and let them get used to studying, and the benefit pursuaing group leads to opposite result to them, study hard seems to be the only way for reward and honor.
Education is important, however, the way of eduction is important too. Diffrent ways of education fits on diffrent types of students, there fore, leaving how to use the right ways seems to be the priorty mission for the teachers and fitting it well is the student's.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think rewarding students for learning is more effective than using punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. When a teacher punishes his students by using sticks to hit them, they may feel not good or maybe angry with their teacher. And the student may be more unvulunteer to do the homework the teacher gives. In the contrary, when a teacher awards his students of doing well in the class, at the moment, the students may bust into happiness, and they will be more willing to do their best to show their capability to the teacher.
Like me, for example, I used to be punished by my teacher because I was usually late for school. So I was hit by my teacher for many times. A semester later, I found that I couldn't quit being late for school. Everything change till one day, my teacher gave me a present as a result of my on-time for school. I was so terrific that I can't help but cry my teardrops out. I told myself I would never be late again.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays it is usual to see some teachers arguing with some parents, for the student frequently make troubles. Hence, some teachers use punishment rather than correct students' faults by alarms or giving some suggestions to them. I am strongly pro that teachers should give rewards on students' learning.
To begin with, teachers are endowed with responsibility to teach students. However, they should also be aware of students' emotional attachments to learning. Sometimes teachers need to encourage students to make progresses on studies and understand why students fail in the exams. Take myself for example, when I was in junior high school, I was not good at science. Every time I studied hard, I still failed. The teacher used punishment to force us to study. If students got below sixty, he would punish us by stick. I was always one of the students who received punishment. Though teachers used punishment to spur us, I did not benefit from it. Oppositely, I was afraid of science. Therefore, I don't want to use punishment; instead, I prefer to give students rewards.

subject: HW1001
content:
Rewarding students is a better way in teaching field. A student can be easily motivated when given an oral reward or a physical prize in the class. They feel they are in progressive in learning when teachers give them positive encouragement, and therefore, they are willing to study harder in return. And when teachers see the good result once students do so, then, I believe, they are happy to do their best in teaching. This is a win-win situation, isn't it?
I have a cousin who is now a senior high can prove my opinion. When he was junior high school student, he was often scolded or punished by his teachers and parents owing to his awful grades in every field. Luckily, an English teacher changed this. The teacher, Wang, encourged my cousin with every positive way to motivate him. And now, my cousin is a good student at school.
So, I believe rewarding students is a better way in teaching and can lead good results.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the past, teachers tended to use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. However, in my opinion, rewarding students for learning is more effective.
All the people like to be rewarded, and so do the students. If they are encouraged, they will do their best to do something better. Take me as an example. When I was a junior high student, I wasn't interested in learning English and always got bad scores on the English tests. Then I met a very patient English teacher. She told me that my pronunciation was very good and encouraged me to read some interesting English materials. When I got improved on my tests, she always gave me a hug or a big smile. Since that time, I can not quit reading English books or watching TV programs every day.
On the contrary, punishment can not make students to obey the teachers or learn something from their heart. They are just unwilling to follow the teacher's directions, and they can not keep the good behavior for a long time. Therefore, rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
As for me, I would be favor of punishment I think punishment is far more effective than just rewarding the students. Because there are various forms of punishment which you can use to make them learn a lesson. It is totally wrong that punishment is confined to just one form: corporal punishment. You can express it in many ways. The reason why I don't choose rewarding is that you will gradually spoil a child through every reward you give.
My elementary school life is a suitable example to prove and support my point of view. When we don't behave well, she always tells us to clean the classroom as a punishment. Besides, if we don't hand in our homework on time, we should deliver a speech in front of the whole class. Furthermore, cracking a joke for the whole class is necessary if you talk with you classmates in class. Through all these punishments, I learn a bunch of lessons. My teacher uses different forms of punishment, however, not including corporal punishment The punishments I got not only enhance my ability of delivering a speech but also have me make a difference to the environment of the class. Therefore, punishment is still better than just rewarding.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students is more effective than using punishment in teaching students in the class. In the past, our social perspective think that a teacher who have exercised physicial punishment on students is a good teacher, but they don't consider the responses of students in their mind. The students who have been gotten physical punishment are usually easier to downgrade and give up themselves. Finally, they escape the real world and become a lonely person. On the contrary, a teacher using rewarding ways to motivate students could protect students' dignity and give students one chance to correct their behaviors. In this way, students are usually grateful for the teacher to give him a chance and it is easier to stand up again for them. So, I prefer rewarding students than punishment.
In the class, if a student made a mistake, it would not be the end of the world. If I were a teacher, I would call the student to give him a chance to explain his wrongdoing. After a explanation from the students, I realized the fact why he did the wrongdoing, and I would analyzed the advantages and disadvantages to him. The student would learn a lesson from this experience and correct it. If they meeted the same situation again, they would think twice before they act. I think it is a good way to help student stand up again.

subject: HW1001
content:
In order to make students learn and control their behaviors, many teachers choose punishment to achieve the goals. In my opinion, however, I think rewarding students for learning would be a better and efficient way because of two major reasons. First, students will know that learning is such a happy thing and they will learn "actively" by rewarding them. Forcing students to learn may make them feel pushy and reduce their motivations in learning. Secondly, students will put more efforts on study for getting rewards. Rewards, they're not only an encouragement for studying but also an agreement toward their accomplishments.
Take one of my students for example, he is a person who is lazy in learning but actually very smart. Because of knowing that he is just lazy and unwilling to study, I blamed on him and even asked his mother to punish him for his lazy. I thought he would study hard after being punished; however, I was totally wrong. His performance started to get worse. Not only that, he even wanted to quit his study. This situation became better after I rewarded him to study instead punished. From this case, I realize punishing is not the best way for pushing students to study. Rewarding them is more effective instead.

subject: HW1001
content: I think it is more effective when some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior, but it must be used in a proper way. There was a classmate in my class whose name was James. He was a naughty boy that he would come up with some evil thoughts to play trick on others in our class. The time when I were sitting with him almost killed me. I couldn't help but tell our teacher, Ms. Lin, what he had done to us. Ms. Lin was a young, kind and tender teacher, who had never scolded anyone. Despite the fact that she was really angry with him, she just told him to be good and supported him to have creative ideas which could be used in a right way. The day after, James pulled off the chair which my best friend was going to sit. "Bang!" A loud sound shocked the whole room. Some classmates looked at them agaping. Then my best friend cried and so did Ms. Lin. My best friend was sent to the hospital and was said to be paralyzed in her life later on. Tears rolled down my cheek upon hearing this. Ms. Lin quitted. The whole class were in a shade of sorrow and couldn't be cheered up. I think it was better for Ms. Lin to be strict on James and to punish him or at least blame on him. So that I wouldn't lose my best friend and Ms. Lin might not have to quit, further more James would not have make this unforgiving fault.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers are used to punishing students when teaching in schools. However, in my opinion, giving punishments is not a good way but rewarding students is much more effective. I think teachers regarding punishment as a way when teaching students are inhuman. The students would sometimes get injured and they may not realize the authentic reasons why they are punished. They just correct their behavior tentatively to avoid punishments.
On the contrast, rewarding students is much better. For instance, when I was in the primary school, there was a naughty boy in my class. He used to chat during the class, which annoyed my teacher and other classmates. At first, my teacher blamed him and punished him for his bad behavior. However, the boy didn't correct his behavior at all. Then, my teacher started to give him a candy after class as long as he kept quiet during the whole class. It was effective. He at first just wanted to have the candy but finally he knew that chatting during the class was wrong. I always think it was a good example of teaching students in a proper fashion.
I think that rewarding students is much more effective when educating students. The students will learn the correct things in a glad way and will not be afraid of the teachers.

subject: HW1001
content:
There we see lots of news reporting inappropriate physical punishment at schools nowadays, while there are news reporting how the good teachers reward the students to encourage them. Comparing the two educating methods, I think the latter one is better and more effective.
I believe encouraging words motivate a student's efforts to behave well the best. Positive teaching attitude can lead to well-focused improving spirit, and when both teachers and students feel they are highly respected by one another, the interaction during the class is certainly improved, making a wonderful environment for everybody. Not only when it comes to learning, but also the behaviour. I see the influence among the peershow it teaches a bad-manner person behave oneself, and the progress on their studies. That's why I think rewarding and encouraging words or attitude make the students behave the best.
When I was in kindergarten, I often got scolded for eating late at lunch. The punishment was standing outside the classroom and finished my meal; it was terrible enough for a five-year-old kid. I have been wondering if the teacher could have changed the way to make me eat faster. And after I left the kindergarten, I started understand that a positive, inspiring way can lead to a very different result, which can also reach the same goal.

subject: HW1001
content:
As for me, I am in favor of rewarding students for learning on the ground that most students, especially teenagers, need someone to praise them when they behave themeselvs well. Besides, the teachers are supposed to help their students to find their confidence in study again. When they fail the test instead of punishing them or scolding at them. I'm convinced that only through love and compliments can teachers lead students to success.
Take two friends of mine, Tom and Jack for example, Tom, my junior high classmate, had an unhappy childhood. His parents divorced when he was little. So, because of lack of parental love, he went astray. However, lucky enough, he met a wonderful teacher. She never gave up him. She not only talked to him in a solf voice but also rewarded him whenever he did the right things. Therefore, Tom turned over a new leave and led a good life. Jack, on the other hand, encountered a inpatient teacher. His teacher scolded at him when he got poor grades. What's worse, he even smack him on the cheek whenever he did something wrong. Thus, needless to say, Jack ran away from school and joined the gangster. Hence, rewarding students for learning always better than using punishment to motivate students to learn.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the past, teachers always carried a stick while they were teaching their students. With a stick, teachers can punish the naughty students and give them a lesson not to do the same thing again. In contrast, more and more human rights group claim that punishment will leave shadows behind on children's minds and make them feel uncomfortable when they are being punished. Therefore, they would reward the good students rather than punish the bad students. In my opinion, punishment is needed when a student does something wrong.
Take my brother, Wayne, for example. Wayne was such a naughty boy that he always did everything he wanted to do and never cared about how others felt. One day, Mom got a phone call from his teacher and she realized Wayne pushed his classmate to the ground. That unfortunate student was sent to the hospital immediately. Mom went to school and picked up Wayne. But my brother didn't think he was wrong and his attitude showed that he was right Mom was so upset that she used a tube to punish him. In the end, Wayne cried for forgiveness and became a nice boy. I think this story tells me that punishment is indispensable for people who do the wrong thing.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some may claim that punishing students can motivate them to learn and control their behavior. On the other hand, some insist that students should be rewarded to lead to better results. In my opinion, I firmly believe that rewarding students is more effective for the following reasons.
First, students should be confident. By giving rewards to them, they will be sure of themselves. They would be more confident of their own work in the future.
Second, students should be independent. Punishing students to motivate them wouldn't make them an active learner. In the future, there won't be someone behind them telling them to work hard. They have to be able to do the right thing in the correct situation without being punished.
Last but not the least, rewarding students encourage them to find their passion in learning. They would be more eager to engage in study. In the future, they would study to get more knowledge, not to avoid from getting punished by the teacher.
In conclusion, students should find their passion in learning, be independent, and also be confident. After all, teachers should let students understand that learning can benefit them, not to avoid getting punished by the teacher. It's crucially important for teachers to lead students to a correct study habit and enjoy the fun while study. For all of these reasons, I believe that rewarding students for learning is a better perspective for teachers.

subject: HW1001
content: Thanks to the fear of being punished, students may prevent doing the same things again and study harder. So, I think it will be more effective if the teachers use a little punishment. In fact, when I was in junior high school, my teachers would punish us when we didn't do well on the exams or we did things which are really improper. They always had us brush the floors until the floors became very clean and white. That was pretty tired and took us a lot of time. However, I could think why I was punished and what I should do to make up the mistakes when I cleaned the floors. In order to prevent being punished again, I would remind myself not to do the same things again and studied harder. At that time, I really learned a lot of things and behaved well. Now, I'm in senior high school, my teachers won't punish me anymore. So I become a little lazier now. I think it's pretty awful. Since the own experience I had before, I think that the punishment really can motivate students to learn and behave well.

subject: HW1001
content: Everything has pros and cons, including punishing and rewarding. First, let's talk about punishment. Usually, teachers punish students when they make mistakes or behave bad. However, I think that's just keep students from not learning but not encourage them to be enthusiastic in learning. For example, if we punish students whose grades are lower than sixty, the result may be that most students' are higher than sixty, but there are seldom students who get really high scores like ninety or even higher. But, when it comes to encourging, the situation will almost be in the contrast. If we reward students by seeing how great they perform, then they will try their best to learn and to get the reward. The more you learn, the more reward you deserve, this will encourage them to do their best, and maybe they will start to compete with others. At the end, teachers may not need to offer any reward, or just praise them verbally, and they will become better and better just by competing with their peers. For instance, there is a test today, and the teacher says "Those who get the score over sixty deserve a candy, and those who get the score over eighty deserve two." Most students will try hard to get the score over eighty to win two candies, and those who just get one will also be happy, for their efforts are worth it. Everyone is happy, and everyone like learning. So, obviously, I prefer the method of rewarding students for learning. But the only drawback is, rewarding students can't encourging those students who really have no interest in learning. Maybe, the best way is to combine both rewarding and punishing.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think there is no right answer to this question. Because people born in different families and they have different backgrounds, personalities and thoughts. Different students should be taught in different ways. Otherwise, it may lead to worse results if the method is wrong.
Forexample, I have a brother who is smart but naughty. He used to enter a good junior high school. The school gave students much freedom and had lots activities. My brother's grade slided down quickly. After he translated to other school which was strict. The punishment really worked. He got good grades on the final test.
Another example was one of my friend, Cara. Her teacher used to punish her when she got bad grades. She felt stress and frustrated. Her parents talked to teacher and advised the teacher to give reward if Cara do well. Cara didn't feel nervous any more and did a good work on study.
By this two examples, we can know it is important to find a right way to teach student. We should realize that everyone is different, and should be taught in different ways.

subject: HW1001
content:
How to motivate students to behave well and be willing to learn is always one of the most important lessons for teachers. Though corperal punishments were extincted in Taiwan, some teachers might feel exhaulsted to find out motivable ways to teach students' behaviors. In my opinions, no matter what methods the teachers adopted, they should revise the methods depending on the situations. Most importantly, they should be ware not to "over used" the methods.
For example, some teachers like to give rewards when students get good grades or behave well. They use points or stamps to assemple the rewording. Once students collect enough stamps, they can exchange a present like a doll or game cards. This is a good way to motivate students control themselves. However, when a small gift is not appealing enough for students to persue, the teachers start to choose other more expensive or "more attractive" rewards as the goal, which makes students form a false value on persuing practical materials but not really behave well.
In fact, I am a starting teacher in a junior high school. From my experiences, children hate punishments when they do something wrong. Rewards of course make them happy, but for some low-proficiency students, the standard to get a reword is actually too high for them to acheieve. Then, they just give up themselves trying. So every time before a test, I give different standards for each student. In this way, every student has a goal that suit oneself.
A good method that motivates students to learn can help them to improve themselve a lot. While using it wrong may get a worse effect on students. That's all teachers should be careful.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, some teacher use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.
In my opinion, what kinds of ways do we teach students is according to what kinds of students we meet. But at the most time I prefer to reward students for learning than punish them. Because I think making a deal with students is better than let them be afraid of me. For example, if a student doesn't like to study and you just keep forcing him to study or keep punishing him then I think he will have a deep hatred to study. On the contrary, if you keep encouraging him or making deal with him such as give him a wish that is not too hard to achieve and make it come ture. I considered that he will have more motive to study and when he get good grades he will have more confident to keep going.
Above all, I prefer "love teaching" but it needs not only teachers' but parents' help. If everyone can make it to practice, each student in Taiwan can study happily and learn joyfully.

subject: HW1001
content:
First, I think that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, students are always in high confidence. If you use punishment to control the students, it may be a big mistake.
For example, if the students who are punished are self-centered, they will trick you to against you. Sometimes it may be more terrible in that the students who got insane, you will be hit or injured deadly.
Besides, if the students who are punished are cowards. It may let them into more depression so that they are afraid to ask anybody about the problems on the study or it may cause suicide deadly.
In conclusion, I think that rewarding students for learning is the best method. Unlike the punishment, it will not cause the students to feel uncomfortable. It can encourage students to spend time in learning and prohibit the quarrel between the students and teachers. So I prefer to reward students rather than punish the students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Education is very important to every kid. However, What are good ways to teach children?
In my opinion, I think that whether using punishment or rewarding depends on the child's personality. Take me for example, I am a sensitive and shy girl. All things can easily make me feel nervous. Nevertheless, my mother used to agreed with the concept of using panalty to teach children. She often blamed on me when I did something wrong in my childhood. Therefore, I became unconfident and were afraid of doing everything. After noticing this, my mother tried to relieve and made up her mind to change the education upon me. With her encouragement, prize, and compliment, I turned into a happy and independent girl now.
The above is my experience. It shows that some people can only build up their confidence by giving them a big hand without punishment. In contrast, some kids will not follow our advice unless we force them into listening to us. The number of this kind of children tends to increase these year. Nowadays, many kids are spoilded and need some punishment to teach them lessons. Simply that, parental education should reach the balace between punishment and compliment.

subject: HW1001
content:
As the proverb goes, "Education is the foundation of a nation", we should motivate students by good methods actively. In my personal opinion, I believe that rewarding students for learning is better than punishment. students would learn much more better if ther are encouraged. On the other hand, punishment would keep students from learning.
Taking myself as an example, my mother always encourage me to study hard and push me forward, which makes me learn actively and have no fear of any kind of exams. However, some of my friends are afraid of learning due to punishment and stress.
To sum up, I do enjoy learning since my mother encouragement which keep supporting me forward, and I strongly believe that rewarding makes me so.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers regard punishment as an effective way to motivate students to behave themselves while others reward students for learning. Both side consider their methods the best way that leads to better results, and it's quite difficult to determine which one is absolutely right.
Punishment for students, though always controversial, is an "efficient" way to force students to behave themselves. The scary physical pain and feelings of shame carve a deep imprint on students mind and stimulate them to study harder or behave better next time in order to avoid facing the horrible punishment again. However, it also casts a shadow on children's vulnerable mind. For instance, during my first grade at elementary school, I was punished in front of the whole class because I had made the same mistake on my test. It was such a shame for me that I didn't dare to look straight into my teacher's eyes for several days!
On the other hand, rewarding students seem much friendlier than punishment. rewarding becomes an attracting incentive that unconsciously fills students' mind with ambition. Ambitious students longing for the fantastic reward and a sense of accomplishment will spare no effort to improve themselves. Neverthless, rewarding students for learning may lead to a fact that students make great effort only for more and more rewards and forget their initial goal. I have got a diligent cousin who is praised by everyone for her good grades, and she regards others' praise as her rewards. However, she once told me "I'm so tired. I found myself lost in the pursuit of rewards and I can't even recall the dream I have before!"
Comparing the pros and cons of these two methods, I refer to rewarding students as a more effective way. Since both ways can force students to have a better performance, rewarding seems to be a milder way. As long as students can always remind themselves of their initiatives, I regard rewarding as the most suitable way for them.

subject: HW1001
content: The education problem has much to do with our life. Therefore, many education experts provid some advices. Some think punishment is worth, others believe rewarding is better. For me, I regard that rewarding students is better than punishment. Every student does not like punishment and afraid of it, so, in the bigining they all behavior themself because of the punishment. But, that is temperary not for long time. In contract, if we give students rewarding when they do thing well, they will feel happy and would like to do this next time. Take me for example, when I was in elementary school. I was bad on math, usually recieved bad record. But, my teacher didn't punish me, he gave me some advices, hoping me could do well in next test. Because the teacher's rewarding, I had more confidence and not gave up any more. Even today, I still thankful for my teacher. If he punished me that time, I may hate math forever. So, the power of rewarding is more stregth than punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
Recently, some incidents with regard to teachers' punishing students are reported by mass media, which raises awareness of Taiwan's educational system. In the past, strict parents agreed that teachers used punishment to motivate their children. However, the trend has changed. Parents are inclined to hoping that children learn without pressure and punishment in the school. In my opinion, I agree that teachers take advantage of appropriate punishment to motivate students. This kind of mathod is sure to be more effective than reward only.
Take myself for example, I'm a senior high school student. What bothers me the most during the class is my classmates' dicipline. Sometimes, their chatting is so loud that some attentive students even can't hear what the teacher is say. In order to solve the problem, the teacher uses reward as an induction to improve some students' concentration but to no avail. Finally, the teacher regulates the class rule clarifying what kind of punishment should be inflicted on absent-minded or chattering student.
Surprisingly, the effect is extremely good. Few students dare to chat during the class. In addition, I realize that punishment is absolutely an effective measure to motivate students to learn.

subject: HW1001
content: It is important for teachers to find their own way to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. In my view, rewarding is much more efficient than punishment. According to psychological researchers, using punishment to correct students' behavior may be useful for one or two times. Students soon will redo what is forbiddened. As regard to rewarding, researchers believe that students may seek tangible reward at the beginning, however, a sense of fulfillment will then replace the tangible gifts. The sense of fulfillment is believed to last much longer than frightening of punishment. In addition, rewarding makes students confident. A confident student is less likely to behave bad and is encouraged to work harder in their learning at the same time. Taking myself as an example, I had been praised by many teachers during my high school life. Because of the rewards, I considered myself as a person who is able to have terrific performance on school works. Hence, I spent more time studying to meet their words. On the contrary, I did not do well in my first year in the college. No compliment and no rewarding. I did not care about the grades as much as I had done in high school. Sometimes teachers used punishment to motivate me to learn, I just worked unwillingly and passively. And as researchers' belief, I stopped working hard soon because I was not willing to do what I was asked to do. To sum up, rewarding can not only encourage students but also make them confident. It is much more efficient than punishment in motivating students to learn or controlling their behaviors.

subject: HW1001
content: In the past, most people advocated that physical punishment enabled students to enhance the efficiency in studying, and behave themselves. However, a number of people believe that rewarding students for learning is more likely to make students interested in learning and perform better on many aspects. In my opinion, rewarding students for learning is more effective. There are several reasons. First of all, rewarding students instead of giving them phisical punishment in the process of learning can motivate them. Motivation of learning is the fountain of success. Furthermore, students will get hurt mentally and physically when teachers scold or punish them, which will probably lead to terrible imapact on students. Moreover, rewarding students for learning can strengthen the relationship between teachers and students. It is sure that students will learn more effectively because of the joyful atmosphere in clase. Last but not least, the more teachers treat students with love, the more students will gain. Take me for example, when I was in elementary school, my teacher emphasized on giving love to others, which made a great influence on me and made me a better person and enabled me to progress on my study. In brief, rewarding students for learning not only is more effective, but influence students to be useful people.

subject: HW1001
content: Nowadays, some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, teaching with carrots is more effective than teaching with sticks. Thinking of my life in elementary school, once I got a test paper with score 85 and my classmates, Winston, who is also my neighbor, got a test paper with score 93. After school, we went home together. My mother ran out of the house and gave me a hug for improving a lot and getting 85. By contrast, Winston's parents hit him for 7 times with a wooden stick, because he lost 7 points in the test. Time is flying, although I don't live at there now, I hear some news of Winston. He is addicted to drug, being the head of gang-society, having tattoo all over the body, betraying his parents and has many dangerous behavior. It goes extremely different, I have the bright future and live happily. Teach with carrots or sticks? As a matter of fact, teaching with carrots, rewarding students for learning is more effective and good for the development of children.

subject: HW1001
content: As a saying runs, "Spare the stick, spoil the child, " some teachers are of the opinion to use punishment to motivate students to learn. Though, others are convinced that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. I think there are both pros and cons of both statesments. From my perspective, using punishment seems to be much more effective because I was punished by my teacher in the primary school when I got bad grades on an exam. While I was being punished, I would question myself whether or not I hadn't tried my level best studying. Moreover, I regarded punishment as a motivation to make an advance. However, I frequently see some teachers punish their students too much on TV. It is often reported that the teachers use an evil way to punish their students. The teachers are accused of being violent. Exposed to such violence, the students might be under great pressure, and they are afraid of their teachers. In other words, punishment may have negative influence on students. Therefore, it is believed that only brutal teachers would punish students and that amiable teachers would praise students. In conclusion, a teacher should find out a proper way to treat different kinds of students. Also, a teacher can comprise with parents to decide how to teach their children, so that students can learn happily and healthily in the school.

subject: HW1001
content: Nowadays, we can often hear the news about teachers punished their students just because they didn't do well on tests. In my opinion, I think those teachers don't know what students really need. As a student, I think punishment is not the best way to solve problems. I believe that teachers can praise students instead of punishing them. Everyone wants to listen to good thing. And if you say something bad about them, they may be mad. I read a story in a book before. A teacher told the class leader to write down the names of the students in class who were naughty. The first day, many people talked, so the teacher was unhappy and punished the students. Several days passed, many people still talked, and the teacher kept punishing them. Until one day, the teacher was astonished that nobody talked. She asked the class leader what had happened. The class leader smiled and took out a paper. She wrote down the names of students who were quiet. All students in the class wanted to be praised by the teacher, so they obey the class rules. So I think that rewarding students is more effective, everyone wants to be rewarded. Undeniably, many teachers just want their students to be obedient, so they punished them to control their behavior. I support that rewarding is more effective, but it doesn't mean that punishments are all wrong. I think that some rebellious students need a good beating. Then what teachers have to do is to make a balance between punshing or rewarding.

subject: HW1001
content: Some teachers prefer using punishment to motivate their students to learn and to control their behavior, while I strongly support that rewarding students for learning would be better. The reasons are as follows. First, no one want to be punished, and neither do I. Though punishing students sometimes can make them do better in a short time, students still don't know why they should do that. They just know that if they don't fullfill what the teacher expects, they would be punished. I don't think it is education. However, I think rewarding students is a better way to educate them. Teachers should tell the students why they should learn and behave well and teach them how they can do. In this way, students would really want to learn and behave well from their hearts. Take myself for example, I met a serious teacher in my elementary school. She always punished me when I didn't do well or failed the test. She punished me for my mistakes and even hit me. During the hard time, I always felt upset and afraid to school. Luckily, the next year, I met a nice teacher, Lily. Instead of punishing me all the time, she always encouraged and rewarded me whenever I did well or failed it. It was my dear Lily teacher who made me happy during school days and love learning everything. Without her, I think I wouldn't be interested in learning. To conclude, I believe that rewarding students for learning is the best way to educate them. Also, it can lead to better results.
