If I were a teacher, I would be a teacher like my favorite Lily teacher. I would like to encourage and reward my students, and lead them to a better future!

subject: HW1001

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, punishments serve as the more effective tool to motivate students to learn. My reasons are as follows. Despite the fact that some students are active, the majority of students need punishments to trigger them to study. Another reason is that punishments can warn students not to make repeated mistakes. With punishments, teachers can effectively command students to learn. The last but not the least, some opponents may question that punishments are likely to block students' creativities. content: In my opinion, I will say using punishment to students is more effective to make students behave as teachers' expectations immediatly. such as: good scores, disiplined behavior, good manners ....etc. it's humen nature to avoid from punishment. If teachers threat to punish them, most students might try harder to achieve the goal. However, in the long term, punishment can not necessarily lead to better results. Once the students graduate from schools, many of them stop learning or reading because the threats from teachers or parents are gone. On the contrary, rewarding students for learning might be a slower method. It can influence the students in a good way. With no fear, they might enjoy learning more in the future. Hence, there are advantages and disadvantages for both ways. I think, using them appropriately is the most important lesson teachers and parents must learn.

subject: HW1001
content: The problem that how to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior still remains a delima. However, I agree with the solution by rewarding students. In my opinion, everyone has a desire that they want to be honored. To stay in the peak and let others respect them, people would spare no effort to achieve their goals. Once teachers rewarded the student, they may have more and more to power to do better next time. Or others may prepare themselves, equip themselves with strong desire to get the honor. When I was in the primary school, I had a classmate named Tom. Tom was a smart but naughty student in our classroom. He alway got an egg on his test although he could wrote down all answers accurately. My homeroom teacher punished and shouted at him, but in vain. However, we had a new homeroom teacher during the next semester. I remembered that teacher rewarded Tom because he had done an excellent performance in musical drama. After that day, Tom turned to a hardworking student. Moreover, he graduated from our school with the highest score. Owing to my teacher's work, I consider that rewarding is more efficient than punishment.

subject: HW1001
content: Rewarding students is more effective. Encouragement is the power to motivate students to learn better. It can give students more confidence to believe that they can do well. Not only on their studies but also on their behavior. I have seen a movie. In this movie, there was boy, he had some problems on learning. The teachers in his school, they punished him and scolded him. That made him feel frustrated. He started revolting his teachers. Their parents have no choices but to take him to another school. A teacher knew about his situation. He used his methods to encourage and reward the boy. The boy gradully made progess on his studies. This shows that punishement is not a good way to motivate students. Students need rewards. That is the power to make them feel they can be successful.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, rewarding students to learn is far better than threatening students. Teaching is not only about teach the academy but also direct the students to the bright future and give them the courage to try, to face the challenges. Students may feel upset and frustrated being blamed by the teachers, in oppsite, the students may feel even more courageous and posstive being praised by the teachers and they may work hard learning. I once was blamed by my homeroom teacher, she told me to stand in the corner with my arms raised and teased me that I would never have the chance to be accepted by a national university. I could not help but cry and felt helpless. My grades didn't go better but unbelievably decline with a wide margin. Until the day that my geography teacher encouraged me with his warm smile and told me never fret when facing the problems because he would always be there for me. I started to work hard and I promised I would never let him down. I thought giving the students encourages was really important.

subject: HW1001
content: In recent years, lots of families only have one or two children. Parents' natural tendency is to spoil their kids. Thus, it makes school teachers more difficult to teach students. So some teachers try to use punishment to control students. However, the result shows that it doesn't work. In my opinion, learning happily is more efficient for students. As a substitude teacher in elementary school, I used to yell or punish students when they don't meet my standard. Clearly, it only makes them dislike or even hate me. Moreover, they refuse to study harder. As a result, I have to change my way. I try to understand what they need. When they didn't do a good job, I choose to encourage, not punish, them. I always prepare some attractive stationery and toys to reward students who make process. Finally, they become different. They like to chat with me and try to get better grades. We are not only teacher and students, we are also friends, too. In conclusion, punishment cannot solve the problem about students. We should pay more attention to them and try to reward them. It's important to make students learn happily and efficiently. I believe it can make them winners-both in school and in life.

subject: HW1001
content: I believe that teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior is more effective. I have an example to support my opinion. Nowadays, baby's born rate is lower than usual which means children are precious for parents. Parents do everything to support their children and give them almost everything they expect. Moreover, it is hard for parents to punish their own babies. In this case, children are spoilled actually. To sum up, because children is hard to teach now and their parents could give all the materials they want, teacher is playing the important roll to motivate students to learn.

subject: HW1001
content: In Taiwan, many parents think that punishment is a good way to educate their children. However, in my opinion, the rewarding way is a better way to educate students. Everyone likes to hear compliments or praise from the other. Some experts of education said that encouragment can give students confidence to perform well. On the other hand, punishment let students lose their confidence and perform badly. Take me as an example, I had got the lowest score on math since I was in the elementary school. Due to the prevalence of punishment, I was always beaten by my teacher. The more punishement I had, the more depression I got. However, there was a transition when I was in junior high school. In junior high school, I had a patient and gentle math teacher. Instead of beating and scolding the students, she always had a smile on her face to compliment on students. She told me that I was not a idiot but lacked of carefulness and confidece. Consequently, I improved my disadvantages and worked hard. Can you believed what happened? I got the highest score on math on the next exam. As far as I am concerned, punishment has a side-effect on people. However, if people could use the rewarding way properly, and it must be the efficient way to teach students and raise their interests on learning.

subject: HW1001
content: Student as I am, I regard it neccessary to punish students in some situation. Children are often naughty, and being naughty can be a big trouble to their parents. The volunteer group I attended has held summer camp for elementary school student for many years. Through the interaction with those children, I found it hard to calm them down only by words. They needed to be treated bad when they behaved bad. In that way, they will remember what they have done and remind themselves not to make the same mistake again. I have been my little cousin's piano teacher for a long period of time. Every time after the class is over, I gave her stickers as rewards. However, I found out that she didn't perform better even though I tell her I will give her more stickers, so I figure out another way to stimulate her learning. Once she performed bad in the class, I gave her more homeworks and compelled her to finish them before the next class. By the punishment, she became a very hardworking student in order not to be punished. I know that excessive punishment do no good to students' mental health, so I regard it important for teachers to work hard and develop punishment that can act as a reminder to the students who had made mistakes.

subject: HW1001
content: Nowadays, many teachers in Taiwan still use punishment to control their students. However, in my opinion, I think teachers should stop punishing students. Instead, they can follow three tips. First, teachers should give another chance for students. For example, a student forgot to do his assignment. In stead of punishing him, teachers can ask him to compensate for the homework in the break time. This way, the student would be more comfortable and have less pressure. Second, teachers should know why students do something. For instance, a student is always late for school. Teachers should try to understand the situation, such as talking to the student directly or contacting with his parents. Everything can be solved easily. Last but not least, teachers should control their temper. Many Taiwanese teachers hit their students and cause physical and mental damage. Therefore, teachers should learn to control their temper. In conclusion, there are still many useful and effective ways for teachers to motivate their students. Students would rather teachers be their friends, not punishing machines.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I support the idea of rewarding students for learning more. Take me for example, I once got a pretty bad grade in my junior high school's monthly test. My teacher was surprised, and had a talk with me. My teacher wanted to find out the reason. He encouraged me to tell him why I did so bad about the exam. At first, I was afraid that my teacher might punish me or tell my parents about it. Instead my teacher showed his patience to let me know that he just wanted to help me, he didn't' have the desire to blame me at all. Encouraged by our teacher, I told my teacher the truth that I did not study a lot recently, because I was addicted to play computer games a lot. I found it fun to play computer games, so I usually did some of my studying, and then spent most of my time indulging in the world of computer games. That's the reason why my grades of school study were so bad. After knowing the real reason of my failure, my teacher didn't get angry about it. Instead he comforted me, and told me that the time of my youth is a very valuable period in my life. If I don't cherish my youth, I will feel regret when I get old. Also my teacher promised me to give me a gift if I could get rid of my habit of playing computers, and make the most use of my time to study. I was moved by my teacher, and I decided to turn a new leaf from then on. I tried my best to use the time I had to study. I not only reviewed school's lesson but also previewed the lesson. By doing that, my school study did improve a lot. I got a flying color in my next exam. My teacher was so delighted that he praised me in front of my classmates. Now I am very obliged to my teacher. I also pass my teacher's favor on by encouraging my friends or classmates to study hard by giving them good advice and sometime a proper gift for them. And all the nice word and the appropriate gifts do work wonders. I have seen a lot of students improve a lot by rewarding them some gifts. So I pay my sincere heart to the way of rewarding students for learning.

subject: HW1001
content: Since I am still a student, I think teachers can try to rewarding students for learning more. In Chinese traditional perspective, people think that only harsh punishments can make students improve, and it's the most beneficial way to bring out students' motivations of learning. However, the most important point of education is to make kids feel comfortable and confident while they are learning. It seems like punishment can improve students grades just because they are afraid of not reaching the goal that parents and teachers gave them. My mother is a teacher in an elementary school. She said that when she was a young teacher. She also followed the spirit that punishment can bring advantages. She hit students and made them stand behind the class while her students behaved bad. Nevertheless, she started to find out that her students neither loved learning nor enjoyed the lesson. She finally tried to stand in her students' shoes. As a mother and a teacher, she realized that kids shouldn't be taught like this. Every student likes to be admired and be rewarded, and so does she. While her students appreciating her as a beautiful and intellegent teacher, she would also feel delightful and paid more attention on her teaching. Since everyone need to be cared with soft encouragement, why does she still punish her students? Nowaday, she had altered herself into a really "kind" teacher. She always tells me what happened in her class and how did she use a considerate way to teach her students telling right from wrong. Through my mom's experience, I deeply believe that rewarding students is the most effective way which can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content: I believe that rewarding students for learning is the better way than using punishment. Many researches show that the children under the proper praise could do better than getting punishment when they make mistakes. People need the target which they have to attend. In that way, when they know they will get reward after finishing all their jobs, they could be motivated to do their best. Making mistakes is not a shame. It's only the necessary step to achieve success. The rewarding way shows this spirit. Here are two examples. The NBA player, Raggie Millor, was not a natural-born athlete. He had disorder on his legs which made him hard to walk or even run in his childhood. His family did not give him up. By the encouragment and rewarding, he not only ran faster but also jumped higher. With his own effort and his family support, he finally became one of the best three-point shooter in NBA games. The second example is Washington, the father of the United States. He was known for his honesty to his father that he cut off the favorite tree of his father. It's difficult for parents in the moment not to punish their children. But Washington's father did not punish him, instead, he praised for Washington's honesty. And finally, Washington did a great job, establishing the great country.

subject: HW1001
content: Different teachers use different ways to educate their students. Some punish their students to regulate them while others reward their students to make them confident. In my opinion, giving students more award is a better way than giving them punishment. In my class, I have a really naughty classmate, Sam. He always argues with teacher, break the school rules, do the opposite things as the teachers ask he to do, and even play tricks on our teachers. However, Sam has a really good relationship with our math teacher. It is not because they are relatives but because our math teacher is always nice to Sam, unlike other teachers that are mean and strick to him all the time. Our math teacher won't blame him if he doesn't get a correct answer but will surely reward him if he get the answer correctly, which really gives Sam courage and confidence when dealing math problems. Rewarding students can surely keep them with the interest of learning the subject, and the desire of learning more while punishment might lead to a result of students' afraid, not only of the teacher but the subject all together. I think a friendlier teacher who rewards students more often is a teacher that is more effective toward students.

subject: HW1001
content: Every teacher has his or her own method to motivate students to learn and to control their behavier. In my opinion, rewarding the students is the better one. Some students can learn very well while others can't. The student who can't learn well must has his or her reason. For instant, a poor student can't afford the tuition of the cram school or buy some books to help the learning, it may cause the poor grade in the school. If a teacher punished the student just because the bad grade, I think it is unfair. We should help and encourage the students those who can't learn well. Besides, when students were the teenagers. They didn't like to obey the rules or study hard. It just a period of the life journey. If the teachers put to much pressure and punish them, it may make the students go into the wrong way. In this period, they need more encouragement then punishment. If the teachers can stand on the students shoes, they can make great progrem on every thing. The only thing you need to do is rewarding students not punish them.

subject: HW1001
content: Since I was a little girl in elementary school, I always got the first grade in my class. Of course, teachers liked me and often awarded me, then I would study harder to get more permission. But what about other students in my class? Some of my classmates wanted to get the same honor from teachers so they tried to keep pace with me and did their best to do the exams, while others didn't and never care about their tests even their behavior. They would not pay attention to teachers and seldom study after class, thus, they often got bad grades on every exams. In order not to get punishment from teachers, sometimes they might cheat on the test to pretend that he did study but actually not. So my opinion is that rewarding students for learning would be better than punishing them. Though sometimes punishment seems work, it may do harm to students' mind so they might not like to go school and study anymore. That's what teachers and parents not like to see. They just want their children to learn happily and live easily without this kind of pressure on their kids.

subject: HW1001
content: Punishment is the best way to motivate learners. I believe this is what most of the elderly or even the generation before us think. Indeed, people who are educated under this thought grown up to be more self-disciplined and have a good control of their behavior. However, I believe rewarding and encouraging students is a better way to attain good results. Every human beings likes to be praised and encouraged, no one likes to be punished and be harshly treated. Same for the students, gentle way of education may increase the information being absorbed. This could lead to better results, as students are learning under a relaxing condition, but not a stressful situation. To enforce punishment in education, I may say, is useful in some way, but it is only for a short time. Students will get tired of studying and study very hard just because do not want to get reprimanded, at last, in the worst situation, they would give up and have hatred towards studying. Just like an experiment I heard before: prepare two pots of plants, tell good words and praises to one, and tell nasty and negative words to the other. The result seems surprising but true that the "good words" one seems to grow better and higher than the "bad words" one. Plants are just like human, we are all living things, we progress more effectively with praises. I am a student and I always feel that rewards motivate me and make me keen to study, that is a good feeling and I appreciate that. In my opinion, to learn in a stiff atmosphere is a kind of killing, it kills my interest of study. Therefore, I prefer and believe rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content: In my humble opinion, I agree with the point rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Punishment can only scare students for a short term, when students are out of school or graduate, the punishment lose their work. With no teachers scold it them, they starte to do anything they want. The worst is, they find back their bad behavior. Rewarding students in they way that can really change students' attitude from inside their heart, albeit it takes time. Rewarding makes students contemplating, but punishment don't. when the time students start to think by their own, they get their faith and figure out what is the right behavior. When I was in junior high school, one of my classmates love to hang out with a group of bad students, and seldom came to school. Our teacher got this information, and punished that student. At first, it really worked. They guy came to shool but without any attention. He failed every subjects, and still quited the ultimately. As I know, he is a real gangster now. Finally, he is everything, but a good person. I can't agree any more that rewarding students in the better way. With a propel rewarding, and do not spoild students, you can change a bad student to a good student, and motivate a good student to a excellence student.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, it is more useful to reward students than to punish them. Maybe punishment works to control the behavior of students. But students could be getting worsen without punishment. So, the best way to motivate students is to get their trust and to know what they want in their bottom of heart. To reward students could motivate their attitude for learning. Students who get award can build the sense of honor and responsibility in their heart. If teachers set a role model sucessfully, other students could follow her(his) steps and study harder. For the perspetive of longterm, rewarding students is more effective than punishing them. Punishment maybe destroy the self-esteem of students and motivation for learning. In my experience, I ever be punished for bad grades. And I lost my confidence and the intrest for learning. I became afraid of learning and taking exams. It was a really bad experience. So I suggest that teachers should inspire students through moderate reward.

subject: HW1001
content: I think both method has to be used at the same time. While people were born with different personalities, one measure couldn't be applied to two different guys. It would be more effective if the teacher could use two methods appropriately. Everything has its pros and cons. Committing a crime would be punished is a common sense. However, as the laws were well-built, the crime rate was still high. So what is the problem with it? With horror punishments, nevertheless, someone who acted as he obeied but felt angry in their mind. On the other hand, giving praise or award makes us willing to work hard. But someone would take it for granted and stop to finish his obligation if teacher didn't give some tasty candies. As a result, I think we can't give priority to praising or punishment, but to observe the situation at first. Take my classroom teacher for example, she plays a great role in educating us. While we were naughty, she would pretend that she didn't see any thing if it was only a silly trick. On the contrary, if the trick was harmful or very immoral, we boys will be blamed and have to clean all classroom after class dismissed. Honestly to say, even though we were punished, we still paid respect to our teacher, because she would also buy yummy foods for us as the desserts. It is her proper handling between punishing and award that makes us not only obied to her but repected her as the greatest teacher we have ever met!

subject: HW1001
content: Different teachers have different teaching styles. Some teachers take punishment as a strategy to force the students to learn well. Others think that rewarding is better than punishment. In my opinion, rewarding students for learning is more effective. Students may meet many frustrations on their learning, giving the punishments on students will make them feel upset, and stop learning for escaping from the pressure. Teachers should encourage their students when they met difficulties on learning istead of punishing. Rewarding can give the students confident, and motivate them to persue their better performance as well. I had been a tutor before, for instance. The student I taught was a timid boy, and he lacked of confidence on his study because of the poor performance he had made. However, I always encourage him to have another try when he met the difficulties on learning. Moreover, I did praise him when he perform well on his study. Finally, he had good academic performance.

subject: HW1001
content: Generally speaking, in school, when students make mistakes, do not obey teachers' instructions, or do not do well on their schoolwork, their teachers may use punishment to correct their behaviors and motivate them to learn; while, if they do well on their schoolwork, or behave well, they would be rewarded by their teachers. These are the two common ways that teachers teach their students. However, some way say that punishments are good for students; whereas the other may say that rewarding is more suitable. In my opinion, I have no have absolute answers. I think moderate punishment is as important as rewarding. Here are some reasons and examples to support my opinion. First, once students make mistakes or do not do well on their schoolwork; moderate punishment is acceptable and reasonable, because if teachers blindly punish students without any praising and rewarding, in the long run, students may lose passion toward learning and become more and more obedient. Secondly, moderate rewarding instead of instant punishment sometimes can motivate their passion and willingness of learning. When I was an elementary school student, my school teacher was a kind and tender, but sometimes harsh and serious person. When we behaved well or did well on schoolwork, she often gave us some gifts as rewards. While, once we didn't follow her instructions or make mistakes, she gave moderate punishment to us in order to let us realize whether we did wrong or not. Serious as she was, all of my classmates and I liked her very much. For the reasons and the example, only moderate punishments and rewards can teachers teach their students more effectively.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I think the latter is better. Although using punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior is effective, it may cause the less motivation the students have to read by themselves. Take me as an example, I don't like to be controled and I will think that it is not free so that I will study unhappily. If one's mood is not good, his/her studying effect might be less than usuall one. Rewarding students for learning can lead to better results because they won't study reluctantly. In addition, they will understand the teacher's advice is good for us. It can also promote students' motivation. Above all, the method of rewarding is more effective. First, it can make students realize that if they want something, they should pay a price. Second, they are able to study happily and they might be interested in studying. Third, if someday no one limits their behavior, they still behave themselves as usual. Finally, they will have good experiences on their studying way.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I prefer the use of punishment. Using punishment is more effective than rewarding students. In my childhood, I had a classmate called Jack. We had been in same class for two years. During that time, We had been taught by two teachers. These two teachers were quite different in their teaching style. One of them was kind, considerate and she was like a genuine mom. She never hit any of the students in the class. By virtue of that, Jack and other students were not reluctant to do homework and study. They had no interest in the reward given from the teacher. Eventually, Jack's grades became worse and there was no rules in his sight. The other teacher is much more serious. Though she was not in the classroom, we still weren't dare to talk or play. At first, Jack was unwilling to follow her rules and even talked back to her. After her intensive training and frightening punishment. The naive Jack came back. Undoubtedly, his homework became better and he did his best to correct his bad behavior. The last time I met him was in a science camp, he said that teacher was the gift given from God. Punishment is more effective, isn't it?

subject: HW1001
content: In order to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior, teachers try various ways for the best result. For some teachers, punishment may be very useful, considering the fact that no one likes to be punished. Students might behave better in order to prevent punishment. However, in my opinion, rewarding students is the most appropriate method for better results. Rewarding students may gain their confidence, and it could be their motivation for improving themselves. While punishing and scolding may hurt their self-esteem, and may also bring negative reaction, which would only make the 2 problem worse. Therefore, I believe that rewarding students is more effective than punishment.

subject: HW1001
content: When it comes to the method to motivate students and to control their behavior, it is not punishment but rewards and praise that lead to satisfactory results. This is due to the fact that students perform better in a relatively relaxed atmosphere than in a tense one. I started learning violin at the age of six. Sadly, the first teacher I met tended to lose his temper when I made mistakes, even a minor one, making me afraid of every lesson. Therefore, I became increasingly unwilling to practice violin, and thus I made little progress. What's worse, this infuriated the teacher. I was tragically trapped in the vicious circle. However, this story became completely different after I decided to learn with another teacher who attached great importance to encouragement and who was willing to reward her students when they deserved so. Since then, I found myself enjoying not only every lesson but also music itself. In addition, playing violin became a way to entertain myself when I was at leisure, to relax myself when I was confronted with pressure, and to soothe myself when I was sad. Hence, I was most grateful for my teacher, who helped me forged the interest in music through compliment, encouragement, and rewards. My personal experience explicitly shows me that rewarding students for learning helps them a lot. As a result, if I have the opportunity to become a teacher, this will definitely be the essential principle in teaching.

subject: HW1001
content: Teachers have their way of teaching students to learn and to behave. Some teachers does use punishments to push these youths to learn and to control their manners. Others believe that, for better results, you'll have to reward them. To my opinion, I say both two ways have their goods and bads. To me, some children make teachers go mad. The only way to make naughty students behave well, is by punishing them. To let them know that their actions are not necessary or impolite is a teachers duty. Some skills and manners are also what students have to know. These skills and manners may be about saving their own lives and to respect others. It is necessary to let students know that some actions they make may interrupt someone or that may be about the safety of themselves. However, an unappropriate punishment may make students get scared of going to school, or make other problems which may harm a student from learning. We should consider more about punishments for students and which punishments are necessary or not. On the other hand, rewarding students may be good and bad, too. By rewarding students, they get used to getting rewards. After they grow up, they will still hope they get rewards, and things won't always be like what they wanted to be. Still, rewards may lead to better results in a short time. By rewarding them makes more power to lead students to success. As for a teacher, they still have to let youths know what really is the truth and what isn't. They'll have to let students know that rewards are only prepared for hard-workers, and sometimes, hard-workers won't get rewards. Teachers should make more decision about rewarding students and what is the best for them. What I have to emphasize is that, both ways used together is what I think the best way to teach students. For example, my father forced me to learn swimming. In these few days, news about teenagers drowning from lack of swimming skill kept showing up. I was shocked and also a little bit glad that my dad had forced me to swim. Another example is that, after I came back from a couple of years in a foreign country, I found out myself not knowing any Chinese. My aunt rewards me by giving me snacks for every correct answer. All above, I think the best way to make students learn and to behave is by using both appropriate punishments and rewards. But still, teachers have to decide which way may be the best for students.

subject: HW1001
content: Many people may consider punishment the method to teach animals not human. However, I think of punishment as a necessary evil, and appropriate punishment is more effective than just rewarding students. With the rapid growth in economy, many parents are busy at work so that they only want to raise one child. Moreover, because of their affluence, they always buy whatever their child wants. As a result, these children are satisfied with material life so that a small reward seems not attractive enough to motivate them to study. In these cases, an appropriate punishment may scare them, so they are willing to study. When I was an elementary school student, one of my best friends whose father is rich sat next to me. He didn't like to do homework like other students. So our homeroom teacher decided to give us a candy when we finished homework on time. Everyone except him were motivated to do homework. The day after that day, our teacher told him that he would be punished if he didn't do homework. As a result, he was so afraid that he finally finished homework on time. This incident convinced me that a small punish is more effective than rewarding. But it is important for teachers to think which punishment is appropriate.

subject: HW1001
content: We are not the saints and we can't do everything correct, not to mention for students who are just learning, it is very usual for them to make mistakes. If I am going to choose a way to help them learn, I will prefer to reward them by giving them compliment rather than just punish them. First, if teachers give the students reward when they did something right, they will have sense of achievement, which means they are encouraged to learn new objects then have their own questions. This turns out to be a good cycle for learning. On the other hand, if students are punished by teacher, they could be disappointed not just for their grade but for themselves. Finally they have less and less confidence for learning or even are afraid to learn. I heard of a research from England which surveyed lots of people, and it shows that positive compliment does more effect on learning than punishment. And the theory has been conformed. When the time comes for me to choose one way to either reward students or punish them, I would definitely choose the former one based on one reason: it is more effective.

subject: HW1001
content: Most teachers want their students to be better. Thus, they use many ways to elevate the learning of students. I think rewarding students for learning is an effective way. My opinions are as follow; First, punishment may be effective sometimes, but it indeed will frighten children. The students' mental and physical development are still not complited. If you use punishment like; doing push up, hitting them or subscribing books. All of these are not good ways. Therefore, you may get the results you want, but you may hurt the children seriously. Second, rewarding can encourage students and guide them. We can reward students when they perfome well. This can promote their confidence and we can through the process of rewarding teach them somethings. Some experiments say, if a person is in a good mood, his brain will be active and the learning is very effective during this time. On the contrary, we can use punishment to push the students to learn new things, but their brain and mental are too nervous which cause bad learning efficiency. In brief, learning is a very important step for everyone. So, we should find the balence between learning results and which way to push them. I believe what all of the parents want are the pure smile on thier children's face.

subject: HW1001
content: I am a supporter of abolishing punishment. And the following are two methods that I think is more effective. The first, we must reward students to learn rather than force them to learn. Through this way, students will become willing to learn and pay more attention on studying. On the contrary, punishment will give them terrible impression to studying. And even they study, they won't try hard to study well. Take my classmate David as an example. He learned English under the pressure and punishment of his parents. Finally, he lost his interest in English, and became reluctant to touch anything about English. And the second method is providing students an ideal learning environment. By providing that enviroment, students will learn actively. Under such circumstance, they will find learning is easy as breathing. My friend Jane is a nice example. Her parents provided her a wonderful learning environment. They have weekly reading disccuzion gathering. Every weekend they will talk about a book they selected. Emerging in that atmosphere, I think everyone will become willing and naturally to learning and studying.

subject: HW1001
content: What kind of approach should be used in order to motivate students to learn and make them behave properly has been in dispute for several years. Some insist punishment is cure-all while others beheve in the effect of rewarding student. To my perspective, I will stand for the latter. The reason I opposed using punishment to control students is that it will cause them to feel frustrated and even lose their zeal to learn. Once students are scolded, they might ask themselves, "Why do I keep making mistakes? " and thus have less confidence in themselves and make them confused about how to improve their behavior. These results could be seen in newspaper when some children being punished begin to dislike the school. That's why I consider punishment is not wise for students, who have not developed mature thoughts. On the contrary, rewarding students as they accomplish some works or behave better may be a efficient way. I think there are two main reasons. First, students being rewarded are always excuding their confidence. They know they will get rewarded if they behave correctly and thus will make more endeavor to complete it. Second, once a student is praised, others can intimate him or her so as to be rewarded as well. This way, teachers can make whole class improve without indoctrinating them all day long. The author of many educational books, Clark, claim that if he praise a child for his efforts to protect enviroment, the next day he will see everyone picking up garbage. In my opinion, I prefer rewarding students, which is more effective and can always serve teachers' propose as they want to teach their students how to be more mature.

subject: HW1001
content: From my point of view, I consider rewarding students for learning and using punishment to motivate students of the same importance since they are interrelated. Without rewarding students for their exceptional behaviors or acedemic performance, it is likely that students will lose their interest in learning gradually. In addition, rewarding students can thus bring positive thinking among the students. Moreover, it can become a motivation for them to encourage themselves to broaden their horizons. However, over rewarding may lead to the unappropriate indulgement of students. That is, on the other hand, using punishment to control students' behavior is important as well. Through punishment, students can modify their wrong behaviors and it may be an alert to them at the same time. Punishment can be looked upon as an effective way of reminding the students and preventing them from making the same mistake. Therefore, as far as I am concerned our teachers should work along both lines. Rewarding is as important to punishment to our education. Neither the former or the latter should be neglected.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, students should learn for themselves but not for others. In this way, students are given the responsibility of their own learning. With their future in their hands, it's the students' choice to make the most of it or just abandon their own future. If students learn simply to avoid punishment, they would fail to find the real motivation when there are no punishent any more. On the other hand, hard work often leads to good grades and achievements which are already rewards for students. Besides, teachers' praising can also reward the students with a sense of achievement. Paul, a close friend of mine, is a good example. Begining as a students with poor grades, he put a lot of work in learning. With his grades getting better, he feels more confident with himself and gets impressive grades now.

subject: HW1001
content: Teachers used to punish students who are naughty in the classes. It may be useful to stop students from doing the wrong things again, but students would get hurt or feel guilty in their hearts. In my opinion, rewarding system could be a better solution to end student's bad behavior. Teachers set a rewarding system for students to follow. For example, if one student turn in his homework on time for a week, teacher would give him one token as a rewarding. After this students collect ten tokens, he can exchange it with gifts from the teacher. These gifts includes pens, rulers, erasers and so on that teacher need to prepare before hand. If the student has more tokens, the better or more gifts he can get from his teacher. In this case, rewarding system would motivate students to turn in their homework on time. In my point of view, I think teacher should provide rewarding to his students instead of punishment.

subject: HW1001
content: In recent years, people debate on whether the teachers should use punishment or rewards to motive students. It seems that there isn't a right answer but I suppose using rewards is a better one. Following are two reasons to support many choice. It is inevitable that students make mistakes and it's up to teachers to decide the way of education. Punishment may control or revise the student's behavior at the time but in a long term, it can't change the student's habit thoroughly. On the contrary, rewarding enables students to think and improve. For example, the education system of America aims to cheer students up to inspire their creativity instead of scolding them. You can hear the words like "good" or "excellent" very often in a foreign teacher's class. It is this verbal praise which can't be heard in the traditional education system that creates the power of this country and its prosperity. There is no denying that all glitters are not good so teachers are supposed to reward students to raise their confidence. To conclude, using rewards is more appropriate than using punishment.

subject: HW1001
content: I always think that punishment couldn't solve any problem. In this case, rewarding students on their achievement is a better way to educate them. Although using rewarding may not really motivate students to learn from their deep inside, it still provide a stronger motivation for students to get what they want. If punishing them, they study or learn just in order not to be punished. After growing up, this urge will be removed. At that time, there is nothing could make a person truly like to learn a certain kind of knowledge or skill. By rewarding a child, the feeling of trying to get something fatastic motivates them to achieve a higher goal. Although this motivation will disappear sooner or later, but I think the reward embeded some rigid personality into the child's mind. Depending on my experience of watching TV, education experts say punishment is the worst method to educate children, rewarding is not best but is still an acceptable approach. On the other hand, rewarding improves the relationship between teacher and student, this better relationship gives students a powerful will to learn and study hard. On many aspects, rewarding is better than punishing. I persist this opinion.

subject: HW1001
content: Suitable punishment can help the student get rid of their bad habits, such as being late, saying impolite words, fighting and so on. It's much more effective than having no punishment in a class. Compared with the law in our society, a proper rule is neccessary in a school. When doing something wrong, the student's punishment given by his teacher can help him not make the same mistake when facing with another situation. Meanwhile, that can also give the other students a good experience. Being a student in senior high, I found that a punishment benifits me a lot though it would be really a terrible memory. For example, I forgot to write down my name on the test paper for seven times in the same semester in the elementary school. That makes my teacher had no choice but to ask me to write my own name for one hundred times. As an excellent student in the class, I couldn't help crying after hearing that. Magically, I didn't make any mistake like that even one more time. It was only one of the punishments I've experiented but the most memorable one. I found that after getting every punishment. It's difficult to make the same mistake. In order to avoid any punishment, I asked myself to try my best.

subject: HW1001
content: As far as I am concerned, rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. There are several reasons for my opinions. First, no one can be touched without his permission. When teachers punish students, they may hit them under student's unwilling. It's human right that we can't touch others before their allowance. If a teacher punishes a student harshly, it may lead to physical harm. Besides, everyone likes to be praised instead of being scolded. I deeply believe that one man will become what you expect. Therefore, when a teacher rewards a student, he can receive good behavier in return. Third, I strongly suggest that don't punish students in public because it usually doesn't lead to good results but just causes bad endings. It really hurts one's dignity. More seriously, it might take away their confidence and make their life darkly. For example, one of my friends hated math just because of their math teacher punishing him all the time. He was so afraid of math in his life. In other words, he didn't believe he could solve the questions when he got a math test. On the other hand, I was very lucky to meet my first English teacher. Because she was so nice and humorous, so I had a great interest in English. She always prepared a lot of games for us to play. When I met difficulties in English, she was very kind to help me solve the problems. I remembered that she always said "good job" after teaching me. I was very gratitude for her rewarding. In a word, I know that teachers should praise students instead of punishing them because one will become what you expect.

subject: HW1001
content: I would reward students for learning instead of punishment. There are some reasons as follow. First, I don't like being punished in front of my classmates. Being punished in front of my classmates makes me feel embarrassed and shamed. I believe that no one will be happy when teachers punish you. Second, punishment is just a way for a shot time. If no one keeps pushing them behind, do they really have motivation to study? I don't' think so. Take my friend for example. He had a teacher who use punishment to motivate students in junior high school. But after he graduated, he started playing on-line games day and night. And he is totolly out of control now. Third, reward to students is as candies to small children. It let people know the advantage of studying. Last, you still have to stick to your principles. If you give too many candies to them, they may become spoiled. So, make good use of the correct methods, and they will become better and better.

subject: HW1001
content: Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, I think both of the ways should be exist at the same time. Because all the students are so diffenent that we can't just use one to make students study hard or behave well. As I am a teacher in a cram school, I have more time to stay with kids. I prefer to give the students some gifts if they do well than punishment them. If they do well, I will give them a gift and tell everyone in my class how well they do. I believe that would also encourge others. And the student who gets the prize will feel so proud, no matter what the gift it is. And recently, we can watch more and more news about some teachers using the wrong way to punish the students I believe that more and more teachers are not willing to punish them. I believe that students have to learn by themselves. What I can do is to teach them and encourage them, and it works most of time. Just like what I said first, all the students are different. There must have some students that really don't care about the prize. So if students don't do well, teachers still need to give them so punishmet, but not hitting them. Maybe we can use some way like singing infront of class, they will feel ashamed and try to do better next time. Just make it easier but not hurting the students. We can all enjoy learning and have fun. All of us can enjoy our life.

subject: HW1001
content: In the past, many people deeply believed that teachers need to punish students to motivate them or control their behaviors. In my point of view, it is not a good method. I do believe that rewarding students is better than punishing them. Also, it is not only a world current but also a tendency in Taiwan. Here are my reasons to support my opinion. First, teacher may distinguish students' motivations to learn by punishing them. Take me for example, when I was a junior high school student, I always got bad grades on math. Because I wasn't good at numbers, math became the most difficult subject for me during that time. As a result, my math teacher was mad at me all the time and tried different ways to punish me each time. However, that was not a good thing for me. I didn't want to study math and spend time reading them. Until now, I still don't like math at all. Second, students can get higher sense of achievement if teachers can reward them. Student don't need to worry that teachers will punish them or not, but only care what they get after they achieve their goals. It is quite vital because they can feel easy or relax to learn. In sum, it is beeter that teachers reward students to enhance their learning efficency and motivation.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, punishment is a better way for the teachers to control the students' behavior and to motivate their study. Students are usually not so active to study, therefore, they need someone to give them a push. This push can be punishment or rewards. But usually it is punishment that force them to study and to behave. The difference is that punishment gives them fear, but the rewards is usually useless to lazy students, for they don't even care if there's a reward or not, they just don't want to study. Take my classmates for example, our English teacher is a teacher who will punish use when doing bad on test. On the other hand, our Chinese teacher will not do anything even you fall asleep during the class. When it comes to exams, the difference can be seen on the scores. Our classmates' English scores are always improving, while Chinese scores just stick at the same range. That is because the students are afraid of being punished, it doesn't matter whether they get the rewards or not. To sum up, although lots of people don't agree with the way of using punishment, I still think students need to be ruled properly, and giving rewards is definitly not the best way on my list.

subject: HW1001
content: I think rewarding students for learning leads to a better result. Using punishment to motivate students to learn may lead to a immediate change of the current situation. However, students couldn't realize that behaving better is for his or hers own good. While it may take a long time for rewarding to have effects, students would not learn and behave better only because of fear. When I was studying in the elementary school, a boy in my class was considered a bad student because he seldom go to school and didn't work hard. My teacher spent a long time talking to him with patience and love as rewards, and everyone indeed saw the obvious change of that boy. If the teacher has used punishment to control the boy's behavior instead, I think the result would be a lot different. Through the example above, I believe that rewarding is absolutely a more effective way to motivate students.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I think teachers should use strict methods to motivate students, because the most important thing to the students is learning. It may not be a errand way for teachers to use, but it surely is the most effective way. Take me as an example, I used to studied in private school before I went to senior high school. Before I went to the public senior high school, I always got good grades because of the private school's teaches. The teachers in private school are always strict to our learning attitude. In order to avoid the teacher's punishment, I always handed in my reports and homeworks at time. Because of my learning attitude, I can always preformed well. Now I'm in eleven grade and I go to public school. In public schools, there are no rules for student's behavior. Without the strict rules, my classmates are always playing and making evil jokes to others. They do everything without studying. But for the education system of our country, students need to study hard to get in good universities. According to the experiance of myself, I prefer teachers use punishment to motivate students and make students taking errand attitude for learning.

subject: HW1001
content: Thanks to the improvement of our society, now there are only one or two children in a family. As a result, how to make children be well-educated has become a serious problem for both parents and teachers. From my point of view, rewarding students for learning is more effective than using punishment. All the people in the world like others to praise them and be proud of them. No one would like to be denied. Hence, take this way on students, when they perform well, give them courage and praise them. Students would have a sense of achievement, and after that, they would try their best to do all the things because they want to be reconized. On the other hand, if teachers use punishment to control the student's behavior, some students will feel frustrate and have no courge to take defeat. Worst of all, this kind of children will become social problems in the future. Take myself as an example, when I was a child, I often took part in music contests. Each time, before I performing on the stage, I felt nervous and worried about that I will make mistakes. Nevertheless, the thing I worried about happend. I played the wrong song and failed the competion. After that, my teacher and parents didn't blame me at all. They tried a variety of ways to prevent me from being nervous; meanwhile, they also encourage me not to be defeat by this small mistake, and told me that I should be more confidence of myself. I took their advice and finally won the contest. During the times in school, we have to face lots of difficulties. However, if teachers can praise students for their excellent behavior, I think it will be very useful for learning. On the whole, there are both advantages and disavantages of punishing and prasing students. What we can do is that we should try our best to do all the things in our life. Follow this way, we can get away from punishing and have a sense of achievement.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I think the one which by rewarding students for learning is more effecient. Since more and more children now are being spoild by their parents, punishment is not as usful as it used to be. Moreover, too many parents are just too protective to their kids and don't allow anyone to touch them even a hair. Therefore, it is unwise to motivate students and control their behavior through punishment. In the contrary, the students now are more eager to win, so rewarding them can not only assure their ability but also make their parents feel proud of them. Besides, by doing so may spir those who didn't study hard to take out their best, but punishment may only scare those who could perform well at first to be afraid of making mistakes and thus, give up in the end. Because of the reasons above, I think rewarding is the best policy. Since we can do one thing but lead two different kinds of students to try their best, it is absolutely more effecient.

subject: HW1001
content: It is very frequent to see the news about teaches' punishment to students. Though punishment can be a warning for students to make them study, I don't think it is a good way. I have read many news that students are afraid of school after they are accepted pysical punishment. It not only hurts their body but also their mental part. According to what I just say, I won't deny the effect of punishment, but if someone still gets punishment no matter how hard he or she tries, he or she will become no sense to the blame and just let themselves not study. On the contrary, if someone is praised by others when he or she just advances in grade a little, I think it will make him or her more confident and let he or she has the bravery to accept next challege which will be more difficult. In conclusion, I think rewarding can be more effective than punishment. At least, rewarding won't leave the wound on students' mind or body. But there's one thing needing to be paid attention that complishment for students would make them too proud of themselves and laugh at those who are not as good as them. It is to say, both rewarding and punishment aren't perfect, but the previous one will be better for children's educational development to let them learn happily.

subject: HW1001
content: Punish or reward? As far as I am concerned, it's really a matter of opinions. In my viewpoint, they both have their own merits and demerits. Actually, punishments hurt children's feel more than their body. But it is penalties that let young guys learn what to do and what can't do. To naughty students, a great punishment would probably let them be quiet for a while. The problem is: Do every teachers know each of their students on penalty-tolerance? Sometimes these punishments, physical and verbal alike, could do great harm to young pupils attitude toward education. Even though the teacher are for students' own good, but they neglect that they should think twice before they enforce the penalty. On the other hand, rewarding always make children grow up in a happy mood. But in reality, almost every boss or supervisor are yelling, punishing on their employees. It means if a child lives in applause suddenly has to go for job and find out there are few compliments in the society; then how pessimistic he/she may be? Besides, rewarding can easily make a young mind be too proud of himself, and this could destroy a good personality. Si a teacher also have to carefully use their rewards. In the long run, I'd like to take myself for instance. Since childhood, I've lived in a world of criticals and punishments. My parents always warned me that there were still things you can do. Growning up in this background, I used to be a pessmists. Not until I met a teacher did I change my attitude. She always told me to think of the bright. An unforgettable proverb she told me is "When there is a shadow, there is a light." She elevate my confidence by rewarding. And in presense, my parents' cricticals make me humble while the teacher's rewards let me be self-confident. From the above-mentioned, it seems that a teacher should strike the balance between punishments and rewards. In so doing, students in our country can cultivate a optimistic attitude toward life.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, it is really hard for teachers to decide how to educate their students. Because some students are so mischief that teachers should give them punishment; while others perform so well to have encouragements. Though some laws have been based on not to use physical punishment to treat the students, I have a different opinion from it. I think that appropriate punishment is essential. Education is the most important thing in our life, when we are little, we didn't know which behavior is right and which is wrong. So who can help us correct the mistake? Of course, not only our parents but also our teachers. They will give us punishment to let us know that "I have do the wrong thing."
Take my friends, Joe, for example. Joe is a boy born in a rich family and his parents never scold him even he had stolen money from them. One time, Joe was trying to steal money from his classmate, Sally, our teacher caught him red-handed. She made him stand outside the classroom for all day as a punishment and tell him, "Joe, it's wrong to do such thing, you're a great boy. Don't do it anymore" I didn't know if Joe had listened to the teachers or not. But after that day, Joe has become a well-behaved boy. From this example, I believe that use punishment can motivate students to control their behavior helpfully. No matter which way the teachers use, I think punishment is the last straw for all of them.

subject: HW1001
content: Nowadays, teachers in school use different ways to teach their students. Some of them use punishment to motivate students to learn and control their behavior, while others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, I believe that educating students through rewarding is more effective. I have once read a book written by a mother. Her son studied in an American elementary school. It was a special school because the teachers in school valued every student's performance. If one performed well, he or she would be praised. The school also held ceremonies to award students. The writer said that her son became more confident about himself. For him, learning was not only a duty but also an interest. In sum, I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. By rewarding students, they can build their own confidence and have a sense of achievement in learning as well!

subject: HW1001
content: In the whole history of learning, punishment and rewards have been used on students, neither it's in a little small moden school in the 15th century or a grand university modern people attend. But which one is more useful and effective in helping students? Both have their goods and their bads but in my point of view, rewarding students is the more effective one. There are three reasons to why I think so. The first is that some rewards can give you a goal in the future. It doesn't need to be a physical object. A praise or a word of trust could do. The second reason is that getting a reward would make you eager to get the next one, making you have the heart in studying harder. The last reason is that it gives you confidence in learning. You would start to enjoy learning and be willing to work hard. But of course, there are some negativity to getting eager in getting good grades. Some people might cheat, or use some dirty ways to get the award. There are also some teachers who would argue that the person would only study hard just for the sake of getting that award, and not to learn which is the more important. I would disagree on that. Cheating is a disgraceful action, and it's goes against most peoples morals, so cheating to get the award doesn't make you feel good when you succeed. There would be that unsatified feeling in your heart. Same as not getting it really. And with the second arguement, I can only say that the feeling of wanting to work hard to get more comes naturally. You will want to learn more and succeed in learning in the end. I've had some expierence in the matter of rewarding student. I am a student myself and once a teacher praise gave me a dream that I still have now. It was in elementary school, fourth grade. The teacher told me that I have what it takes to become a writer. I was not sure if that was true but it's given me a goal in my life ever since. There are many reasons why rewarding is better than punishing. You can get goal from rewards, can let you get the habit in studying harder, and can give you confidence in learning. Rewarding is a great way in helping students.

subject: HW1001
content: Being a student, we all know that there are two kinds of teaching ways in schools. Some teachers are strict, so they would use punishment to motivate students to learn, even control their behavier. On the contrary, some teachers would use rewards for their students. However, I think that rewarding students for learning is more effective to help students. First, students like to be praised. If we keep blaming or punishing students, they would lose confidence in studying, even give up the course. Second, we should let students look on the bright side. Just we encourage them, and teach in an interesting way; then, students would be willing to try and study. For example, while I was a junior high school student, my parents or teachers often said "I will give you the gift or anything you want if you can get good grades." Of course, I tried hard to get good grades, but I didn't. As a result, my parents still felt happy and were touched by my effort. Hence, they bought a gift for me. To sum up, we should encourage students as possibly as we can. Then, students would have courage to learn the subject they are scared. So, rewarding students is much better than punishing them.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinions, rewarding students is better than punishing them. Though some teachers really put great emphasis on punishment, I think it could only give students negative attitudes toward studying and even make them under great pressure. In this way, students may also feel disappointed and he eager to escape from schools. On the other hand, rewarding students can inspire them to study diligently and give them more achievement as well. As I was an elemantary school student, my Chinese teacher always punished students if we didn't get good grades. Sometimes the test was really too difficult and we all made great effort; however, he just kept scolding us no matter how hard we have tried. As a result, Chinese has been my poorest subject until now. Moreover, I consider passing the Chinese exams with flying colors as nothing but a fairy tale. On the contrary, graduating from the elementary school, I met an English teacher that always praised her students. However bad grades I got, she just explained every question down to the last details and encouraged me not to give up. When I performed well on the exams, she gave me some compliments and also reminded me of studying diligently continualy. Thanks to her, I always have confidence in English and learn it actively. Juding from my own experiences, rewarding students is no doubt superior to punishing them. Consequently, if I was a teacher, I would deem rewarding my students as my own duty.

subject: HW1001
content:
Undoubtedly, some teachers regard punishment as the best way to motivate students to get better grades. However, more and more people think that teachers should reward students and encouage them instead of forcing them to learn.
In my opinion, rewarding students is much better than putting punishment on them. If students get praise or encouragement after finishing some hard work, they will become more satisified and much willing to learn. The most effective way to motivate students is to develop their interests on learning so that they will learn aggressively.
It's reported that students are so afraid of punishment that they learn reluctantly. As far as I am concerned. After obtaining rewarding, I will try my best to face anther chanllenge. In addition, students who has interest on learning won't be afraid of hard chanllenges while studying.
In view of above points, It's better and more effective for students to learn by rewarding them.

subject: HW1001
content:
Teachers nowadays can be divided into two seperated groups. One group is the "lion-like" group, which believe that punishing a student can make the student in a good shape. Another group is much more friendly. They believe that they can reward the students to let the students change their attitudes. These two groups of teachers have a large gap between them.
I'm of the opinion that students that study in the "happy" environment, which is the rewarding group, can grow better. The students can be over the moon when they get a reward. With the rewards, the children would do even better. When I was at elementary school, I've got classmates that noisy all the time. With the help of "Good Student Cards," our class behaves like "normal people." On the other hand, I go to Junior High, and our teacher punishes students when we get low grades. My classmates even joke around when they get punished. See the difference? One works while the other brings the opposite effect.
However, several students that get those nice teachers, don't have nice attitudes toward those teachers. Instead, they play tricks on the teacher. While the teacher asks, "Who was the one that came up with this idea?" Later, no one raise their hand, this is the time that the other role of a teacher should show up. It's of paramount importance for a teacher to get a measure of their emotion.
All in all, I still want to say a teacher also should have a nice relationship with students. Don't hestitate to be a nice teacher. It's guarenteed that the students will change their minds on you immediately.

subject: HW1001
content: According to the two methods, I think that the method of rewarding students for learning can lead to better results is more effective than the other method. There may be some reasons why I feel this way. First, some students are smart, but they are too lazy to learn things. Besides, some students are not good at learning, and their grades are poor no matter how they work hard. I think if teachers are patient and are willing to help students with the rewarding method, their inner potential would be aroused at the same time. Also, the smart students would assist teachers to help those students whose learning methods are wrong. Therefore, it is a good method for teachers to do this. Second, students can learn things without a lot of pressures. If they obtain good grades, teachers would give them a reward. They would not take the serious punishment but could learn much more happily. Anyway, I think it is effective to reward students without punishment.

subject: HW1001
content: I believe that rewarding students for learning is more effective. For one thing, doing so provides a joyful atmosphere. Students will have a positive attitude toward learning and will also be more willing to spend their time on it. For another, when students are rewarded, they will become more confident. The feeling of being praised and rewarded gives them a strong motivation to improve themselves by keeping learning. On the contrary, if teachers use punishment to control their students, it might work in the begining but won't last long. Students will learn not because they want to but because they are afraird. This motivation isn't strong enough to keep them learning. Take my cousin for example. When she was in junior high school, the teachers there always scolded them for their poor grades. If they didn't do well on the tests, they would get a punishment. She was so unhappy that she didn't want to go to school. However, she entered a senior high school three years later. It was a totally different environment. Students there were happy there because their teachers always encouraged them to learn and rewarded them when they got good grades on tests. My cousin told me that she was much more interested in learning and was eager to go to school every day. For these reasons mentioned above, I think the best way to learn effectively is to reward students for their learning.

subject: HW1001
content: From my point of view, I think rewarding students for learning might have a better effect. When a child does a great job, you can show your appreciation to him to encourage his interest of learning this subject and motivate his desire to take advanced studies. Take my own experience for example, when I was taking an earth science lesson in senior high school, I answered a question about the composition of a kind of unknown volcano rocks correctly on my own, and the teacher and all of my classmates clappsed their hands to encourage me. I felt proud and the interest and motivation to study earth science was strengthened intensively. I think the phenomenon of learning and the sense of achievement have much to do with the high efficient and success in the consequence. On the other hand, if teachers punish their students too much rather than giving them the rewards they deserved, students will lose their interest of this subject in the long run, causing a negative effect of learning. To sum up, encouraging can lead to a better result.

subject: HW1001
content:
In our school, some teachers prefer to punish students to motivate them to learn and to control their behavior. Others think that rewarding students for learning is a better policy and can lead them to a better result.
In my opinion, I think that punishing students is a more effective way to motivate them to learn and to control their behavior. Punishment makes most of the students scared. When students are afraid of the punishment, they will tend to fullfill the requests in order to avoid the punishment. On the other sides, rewarding might give students the motivation of studying. However, when the reward is not attractive to some students, they will tend to do something else rather then study.
When I was in Junior high school, our teacher had made a test. He tried the way of rewarding in the first semester and tried the other way in the second semester. At first, the teacher told us that he will give one hundred dollars to the person who can get the grade more than 90. Most of the students were interested at first. In the end, most of the them gave up, because they didn't think it was worth of studying that hard. In the second semester, he told us that he will punish the people who get the lowest five grade. Everyone was so scared that they studied hard to avoid being punished.
From this test, I think that it is the pressure that can motivate people to do what they should do. Although rewarding does work a little bit, getting pressure from avoiding punishment is more effective.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, educations become one of the important topics to discuss. The ways of teaching the children also leads to a great variety. In some teachers' opinion, awards usually cause a better result. To the other teachers, punishments can deal with problems much faster. In my opinion, I would agree with the latter.
In the past, most of the families have more than one or two children in their house. With the additional help of traditional ideals, children understands why respecting the elders, teachers, and each other. In this way, when they gain rewards from the teachers, the feelings they have are mostly graceful and thankful. However, because of the busier city life, some families only have one or two kids, and give their only kids all their love and care. In this way, all the little "kings" and "queens" no longer understand why to appreciate when recieving goodies, and the "love education" seems to lose its charm because kids are starting to take things for granted.
The punishments are starting to have better effect in this age. While the kids don't appreciate rewards as much as before, punishments can help them to redefine what they actually deserved and make them understand what thing should be appreciated or obey. This can motive them way easier than rewarding. In addition, children are mostly afraid of punishments and learn to obey, just like the relationship between citizens and laws.
With the above reasons, I believe punishment works much better than rewards because this world is changing, and the education need a change, too.

subject: HW1001
content:
The education in Taiwan is usually seen as a strict part. Teachers have their own style for teaching students. I support our teachers, from elementary school to the senior high school, to believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. I can't agree to the punishment which force the students to be the one the teachers like or the society accepts.
Every students have their own interest, some like science, others like to social with others. I think that one can find his way if the teachers give him enough time and freedom to explosure his mind and his favors.
Take Newton, a well-known scientist, for example. When he was at his early age, his teacher found that Newton had a massive potential of learning. But Newton was not interested in the studies, he always fooled around. His teacher encouraged him to observe the things around him. One day, he sat under an apple tree, he was bumped by an apple. He began to studied the majestic phenomenon, and pronounced his thoughts of gravity.
If Newton's teacher then just forced him to concentrate in the studies which he didn't like. Maybe he would not be a somebody but a nobody.

subject: HW1001
content:
Almost every student has the experience of being punished and being rewarded. We will work harder to avoid punishment or to win awards. Which way is more effective? In my opinion, I think both two ways can make our grades better and should exist at the same time. Punishment is a strong threat that force us to study. However, if there is only punishment, students will lose the interest in the subject with the efficiency decreasing. In the other side, if we have no punishment but awards, some students will become lazy because they will not take failure as a serious thing and try nothing to solve problems.
