Take my class for example, our English teachers is a tough person. She diverts our class into seven groups and makes us compete with other groups. If the total grades of a group is worse than others, the group members much spend holiday studying in school. In other hand, the group performing well can receive money. Awards makes the punishment seem more terrible and in the same way, punishment makes awards more attractive. As far as I'm concerned, it is the contrast between the two that enhance students' willing to study. And our fabulous English grades in the entrance exam proved the idea. As a result, only through both ways used properly can we raise the efficiency of studying most.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are many kinds of methods for teachers to teach their students. In the past, teachers always used punishment to force the students to study. Now, some people disagree the issue and believe that rewarding students for learning is a better way. How can we make a decision?
In my opinion, rewarding students for learning is more effective. Using punishment can only scare the children, but in fact they don't have motivation to learn. They study just because they want to avoid punishment. They can't realize the advantages of studying. Then the education lose its true value.
I have a smart friend, he has become my classmate since we were elementary school students. In elementary school, our teacher preferred to use punishment to force us to study. My friend hated this way, so he often got terrible grades. But after we entered high school, our new teachers didn't punish students but rewarded and encouraged us. In this way, my friend got good grades in almost every exam and became an outstanding student. Different ways cause different results, using a presice approach to teach students can make them achieve more.
Many teachers have changed their mind and don't use punishment anymore. Children can learn knowledge more happily and with less worry. Therefore, I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
When it comes to teaching, rewarding students for learning is more effective than punishing them. The praise and rewards not only motivate students to learn happily, but also create a great environment form their attitude and confidence.
With rewards, student are willing to learn and can learn happily. They would try their best to achieve goals teachers set to win praise and rewards, which make them grow and learn unconsciously. If teacher us punishment, students are forced to learn under threats. When teacher stop punishing, they would not learn by themselves anymore cause punishments give them bad images of learning. Only rewarding can motivate them to learn by themselves.
When learning, teacher is a great model for students. Praise and rewards create a great environment for students to learn. They are given great opportunities to learn.

subject: HW1001
content:
As lots of people talking about the importance of human rights, some of them now concern about the rights of students.
In the old days, teachers use different kinds of punishment upon those who didn't hand in their homework, didn't pay full attention on their studies, or didn't obey the school regulations, and so on. It was an easy way to control students behavior. Students performed like a tame lamb in the school. Nevertheless, no one can promice that, when students grow up into adults, they will be following the rules though there is not always severe punishment. This sort of education, I think, doesn't last long owing to its largest defect-if no one restricts them from doing wrong things in the future, will they still follow the law?
On the other hand, teachers nowadays choose to award students for good performances instead of scolding them for bad ones. That way, students will try to do their best in everything, and this kind of education cultives their self-motivated attitudes. Take my own experience for instance. When I was in elementary, I was in a normal class, however, we had the most outstanding teacher. Since the first day in the class, he had always been telling us the motto-"You sow what you reap. It's certain no one wants to get bad results, so why not work hard and try your utmost to get the best one?" As a result, to live up to what he said, he always gave us notebooks, dictionaries, and several kinds of stationeries, so as to award us for our good behavior. Believing in this magical rule, I can always concentrate on the goal I have to achieve.
Simply put, I think the latter method works much more efficiently than the former one. If one believes that his hard work will definitely be repaid, he'll do his best to realize his ideal.

subject: HW1001
content:
No one can deny that punishment is able to make a student live with strong discipline. Indeed, not a few parents agree with that, but does punishment leave a good effect on the students? Under the shadow of the punishment, do students really grow without psychological impacts or side effects of it?
As fas as the studies are concerned, more than a half studies show that rewarding students for learning can make students more complete charateristic and positive attitude toward life than severe punishment. As for me, a teacher in senior high, I take it for granted that rewarding is a more effective way to motivate students to learn. The following is my student that is treated completely differently during his school life.
Tom, a basketball player in school club, is used to be punished severely by all the teachers in the school for the sake of his giving up of school work. It wasn't until he met me did he change his whole life. I tried to encourage him to take interest in the school work by rewarding him to play one hour of basketball. From then on, he became a positive boy that I have ever seen, and finally succeed in the school work.
From the example that Tom gives us. We can easily tell that rewarding and love teaching are the most important parts of the helping a student to get somewhere.

subject: HW1001
content:
To let students do better jobs, I think the most important factor is confidence. And to enhance their confidence, rewarding students is more effective than punishing them. Maybe giving them punishments can change what they do instantly, but they will be unhappy to change their behavior because no one likes to be punished. Instead of that, praising them with a simple "Good job!" might be better. In that case, they will change their behavior because they want to, and not because they are afraid of punishments.
When I was in junior high, I wasn't good at math first because once my grade was lower than eighty five points, my teacher would hit me by a thin stick. If I got seven points lower than eighty five, he hit me seven times. On year later, my math teacher changed. He never punished me, instead, he always tried to encourage me and helped me find my problems. From then on, my math skills improved rapidly. This example shows that which way is better for me.

subject: HW1001
content:
I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results, because there are a lot of students are high-esteemed. They can not stand other people blame or punish them. When they are blame, they always feel frustrated, and some of them will give up on themselve. Therefore, I don't think that punishing students will get better results than rewarding students.
Take myself for example, nobody likes to be blame, and so do I. When I was a junior high student, teachers often punished me because I did not get good grades. However, due to the punishment, I hated learning more and more, so my grades were always terrible. When I finally became a senior high student, I studied hard for I could get rewarding money. On the other hand, even if I got bad grades, my teachers of senior high school would not punish me; instead, they encouraged me. Because of that, my grades in the senior high school are very outstanding.
To sum up, I believe that rewarding students can encourage them, but punishing students can do nothing but frustrate them.

subject: HW1001
content:
If asked which method I think is the most effective way to educate students, I would like to choose to reward them for learning instead of punishing them when they make mistakes. In my opinion, every student must go through a period of time in which he or she has difficulty learning new things. When students are faced with things they are not familiar with, they would feel stress not only from the fear of learning new things, but also from the doubts about their ability to solve problems and to catch up with other classmates. Therefore, using punishment may give students more stress. And they will feel so stressful that they can't concentrate themselves on their studies. What's worse, they may even give up learning and refuse to touch any new things.
I have ever taught several elementary school students. If I tried to scold them about their mistakes, they always revised the answer with tears rolling down their face. However, they are too nervous to check out their mistakes calmly. Instead, they made another mistake and got something far from the real answers. So I changed my way of teaching them. I explained why their answers were wrong carefully and slowly, and attempted to realize why they made such mistakes. In addition, if they successfully correct their answer, I would give them candies as rewards. In so doing, I gradually found them doing better on the tests. Further more, students and I become closer and always talk about problems happily together. After that, I decided not to punish students. We should use our love to motivate students to learn instead!

subject: HW1001
content:
I am in favor of rewarding students for learning. Punishment can do nothing to improve students' attitudes toward learning. If teachers always punish students for their bad grades, they will get hurt mentally and physically. On the contrary, if teachers always praise students for their progress, they will feel confident. Praise can help students build confidence and they will try to do better on every subject in order to receive praises from teachers.
For example, when I was in eighth grade, once I sang a song for the performance in the music class. Before I started my performance, I felt so nervous that I shivered all the time. My teacher told me to take easy and do my best. Then I began to perform. After my performance, my teacher said "Good job! Your pitch is not bad." The teacher's compliment gave me great courage, and now I am not afraid at all. I have enough courage and confidence to perform on stage no matter how many people are looking at me.

subject: HW1001
content:
Whether today or the past, I think teachers play a vital role in everyone's life. However, the attitude toward teaching methods can vary from teacher to teacher.
As far as most students concerned, a teacher who is very stern will decrease their motives toward studying and even don't want to take his or her class. On the contrary, a teacher who is nice and charming will attract their attention.
In my opinion, teachers should take the resposibilities to their students. Sometimes, moderate punishment is needed, but patience is the most important, because no one is perfect so a few mistakes can be somehow ignore. I think rewarding students for learning is essential when students have improvement. For instance, I had poor grades in math when I was in seventh grade. But thanks to my patient math teacher for always encouraging me to practice more. Once I had a little improvement and she gave me a watch for rewarding me, since then I was encouraged and never afraid of Math.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, I prefer rewarding students to punishing them.
Rewarding is more effective than punishing. First, everyone likes to be praised but not blame, and so do students. When students make some mistakes, teachers have to be more patient and tell them the right answers. Also, when students get good grades on tests or make progress, teachers should give them little prizes, such as candies, as a reward. Last but not least, teachers can design some fun games for students to relax after their montly test. It can not only raise students' interest in class but learn more quickly than boring class.
Based on my examples, teachers and students will have a good relationship via their interaction. Instead of punishing, teachers can motivate students to learn happily and control their behavior easily by rewarding them. It's a wonderful method, isn't it? Let's reward!

subject: HW1001
content:
To my opinion, it is allowed that the teachers use punishment. There is a Chinese proverb "Children won't be successful if you don't hit them when they make mistakes.", it seems that even people hundreds years ago agree with the point that teachers should give the students punishment. At first they would be afraid, then they change theirselves.
Teachers in my elementary school used to punish me whenever I did something wrong. Since then, I have usually tried to make myself improved, be a better me, and not to make the same error twice because I do not want to recieve punishment. Now I go to a famous school and have a fine grade. I think that's because of the punishment from my school, it's really effective.
In fact, the reason why some teachers use punishment is not because they like to. Teachers are important in students' life, they merely want their students to be better; therefore, they punish students. To sum up, I think the effective way to help students is give them punishment. Rewarding can be just spoil them from my point of view.

subject: HW1001
content:
There is a controvery about whether teachers should punish or reward students to motivate them to learn. In my opinion, rewarding students is a more effective way of teaching students. Unlike punishing, students will be more willing to come up with their own ideas. They will feel more confident about themselves while making themselves understood. Also, rewarding encourages students to fight for the award voluntarily. Thus, there will also be chance to make mistakes without being punished.
Take one of my classmate as an example, she prefers teachers who encourage students to the ones that criticize or use punishment as a way to teach. If the teachers punish her in order to teach her, she will be unwillingly to learn and make herself become a worse person instead. On the contrary, if the teachers give out awards for getting the right answers or encourage students while making mistakes, she will show great interests or positive attitude toward learning.
There might be advantages for punishment. However, rewarding would be a better way for me while learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
For me, teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn or control their behavior is more effective. As we all know, humen cannot be enthusiastic about one thing for long, especially for students to concentrate on their schoolwork. As a result, reasonable punishment is required, for it can give students some pressure to keep working hard on their schoolwork. On the other hand, to students who are still young, they may occasionally lose the judgment of good things and bad things. Therefore, they make mistakes and break the school rules. In such situation, teachers must use punishment in order to adjust their behavior, bringing them back to the right way.
For instance, if a sudent cheat on the exam because he has not prepare for it, how can a teacher say this, "if you do not cheat next time, I will reward you." On contrast, a teacher should give the student punishment strictly so that he will not dare to cheat next time and start to work hard on his schoolwork. We know that rewarding students can protect them not to be hurt, but the progress is made from hurt. Without hurt of punishment how can a student behave themselves and do the best as possible as they can?

subject: HW1001
content:
Rewarding students will undoubtedly lead to better results. In my opinion, punishment is like a kind of effective drug, powerful but dangerous. Once it is overused students' immune system in the heart may grow stronger and stronger; finally when students get used to the punishment, the "final weapon" would be no use. On the contrary, rewarding students is capable of encouraging them, arousing the passion for learning in the bottom of the heart, and making good relationship between teachers and students. Futhermore, the rewards not only satisfy children's desire for toys or foods, but they're also accompanied with the sense of acheivement!
There can't be any other story that is so real to persuade me to believe in the benefit of rewarding except for my little brother's one. My parents believe that "spare the rod, spoil the child", thus always punishing my brother for mistakes. Two weeks ago they said that they surrendered to that naughty little boy. I then took the responsibility to teach him. Reluctant as I was, I tried the rewarding way instead of the punishing one. To everyone's surprise, after two weeks of experimetal period of time, my little brother became obedient and like this elder brother more and more! Since there's no strict rules of how to raise and teach a child, why not choose the more peaceful one?

subject: HW1001
content:
In the past, both teachers and parents thought that when students did things wrong, they deserved punishments. And most of people thought that if you didn't hit students, they would not become successful. Nowadays, people consider corporal punishment should be banned because some students might be hurt seriously or even get mental diseases.
My opinion is that teachers should try to make their punishments moderately. Teachers cannot be too stern or too good to the students. If they are going to be stern to the students, they can't do things that will hurt students like hit them until they're bruised. On the other hand, if teachers are going to reward students read some benificial sentences to the students, for example, the sentences in Confuscious Analects always have positive influence on students.
Once, I read a story about a bad-behavior students and a kind teacher. The student used to do many bad things. One day, he met the kind teacher. The teacher told him a story of a man who did many bad things when he was little, but became a successful businessman when he grown up. The story inspired the bad-behavior student and he eventually turn into a good student.

subject: HW1001
content:
"How can a proper school teacher hit a child like this?" Many times on the news we can hear this line being said over and over again. In the Chinese culture, not only parents, but also teachers use strict punishments on children. On the other hand, more and more people are coming out and saying that "love" is actually the proper way to teach a child. To me, I stand on the "love" side more than the harsh and unhuman like punishments.
Since I have gone through the punishments myself as a student in Taiwan, it doesn't really make me or the other students more motivated on our work. We just become more and more afraid of the teacher and will start to dislike that specific sudject. Many teacher punish students thinking that they will become more hardworking but that is not always right.
Many times on the news you will see students who do suicide learing a note saying that how mean the teacher is and how much presure he or she is having. Also you can find many students that drop out of class because of what the teacher will do to them. On the other hand, I have also studied in the United States for several years and know what it is like to be rewarded by a teacher.
I used to hate going to school because I was so afraid of getting harsh punishments but it all changed after I got to the states. Using love and rewards towards students was such a big difference and made me want to do good in class. Teachers of different grades rewards the students with different presents but this can catch their attention towards their studies. Since than, my grades become better and better because of the rewards I have gotten.
From my own self experience, I can sure tell you from a student's view, rewards are far more better than punishments. Teachers should encourage students rather saying that they are dumb and hit them. But still, it depends on which kind of teacher you get during school.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, corporal punishments are prohibited and many people suggest that rewarding be the better way to motivate students. However, in my opinion, I still suppose the punishment is more efficient. Perhaps physical punishments are too serious, but light punishments are acceptable for me.
For example, students tend to ignore the importance of respecting the senior, handing in their homework on time or being honest and responsible for their studying and exams. If we only reward those who obey the rules, and what about those who break the principles and expect nothing for rewarding? Take cheating for instanse, no cheating for a box of candy, no candy for scoring one hundred. On the other hand, no cheating for nothing, but cheating leads to a great punishment.
As I have mentioned the above, students are more likely to prefer no punishment to a box of candy. Consequently, it goes without saying that having punishments is inevitable for students.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think rewarding students for learning is better than punishment. Everyone is afraid of punishment. Punishment plays an strict role in our life. Roaring loudly at you, ordering you to stand outside the classroom, or even hitting you with a stick, these things will become a nightmare to us. Because we are afraid of punishment, we will not like the class or the teacher. The heart of learning is broken. However, if teachers reward students for learning, we will enjoy the happiness, and want to behave better. It is clear that rewarding students is more effective than punishment.
I remember an experience vividly. When I was in elementary school, my math was worse than my classmates. I didn't do well in any math test. The teacher was unhappy at me. He though I didn't study hard, so he punished me with a stick. The hurt which the stick gave to me I would never forget. However, I did not have better grades after his punishment. I felt math is an evil who will hit me with a stick.
After two years, my math teacher was replaced with a young lady. First, I was still afraid of her and math. However, she found this situation. She tried to talk to me that math is very interesting. Although my math grades was still bad, she also encouraged me. I wanted to thank to her. The only thing I chould do was getting good grades. Then, I studied hard than before. Finally, I behaved more and more good on math. Not only my new math teacher but also I was glad of my behaves.
So, I think that punishment is the worst way to order student study hard. Rewarding and encouraging are more effective to everyone. In the future, I will not punish my children. I will encourage them to do their best. I think they can find the happiness of learning and behave better than me!

subject: HW1001
content:
As far as I am concerned, I think that giving rewards to students is a better way. For one thing, human beings is born to pursue the things which they want. Therefore, longing for the rewards, students will study hard to get them. Second, punishment will do harm to both of students' minds and bodies. What's more, using punishments is probably to make students afraid of learning. To avoid the worst results, I prefer rewards to punishments.
Take me for instance, I used to be a students who was too lazy to study hard. Undoubtedly, I had a bad academic performance. However, I was lucky enough to meet my homeroom teacher when I was third grade in elementary school. My teacher would encourage us by presents and praises. Since then, I became a hardworking student and felt satisfied with the rewards. Owing to the teacher's proper way of teaching, everybody in my class seemed to have a great progress. As a proverb goes "All work and no play make Jack a dull." The proverb is a metaphor. If teacher don't offer rewards but only punishments, students will become dulls as well. According to my personal experience, I am convinced that rewards are more effective than punishments.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I do not approve of using punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Virtually, if teachers want to control their behavior, they should show them the consequence of the conduct but not let them feel scared of the stick. Besides, I think that it is better to motivate the desire of acquiring knowledge and to understand the importance of learning.
Take Elva Edison for example. As he is a child, he is so-called "bad" student but not the "talented" student on the class. Thank to his mother, she used rewarding means to teach Edison. For this reason, he invented the greatest things-bulb in the future. Given that Edison's mother didn't take an adaptive action and let Edison follow the formular education, we could still use the candle to light our darkness. Nevetheless, no matter how great the approach of teaching, it still have the same ideal between teachers and parents or it will hinder the growth of chidren.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers ask their students to have good behaviors through corporal punishment. The motivation is ok. But sometimes, they don't realize that their punishment really hurt the prides of children. As a result, more and more people support to ban corporal punishment, including me.
A lot of teachers punish their students in great anger, and that often cause serious consequences. For instence, there was a ten-year-old boy who studys in elementary school; one day, he said something bad about his teacher. But unfortunately, the teacher knew about that, and he punished the boy by hitting him until the boy got serious bruise. Actually, the boy's behavior shouldn't deserve such a serious punishment, all this happened just because the teacher was too angry.
To sum up, corporal punishment should be banned because there are still so many teachers don't know how to control their emotions. Teachers should teach their students in gentle instead of controling their students through violence.

subject: HW1001
content:
Wether teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn or reward students for learning have been broadly discussed in recent years. As being a junior high school teacher for more than five years myself, I strongly surport rewarding students for learning more than punishment.
Compare these two methods, you can get an effective attention by using punishment, and it takes long time to see the outcome with rewarding. That's the main reason why most teachers choose punishment because they can get students' attention right away by giving them more pressure. As a result, teachers have to be strict and mean to gain respect from the students, and I don't really approved this way of teaching.
In my opinion, rewarding doesn't neccessarily to be giving prize or gifts. It could be the compliment you give to the students, "Well done!" is a very powerful phrase than anything. Several studies showed that anxiety decreased students' learning outcome. Especially when teaching junior high school students, my experience told me that when increasing messure, they often choose not to face it. Some of them even make the class worse by talking back to the teacher who punish them.
Learning is a life time lesson to motive students' learning, encoraging the students is better than punishing them and make the lost the interests of learning.

subject: HW1001
content: Both punishing and rewarding have benefits in education. To my opinion, rewarding students may be more effective. Punishing may make students behave for a while, but they will not be happy. By rewarding, students will be willing to be good, and the effects last longer. When I was in elementary school, one of my classmates often talk in class. The teacher punished him by hitting him. The boy stopped chattering in class but he also hate the teacher for his punishment. A year later, we had another teacher. The boy still keep his bad habit, talking in class and making fun of others. The new teacher had a different method for him. "Behave," she told the boy, "and you will get a special prize when the semester ends." Like a miracle, the boy's bad behavior ended. The new teacher had never hit him, nor did she ever scolded him, but her method worked well for him. Therefor, I believe rewarding students is a better method of education. Punishment may work, but it's not the best way after all.

subject: HW1001
content:
Education is one of the most important things in our life, and the teachers we meet often have a great impact on how successful our learning will be. Some teachers view punishment as the best way to motivate students, while some consider rewarding students a better way to help them grow and learn. However, in my opinion, encouraging and rewarding will always be the best and only way to benefit a student's learning and personality.
First of all, rewarding students can motivate them to work harder. Take my teacher's story for example. In her first year of teaching school, she was assigned to teach in a class that was known for being overly calm and quiet. Their shyness often made it difficult for classes to go on. However, when she started to help the students speak by giving out prizes and chocolate, it really did help her students to participate more in class. Nevertheless, we should always remind our students that they're not studying for the prizes, but for themselves.
Secondly, giving encouragement is also extremely important in education. Encouraging students can not only help them in their study, but will also give them confidence and make them feel like a better person. I used to be a student who often faced the failure in study, and it was my teacher's encouragement that helped me get through all the difficulties. Thus, I'm always appreciated to all my teachers, and I also give a lot of encouragement w ho have problems with their study.
Both punishment and rewarding can be effective to a student's learning, but it is the latter that provides students joy and happiness on the road of education. Rewarding doesn't always mean giving prizes or gifts. Encouraging and giving compliments can also be the best reward for a student. Therefore, I consider rewarding students with prizes and words the best way to help them grow and learn.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, rewarding students for learning is much better than using punishment. Students have the right of making mistake, so they can have more opportunities to learn. If we just using punishment to motivate them and to control their behavior, they won't keep the lesson in mind forever. They just demostrate the good side to prevent themselves from being punished. Therefore, rewarding students is the better way to teach them. By giving them some treatment, student may have more willings to do things correctly. I have some experiences about this: my brother was extremely naughty when he was a child. Sometimes I scolded him or hit him to let him realize that what he did was wrong, but he always did the same thing the next time. That really drove me to distriction! My mother told me that children should be treated not scolded, so I changed the way to teach my brother. I tried to give him some candies or admiring him when he did something good. By this way, he realized the principle that I wanted to let him understand. The older he grow, the more considerate he is. Now, he is a well-behavior teenager and everyone likes him very much. By this experience, I think that teaching students should not use punishment seriously, but admire them more. Rewarding students is more useful. Only do the students want to be better from the bottom of their hearts can motivate them to learn effectively!

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Over the past decades, teachers were allowed to use punishment to make students behave themselves, and I believe it worked. But when it comes to learning, if the teachers use the same means to teach their students, perhaps it will cause negative effects, such as students may lose their self-confidence. Hence, I choose the method that rewarding students for learning.
Take myself for example, I used to be afraid of taking math class becase I thought math formulas were all Greek to me! Fortunately, I met a good teacher when I was in the seventh grade, he taught me patiently and explained every detail for me. From then on, I tried my efforts to study more about math and my grades are now getting better and better. It dawns on me that without his encouragement, I won't have the chance to get high score on math. Most important of all, my teacher helped me overcome my dreads in an effective way-instead of punishing me for poor grades, he praised me or rewarding me whenever I made progress in math. Therefore I support teachers should reward students for learning.
No matter what the teachers use, they all hope to see their students have good achievements. There's still no absolute answers to which ways are better, but depends on the interactions between teachers and students.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. I have two reasons to support my viewpoint.
The first reason is that students can be motivated to study hard while teachers encourage them to learn better by some rewards which students are desired like taking them to have picnic. With the desire of getting the rewards, students will do their best to improve their learning performance.
The second reason is that the atmosphere for learning will be more encouraging if teachers design a special activity for students to compete and to learn the teaching material by heart pretty soon. Students can be divided into groups and compete with one another by finding the answers to questions designed by teachers. It will be thrilling and exciting for students to learn and the the group which wins the game can obtain rewards from teachers. Therefore students will be more willing to learn, and even love to acquire knowledge from teachers.
To sum up, giving students rewards for learning is more effective than punishing students for misbehavior. In this way, students will love learning actively and improve their studying performance.

subject: HW1001
content:
"Wendy! What are you doing on my class! Playing video games or sending text messages? Come straight to the front!" Sounds of "Boo" and her shouts for help have become everything I remembered since that horrible incident.
In my opinion, corporal punishment shouldn't be the only way to educate oneself. There must have been so many methods to teach students the right attitude and concentration required in the class. Punishments won't alter anything but sometimes raise one's hatred toward the teacher which makes the condition worser.
Instead of corporal punishment, I think that rewarding students for learning can simply contribute to better results. Rewarding can encourge students to pursue better grades and enhance their interest toward learning. Simultaneously, an improvement for lines, of communication can exactly make a big difference.

subject: HW1001
content:
Teachers in the past used severe punishment to stimulate their students to learn most of the time, but I oppose this way of teaching. In my opinion, giving students reward and compliment will really motivate them to study willingly and happily. I have read a study shows that students acquire more efficient and effective learning when they are under a relaxed living environment instead of a strict and tension one. Indeed, education will be carried out effectively when students are really willing to learn. After teacher's compliment, students will gain more confidence in their learning and keep working on it.
In my junior high school period, I was very luck to have a good English teacher. She wouldn't punish us when we did wrong; instead, she would give us reward when we finished our homework and she always compliment students. Under her teaching, I was very happy to learn English and willing to study English hard because I got much confidence from her. At that time my classmate in another class skipped classes often because his teacher would scold him and hit him if he hand in his assignment late. From my experience and this comparison, I firmly believe that students will learn more and better if they are in a happy-learning environment, and I swear I would create this class atmosphere if I were a teacher.

subject: HW1001
content:
I believe that most of us had been punished by the teacher when we're young, and most of us dislike it. Nobody wants to get punished but to get rewards. Because of that, I think rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.
For an example, our math teacher often blames us and makes us feel shame, most of us are good in his class but some of us don't like it, and they behave badly. Then, our math teacher retires and another teacher came to teach us. This teacher won't blame us but rewards us, guess what? We learn better and more happily.
In my opinion, I think rewarding students for learning leads us to a better and happier learning. Rewarding students can make the students want to get rewards and are willing to work for it. In the future, they will work hard for their salary.
I believe that rewarding students leads to a better and happier way to learn. The example of our math teacher and the changing of modern society make me think that rewarding students is a more effective way then punishments.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the past, it was common that teachers used punishment to control students' behavior. However, instead of punishment, teachers prefers rewarding students than punishing them nowadays. In my point of view, rewarding students when they learns is more helpful to students. Once a student is stimulated by the reward, they will be more likely confident in their behavior and they will have better behavior afterwards.
Take my sister, Emily for instance. Emily was a naughty girl in her childhood. Every time when she made a mistake, her teacher used punishment on her, such as asking standing out of the classroom for an hour or cleaning up the classroom after class. Nevertheless, the more punishments the teacher compelled on her, the more naughty Emily became. It seemed that punishments had not effected her. Not until Emily met Ms. Lin did the bad situation improve. Ms. Lin have never used punishment in students. Instead, she usually asked students why they made mistakes, then she would patiently tell students the right direct. When students did well on their behavior, Ms. Lin would give them some reward such as candies. After meeting Ms. Lin, Emily became a tender and nice girl. Seldom did she have bad behavior.
Rewarding students is the best way to lead students to better results. After all, everyone need spurs and encouragements when one learns.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think that rewarding students for learning is more effective. Education is more difficult for students now because these children have more strange ideas and they are protected by their parents. When you punish the students, they can accused you, because the law ban you to do that. But if you reward the students, it would go to another way. The students will full of confidence and happiness about learning. And they will do better in the future.
When I was a junior high school student, I was empressed by two of my teachers. Mr. Yang was my biology teacher and he was serious. Mrs. Lin was my chinese teacher and she was nice. Everytime when we were at biology class, none of my classmates dare to speak. When we got poor grades in the test, Mr. Yang would punish us. Gradually, nobody liked Mr. Yang, and our performance in this subject was poor. Converesly, my classmates always did well in the test of Chinese. Mrs. Lin never punished us even we did worse in the test. She always rewarded us on little things, so every of my classmates liked her.
Punishment is not the effective way of teaching, you have to trust your students and reward them all the time.

subject: HW1001
content:
Taiwan's teaching methods have changed from time to time. In the past, teachers could be nothing but rules in the class. However, in Taiwan today, I think that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Studying is not only students' responsibilities but also our rights. Therefore, when we enjoy our rights, we should be happy instead of being punished. To a large number of students, punishment means pressure. Nonetheless, the more stress we have, the less efficient when we learn.
Take me for example, when I was junior high, my parents put lots of expectations on me. All of them caused me feel so nervous that I couldn't get good grade in the exam. What's worse, they led me to a bad health condition, for I couldn't eat much even sleep well. To my relief, when I am senior high, my parents know what is the best to treat me. When I get bad grades, instead of punishing me, they will talk to me with affection. On the other hands, when I get good grades, they will hug me and share my happiness. Now, I know there is always someone behind me, supporting me to face up to all discouragements when studying. To sum up, punishment is no longer the best way to motivate students to learn.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, as we turn on the TV, the terrified tittle about some teachers tring to teach their students in an unproper way came in our sight. And then we can see the student's parents arguing with the teacher. The parents think the teacher shouldn't punish their child; on the contrary, he or she should encorage their child.
Some people believe that one student can only advance through punishment. Others believe that we should have more love and encourage the student to do things which do good to the student themself.
In my thoughts, both methods can control student. But the deffirence between the two methods is that the former's effect is out of students' terror of "hurt", and the later is because they think someone agree with what they do. In additions, the later's effect can last longer; while the formers' effect maybe is only in this short time.
Take myself for example. When I was found using computer, my parents always punish me by I couldn't go out with my friends. But now, they talk to me and tell me that the computer is hormful to my eyesight, so I should control my time using the computer. In this way, I can accept my parents opinion and there is less argument as well.
So, I think it is a proper way to encourage students instead of punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
The world is changing, and we need higher-quality citizens. As a saying goes, "Children are the masters of the twenty-first century." Children need to be armed with politeness and better personalities as well as characteristics. They are meant to succeed. I strongly agree with rewarding and encouraging students.
Imposing threats and punishments is a no-go. Students would oppose to learning and see it as a difficulty. They wouldn't learn to step across their limitations. In short, punishments would only make them shrink fearfully into the darkness.
On the other hand, rewarding and encouraging students would motivate them to accept learning as a fun activity. Moreover, it would cultivate the students' interests. Helen Keller, for instance, found her own voice and succeeded eventually, thanks to her encouraging and optimistic teacher. Helen Keller was physically and mentally challenged, but she proved that the sky's the limit.
Last but not least, giving encouragements pumps up one's spirit and leads them to success. A rewarding and guiding teacher paves the way for students. Who says punishments were the best?

subject: HW1001
content:
In the past, people believed that the more punishments students received, the better they would behave when they grown up. However, people promote that we should teach our next generation with our love and patience in recent years. Instead of punishing students when they do something wrong, people nowadays tend to reward students when they do well on schoolworks. In my opinion, punishment made students alarmed when they faced familiar situation; as a result, they were less likely to make the same mistake over and over again. But punishing students may also lead to the hesitantion when a student is trying something new because the fears of being blamed. How to make a balance between punishments and rewards is very important.
When I was in elementary school, my homeroom teacher was a very stern man. He punished us when we made any mistake on our schoolwork. Therefore, I became more careful when I was solving every problems and got into a habit of thinking before I leap. He was very strict with our studying yet not too mean. Sometimes when we did well on our tests, he rewarded us with some candies and was never stingy with praising us.
As long as one finds a balance between punishment and reward, it is beneficial to both the teacher and the student.

subject: HW1001
content:
As for me, I think rewarding is a better and more effective method to encourage students to learn and to manipulate their behavior.
Basically, I perceive that everyone, including kids, likes to listen to sweet words. When an elementary school student were praised by his teacher for doing something well, he would smile and would like to behave even better to please his teacher.
On the other hand, if a teacher scolded, even punished, his class quite often, the atmosphere of his class would not be very good. Seeing the teacher's dull face all the time, the students won't be happy. They may think unconsciously that their teacher doesn't like them, so that they don't have to behave well for him.
The material rewarding method is prevailedly used in English classes of elementary schools. The teachers give points to the team which behaves well in class and give prizes to good individuals after the whole semester. It works and thus encourages a lot of our students to learn English.
Therefore, I suggest that rewarding, no matter in the form of oral or material one, would be more effective than punishment and will lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
If I am a teacher, I will reward hardworking students as well as punish students who always fooling around. In my opinion, rewarding or punishing students depends on what kind of students they are. Take the student's personality into consideration, it is no use to reward a negative student who doesn't even have a bit of sense of honor and no need to punish a positive student who is always afraid of losing chance to get new knowledge and falling behind.
For example, when I was in junior high school, there were many kind of students in my class. Some speaked dirty words every moment and never pay attention to the teacher. Even if the teacher said she would give a secret present for those who progressed most in final exam, they didn't change their behovior. After three years, I graduated from junior high school and went to Tainan first senior high school. Every student took good care of their study and no need teachers to push us. When we felt tired of the overwhelming test, the teacher sometimes rewarded us in order to increase our studying power. However, to cultivate a good learning habit is the most important thing to build a successful man.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the old time, parents definitely agreed that they need to punish their kids if their kids doesn't get a good grade. Now, the world is changing. This is a world that we should respect everyone's human right so I disagree to punish students to make them study.
I am a senior high students now. I have lots of subjects to study and I have to go to cram school almost everyday. My mom never punish me when I get a poor grade instead, she will cheer me up and tell me that I can do better next time. I always put this words in my mind which make me study harder and become more consentrate. When we are under lots of pressure, we need someone to get along with and help us to overcome the obstacles.
In our country, students are working too hard. If parents still punish or scold their children, they will eventually loss their confidence for studying. Parents should talk to their children when they are in depressed and give them awards when they perform well. If the children know their parents' love, they will surely put their whole heart on studying.

subject: HW1001
content:
I support using punishment to make sure students' learning and their behavior. I think punishment is more effective than rewarding. Because punishment, in my opinion, can establish a kind of attitude in childrens' brains, telling them what they should do and what they can't do. Children might be very upset and even curse the one who punish them when they are punished. But I believe after they grow older, they would appreciate those strict adults for taking them to the right way.
As to rewarding the students, I don't think it is as effective as punishment. To me, rewarding is just like for someone who did something good, instead of not doing something wrong. Rewarding might be effective when it comes to learning, but it may not did as good as punishment when it comes to control students' behavior.
I'm the best example for punished student. When I was in junior high school, my teachers are strict, which makes me have good grades because I was scared of being punished for poor grades.

subject: HW1001
content:
If I were a teacher, I would choose rewarding my students rather than punishing them. In my opinion, punishment makes students feel negative and reduce their will on studying. On contrast, rewarding students may let them have a positive attitude toward studying.
I am a student now. My teacher is a very nice women. In her mind, she believe punishing student is the worst thing in the world because it make the relationship between she and the student become bad. Besides, punishment make students fear to face the wrong thing they've did. So my teacher seldom punished us. Instead, she rewarded us for good behavior. Therefore, my classmates always did their best to help others and my class usually get the best grades in my school. I think that is the power of rewarding.
To sum up, I think rewarding studen may be a better way to motivate students to learn. Through rewarding, student may try their best to purchase the honor. Besides, students begin to do things autometically. This is why I think rewarding students is a more effective way.

subject: HW1001
content:
News like teacher punishing children in school or saying something mean to students isn't uncommon in the modern world. In old days, children usually got beaten up in school when doing something wrong, and when they went home, scolding and beating is also unavoidable. As the time changes, we prefer praising kids and awarding them in order to bring out their best instead. But there is an extremely enormous gap between these two ways.
I come from a wealthy family, my parents seldom interfior with what I do. They believe that I have the ability to separate right from wrong and that I understand what I want and what I am doing. They care about me, but they loose their hands to let me fly. Striking a balance between schoolwork and activities isn't as easy as it seems, but I am doing a pretty good job.
Other classmates in school aren't as lucky as I am. They are often grouded or punished because of getting home too late or going out without telling their parents. They have to be watched every moment so as to finish their homework and studies. If not, they would totally lose control and have fun all day long.
The point I am trying to say is, everyone in the world comes from different families and has different backgrounds, the best and most effective way to teach them should be choosen carefully based on their very own personalities. There is no absolute answer to what method is the best, it depends on whom you use it on, for everyone is an unique individual.

subject: HW1001
content:
Teachers usually want to find a proper way to educate their students in their studies as well as their behavior. Some prefer using punishment, while others prefer giving rewards. Both methods have their advantages and disadvantages. If we always punish students for their poor performance, they will probably be more diligent to improve themselves. However, giving punishment excessively may cause negative effects. Students may lose their confidence and interest in what they are planning to do. On the other hand, rewarding students can build up their confidence, motivating them to improve in a better way. Nonetheless, too much encouragement will make students too proud to notice the efforts behind their success. For me, I like to reward students instead of punishing them because people usually work better with positive mind.
Take my cousin for example. He used to get awful grades in his elementary school, and thus his hands were always hit by his extremely strict teacher. Under the huge pressure, he performed worse and worse, finally being filled with frustration. Fortunately, he met his mentor in junior high school. She was a patient teacher who always listened to my cousin's questions and helped him figure them out. With her assistence, my cousin reobtained his confidence in his studies. Because of his experience, I agree that rewarding students can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, how to motivate students to learn has become a controversial issue. Some people think using punishment is a good way while some regard rewarding students is better.
In my opinion, I support that teachers should punish students to let them learn better. First of all, I don't think students in Taiwan have enough willing to study. They might want to play on-line games or do anything else instead of learning. Secondly, because some students afraid of being punished, they might choose control their behavior and spend more time on study. And these can help them studying more. Thirdly, some teachers punishing their students by asking them to do extra homeworks. Through this, students would gain more knowledge or paying more attention on schoolwork from it.
To sum up all reasons, that is why I think punishing students is more effective.

subject: HW1001
content:
When I was young, it is quite easy to see teachers punishing or yelling at students in school. Nowadays, however, thanks to the thoughts of educational revolution, more and more educational institutions and parents claim that they oppose the way of rewarding students for learning, though there are still sounds of disagreement.
In my opinion, I think that teachers should reward students when they have good performances instead of punish them when they err. By doing this, students will feel pleased and therefore have more motivation to do better and win more plause from teachers or friends. On the other hand, teachers won't have to yell madly all the times, which may lead to health damage and depression.
Take my own self for example, my homeroom teacher in the fourth grade of elementary school would never blame me if I didn't mean to make the mistake. On the contrary, he would only tell me how to do better next time. This unforgettable experience is still in my mind though we haven't meet for years.
As a conclusion, I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the past, most teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. As a result, students in the past usually behave well and do their best to prepare for all tests because they are afraid of punishment. However, most teachers nowadays reward students for learning. As a result, students do not work hard and even argue with their teachers because there is no punishment. In my opnion, I think that rewarding students for learning is good, but sometimes it is essential to give students punishment if they do not behave well or get bad grades on exams. If there is no punishment anymore, your students will become spoiled.
I have some examples to support my opnion. To begin with, my mother is a teacher, and she didn't give punishment to her students in the past. One day her students talked in her class and she was very angry. As a result, she gave punishment to them. Next time there was no one dared to talk in her class. Second, my history teacher always gives us punishment if we don't do well on her tests. Because we are afraid of her, we spend a lot of time studying history. There is no denying that we get a good grade on the college entrance exam. And the last but not least, I find that if one student have a lot of tests tomorrow, he or she will choose the subject whom the teacher is more horrible to prepare. If he or she get a bad grade tomorrow, he or she will be punished. In conclusion, I think that punishment is neccessary and teachers should use punishment in the right time.

subject: HW1001
content:
I firmly believe that rewarding students for learning can led to better results. Even though many seniors say that they educated their children by using punishment which is the most effective and direct way. Yet, as time passes, a lot of things are absolutely different from the past; that is, it is high time for people to change and improve the traditional conservative concept. Due to this, I think to reward students for learning is more effective. Take myself for example.
As a student I was, I didn't know how to study well. I was afraid of the bad feeling of failure, so I just study and study but without any effective ways. I didn't think that I didn't like to study or I wasn't active to learn, but it was quite impossible for me to get good grades. In the meantime, I met two teachers who were really different from each other. One was very serious and think that good students ought to get an A in every test while the other was trying her best to help the students solve their problems. Even though I knew that two of the teachers were trying to make students better, I just couldn't accept the way the first teacher used-punishment and scolding. I thought that she hated me so she blamed me, and that's why I wanted to rebel her. On the other hand; the other teacher taught me patientatly and thoroughly. She inspired and encouraged me and that made me improve my work at school willingly.
To sum up, I think rewarding students is better to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior for now.

subject: HW1001
content:
Needless to say, knowledge is fairly imperative. By means of making it more effective to motivate students to learn well and control their behavior better, different teachers have got their own distinct methods. There are many prons and cons for both the punishment and the rewarding. In my opinions, I think teachers can reward students more often than scold them.
To cite one of Edison's famous quotes, "Genius is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent perspiration." Once students are willing to accept the concept taught by teachers, it's not necessary to use any kinds of punishment. Teachers can inspire students to study harder by just only giving them a little compliment. To take some slower kids for an example, they are easy to feel sad when they are scolded because they can't approach the goals which are set by the teachers. At this moment, I believe that encouragement is much better the punishment. If teachers could seperate the big goals into several small parts and inspire students to try hard to make it, students would be more craving for studying.
However, that's not the only challenge the teachers will meet. Once students are in bad attitude, I think teachers will need some punishment to control their behavior. Since they have no choice but to face reality, teachers should choose some milder punishment to avoid making severe injury to students. As for me, I would punish students by asking them to stand still for 10 minutes instead of hitting them with a stick.
No matter punishment or rewarding, teachers are really hard-working. Maybe we should require ourselves to respect teachers more and study harder. Learing knowledge well nowadays has been really on the rise. Once we get it, we will success.

subject: HW1001
content:
Which one will make you more willing to study hard? Punishing you if you don't get good grades on the exam, or rewarding you if you do a great job during the semester?
Many people might think that neither punishment nor reward is a good method to motivate students to learn; they consider love and communication is the best way to educate students. However, in the reality, it is essential for teachers to use some "tricks" to push their students. They have no choice but to make a choice between punishment and reward.
In my opinion, punishment is more effective. Nowadays, people in Taiwan have become richer and parents have tried their best to give their children high quality lifes. As a result, the gift that teachers reward students might not be prescious to students.
Take a story I have read for example: students reguarded the pen which teacher had given him as a present for good grades as a cheep junk, and threw it a way.
The punishment, in the contrary, is easier to effect students. They will try hard to finish their homework in order not to be grounded or else.
Though it isn't the best way in education, punishment is sure to be an powerful way to control students.

subject: HW1001
content:
As far as I am concerned, I think rewarding students for learning can lead to better results, for I consider that it is a fabulous motivation to spur the students to make endeavor to get good grades and encourage them to sort out the difficulties they face.
However, there are many teachers who still want to control the students' behavior by punishment substantially. They not only hope to impress the students on not obeying the rules but also vent their fierce anger. In addition, even the parents also treat their children in this way. It has turned out a common phenomenon among the Taiwan's society.
In fact, I was an authentic victim of punishment, for I was unable to grapple with a math question. I was hit by my teacher excessively so that I was immoderately afraid of the math exam. What's worse, I became a unhappy girl in despire, for I didn't have any confidence. Fortunately, after going to the senior high school, I met a great teacher. He rooted for me and adhered to help me comprehend the math in details.
He always praise us and reward the students who improved their math grades with a delicate gift. From then on, my grades became very excellent. Therefore, I believe that rewarding students is a really good method.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, the issue of whether instructors take punishment a way to motivate students to learn and make them behave well has become more and more controversy. Both methods have their pros and cons in educating a child to be a more complete man, but with a view to having positive and permanent effect in children's mind and to letting the children's to know the spirit of learning, I prefer to take the dicipline of rewarding.
In the past, it was common to see parents hitting their kids hands with a long, thick stick. People discovered children applied with such physical punishment learn very fast, but they failed to understand underlying passive influence to give to their children. According to recent studies in American, children are more likely to form pessimistic personality and are less active and innovative in their career.
On the other hand, appropriate rewarding not only can keep children from fears and anxious of being punished, but are able to telling them right from wrong without confusing them. In the same research, the scientist claims that they have found children tend to be more confident and even more responsible in those of rewarding-teaching diciplines.
As a result, compare to those punishment dicipline children applied rewarding dicipline are more likely to know what they are doing and are not likely to know why they have to behave well. Besides, children's mind are so sensitive that it might have bad experience in front of the fear of punishment. In short, for the children's sake, it is necessary to wish children to have a harmonious children childhood.

subject: HW1001
content:
As far as I am concerned, rewarding students for learning can be more effective than use punishment.
First, everyone likes being rewarded when doing well. As a result, take rewarding as a motivation for students to progress will be more useful. Take my own experience for example, I used to perform very bad on math. My mother was very angry about that and she always scolded or punished me for my poor grade. However, the more punishments she used, the pooer grade I did. Since I always under the high pressure before I took the exams, I was unable to do well. Finally, she realized the reason why and replaced punishment with reward. She stopped blaming on me but encourge me whenever I did poor grade. As I made a progress, she will please me or sent me a present. Surprisngly, my math grade was gradually progress after she changed her way to educate me.
For this reason, I was firmly convinced that rewarding is better than punishment as the way to make students progress or behave well.

subject: HW1001
content:
Every teacher has the responsibiliy to educate students. As a result, each teacher has their own methods and ideas toward education. Some teachers chooses stricker ways like punishment, and the others refers to nice attitude. In my viewpoint, I think that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results, and it is more effective. Although I am not a teacher, I think the things which students need when they are learning are clear communication and completely understanding. We students should have much talking with their teachers when we did something wrong or made mistakes so that we can know how to fix or solve the problems and troubles. Also, students and teachers can exchange their thoughts and opinion by much talking. In other words, teachers should ecourage or reward students while they are learning so that we students won't fear any difficulties when we are facing the challenges.
Take my intimate friends Lily for example. She was my best friend when we were only ten in elementary school. I still remember that she had ever cheated in test which was quite important. And she was found doing that by two of my teachers in class. One of them was strick, but the other one was kind. The strick one punished Lily to write "Sorry" for one thousand times. As a consequence, Lily was deeply sad and depressed, and even didn't talk to me for a week. Oh my god! I felt very unhappy, too. But luckily, the kind one had a nice talking and communication with Lily on the other day. The kind teacher also rewarded her a chance to change herself. As a result, Lily was alive again! She became more positive and confident.
To sum up, I really want to say that rewarding students for learning is absolutely correct education.

subject: HW1001
content:
I hold the opinion that teachers should use punishments. Punishments are necessary for students to study hard and behave well.
Due to the increase of entertainments, students pay poor attentions on their learning. Punish them is the only way to push them to learning. The number of the students drops every year, therefore, every student is the preasure of their parents. Parents rarely punish them, so, if teachers treat them like their parents, those students will just like the flowers in the greenhouse. Once they have to get a work, they are too weak to compete with others.
Rewarding students for learning is a good idea, too. But, students had already get enough rewards from their parents. The rewards they recieve from teachers seem nothing compare to the rewards from their parents. As a final word, teachers should use punishments.

subject: HW1001
content:
Using punishment to motivate students or rewarding students for learning has always been an educational issue. In my opinion, rewarding students for learning can lead to better results instead of punishing students to motivate and control their behavior. Students may feel pressured because of the punishment have been put on them so that they can't try their best or express themselves' opinions to their teachers. Nevertheless, rewarding students for learning can make students build confidence and feel the sense of the achievement in their mind.
When I was in elementary school, our teacher used to give our class some gifts or promise to take us to some famous sight-seeing spots because we got good grades in a few competitions held by our school. Therefore, we usually got first place in most competitions. We not only got the prizes that our teacher had promised to give us but we also had good memories of our classmates. In addition, I formed the habit of doing my best to complete everything when I grew up.
Providing some moderate prizes to students is beneficial for their process of learning. Teachers can not only pay attention to students' grades but also their mental health. To sum up, I think rewarding students is the better way for students.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the area of education, to judge what is right and what is wrong is out of question. It is a complicated issue. Punishment is a way teachers tell children that their behavior are not appropriate. Compliment is a opposite manner to inform them that they are doing well. The two methods cooperation with each other and you can not separate them apart. There are no knowing which one is more effective and which one is less worth. My opinion is that you should choose the right one in the right situation. If the students didn't hand in the reports before deadline, you could punish them. If children gave others a helping hand, you could compliment on them for the good behavior. Thus, punishment can prevent children from doing bad and compliment can be hidden power to push students upward. The most important thing is not to argue which method is the best, but the moment.
My aunt has a daughter, who is the only child in the family. She is the apple in my aunt's eye. My aunt never punishes her and keeps a blind eye to what she does wrong. The girl has grown up, and always talks to everyone with her nose in the air. She told me that she was lonely. I knew that answer, but I didn't tell her. The answer is that she never know she was wrong.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, the education gradually have played an important role in this era. Thus, teachers play as a vital role in teaching and cultivating students. I am of the opinion that a good teachr not only have to acquire a large amount of knowledge in his or her professional field but also be good at teaching the students in an efficient and propre way.
As a student, I prefer teachers who are patient in teaching and encouraging students who are not good at their academic performances. On the contrary, if a teacher is used to punish and mock at those students who are lazy and in poor grades, then, the students may not become more and more confident in their studies.
Furthermore, teachers who tends to encourage students on their academic performances are more respected and loved by students. Thus, students are willing to do their best on studying and listening to what teachers said in class. In other words, both teachers and students can create and enjoy the efficient and harmonious atmosphere in the class.
Last but not least, teachers who tend to reward students for learning can lead to better results because every student will step into the society some day in the future. In this way, the students can be accustomed to the regulations and rules in this society. There is no such thing as a lunch. Therefore, through the rewards, students can learn that they have to study hard in order to gain the goal in their future.
As far as I am concerned, students prefer to teachers who do not punish to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Students are creative and aggressive enough to pursue what they want in their future. Therefore, teachers who reward students on their excellent learning and attitude is a better and appropriate way.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, although students can learn and behave well by being punished, I think it is temporary and it may harm students. For me, I think rewarding is more effective than punishment. There are some reasons and examples.
First, learning should be interesting. I also think that students with confidence, curiosity and good mood can learn better. On the one hand, if a teacher always punishes students, students will finally think that learing is terrible and they may be afraid of it. On the other hand, if a teacher always rewards students, students will find out that learning is delighting and they will keep going on their own.
Second, students need to be responsible for their behaviors. I think it is difficult for students to realize they are studying for themselves by punishment. Instead, studends who are given rewards and encouragement can be responsible for themselves, even there is no teacher beside them. Take an American Teacher as an example. In his class, there is a boy who hates studying. Many teachers punish the boy but the situation doesn't improve. Instead of punishing, that teacher teaches the boy patiently and encourages him all the time. Gradually, the boy makes some progress in his grades and that teacher gets awards, too.
In conclusion, I think students need more love and encouragement. They can learn and behave well by giving rewards. For these reasons, I think rewarding students is more effective.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, punishment doesn't work. Many students are forced to learn because of punishment. Definitely, they may really learn something, but forget it quickly as well. This doesn't reach the goal of learning.
As I was a junior high school student, my grades were not so bad but I always couldn't reach the best. At that time, my home room teacher did something. He punished all of my classmates with a strange way. If my classmates couldn't reach the standard he set, we must pay one dollar for each score. Rediculously, this way made our grades worse and worse than before. My home room teacher was confused about it and tried to talk with class leader so as to find a way out to solve the problem. After their talk, my home room teacher decided to ablished the punishment, and tried to encourge us to learn. With his love and care, we got better grades and even reached the third in my school the next year. As far as I'm concerned, learning with pleasure is the most effective way. If we no longer have to come to terms with learning because of punishiment, it is no doubt that we have more passion for learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, the ranking of birth rate is lower and lower. Most of family have only one child. However, parents always give their baby whatever he/she wants. So, the only child in the family has been spoiled since he/she was born.
To motivate these children to learn and to control their behavior well, I think using punishment is more effective than rewarding. A propriate punishment is neccessary for teachers to teach the students right or wrong. In addition, students can learn a lesson after they do things wrong.
Through a punishment, most of students won't go wrong over and over. Take me for example, I am so careless that I always forget to bring things with me. Each time I forget, my mom will scorn at me and ask me to do housework as a punishment. as a result, I have never forgot everything I should do. By means of this experience of me above, I think a proper and effiecient punishment is the best way to teach students.

subject: HW1001
content:
In these days, people began to put emphasis on how we should educate our students. Most people agree the idea of teaching students with love, so am I. I think students should be encouraged or rewarded when they do something right, not just be strictly scolded when they make mistakes.
As a teenager, I still love to be praised by my parents or teachers if I achieve my goals. However, if I make some troubles, I do not want to be blamed badly. I will listen to my parents or teacher when I do something wrong. This also gives me a chance to learn how to distinguish what is right or wrong. On the contrast, if I am strictly punished, I may be heartbroken or upset, and it doesn't help to make situation better.
As a result, I wish teachers can educate their students with love. Try to reward them more and tell them the reason why they do something wrong instead of just punishing them will make study an interesting things to students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowaday, we often see the teacher punishes students which cause controvercial issues in news. But why do teachers punish students? The reason might be that some teachers use punishment to motivate students to control their behavior. However, others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, I prefer the second perspective-rewarding students for learning.
I prefer to reward students because I have seen an experience before. A teacher has a student who doesn't like studying and make troubles frequently. In this situation, most people would use punishment to control this kind of student. However, the teacher is concerned about that student instead of using punishment, for example, the teacher helps that student do homework after class and encourages the student to confront the difficulties. What the teacher does makes the student change her attitude and behave herself. In conclusion, from this example, teachers can also use the reward or compliment to motivate their students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Recently, we could see many news on the TV about school teachers punishing their students just because they did something wrong. In my opinion, I don't think this is a good way to teach students and not to say to motivate them. I think reward or encourage the students is the best way.
To take myself as an example, I attended a piano competition when I was a junior high school student. Because I was pretty young then; therefore, I felt so nervous and also lost self-confidence. At that difficult moment, my mom comforted and encouraged me. After hearing all the motivative words my mom told to me, I suddenly felt that my body was fulfilled with energy. At the end, I got a good grade when the competition was over.
As the above-mentioned, I'm certainly much prefer that teachers should encourage their students more often instead of punishing them. The young students are not already mature no matter in their soul or body. Punish can leave a bad influence in their mind and probably won't wash away when they grow up.
