Through rewarding the students not only can direct them into a right way but also let them know what is good and bad.

subject: HW1001
content:
Education is necessary to all the students. There are some teachers prefer punishing to rewarding students. No matter what the teachers do, they all concern about students and consider students to be their own children. Teachers educate students in the way which they think is the best for students.
In my opinion, I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. No one likes learning without rewarding, and so do I. Students who receive rewards always get a better grade than others. Moreover, rewarding is effective for students in learning or facing difficults.
For example, I am a student who always get rewards from teachers. The admirations from teachers give me motivation to accomplish every thing. Even it is really difficult to achieve the goal, I will try my best to complete the hard work.
Nowadays, rewarding helps students to get better grades. In this way, the more rewards students get, the more effective the learning is.

subject: HW1001
content:
When it comes to teaching students, I believe that rewarding them for their good behavior can lead to a better result than punishing them to motivate them to learn and to control themselves.
First of all, we should stand in the students' shoes. No body is perfect. In other words, everyone makes mistakes. When you make a mistake, would you want someone running after you with a stick, or forbidden you from playing? As Jesus said, everyone deserves more than a chance. We should give students opportunities to correct themselves.
Moreover, if punishing students strictly for their bad behavior is really useful, why are there still so many students doing bad things such as taking drugs?
Furthermore, studies show that a child's lack of sense of security can lead to his teenage's bad behavior. if a child is often punished for little mistakes he makes, chances are that he loses the control of his behavior in the near future.
Any method has it's advantages and disadvantages. In my opinion, teaching is a holy job made of love, so I prefer giving students rewards than punishing them.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are two avenues teachers avail theselves of to make students behave; one is punishment, and the other is the compliment. In my opinion, the latter is more effective than the former in that every student requires confidence to boost them to make progress. As a consequence, teachers shouldn't punish students intensely lest students abandon themselves.
Take myself for example. In elementary school, I participated in swimming courses. Initially, I was afraid so that the swimming pool was to me as the hazardous monster was to another creature. I couldn't help but burst out crying, compelling the coach to come to concern. Instead of any punishment, an angel of the coach inspired me and gave me tips to cope with this problem. Little by little, I overcame all hindrance, making rapid progress. Ultimately, I was fascinated by such exercise and could take it well. Due to the coach's inspirations and praise, I accomplished and was confident of myself simultaneously. Hence, it is rewards to student for learning that is indispensible and effective rather than punishment.

subject: HW1001
content: There are two different opinions about whether teachers should punish students or reward them. I believe that using properly punishment is better for teaching students. First, punishment makes students scared, so they won't make the same mistake again. Second, some students prefer punishment more because if teachers didn't punish those bad students, they wouldn't learn a lesson and might create more problems next time. Still, other students don't like punishment. But if they don't make mistakes, no one will punish them. My school teachers also prefer punishment more than reward. There is a lazy classmate in our class, and he's often late for school or nods off during class. Our class-teacher tried to told him not to do that anymore, but he just wouldn't listen to her. Soon my teacher lost her temper and started to punish him whenever he makes a mistake. Now he seldom makes mistakes and my teacher stops punishing him, too. Although no one like to be punished, it is still worth to try when rewarding is not working.

subject: HW1001
content:
With the change of high-tech, students are getting more active. Teachers need to change teaching methods to fit different kinds of students.
In these days, most parents don't accept the punishment. Instead they'd like to praise their children to behave. Communicating with them is a big topic amoung parents now. For teachers, they have to balance punishment and rewarding. Some students need to be punished to behave like younger ones. Some are too shy to say the feeling. And teachers would like to reward them to do things well.
In the elementary school, teachers in class would like to inspire students to talk about their own ideas and then they need students to speak and react with others. But it will cause a mess. Maybe one or two of students will have a fight or quarror so teachers need punishment to control this situation. Otherwise, no one is going to quiet down. In the end, teachers want some good results and then rewarding would be the best motivation for students. It's not the only way to motivate, but students will make a big effert to do their homework. Teachers just use some tips to push students to do boring homework.
Different students need different methods. Not only punishment but rewarding could lead to better results. It depends on types of students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Contrary to the conventional educational system, many experts support that punishment should not be the only way in teaching children. Rewarding students is another effective way as well. Frankly speaking, in my opinion, students under the punishment education show more positive attitude to study than others do.
After I graduated from the junior high school, some of my friends made up their mind to study in the public senior high school. Nevertheless, I determined to go to a non-public senior high school. We didn't have any contact until we hold a reunion. At the party, I almost passed out as soon as I saw my friends studying in public schools. Not only did they dye their hairs, but they also had lots of girlfriends. Due to the rewarding concede hold by the teachers in public schools, two of my friend, who used to be more diligent than me, made lots of massive changes, such as neglecting their scores and starting to smoke.
Thanks to my friends, now I'm glad that I resolved to stay in the non-public school. In spite of the fact that teachers here are famous for punishing students, I think it is far better than cultivating some bad habits under the rewarding education. In conclusion, a comfortable atmosphere will transform a hard-working man into a man of laziness.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers tend to use punishment to motivate students, and others like to reward students. In my opinion, a good teacher should use different ways in different students and different conditions. The two methods are both effective if teachers take them in appropriate way. I will provide two examples to support my opinion. When I was an elementary school student, I had a classmate called Patrick. He didn't do well on his studies but he was good at running and playing basketball. Our homeroom teacher, Miss Huang, made a deal with Patrick that if he could finish all his homework every day and behaved himself well in class, she would help him persuade his parents to their permission of school basketball team. At last, Patrick did make it.
Another example is about my junior high schoolmate, Bobbie. He liked to talk in class all the time. In order to stop Bobbie's behavior, the teacher asked him to do more homework. Besides, Bobbie could just sat far away from his good friends. Bobbie hated doing homework so he talked less and less.
According to the examples above, I'm sure that there is not so called the "perfect" way for teachers. Good teachers should depend on students' personalities and change their methods properly.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I do support that teachers may sometimes use punishment to motivate students on their studies or behavior. We, humans, are intelligent, but by times we may use our intelligence in the wrong way. By this condition, there must be some strict and effective methods to tell us that what is right and what is wrong. Not only parents but also teachers play the important role in our life. When we have poor performance on studies or obtain inappropriate hobbies, we become rude and selfish. At this moment, rewarding us to pursue better performances is not the most proper way. By contrast, suitable punishment and timely teaching are the most effective way. If we are punished "suitably" and "properly" by our teachers, we will realize that our performances are incorrect. Therefore, we shall try our best to correct and fix the mistakes. We can also learn to be a more self-discipline, responsible and rightous people. Teachers still love us, but they just show their careness by other ways-by the strict but effective way.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the traditional times, almost every teacher in school used punishment to control students and motivate them to learn. Nowadays, however, most teachers reward and encourage students to learn better instead of scolding or punishing. I personally believe that encouraging students is more effective. I have some reasons and examples to support my point of view.
For one thing, I think that the true meaning of education consists in learning happily and efficiently. Students in school are always facing to plentiful tests and studies. If teachers punish students when they get poor grades will the students loss the motivation of learning. For another, a teacher, with patience and a kind heart, who praises students in time, gives encouragement to students while they are upset, shares joy with them when they are happy, is able to teach students better. Namely, students can have great learning experience and efficiency.
For example, when I was a junior high student, I remembered that once I had a really bad grade, I cried horribly all day and didn't go to school, staying at home instead. Therefore, my school teacher came to my house and gave me some words of encouragement. Afterwards, I recoveried from that terrible misery and started to go to school with a happy mood.
Sun is to the plants as rewarding and encouragment are to the students. That really makes sense! For me, rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
School education is becoming more and more indispensable in the digital era. Namely, the methods teacher choose to play an important role through a student learning process. As far as I'm concerned, a good teacher should be patient and the method of rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.
Everyone likes to be praised, let alone students or children. When we perform well in our field, we are not only enjoying the joy of achievement but also eagering for others' compliment. It's like being recognized and regarded as a more valuable man. Take my friend, Pete, for instance. He used to be a shy boy and afraid of trying all kinds of new things, but after a series of encouragement and rewards provided by his music teacher, he started to find out that he was expert in playing the violin. A concert, inclusive of my cousin, had changed his whole life. He now become a energetic teenager and full of enthusiasm. By contrast, too much punishment would definitely be harmful to a students growth development, they might come up with more inferiority complex.
To the best of my knowledge, a teaching method which is full of praise and compliment is however not ideal. So I think it's a teacher's responsibility to strike a balance and discover which method will be more suitable for a student.

subject: HW1001
content:
Certainly, in my opinion, using punishment is the effective way to manage students. Without punishment, students will not behave well for theirselves.
All the students are the same, they have to be punished and then they will know which is right. It's similar to the proverb "No pain, no gain."
Just take an experiment for an example, there are two doors, one is red and the other is blue. You have to get through one of the door to have a dinner. The red one is a room which is full of bad smelling gass, and the blue one is a table with supreme cusines. If you go into the red one, next time you will not get through it anymore. That is why we students have to be punished.
Though punishment is the short cut to manage our behavior, we can't use it too often. Because of the confidence of students will lose. That makes students hard to accomplish everything they prefer to do.
The perfect method of controling students' behavior is to tell what's wrong with what they have just done at the first time they make mistakes. Punish them if they did the same mistakes twice. It is the right option to help them on their life road.

subject: HW1001
content:
I agree with the statement that students can be motivated by rewarding them. With the following reasons and examples, I'm going to explain and confirm my point of view in details.
Students who are eager to learn but not so talented during the process of learning would feel frustrated when they are caught in some obstacles. This kind of student, in my experience, is a big proportion of the group. To their disappointment, they might become past caring and then give up. However, if people around them give them some encouragement, they would figure out that they still can overcome these hurdles with more perseverence required.
For example, my mother is a teacher. During the learning process of mine, she has never blamed or scolded me for any bad performance in academy. Instead, she cheered me up and sensibly helped me pick out the problems I may face. Then, without pressures, I've always ranked as the top 10 in school.
Hence, I beleive that rewarding instead of punishment for students is more effective and feasible. After all, a good saying goes, "Err is human." Make students confident, and they will improve.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are many teachers in Taiwan and each of them may have different ways teaching their students. Some will use punishment and others may reward students. In my opinion, rewarding students is the best way that teachers treat to their students.
Learning may be a very boring thing. A serious teacher will make you lose interest in learning. Even teachers use punishment to motivate students, the consequence is just let all the students extremely against learning. On the contrary, rewarding students for learning can not only arouse students' confidence, but also strength their wills to learn harder. Because of the rewards, learning won't be just a boring thing. It will make you more concentrate on the learning.
Take my experience for example, once I was a child my mom always motivated me to study by punishment. As a result, I become lazy on studying. However, when I met the first teacher of my life in primary school, I changed my view on learning. The teacher's encouragement made me feel confident and when I got a fault, he would teach me instead of punishing me. When I did well on something, he might reward me a lot. From then on, learning become my favorite thing in my life.
Due to the advantages above, I believe that rewarding students for learning can really lead to better results and the teachers who always use punishment can try hard to change their teaching style to make the education better.

subject: HW1001
content:
During the transition from traditional and conventional society to a modern one, there are more and more discussing and debate over how we can educate our children well. In the values of Westeners, children ought to be taught in a positive way, while in those of Chinese, teachers must use punishment to motivate students to learn.
In my opinion, it leads to better results to reward students for their good performance or behavior. For example, when I was a junior high school student, I hated math so much. I always got bad grades in math exams. Nevertheless, when my teacher told me that if I could solve some math problems, he would give me some presents such as chocolate, pens, and so on, my interest in math was been aroused. After that, my confidence has been boosted greatly, and now, I can even get prizes in math contests. I think it was my teacher's encouragement that made me make a big progress in math. Indeed, students tend to accept teachers' words if they use a positive way. However, if there is no punishments, some students may ignore everything. Because they realize that they won't be punished if they make mistakes, they will do anything they want.
In general, I suppose students shoud be taught in a positive way. After all, people love reward and praise, and hate punishments, don't they?

subject: HW1001
content:
Recently, we can see many punishment cases in Taiwan's campus. Some people are in favor of using punishments in the campus, and others are in favor of rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. As a student, I agree to reward students in the process of learning because of students' confidence and the sense of honor.
If a teacher can use the right way to teach students, the students' confidence can be awakened, and they can learn better. No one can deny that everyone likes compliments from parents or teachers. Students can gain more and more confidence through teacher's rewarding or praising, and they will seek better and better performance. Moreover, teacher reward students not only in the students' academic performance but in students' behaviors such as politeness. If a student get a compliment from his or her teachers, he or she will gain much confidence and encourage themselves to have good performance in the academic or manners.
Needless to say, as a human being, sense of honor is the one which everyone desires. Especially when one is rewarded, he or she will attain much better performance. Teachers reward the students more, and the students have much sense of humor. They are even eager to achieve better performances without teachers' reminding them of. By being rewarded, students build a sense of honor in their mind and they will be motivated to learning by themselves.
In a nutshell, everyone has differet opinions to this widely disscused issue. And in my opinion students become much confident and get the sense of honor which are two major reasons why I believe rewarding student for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are two kinds of teachers treating students in different ways. Some teachers choose to punish, while the others think that encourage is much better. In my opinion, students who are encouraged and get awards by teachers perform much better.
I don't agree with teachers who punish students because that will only let students get hurt, and students will be afraid of going to school. Students' parents will also feel sad or mad, and teaching students patiently without punishment is the trend now in our society. In the other hand, teachers reward and encourage students to study and learn hard, and students will really try their best and also let them be more confident. If teachers respect anyone except students, people will admire and be thankful for them, vice versa.
Although many people live in a better life now, there are still many families poor, so that their children cannot go to school. However, after going to school, their behaviors are not worse than other students, and teachers play important roles on them. Teachers don't use different way to treat them though they are poor. Therefore, the method of rewarding students is more effective.

subject: HW1001
content:
Teachers nowadays use two kind of teaching methods-punishments or rewards. Although both of them can reach the goal of tutoring and controling students, as far as I'm concerned, rewarding students is a better way rather than punishing them. I have two reasons to support my opinion.
First, all people, including students aren't favorite with being blamed or punished. So why do we have to punish students? It can only make students get angrier or more frustrated. Thus, they won't fix their faults and even behave worse. In other words, this means that students want to be congraduated, if teachers give them positive ideas and advices, their schoolwork will gradually become better.
Second, students know are hard to catch their attention. If teachers want students to have good grades, they need to win students heart, so they will focus on the teacher in class. In this kind of situation, teachers cannot be disliked by students. For example, if teachers always shout at students and give them heavy punishment if they make mistakes, the relationship between them will become extremely bad. Thus, students won't listen to the teachers' quidance. Hence, rewarding students is absolutely better than punishing. Who wants to be a everyone-hate-you person?
In conclusion punishing students can make them more upset and dislike the teacher. However, rewarding is totally the opposite. It can help students have the desire to study hard. Punishing is merely a foolish way to teach students. So, my dear teachers, why don't you throw your hammers and all your other punishing equipments away now?

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, ponishment and reward are both required. You can't always treat students only with ponishment either one another; it is teacher's responsibility to help students depending on their personalities. As a result, I don't think there is no property saying of "which one is better," or more effective.
Why do I say so? Well, take myself for example, when I was a high school student, my english teacher tended to give punishment if we did bad on tests. She knew that it was the only way to force us to study, so did we students. So, to avoid the punishment, we usually took her class as a serious thing.
However, now I am a teacher myself. I teach two junior-high students history, what I have found is that ponishment seems not to work on them. They show no interests in textbooks, so it is reasonable they have poor grades at school. They treat punishments as a common thing from teacher and they just don't care.
To their surprise, I never punish them. They get cookies and smiles from me as long as they do finish they homework. If they can't concentrate on my teaching, I prefer tell them they are wasting their life. And it works, they seldom disappoint me.
In short, different people needs different treatment, and that is what I believe.

subject: HW1001
content:
Teachers all hope their students can have good grades and well manners. Teaching students to be outstanding is not only for teachers' own senses of achievement but for parents' expectation. To reach this goal, there are two ways, one is punishment, and the other is reward.
As far as I am concerned, reward is much better than punishment. It is doubtless that people like to be encouraged and praised, let alone children. I believe human's nature is kind. As a result, when students get good grades or have well manners, we should give them some rewards to encourage them. In this way, we can stimulate their sense of honor and make them pursue higher goals.
I consider myself as an example, my teacher always praise me whenever I do well. Of course, I am happy and I also want to perform well. However, on the other side, my cousin's teacher doesn't praise any students. He always use punishment to his students. My cousin is unhappy and want to graduate from school as soon as possible. He also says his learning is a torture.
Consequently, award is absolutely a better method than punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
Punishing students or not may be a big question to most teachers. If teachers punish them, they might speak ill of teachers; if not, they would do what they want to do and become very rebellious. In my opinion, I think teachers had better punish students. First, I think everyone has responsibility. When they do something wrong, they would be very regretful in their mind. If teachers punish them when they are upset, they would know what they had done was wrong. So they would never do that again.
Second, everyone has curiosity. When they see someone do something illegal they might want to immitate them. If teacher punish those who did illegal things, other students would be very scared. Therefore, illegal things can reduce.
Finally, many students are smart but not active. If teachers make a rule that anyone whose score is below eighty have to be punished. Then everyone in the class would be very diligent in studying. Thus, students' potential can be raised up, and it is benifitial to them.
As a result, punishing students is a good method to control students. It can not only make them behave themselves but also make their grades better. So I suggest that teachers try it. Maybe by doing this, the management of the class would be easier.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, teachers should reward their students for learning. This method can lead to better results.
The first reason why I think teachers should reward their students for learning is related to my own experience. When I was studying in primary school, MR. John, my English teacher, forced us to study English. As long as we had his class, we needed to have a quiz about what he had taught in class. We were reluctant to do that. If we got a poor score on the test, we would be punished. As time went by, my classmates and I started hating the subject of English. Every time when we had a English class, we just wanted to escape from the classroom if it was possible. As a result, we lost interests in English. Thus, I believe punishing to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior is not a good idea because it might lead the students to losing the interest in the subject.
On the other hand, the second reason why I think that students should learn by giving them rewards is because of the will by their heart. Nowadays, students are indulging in the fantastic Internet world. Televisions are also a vital attraction to the students that are going to take the exam for going to college. It is bad to be hooked on the virtual Internet world and the world of televisions. However, don't take this phenomenon too seriously. When students get a good performance in school or on their tests, I think it is a good idea to give them some rewards from watching televisions or playing online games for roughly an hour to two hours. This action might ameliorate the anxiety or tension faced by the diligent students. This motivation might give the students some power to study. Hence, I think giving some relaxation to the anxious students is a good suggestion.
Finally, I believe that instead of using punishment to motivate students to learn and control their behavior, we should give them some appropriate rewards and let them be interested in what they are studying. As far as I am concerned, these are more imperative.

subject: HW1001
content:
In recent years, the number of punishments that teachers use to students has been increasing. Somebody said such behavior can't lead children to be better, believing rewarding is the only way. But the others said only with sticks can make children know what they did is good or not.
In my opinion, I think the treatment to children contains not only the proper punishment but also the little rewarding. For example, I was passive and shy when I was little. Whenever I did mistakes, my parents punished me that made me scare about doing anything that I might get wrong. Not until I entered the elementary school did I change! My teacher was so considerate that she always cheered me up. However, if I make same mistakes again and again, she would give me proper punishment and tell me the reasons; otherwise, if I perform well, she would reward me, asking me keeping going on. Therefore, I had turned into a new leaf. I am like an oasis in the dessert requiring water to relieve my thirt for knowledge and good behaviors. I will spend no effort to be a prominent guy.
Thanks to my teacher, I have the optimistic attitude toward my future. It's believed that I will treat my children with the same way which had changed my whole life.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the past, most teachers in school used punishment to force their students to learn and to improve their behavior. Nowadays, more and more teachers gradually believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, I consider rewarding students for learning and improving their behave is more effective than punishing. Rewarding always draws students' attention and big concerns, and encourages them to motivate their potential and gives them more confidence. But punishment may hit their confidence and result in the loss of learning interest. Encourage is always better than punishment in the area of educational psycology.
Recently, some teachers in school have given their students points, stamps or smiling faces which are collected to a certain amount to get a reward. Students want to get the reward, so they always study very hard or improve their behavior to win the points, stamps or smiling faces.
To sum up, I believe rewarding students is the best way to lead students to better results. Comparing to punishing students, it is more humanly and positive.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinions, both using punishment and rewarding students are good. But the teachers can't use only one of the two methods to control the class. The teachers can set some prizes to motivate the students to achieve the goals. The students will be happy by being rewarded because they can be proud of themselves and it's a kind of fullfillments. Sometimes the teachers should punish the students because some students are lazy and have no interests in the prizes. It's time to punish the students, then they will know what they are going to face if they don't obey the rules or study hard.
For example, one of my friends, Joey, doesn't like to study. He hangs out with his girlfriend and plays basketball and computer games all day long seven days in a week. After he got a bad grade in the mid-term exam, the professor punished him and asked him to work harder or he would fail. In the end, Joey tried to spend more times on studying and pass the final exam. Mandy is another example, she studys hard everyday. The teachers satisify about her behaviors so they often reward Mandy. Mandy is happy for that so her grades become better and better.
I think the teachers should choose the right method when facing different students. That's what good teachers have to do. In this way, they can motivate most of the students.

subject: HW1001
content:
How to motivate students to learn and control their behavior is what every teachers are thinking about. In my opinion, reading is one of the best ways for making the students behave better. In the progress of reading, students not only acquire a large amount of knowledge but enjoy both delight and silence of reading. On top of that, when they do other things like studying, they are able to pay as much attention as reading. Besides, more extensively the students read or learn, more appropriately they behave in the classroom and public.
Another effective method is excercising. Most students are too energetic to sit, rooted in their seats, so going out to do something else is a good way. Students can learn not only how to follow the rules but cooperate with others while excercising. In addition, students will calm down and focus on their schoolwork effeciently after excercising. Case in point, one of my classmates has come a long way in studying performance and behaves better after join the sport team.
To sum up, either reading or excercising is a good method to motivate students to learn. Students can learn much from them while having fun.

subject: HW1001
content:
While some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behaviors, others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, I think there is no absolute right or wrong to use either one of the methods. Two methods can be both effective. However, it depends on what kind of students you met.
Take me as an example. I am an English teacher in a cram school. Most of my students are pre-school children. I've met a lot of different personality children. Basically, I find out that their personality traits are determined by their families. As a teacher, actually it is hard to change their personality merely by our own ability. Since we cannot change their personality, we can only adjust ourselves to them.
When I met the bad students, at the beginning, I would get angry and irritating so fast. I threatened them that if they kept having bad behaviors, I would go to their parents and ask them to punish them. However, I found out that it was no use in the end. The more a teacher doesn't get into the core of problem but just scolding students and punishing them, the more the students don't feel they are loved. As a result, it will be counter-productive. Once the students cannot get any encouragement from teachers, they may abandon themselves. They would think that even the teacher thinks that they are done, maybe they are really that bad. Therefore, they will lose their confidence and will be reluctant to behave well or study hard again. One of my students just fixs this situation. His name is Ben. Ben is a very naughty child. He didn't like to study and he got very bad scores on the test. I was very angry so I scolded him loudly in front of the class. I thought he might feel embarrassed and decide to keep up with other students. However, he didn't do so. He got even worse scores after I scolded him. He even said bad words to me to show his anger. I think I really used the wrong way. To deal with this kind of children, I think it is better to spend much time on them and make them feel that they get a lot of attention from teacher. I believe that under this kind of environment, they would be more likely to behave well and correctly.
On the contrary, if your student is the kind who is well self-disciplined. I think some admonishments are necessary. In my opinion, punishments may be more effective on this kind of students. Take my experience as example. I have another children called Jill. She is a very well-behaved child. She has a light voice and her personality is shy. Whatever you told her, she would just nod and reply "yes." Before the test, I will clarify all the punishment to her. I will tell her what is the punishment if she is not up to my standard. This method works everytime. She never gets the bad scores. So I think to use either punishment method or rewarding method depends on the personality of the children you taught.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, teachers use punishment or give rewards to motivate students to learn or control their behavior. However, these two ways might have different effect on students.
Using punishment sounds much more effective. While students do some bad behavior, punishing them may make them not to do it again because they don't want to be punished anymore. Therefore, students will keep this experience in mind and avoid doing the bad thing. However, students change their behavior just due to the punishment! They might never know the true reason why the can't do that kind of behavior.
On the contrast, rewarding may be a better way. Instead of letting students be afraid of punishment, giving rewards to students while they have good behavior may make them like to do that thing even more.
Take myself as on example. When I was in junior high school, I wasn't good at calculating and thinking. Therefore, math became the subject which annoyed me most. What's more, the teacher would punish students including me if we didn't get the higher score than he decided. How terrible it was! Because of this kind of teaching way, I hate math a lot at that time.
But now my senior high school teachers help my deal with the questions I have on math. If I do well on it, I will get awards! Then I graduately like math, and it become my best subject!
Rewarding might raise students interest in learning and studying and it also encourages students to keeping working hard.
In summary, not like punishment that students hate, rewarding is better. Though both two ways can change students behavior, rewarding is more effective to students!

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students for learning is a better way to motivate students to learn. In society, people work hard to pursue what they want, and rewarding students is exactly the same thing. Students work hard because they know what's the reward. If they are encouraged, they will know they're doing the right thing and will be more willing to better themselves next time.
On the other hand, if you oblige students to control themselves by punishment, students won't get the motivation of learning. Though this method the fastest and most effective way to stop students from being naughty or lazy, they behave themselves out of fear. Once they get used to the punishment, they will ignore it or even find ways to get away with their responsibilities.
One of the examples is my experience of learning to swim. I was so afraid of water that I couldn't even put my nose under water. The coach scolded me, trying to let me go into the pod, but in vain. Finally, it occured to him that he could give me a treat to arouse my motivation. Because of the reward, I encourage myself to fight against my fear. Then I am no longer afraid of water.

subject: HW1001
content:
As people emphasize on education more and more today, we start to contemplate some problems with education. And teachers' teaching style is one of them. Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, I prefer the second way. Punishment is negative. It tells you what you shouldn't do instead of showing you the right things. And it may harm a student's self-confidence and mentality. On the contrast, rewarding is positive. It encourage students to learn and build students' belief in themselves. This is more effective than punishment, which restricts a student's space for developing himself.
A few days ago, I saw a famous doctor interviewed about the way he teaches his children on TV. And I was very touched by the show. The doctor said he never anticipated that his children would be as famous and wealthy as him, but he really wants them to be happy. So he always encourages them to find what they love and develop the field. And now, he is happy that through his encouraging and sometimes rewarding, his children find their own sky and are as happy as him. He is very grateful and fulfilled! I think that's what I want-a space to create my own life.

subject: HW1001
content:
Modern education is very different from the old one. For instance, the relationship between them and the ways teachers teach students.
I can't say which one is better. As they both have benefits and negatives. But I think when it comes to which one is more effective, I'll say the old one. In the past, teachers tended to use punishment to motivate their students to learn and to control their behavior. And most of the time, they were demanding. On account of the reasons, students didn't dare to make their teachers angry and had a tendency to be good students.
Take my math teacher for example, if he couldn't get ninety in every exam, he had to be hit on his fingers and be grounded. Although I agree with old education, I still consider it to be changed. We can try to combine the advantages in modern educantion with old education. It's good to let students do what they like to do at their leisure. Stop controling them, but to correct them!

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think rewarding students for learning is much more effective than using punishment to motivate students to learn. We all like reward rather than punishment. No one will like to be blamed or to be punished. Therefore, it is clear that rewarding students for learning is the better way.
Take me as an example, when I was little, my mom always forced me to practice playing cello. If I didn't concentrate on playing, she would yelled at me immediately. It made me so scared that I began to hate playing cello, and my mom was aware of the situation. Therefore, she changed her way. She no longer shouted at me, instead, she promised me that if I finished playing cello, she would allow me to watch cartoons for 1 hour. By hearing the reward, I was so excited that I started to learn it concentrately again. The changing of me really impressed my mom. As a result, by seeing the example I provide. It is obivious that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
The issue that whether punishment should be used by teachers or not has been a hot topic recently. In my opinion, I am on the side that teachers should implement more constructive measures to teach students.
In the past, teachers usually use physical punishment on students who violate school regulations. Additionally, it also a common way to motivate students study hard. However, the side effects of this kind of punishment may lead to terrible results. Punishment may press students to behave well or study hard temporarily, but it could not have positive influence on students. Not only may it cause physical injuries, but leave negative impression on students' minds also. For example, when I was in junior high school, the math teacher of my class did punishment to students who failed on exams, including me. It caused a sigma on students and made me still hate the subject, math, untill now.
On the contrary, my English teacher choosed to encourage students who did not behave well instead of blame. She was always patient with nauty students, and use more constructive measures, such as one-to-one teaching, to motivate students to learn English. As a consequence, most of my classmates have great intrest on learning English and we did get great scores on English tests. In addition, English has been my favorite subject since junior high school.
To sum up, I am deeply convinced that teachers should not use punishment on students. They have to take great efforts to implement more positive and constructive measure to teach students.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I think that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results for two reasons. First, I think teachers can't always decide whether the students should be punished appropriately. For example, if a student has studied hard for the coming school test, but unfortunately he or she is sick and doesn't do well on the test on that day, should he or she be punished? If the student is punished, I think he or she will lose his or her confidence in any coming test. Second, the punishment won't always work. Some students can not be motivated to learn and be controlled by it. Instead, they will get angry and give themselves up easily. As the previous example, if the student is punished just because he or she is sick and doesn't do well on the test, I think he or she will give himself or herself up easily. What's worse, he or she may be angry about the punishment and decide to give his or her homework up and then leave home. Maybe he or she doesn't do well on the test; however, I think at least he or she is well prepared and willing to try. For the two reasons, I think that rewarding students for learning can lift their confidence and lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
In order to motivate students' learnings and behaviors, the teachers try their best to teach them in different way. Some of them prefer the strict punishments, while others prefer rewards and encouragements. As for me, I believe that rewarding students is more effective. Students who don't like to study are most likely being distructed the confidence. They hate books and show no interests in academic performances because they don't feel successful and happy in their learnings. What's worse, some of them even consider themselves as the losers. Punishing will make them feel afraid of the learnings or behave worse.
On the other hand, if we push them by figuring out their learning problems and guiding the right way to them, we can help them not only improving the grades but also the way they consider themselves. Take me for an example, I was a really big trouble when I was in junior high. I met some "cool" friends in school and followed their steps in order to be the one of them. To being "cool", I started to spend lots of time on my dressings and make-up. I also lied to teachers and went out with them in the school days. However, my teacher Mr. Lin didn't give me up. He helped and guided me kindly and patiently.
Today, I will be a freshman in a top-ranked university in September. I appreciate he motivated me in the effective way. That's why I believe rewarding is more effective then punishing.

subject: HW1001
content:
Teachers in Taiwan mainly take advantage of two different ways to improve the students' learning. One is punishment. The other is rewarding. In my opnion, I think that rewarding is more effective than punishment.
The students can have unbelieving improvements in a short time if teachers use punishment to motivate students. To avoid being punished, the students have no choice but to study hard. However, though they can always pass their exams with flying colors, they are dependent. To tell you the truth, these students are likely to fail after graduating from schools.
In contrast, the student will like to study at their own wills if their teachers prefer to rewarding students. These students will spare no effort to study in order to get the rewards. In this way, they are much more active than those who recieve punishment education. That's why I prefer to rewarding student rather than punish them.
In all, I think that it is a wrong way to teach students with punishment. Hence, I urge teacher around the world should make good use of rewarding students to teach them instead of forcing them.

subject: HW1001
content: Every day, when we read the newspaper, we learn that some students have been punished for some reasons at times. When I was a child, I had been punished hardly ever. My parents usually expressed how disappointed they were whenever we made mistakes; it worked so well that we would be well-behaved. I have disoussed the punishing situation with my foreign friends; they say that children will surely get punished when doing something wrong, however, punishment can be done in different ways. In my opinion, Taiwanese teachers have to manage many students; sometimes, they use aggressive methods, such as physical punishment or personal humiliation, to prevent the one and others from making the same mistake. However, those punishments also stop students' courage to try something new. I tend to praise people when they do something well, even they do things wrong. I would also tell them to be aware and not to err again.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the recent society, there are two different opinions on education. One is using punishment can motivate students to learn, and the other is rewarding students for learning can make students improve. There are pros and cons about the two opinions; however, I prefer to choose the method of rewarding rather than use punishment to control our next generation.
First of all, I agree with rewarding students, for it is obvious that no one likes to learn under pressure and punishment. Provided that a student gets a poor grade on this test, we should encourage him, not making him be defeated by just one failure. With the encouragement and rewarding, students will intend to study harder, try again and be brave to stand up in spite of the failure. Take Helen Keller, the most famous and successful, deaf and blind great woman, as an example. Due to a serious cold at her two, she was not only blind but deaf. Then, she became wild and was easy to cry, throwing everything within reach. Luckily, the teacher Annie Sullivian taught Helen knowledge as well as recognized the vacabulary with patience. The teacher, Annie, used love to educate Helen, rewarding her if she performed well rather than punished her mischief and bad behavior. Finally, Helen became the first bachelor graduated from the college, who was blind and deaf. The example can suggest that rewarding students for learning is much more effective, leading to better results.
On the other hand, if students study under punishment, the result may be not as effective as expected. The generation at forty or fifty years old all experienced punishment. They felt uncomfortable and had less eagerness to improve their studies and behavior. The result was not effective, and even would stop students learning.
To sum up, I think rewarding students for learning is much more effective than using punishment. If teachers can educate students with love and encouragement, I believe there are more successful people in the world, making the society more wonderful.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, teaching methods should be different as the students' different age levels. Take the students in senior high school for example, I think rewarding students for learning is the better way.
The students about 16-18 years old start to have their own opinion and they have their own tempo on studying. Punishment or scolding from parents and teachers will only become pressure to them. The students growing up in modern society are more sensitive than before; therefore, the old way of teaching must be changed with the tide.
Just a few months ago, a student suicided himself because of the falling grades. Although nobody can exactly point out the reason about his action, I do think that the pressure from his parents should take a big part. What students need is not punishment but the understanding. Discussion and rewarding are the best way for them.

subject: HW1001
content: As the rapid growth of our society's educational systems and the increasing growth of social competitiveness, teachers have used several methods to raise students' interest in learning. Some use punishment to motivate students to learn, while others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, I think that rewarding students for learning is more effective. First, I think that the punishment's performances can't last long because students are under tremendous pressure. When the great pressure disappears, they won't continue learning anymore. Second, rewarding students for learning can develop students' interest in learning during the process without knowing. Last but not least, the punishment may cause great damage to students and furthermore destroy their interest in learning; in contrast, rewarding has a positive impact on students. They will not be afraid to learn; instead, they love to learn gradually. The goal of our education is not to force students to learn but to raise their interest in learning. Therefore, I think that rewarding students for learning is more effective and can have positive influence on the growth of students' mental and physical aspect.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior; While others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, rewarding students for learning is more effective than punishing students.
First of all, I think punishment can result in good behavior in short time, but it's not a long-term plan. In order to avoid being punished, students may forced themself to study; they'll feel stressful. And learning is no longer interesting to students. Besides, if they didn't get good grades on tests, they would be fearful; what's worse, students may lose faith in studying.
Secondly, using the method of punishment is not always effective. For some students, maybe it's a good method to control their behavior. While for some students, they may want to rebel to those authorities that punish them. Therefore, it would cause many problems.
Last but not least, that rewarding students instead of punishing them is a thoughtful teaching style. According to many scientific reports, rewarding someone for better behavior is more effective than punishing in many schools.
For those three reasons, I strongly support the idea of rewarding students rather than punish them for better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
In past decades, punishing students when they did something wrong is a usual. But it's a complete different situation in this society now. Many parents will consider sued the teachers, if their children are punished or even just blamed. Is this really a good way to teach the children?
I do think that punishment isn't the only way to motivate student. Rewarding is surely a better decision to encourage students. When I was in the junior high school, my English teacher will buy us gifts, if we get good grades in the midterm exam. Everyone studied really hard at that time. And when I was in my six grade of the elementary school, if our behaviors are good, our teachers will give us a dot. After gatherring enough dots, we can use them to change a gift.
But using punishment isn't all that bad. If students do something really wrong, such as smoking or fighting, punishment will be necessary.
Whether using punishment or not can depand on what happens. If this student just get a lower grade or forget to hand over the homework, punish him will be too harsh. The best way is using both punishment and rewarding. It's the great method to lead students to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
Many people believe that punishment can make students behave well. But I don't agree with that. In this way, students control their behavior because they are afraid of punishment, they don't change their mind at all. Punishment may hurt students' hearts and it is difficult to heal them.
I remembered that when I was little, I forgot to bring my homework to school, and then the teacher scolded me and asked me to stand out of the classroom. I felt extremely sad. I hated the teacher at that moment. It's really wrong for me to forgot things, but it hurt my feelings and I never forgot it.
In my opinion, rewarding students for learning is more effective. We can encourage students to do right things. Students will feel better when we give them confidence. Everyone needs confidence! Punishment make students fear to do things, but rewarding students can let students do right things bravely! Support students' heart, they would behave better.
My cousin was a very shy girl. She was reluctant to do anything because she lack confidence. Her parents and teachers tried their best to help her by rewarding her. Just find her advantages and encourage her. They tried to make her be more confident. Gradually, my cousin was willing to do something for her class and express her thoughts. We are all surprised and glad to see her change.
To sum up, I think that punishment for students is inappropriate for their learning. Punishment may make students be reluctant to do things. They are afraid of punishment and may hate the person who punished them. Rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. This way is more effective and better for students. Students need people's supports. I believe that we can make them be more confident and do right things by rewarding them!

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think rewarding students is more effective. When rewarded, students feel pleasant, and they realize what they can perform well. Also, students would be more confident, and have motivation to learn things more efficiently in order to equip themselves with as much knowledge as the can. On the contrary, when teacher use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior, it won't make students good, instead; it can discourag them seriously. It's common to see a student burst into tears when punished. Punishment can make students bevavior well because students are afraid of being punished. However, it won't last long. Students just dislike to be scolded, not really understand what's wrong and what's right.
For example, I once got a part time job in an English cram school, taking care of children after school. When they are nauty, making noise, the teacher would shouted and made them stand straight. The kids become quiet, but later they became nauty as usual. That made me think of my childhood. When I was in second grade of elementary school, I was punished because of talking to others. The teacher made me stand alone and put hands above my head. Although I was little, I felt very very embarrassed. As I grow up, the image is still vivid.
To sum up, I think teachers should be patient to students. Sometimes students make mistakes, but who never make a mistake? Sometime students fail the tests, and it's the responsibility of teachers to know the reason why they fail and teach them patiently.

subject: HW1001
content:
Everyone likes compliments. When someone approve of your hard works, give you some compliments, you may feel pleasant, then you will work more harder next time to fullfill your target. I think rewarding students for learning can encourage students. They will be more confident on doing their job.
In contrast, punishment may decrease the students' motivation. The more often teacher scold them, they more often feel frustrated. When I was in primary school in third grades my teacher was a harsh woman. She taught us math. She often punished us when we got the wrong answer. I was upset in that time, loosing my confident. However, later I went on fifth grades in elementary school, I had a nice math teacher. She was a kind and patient woman. She encouraged us when we got the bad grades. She gave us consolement and told us be better next time. I appreciated her a lot.
It is better to rewarding students than punishing. The possitive influence may affect a person's sight. Being more optimistic instead of being self-pity.

subject: HW1001
content:
Though this topic is open to debate, I tend to agree with that moderate punishment would motivitate a student's potential. In my opinions, punishment can lead to displine which is essencial while we develop a child's personality. However, I can't deny that some punishment may result in a stressful learning environment. I believe that I would make progress provided that someone supervise me. Surely, under some pressure, people tend to stimulate their intelligence, and break the record.
I have heard a story which can actually support my statement. There was once a school in the countryside of Japan, called "Forest School." Teachers mainly rewarded the students for learning daily rules. If they made mistakes, they received no punishment and were soon forgived by teachers. Nevertheless, after they grew up, they found it hard to adjust to the reality. The public was not as lenient as teachers in school while they disobeyed the rules. They failed to cultivate self-displine in such free education system. Reward is good, however too much may be counter-productive. I insist that moderate punishment can lead to success.

subject: HW1001
content:
When thinking about how to motivate students to learn and control their behavior, there are usually two different opinions toward this issue. One thinks only punishment can make students work on their studying, while the other prefers to motivate their students to learn and to behave well by rewarding them. In my opinion, I am for the idea that rewarding can help students to pay more attention to learning and their behavior.
Although punishment can make students do what you want they to do, students do so just for avoiding punishment and they do not really want to learn and behave like that. Just after they avoid the punishment, they will do things they really want to do again immediately. Therefore, I do not think it is a good way to encourage students to learn and behave well.
However, rewarding are better than punishment. Students will gain a sense of achivement or feel very well whenever their teachers reward them. Just by giving some compliment or rewarding them with something not very expensive, teachers can motivate and encourge students to learn on their own will. After all, everyone loves the sense and the joy of achievement.
According to reasons I mentioned above, I consider the idea that rewarding students for learning the better way because no one really like themselves to be punished.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I consider that appropriate punishment is more effective to motivate students to learn and control their behavior. Although there are still a lot of people thinking that punishment is an inhuman way to treat students, it is necessary for teachers to punish their students when the students are out of control.
For instance, some students are lazy to do their assignments. If teachers just encourage them to do what they have to do, they would ignore it or continue to forget to do their homework; whereas, if teachers can use appropriate punishment on students, students would feel oppressed and be forced to finish their assignments.
On the other hand, there are more and more jenvile delicencies on TV. I think it is due to the lack of punishment. Accordingly, the punishment is necessary to motivate and correct students' behaviors, and it can also keep students from going astray.

subject: HW1001
content:
First of all, I would like to express my opinion, is punishment is not the encouraging manner to motivate students' learning spirit. A lot of experiences we learned from West culturares, like cold fashion movie call "Love Education" from Hollywood, teachers tend to use loving or encouraging way to inspire students. From my experience when I was a student, I would suggest loving and caring are the most efficient methods to improve students' learning programs.
When I was student in junior school and I tend to learn English more, unfortunately I couldn't learn it very well particularly I didn't know the exact learn skills. Most of time, I failed my examinations and I lost my confidence for learning English. Somehow, I was lucky to meet a young teacher who was pretty new for teaching field graduated from the university not for long. Her name was Sara. I must say she was the most patient person I ever seen with unique enthusiasm for teaching in class. Her personality is tend to inspire students with their own idea not just follow text books. I think the most important factor is Sara is a person who is willing to care how you feel and learn from the class. Students from Sara's class always enjoy very good and profound mutual influence. That's how to motivate learning progress. As I address earlier, punishment can't do any good to trigge students' learning ambition, but loving or caring can do. Nowsaday, we always be taught many time hard efforts can lead to a rode of success. Then people become less focusing on the value of learning but more emphasizing on control. I would it is very bad idea and teaching System to using anyway to control students' behavior.
The learning patters suppose be more fun and more free-will manner to inspire children's imagination. Controlling can only less the capability of creation. In western learning patterns, you can see students have less pressure from homework but here in Taiwan is the opposite way run in system. Most parents who are capable of financial Support, they will consider to support children to go oversea education eventually.
My conclusion for students learning, I would Strongly suggest to put on more caring and patience to inspire instead of punishing or controlling methods. That's my whole point of views.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the view of tradition Chinese educational history, students usually punished to learn, to concentrate ect by teachers and parents. Why there wasn't any agony sounds until the western education came, it forced us to face the plight-studens have been learning under Chinese education strifled the speaking right and imagination.
I have many friends who goes to the universities in USA and UK, between the difference, they accuretly tell us the point, in western countries, teachers like to reward kids instead of punishments.
