Anyway, punshing to motivate and rewarding both can lead to better results. Learning how and when to use these 2 methods is more important, give the student what they need in a propriate time will be effective. In our lives, living without punishments will make us weak but without the rewards and couragement won't make us strong.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the Montessori's educational philosophy, she said that both rewards and punishments are not benefit for children. However, in my view, I do believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.
To begin with, when children do something wrong, teachers should try to communicate instead of punishing kids. If teachers always blame their students, then, they will gradually lose their confidence. Take myself as an example, my father is an extremely strict person. Whenever I get a poor grades, he never encourages me but blames me. Therefore, I'll always be afraid to talk to him. In contrast, my mom is a loving and caring woman, when I meet some difficulities on studies, she always encourages me and gives me lots of useful advices. Hence, I have a great relationship with my mom and it also shows that rewards can lead to better results.
Last but not least, only by rewarding students can cultivate their confidence and help them do better as well in their future.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think rewarding students for learning is more effective. Now, I will provide my own examples to you.
When I was in the third year of junior, I got a lot of quizs to do everyday. My home teacher said that we had to get 80 on every subject, or we would be punished. I was always punished because my math was too poor to get 60! As a result, I did not like math. Luckily, the math teacher knew I was not good at math. She told me that she was willing to teach me after school. When she taught, she never hited or shut to me. If I did correctly, she praised me. Because of this, I would not dislike math anymore. At least, I could reach 60 in math. I was so glad about what that teacher has done for me. She was my monitor! I sometimes think that if she was not willing to teach me after school, what would happen? Maybe I would hate math forever.
According to my example, I believe that rewarding is more effective than punishment student.

subject: HW1001
content:
Being a teacher, the most thing I really care is not only students' grades but also their behavior. Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. At the beginning, students may be afraid to be punished, but as time goes by, they feel nothing and even act worse. Especially, most students even don't know why they should be punished when they are at the age of the senior high school.
I used to reward students when teaching. In this way, they can be encouraged and inspired to learn things better. Teaching them by giving them more compliments leads to better results. Not only can they be more optimistic but they can also be more active as they are learning new things.
Afterall, we all want our students can be good in the future. Since rewarding students for learning can lead to better results, and be more effective, why don't we choose the positive teaching methods? As for me, I have been exploited this strategy for many years and I think I will keep doing so in the future.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think rewarding students for learning is a good way to motivate students. First, rewarding students can make them happy after they study hard. Students will have their motivation to study. Second, use punishment can make students study hard, too. But it can not insist for a long time, it will made them feel tired. Third, the consequence by reward will help more students to study. Because if using punishment, students who don't like study would think he can just get the punishment, and then he won't have to study. As the above, I think rewarding students truly is an advantage.
Take my experience for example. When I was in senior high school, my math teacher often used stick to hit students if they didn't get enough grade. It was a nightmare, everyone studied hard inorder to avoid the punishment, as time goes by, some people didn't care about it anymore because they tried hard but still couldn't reach the goal. So for my conclusion, I think rewarding students is better than punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
To the first question, as my opinion, I think the punishment is more effective than rewarding. I believe laziness is born nature and without learning. Students, not the all but almost every one is lazy. Without punishment or making rules for them to follow, they might cared about nothing, no studying or no writing homework. We don't need to look the punishment so seriously. The propriate punishment could make students prograss. It is a way to push students go forward. Rewarding migh make the students lazy and afraid of nothing. But there cannot only a one way of punishment. when students doing good or studying well, we also need to praised them. As my opinion, punishment is a way that teacher shows his or her caring of students. It could give a propriate pressure and make students concentrate on their studying.
To the second question, during my school life, almost every teacher I met using punishment to motivate students to learn. I don't think this is bad for studtents. Honestly speaking, I thank them a lot. Without they doing so, I might just don't really think about my future seriously. I could remember my junior high school's teacher vividly. My junior teacher was very strict. He set a goal for every student on the exams. If you failed and didn't achieve what the teacher set. You would be punish. I know that the teacher did this for our good. At that time, I migh complain why teacher was so strict and always want us to do the best. But now, I thank for him, without teacher's "punishment" I cannot be the person who I am. I have no any big success right now, but at least I have my goal and knowing what I am doing. Maybe you will complain when teacher punish you, but one day you would know this is all for you good.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers choose to punish children in order to control their behavior while others believe that rewarding students can lead to better results. Both of these methods have their advantages and disadvantages, but I believe it is more effective to reward students.
Punishment can be harsh for the average students, and should only be applied to the misbehaving and immoral children. Punishment can leave permanent mental scars and it can destroy a child's self-image and confidence irreverseably. If you punish a child in order to motivate him to learn, chances are he will develop a fear for particular subjects, and he will try to avoid instead of overcome his problems.
Rewarding, on the other hand, can make a child feel good about himself. He will become more confident and he will have a higher self-esteem. He will remember how good it feels to achieve, and he will try, over and over, to feel that amazing, inexplicable emotion again.
We cannot supress a child's growth, but we can guide them to become better. Rewarding does this job perfectly.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowaday, our Minstry of Education requires that the teachers should not use any physical punishment to their students. They claims that teachers should use love or rewards to teach or correct their students' learning or behavior. For me, I am somewhere in between.
In my opinion, if love and reward are useful to correct students' learning or behavior, I will choose this way to teach my students becaus I don't want to hurt their dignity or make them feel embarrassed. However, I think sometimes punishment is useful for those students who always disobey the school rules. But before the punishment, I sugguest that teachers should try to understand the reasons why those students always do so. Teachers should try to solve the problems if they have any difficult or obstacle. Don't punish them without any excuse.
Take my elementary school classmate as an example, she stole my Hello Kitty earaser. My teacher found it and asked her. She told the teacher, her ill sister likes Hello Kitty so much but cannot afford it. So she stole my earser to make her happy. After the event, my teacher bought some Kitty stuff for her but still asked her say sorry to me and do more clean job for everyone as punishment.
In final analysis, I think these two methods have their own pros and cons. Therefore, being a teacher, he or she should find the balance to motivate or correct students' learning or behavior. In this way, students can develop their IQ and EQ through a proper way.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are two ways for teachers to choose to motivate students: punishment and reward. In the past, teachers in Taiwan used to motivate students by punishing them. However, teachers nowadays tend to use rewards, and it seems more effective.
Students nowadays are weaker when they face pressure. The suicide rate of students is much higher. In this condition, rewarding is a more suitable way to encourage students. They would not be sad because they do not get the rewards. On the contrary, they would study harder to get it.
On the contrary, if the teachers use punishment to make students study, they may probably get a totally contrast effect, for instance, students give up studying. My classmate, Linda, was confident of her English ability. One day, she forgot to memorize the vocabulary and she got zero. Our English teacher announce her score in front of the whole class and punish her to write all the vocabulary 100 times. Since then, Linda hates English and she does not want to study it. The unappropiate punishment makes a terrible effect on students.
In conclusion, rewarding is a better way of motivating students for modern society. Students are too weak to suffer the punishment, even a small blame would destroy his/her interest on studying. By contrast, giving some praise of little gifts can be an effective and better way to encourage students.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think rewarding students for learning is more effective than punishing students for learning. Though punish the students when they have bad behavior can threaten them from doing it again, it is still not a proper way to deal with the students' bad behavior. Punishment will make students scared by the harm of their body, but they still do not think their behavior is wrong. Therefore, we should tell them the mistake they make and use rewarding ways instead of punishing ways to deal with students' bad behavior. We should encourage them not blame on them when they have problems in learning. I think every students are more willing to be encouraged than to be blamed.
Take myself for example, I'm a tutor now. I have tested these two different kinds of methods on my students. At the first time of the class, I blamed on the students who didn't know the answer and even punish them. The students were scared to death and even became more timid than usual. But at the second time of the class, I changed my way in teaching. When the students had problems in answering the questions, I tried not to blame on them, instead of, I encouraged them and told them if one of them can answer the questions, he or she will get some special reward. Out of my surprise, every students tried their best in order to figure out the answer and they were more active in the class than usual.
After the test, I figure out that rewarding is more effective than punishing. We should encourage the students instead of blame on them. Every student needs to be loved and encouraged. Therefore, we should help them to solve the problems and reward them instead of just punish them.

subject: HW1001
content:
I believe rewarding students for learning is the best way to motivate students to learn and to behave well, and here is why.
First, you can't be passive when you want to learn. Setting a goal and to accomplish that goal is the motive for learning. Rewardings are always the final goal. Take kids for example. It's simple to control their behaviors by candies or sweets. To them, that's the biggest motive, and that's kind of reward. Second, learning often leads to series of difficulties; you learn from trial and error. Once you face a crisis, it's the faith that supports you and helps you stick to it. The faith, generally speaking, is often the benifits, the praises from others, or the good results that will happen when you succeed to overcome it. Those are all kinds of rewardings too.
In short, rewardings are what you need when you're trying to learn. Rewardings brighten you up when you suffer dark, tough times, and it is a effective method to get students to learn.

subject: HW1001
content:
Punishment is a negative way for educating students, but rewarding could be a positive way. Punishment might make serious injuries for students' bodies and mind, and it could become a social problem. In the other hand, rewarding could inspire students in many parts and make them more confident. More and more teachers and parents take serious for punishment in recent years, because they find that rewarding is more effective. Most students study hard or behave their behaviors well when they get reward. Educators can choose no rewarding as a punishment, but not no punishing as a reward.
According to the research of psychology on medical report, students can learn how to punish other people through punishments, and they also can learn how to inspire other people through reward. As adults, we can avoid students to learn in a negative way.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the previous educational system, some teachers and parents believed that punishment was one of the best ways to make students study. As the times change, more and more teachers and professors suggest that rewarding students should be more effective way to improve their studying. Plus, the educational administrational department in Taiwan has made a new regulation that pysical punishment is bannd at school. I totally agree that rewarding students is more effective.
Although an old proverb said "spare the stick, and spoil the kid," the teachers only pressure students to study hard by punishment. If students don't realize the reason why they have to learn and gain information at school, they don't develop longlife studying habits. In contrary, students will have a sense of achievement when teachers praise and reward them because of their good jobs. Gradually, they will love going to school and keep improving themselves even after they graduate from school.

subject: HW1001
content:
No doubt, motivating students to perform well is teachers responsibility. It's also obvious that students, who carry the expectation of the society, should behave well and come off with flying colors in their studies. I'm of the opinion that rewarding students for learning is the way second to none, for it can seduce students to perform well effectively, and triger students' spontaneous attitude for learning, as well as make students feel warm and delight.
First of all, rewarding can encourage students to take pains on studies. For instance, when a student put his nose to the grind stone every day but fail in the exam, rewarding may help he or she make persistent efforts and tide over the adverse circumstances. In addition, some students have vanity in gaining rewards. On account of wanting to gain more presents than any other classmates, they will behave better and study harder on their cord. Rewarding students thus becomes an important motivation for students, even when teachers doesn't supervise them. Last but not least, gaining rewards makes students gay and futher form a sense of gratitude. Everyone feels delight when accepts presents. If it were not for rewarding, and just punishing students, students might feel menacholy and despair, rebel to teachers' instruction, and go astray.
From the reasons I have listed above, I firmly hold that only through rewarding students can students behave better and perform well on the subject which they specilize in. Moreover, it will form a good relationship between teachers and students, as a result, they can solve some problems exisiting in class or help some students go through their impasse with concerted efforts. In short, it's fabulous to reward students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Educating is not only teachers' job but responsibility. The way the teachers teach can make a vital influence on students. But nowadays on newspaper, we can read the news that teachers use punishment instead of reward students to control them. Every time I read this, I can help but feel sorrow.
I think the second method would be much better because in this way can gain more acceptence. No one likes being blamed, and so do I. If teachers can explain why he/she was wrong and led them to the correct direction, they would felt regret and made up their minds to do it in right way next time. For instance, if a student of your class always tells lies to his classmates, you can arrange an appointment with him. During the session, you can tell him the disadvantages of telling lies to others, and let him know the influence after he tells a lie such as losing trust among friends and gaining less help while in need. Maybe he may not agree on you, then you can keep telling him until he realize how ridiculous he has done. Telling lies is not the only way to solve problems, you should be frank to every of your classmates because telling the truth is a virtue, and as a proverb goes, "Honesty is the best policy." If you say so, the student will accept your idea with no doubt, and teacher can avoid punishing them with physical punishment or blaming. Most important of all, in this way can not only strengthen the relationship between teachers and students, but also create a win-win situation.

content: In my opinion, that use punishment to motivate students is more effective. First, when students were young, it's hard to parents or teachers to teach child what to do or not in mild ways. Rewarding always led to woue result, I think that is owing to childs' bad memorize. Students might not get good grades if their parents use rewarding, but if their parents say they will punish the students when they didn't reach the goal. Mostly, the students will achieve. Base to the reasons below, punishment is more effective than rewarding.

It can't be denied that teaching is a long way to go. But what kind of education is mostly suitable for students? There are more to be decussed. As for me, rewarding students for learning is more effective than punishment. Here are the following reasons.
First, I believe that there is still kindness in a student heart, although he might not have behaved well. And unproper punishment only contribute to his hatry of his world. On the contrary, if he is encouraged to behave well next time, there will be a glimmer of hope, a hope for himself, flittering in his heart. Second, over punishment can destroy one's confidence. In conclusion, a well-educated person will go to any length to reward to the society, so a effective way of teaching is important. And I believe rewarding students for I

subject: HW1001
content:
The way teachers choose to encourage students to learn is quite important. Some suppress students to absorb as much information as they can while others hold a soften and easy attitude towards the result of students' learning process.
In my opinion, rewarding students is more effective than punishing them. Because praises often fuel one to achieve a higher goal since the teacher gives him or her more confidence and beliefs. Furthermore, it's also essential to make students enjoy in the whole process and keep in good mood. That way, they're more likely to cultivate the interest as well as the positive attitude on their own. And chances are they will motivate themselves to learn in a long term.
Take Edison, one of the most excellent inventors in the world, for example. At school, teachers always regarded his behavior and questions as nonsense. What's worse, they often punished little Edison in order to shut his mouth up and forced him to sit quietly listening to the teachers as other children did. As a consequence, Edison hated to go to school. But things were tatally different after he returned to his home to be taught by his mother who he thought the best teacher in the world. His mother encouraged him to raise questions and even did a lot experiments with him. Everytime Edison found the answer, his mother would compliment him for the good job he did and his perseverance. As time went by, Edison became more confident by himself and came up with an abundent of great inventions that had make such lasting impacts on human beings' civilization. It was his mother's rewards and couragement that made Edison love learning and then carried his own dreams out; it was his wise mother helped him to light the world up.
To sum up, rewarding students for learning does work to motivate students to keep working. Nothing but soaking in the relaxing and joyable astomosphere is the key to make them love learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
As we know, more and more teachers have changed their methods of classroom management. Plus, some non-profit organizations have drawn the attention of school teachers and parents by promoting "No coporal punishment on campus." In my point-of-view, teachers should be aware that coporal punishment cannot make students behave well in class. Teachers are supposed to encourage their students more, and the reasons are as followed.
For starters, no one likes to be scolded, for being scolded may make them feel distressed; even worse, they might lose their interest in learning. Take one of my students Wendy for example. I did not intend to insult or mock her during class, but she thought my words had hurt her feelings. Thus, she told her father she would like to drop out of my class. Her father also supposed that I was not a qualified teacher as I ignored student's affection.
This case taught me an invaluable experience. Every teacher should mind his or her language and they have to know individual differences.
Secondly, I have found that students will be motivated if I offer them some small gifts, such as snacks or beverages, but they have to get high scores or complete the task I have given them. It really works by telling them they will get prizes. Thus, I am willing to prepare some snacks or stationery as gifts for my students. Most importantly, the learning outcomes have been improving.
Last but not the least, teachers must care about his or her students more often. Student will feel a strong bond between teachers and students. Once they trust their teachers, they will naturally pay more attention in class and learn to respect their teachers.
To sum up, discipline has always been an key issue in teaching. Indeed, as long as teachers spend more time observing and showing care for their students, punishment, coporal or verbal alike, will be the last means of controlling students.

subject: HW1001
content:
The two different styles of teaching, punishing or rewarding students, have been arguing for a long time. For me, I prefer the latter.
When it comes to an appropriate way to teach youngster, I deem that some timely rewards will be a great method. Take me for instance, while I was a junior high school student, my homeroom teacher estabished some principles and carried it out throughout 3 years. She rewarded when we behaved well, and gave us warnings when we were being rude or bad. However, the previous one was much likeing to happen. After most of my classmates entered high school, they performed excellent in their school lives. The advantage of rewarding the children is undoubted.
On the opposite, it is unlikely for you to motivate students by means of hurting them. Some might says, "Spare the rod, spoil the child," but how can you make sure that it will not become worse when you send out a unfriendly and invasive motion to the child. Some kids, instead, hold grudges and eventually erupt their feelings someday.
In my perspective, I firmly believe that rewarding our students is a better way to form their personalities. Knowing that you will receive what you want only if you have devoted yourself in it is a great trait. And I think it is dispensable in our education.

subject: HW1001
content:
I consider that teachers should reward students for learning. Students learn better when they want to learn. Punishment can force them to learn but if won't let them want to learn. What they think about is, "I have to cram these stuff in my brain or I'll be punished." And after the test, they forget everything they learned. On the other hand, rewarding students can make them willing to learn. Only when students know that studying is useful for them can they really learn something.
My teacher told us that he always rewards students for learning. This really make his classes learn better then other classes. The evident is that the grades of his classes are always better than the classes of the teacher who always punishes students to force them to study. This really makes me believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.
Another example is my own experience. My math teacher in juniour high punished us to force us to learn. I hated him but I had to follow his rule and studied. This made me not willing to learn math. But when I got to seniour high, I met a math teacher that always rewarded us for learning. This let me be more willing to learn math and make me more confident on math. The two methods really made a difference on me. One made me hate to learn and I couldn't learn well but the other made me realize that learning is good to me and I learn better. So my opinion is that teachers should reward students for learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
As a teacher myself, I strongly agree with those teachers who reward their students for great learning, behavior and study attitude. I will support my opinion by sharing my experience below.
When I was a young teacher, I used a lot of negative punishment to control my students. As a result, students tended to focus on not to do those bad things I listed in the posters hanging in our classroom. They became afraid of the punishment and forgot what are the good things to do. They became less confident. The whole class became stressful to all the students. Not to mention that they did not improve so much in their study. They were to busy thinking about what not to do!
As I become more experience in teaching, I started to observe my students more carefully. I find that the students have a special need, which is what we call "happiness". How do I provide them happiness? I creat a lot of diffent tasks for them to achieve, such as finishing reading 10 books, getting 10 points from teachers and doing things for your parents. They get awards after they complish a task. Students enjoy the activity a lot. They become happier because they realize what they can do but what they can't do.
In conclusion, I think all the teachers should try to motivate their students in a positive way. You will find that students become better in learning and have more positive thinking.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, punishing student will only negate their motivations, on the other hand rewording students seem to be working better in my case.
When I was in high school, I used to have a terrible English teacher. She punishes us all the time. She wanted us to score high on the test all the time, however I am not that type of hardworking student, I get lazy very offten, however I could still get a "C-" or a "B" in most tests. Ever my parents thinks it's fine I get a "C-" or a "B", but my English teacher didn't think so, therefore she punish me almost everytime after each test. Therefore I started to not show up for her classes, and that pisses her off. Therefore she called my parents. My parents and her had a long talk, they had a complete opposite thery about education. Therefore my parents made me transfer to other school, leaving that dumb teacher behind.
When I got to the new school, things were totally different. I usually do really bad on science tests, but my new science teacher gives out movie tickets to students who do well on tests, then my grade started to go sky rocket.
I thank my science teacher for changing my life. Therefore in my opinion, rewarding students is a much better way to motivate students. I could be wrong, but it is the way that's working for me.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, there are manys news about the teacher's punishment to students. Some people think it reasonable while others don't think so. By watching these events on TV, I also have some opinions to say.
I think punishing students can be much more effective. Many fundations devoted to human rights may think the punishment does harm to the children's dignity a lot. But, how come a teacher wants to see a child being punished unless he really does something bad? If a child really does something bad or annoys teachers, how come a teacher can just forgive him by being unrespected by the child at first? I don't think it logical.
Nowadays, there has been a new word coming out called "monster parent", it means more and more people have found that the behavior of those parents who seriously disagree with punishment are incredible. By the phenomenon, we can see more and more people have considered punishment necessary for those annoying kids. I also deeply believe that those parents seriously disagreeing with punishment will feel sorry to their rediculous behaviors some day.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, learning should be enjoyable. There's no pushing while we are learning. Therefore, I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. I believe that no one likes to be punished while most people enjoy compliment.
Take my 7-year-old cousin for example, he usually turns on TV immediately after school, but there's an exception which is if his teacher gives him a recite test and his teacher offers rewards, he will extremely focus on his study.
Take myself for example, I can still remember that I used to be a lazy students. However, once teacher offered an opportunity which I could be praised or rewarded in front of the rest classmates, I would try every efforts to achieve it because I loved this great feeling. I think that an simple gift or lovely compliment can be great incentives for students to learn and enjoy the process of learning. Once they find their interests, they will know how fascinating learning is.

subject: HW1001
content:
Many teachers and parents assume that the only way to teach a child discipline is to resort to punishment and threatening. But as time changes, others have began to think otherwise. They think maybe encouragement and reward is the better way.
As far as I'm concerned, both ways have their pros and cons, but I still think that the education of love is the better way for a child's learning. There are three major reason for that. First, a child grown up in an environment full of love and caring tends to have a better personality. Second, malicious words and emotions during childhood may cause the child to imitate these behavior when they grow up. Last, but not least, the motivation of learning, afterall, is happiness. If you turn learning into an excruciating bussiness, what kind of child can possibly learn anything?
Take my classmate for example, his parents have always been strict on him. And that causes a great deal of pain and pressure whenever he fails, even a little. At last, he totaly give up learning. It is all because of the wrong methods his parents use when teaching him.
We, therefore, can make clear of the above discussion that under no circumstances should we use violence and malice when motivating children. Instead, we shoud keep a caring heart and loving mind to ensure that our future generations possess them too.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, there are a lot of ways to teach students. Some will use punishment while some use rewarding. Even though, they all have their advantages and disadvantages, we still need to find a better way.
In my opinion, I think punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior is much better. Students are afraid of being punished. Just like the theory of teaching study. They do an experiment. They use a mouse with an eletric box. They put the mouse in the box. If the mouse wants to run out of it, an eletric box will turn on and mouse will get hurt. After several try by mouse, the mouse will not try to get out the box anymore. In the theory, we can see that punishment is work. Students will change their behavior after receiving a punishment.
There is still the other example to support my opinion. I have heard one experience that parents belive rewarding is good for leading better results. Parents made a deal with their child that if she did something right, they would give her a star. After collecting twenty stars, they would give her what she wants. However, the star would be erased by bad behavior. In this case, this method works in the beginning. Nevertheless, after a while, their child do everything just in order to get a star. If the behavior could not make her get a rewarding, she would not do.
From this example, they finally realize that punishment is more effective than rewarding. Because punishment can let children to get rid of their bad habit and gain better behavoir insteaded. However, a rewarding only can teach children to do what we will give them stars. It can not teach them more things.
To sum up, punishment is better than rewarding. However, if we punished our children too seriously, we would hurt them. Therefore, I think punish children in acceptable degree is important. The effect will better than rewardings or punish too seriously.

subject: HW1001
content:
As a teacher, it is important to arouse students' motivation. As far as I am concerned, I think there isn't the only way to teach since each student is an independent individual. Teachers should depend on the situation and make appropriate decisions. So there isn't the only method to teach students. I think if teachers just keep punishing students or rewarding them, they will be tired with the class and even lose the learning willing. Take myself for example, I don't like teachers scolding me first without understanding the problem. I always think that a good teacher should be both patient and knowedgable. Besides, a good teacher should always make the class interesting since once the students don't have any interests in learning, it is impossible to let them learn any knowledge from teachers. Additionally, lecturing isn't the only way to learn, students can also learn something from playing.
If teachers can give appropriate encouragement or reward to students when they make things right, I am convinced that both teachers and students will satisfy the learning result. To sum up, being a teacher has to be really "hardworking", that is, put more passion and enthusiasm in teaching, not just trying to punish students or reward them only.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students for learning can lead to better result. Though the government has ruled that teachers shouldn't punish students, some teachers especially in junior high or elementary schools ignore the law and keep punishing students. This may have two results. One is that students will be afraid of the subject and the teacher. The other is that students will hate the subject and the teacher and thus will be absent from the class. Punishing students obviously can't motivate students to learn.
On the contrary, if teachers give some prize to students for learning, it may lead to a different result. For instance, some students might not be good at tests, but they're adept in organizing datas. Providing that teachers give these students an opportunity to make up for their poor scores, such as handing in the reports or giving an oral presentation on stage, they may have the motivation to search for the data and even gradually fall in love with the subject. In conclusion, I think rewarding is much better than punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
When it comes to education, many teachers start to talk about their methods concerning teaching students. Some teachers agree that they use punishment to motivate and control students. However, other teachers think that students can have better learning results by rewarding. For me, as a teacher in senior high school, my opinion is that proper rewarding can motivate students. The reasons are as follows.
The most important thing is that students can have sense of honor if they are rewarded. Doing the right things can be viewed as the honor in students' mind. Therefore they keep on behaving themselves. Besides, punishing can can cause students negative learning and mental results. For example, some students may have low learning motivation and ability. Punishment just makes student afraid of learning so that they refuse to learn certain subjects. In addition, senior learners need more rewarding methods because their understanding and mental state are quite different. They are almost adults. Rewarding can make them improve themselves by thinking what to do. Finally the birth rate in Taiwan is lowering, parents can't accept that their children are punished because they don't punish them at home.
Therefore, the above reasons and opinions are that I agree rewarding is the proper way to educate students. Motivating students by rewarding can help them a positive learning attitude. Moreover, they won't have negative emotions when they talk about their learning experience. Of course, proper punishment is sometimes necessary for students. However, rewarding is still more effective.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think my favorite method is rewarding students, some old teachers believe that punishment is the best way to teach students, but it only work in the past time. Most teachers now use rewarding instead of punishment, in students' oppion, they think they did something wrong, but you just tell me I am wrong and teach me how to do next time, we don't need punishment, we are not animals, we can understand what you said.
We all don't like someone tell us something with anger, it makes us feel uncomfortable, in this case no matter what they told us, we never keep their words in mind, and will do the wrong things over and over again, so I prefer rewarding students than punishment.
Nowadays, many teachers in school do not dare to punish students, because once they hit students' face, hands, bottom or said something wrong to hurt students, their parents always mad at them and almost have a fight with teachers to protect their kids, or maybe they will be fined and send into a jail. I think the rate of punishment is decreasing now in Taiwan.

subject: HW1001
content:
Every teachers want their student to learn as much as possible and also behave well. But some students rarely pay attention in class or can not control thier behavior.
In Taiwan, most teachers punish these students, and put severe restrictions to them. But I don't think this is an effective way. Many students who get punishments grow hostile to teachers, and they behave even worse to make teachers angry.
My family move to America for a short time when I was 12 years old, I study in the primary school over there for one year. Teachers in that school never hit students. Instead of punishing students, they reward students who do well. And students hardly behave bad.
I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. At least student won't live under panic and fearness.

subject: HW1001
content:
It was common to hear news about the punishments in school in the past. Parents even asked teachers to punish their children in order to get good grades or change bad behaviors. Take my father for example, in his childhood, they awed teachers even more than their parents. In his memory, teachers always got sticks in their hands and were ready to punish students any time. Students behaved carefully and studied hard to keep from the sticks. Even through they were forced to live up to teachers' expectations, they were thankful after they graduated or grew up. Because without those punishments, they couldn't reach acheivements today.
Nowadays, everything has changed. More and more teachers decide to provide students with rewards instead of punishments. We students persue the rewards by studying harder and harder and also good behaviors. We learn happily and of course competitively. My teacher once said that he promise to give us presents if we get better grades. From then on, we all tried our best to live up to the goal. Eventually, most classmates made a lot of progress.
In my opinion, the two methods are both effective, but the first one is not accessible now. Because parents are protect their children more and more than before. They don't allow teachers to hurt their beloved kids. To sum up, the second method is better in this age without a doubt.

subject: HW1001
content:
To my own perspective, I think rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. If a student feel miserable about learning, then how can she/he have the motivation to keep concentrating on their studies? If I were a teacher, I would encourage students to strive for their own personal dreams. Dreams can really push oneself forward to realize what they want.
On the contrary, if a teacher did use punishment to motivate students, I think the students would really find it hard to discover their own interests and happiness in studying. They might always think that they won't behave well on the school exams and performances, and in turn they won't have any confidence in themselves.
To my real experience, I felt more easily to improve my studies when the teacher rewarded me for doing good on learning. At first, when I was first grade in junior high school, our homeroom teacher used to punish students while behaving bad. But then, she changed the way of teaching in the third grade. She kept encouraging and rewarding me and my classmates. Before long, most of the students, including myself, have done well on the school work than ever before!

subject: HW1001
content:
Through our learning process, most of the students make mistakes at school. At this time, teachers' reactions turn to be a point. Whether teachers should punish students or not? For me, I think punishment isn't a good solution to let students know they shouldn't do that again or force them to study harder. I believe that rewarding students can lead to better results, on the contrary.
Recently, I read a report on the Internet. According to that report, a naughty teenager in second grade in the junior high school was really a bad guy and even in a gang. Finally, he became a good student and entered a famous senior high school. How and what caused such a huge change? Due to that teenager's fortune, he had met a wonderful teacher who constantly encouraged him to do better. That teacher said that never did he use any punishment to the teenagers. Instead of that, he gave him a little presents if he did good job and lead him to the right way to do homework gradually. It's obvious to tell that that teacher is so successful.
Well it goes, "Children can't be outstanding if teachers don't give them punishments." However, after reading that report, I am here to say that rewarding students is certainly the good way to educate students. By that way, it can reach the goal to let students know what they should really do!

subject: HW1001
content:
I think rewarding students for learning can lead to better results in teaching. Corporal punishment is severely forbidden in education. One reason is that students have the right to control their body, and the other is that corporal punishment does harm to students' physical and mental state.
Corporal punishment may be a good way to intimidate students to perform better on the study, but it is not a good way to motivate them to be interested in study. Study is a long way to go, so corporal punishment is just a transcient method to motivate students to learn. Worse, it brings negative effects to students so that they refuse and loathe learning.
I think rewarding students is a better and long-standing way to lead students to learn. My English teacher said that once she praised a student that he was good at English. The student told my teacher after several years that he studied English harder since then because of her compliment. This method is also a famous one teacher use in teaching. Moreover, an experiment proves that plants receiving more compliments can grow stronger and more beautiful than plants which don't.
It seems that all creatures like to be rewarded, even to students. People like to get approvement from others, so they will be confident enough and inspire themselves to perform better. As a result, I believe that rewarding students can lead better results because I like to be rewarded and complimented as well.

subject: HW1001
content:
There is always a controversy over punishment or rewarding students when comes to education. Some people believe that to punish students is much more effective than to reward students in gentle way because it tells students if they violated the rule, the result would be terrible. Some hold in the opposition on this issue.
In my opinion, which way to use should depend on the age of students. The students in primary schools are to little to realize, or remember, what is not allowed, so using hush punishment on them might help them to fit into the surroundings and the correct rules quickly. In terms of students in junior and senior high, they are able to think the pros and cons of their behaviors and control themselves. To choose punishment might not be educational to them; instead, teachers should lead them to think and realize the reasons of setting the rules. The education with encouragement and reward would leads to better outcome.
Depend on different factors and situations, the decision on which way to choose should be a consus by teachers, parents and students. Education is an important but uneasy task, it takes the wisdom of the whole society to get better off.

subject: HW1001
content:
In school, some teachers tend to reward students to learn, while others choose giving punishment. In my opinion, I support the former method which is rewarding students when they have any positive behaviors.
The main reason I agree with rewarding is that it can help students build confidence. Students who are praised or rewarded easily gain confidence in their academic learning and behaviors. Through building the confidence, students may possess positive thinkings toward themselves, leading to success more easily. However, students lose their confidence when receiving punishment. They become more coward toward learning, and they may be afraid of making mistakes. It definitely reduce learning motivations and outcomes. The other reason that I agree with rewarding is from the aspect of love. As educators, they need to give students love and encourage them to learn: rather than giving punishment to students to discourage and scare students. How can a teacher teach students without love?
Take myself for example, when I was the first grader in elementary school, I didn't get good grades on math. At that time, my teachers blamed at me or hit me very often. It discouraged my learning. I thought I was the worst student in the world. My math got worse and worse. However, when I was the third grader, everything changed. I became positive and got good graders on math-it was because of my new math teacher. She rewarded and praised me. My confidence increased because I got "love" from her.
In conclusion, teachers should give students reward, not punishment to help students. My personal experience may be a convincing example.

subject: HW1001
content:
Powerful as punishment is, it is more effective to let students correct their behavior by telling them right from wrong. Many teachers tend to punish students because they are lack of patience, so they don't want to spend time telling students why they can't do this or that, and therefore students correct their behavior because they are afraid of punishment. If teachers can be more patient and more willing to hear what the students want to say, they can lead the students to direct way and really let them "learn" a lesson instead of "suffering" from a lesson.
My brother, Jack, was often punished by his teacher because he was thought of as an overactive and violent guy. However, as his sister I knew that he was active because he couldn't wait to receive new knowledge, and he was violent because he tended to prevent others from "violence." After he got into junior high school, he changed because his new teacher told him that it was good to long for knowledge, but it was not good to disturb other students on class, and that it was good to defend others, but it was not good to use violence. From then on, my brother asked questions after class and used wisdom while facing with violence. He seemed to become mature, and it all thanked to the teacher in his jonior high. I thought that it was more active to teach students with wisdom instead of with punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
We all know that physical punishment is controversial in Taiwan now. Teachers who use it might cause the students to get hurt and become the spotlight on TV and even be sent to jail.
As a junior high school teacher, however, I agree to use proper punishment to motivate students' learning and to control their behavior. Indeed, rewarding can lead to good results for learning, but it's not suitable for all the students all the time. What if the students just walk around in class or keep making a lot of noise in class? You can't tell them to sit down and be quiet and give them candy or even money if they do so every time-I did have this experience. They said, if you give me some money, and I will ...."
In my opinion, using proper punishment can lead to good results and promote their learning at the same time. Just be careful not to hurt their feelings and bodies, and it will be fine. If we teach them to respect themselves and others with both proper punishment and admiring verbly, and their learning and behavior will be promoted.

subject: HW1001
content:
In such a competitive period, teachers and parents try any methods to promote students' capability. Some teachers do it by punishment while others do it by rewarding. As far as I am concerned, no education can be perfected without rewarding or punishment. The following is my statement.
First of all, punishment is, in most of educators' opinions, indeed an efficienty way to motivate students to study. It makes students frightened, and inforce them to do their academics well. However, it also impact the relationship between students and teachers. Students study not because of their willing but teachers' expectations. Reluctant learing caused by too more punishment is unefficient.
Secondly, rewarding is believed to encourage students to learn in a positive way. Unfortunately, it also make them lazy if there is no punishment. Students may hang out with their friends everyday and learn nothing.
Accroding to the above-mentioned, give punishment when students perform terribly but reward them when they perform well. That is the best way to educate our students. Last but not least, no punishment or rewarding will be meaningfull if it is not be gave in a suitable way.

subject: HW1001
content:
While I was studying in elementary school, my teacher use more punishment to make my study progress. Besides, when I did some naughty behaviors, I would be punished. For example, I would have more homework than my classmates, or I would have to stay in the classroom during the break to erase the blackbord for teacher. I found that teachers in Taiwan prefer to use punishment to motive their students. From elementary school to high school, most of my teachers use punishment more than reward. If I were a teacher, I would use reward to educate my students rather than punishment.
To begin with, giving students reward when they perform well on school work would definitely increase their learning interests; on the contrary, giving them punishment when they didn't do well on the test, students might not only gradually loose their interests but also confidence on learning. Next, rewarding could cultivate students' positive attitude and thinking. They will be honor when they are rewarded. As they are accomplish a task, they would make a lot of effort to earn the reward instead of worring about being punishend.
In fact, I think teachers should use positive way to encourge students' school work and behavior. By this method, students could enjoy their school life more and decrease some of unnecessary pressure.

subject: HW1001
content:
Generally speaking, most students do not like to study automatically and sometimes make some mistakes. There are two principal methods for teachers to use to deal with these students. The first method is to use punishment and the other method is to use encouragement.
These two method both have their benifits and shortcomings. In my personal opinion, the punishment method could have instant response that most students could obey the teacher's instruction to do because of their fear of the punishment. However, if the students can't achieve the demands from their teachers although they have tried their best to study or to do something, the punishment method will be useless if teachers still use them again and again.
In the above situation, teachers should consider to change another way to do with students in order to have better results. The alternative method is called encouragement or rewarding method. Using this method, students can feel confortbale and respectable. Generally, student can behave better and better when their teachers or parents give them suitable rewards and encouragement.
An obvious example is proposed in the following. When a student is preparing to take the entrance exam of universities or colleges, they always feel high pressure in the periods of their studying. At times, they will get a not so good result when they attend the exam. At this moment, teachers and parents should give them the confidence and encouragement for them to do it again instead of giving them punishment. According to experts' conclusion and experience, at this situation the suitable reward to their effort they made probably will have better response.
According the above article, I prefer to suitable reward and encouragement rather than punishment. Sometimes, giving a student a suitable reward could encourage him to try his best to do again. And it always has a better result than using punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
For some students, school life is an ultimate happy source of gaining knowledge. For the others, learning is unexciting, tedius and even more unbearable. The former differ from the later because their teachers believes that rewarding students is much better to punish them.
I can not agree with the teaching way "rewarding" students more. Both teachers and students can benefit from a vast advantages of it. To begin with, students' learning motivation gets stronger naturally since no terrible punishment subscribes painful memories in their hearts. What's more, teachers can push students to deeply think how and what they learn. Students will feedback and have passion for learning from the bottom of their soul.
Take me for example, I met with a special math teacher in my childhood. She never scolded students, especially those who were not good at math or eve had hatred to it like me. Encouraging students to think automatically, she gave us a point if we answered in class whether it was right or not. After collecting ten points, we could get some hand-made presents from her. Every students in her class wouldn't feel they are neglected or abandoned and have confidence to learn.
It's obvious that rewarding students for learning is more effective. It helps teachers and students bond together and have better academic performance.

subject: HW1001
content: In terms of me, I think that rewarding students for learning is more effective than punishing them. Using punishment to motivate students to study can only have a temporary result. Students might be intimidated by the punishment at first, and dedicate themself to schoolworks. However, once they get accustomed to those punishments, they will no longer be afraid of being punished, and soon they will start to lose their focuses on study, because the stimulation is on the grounds that they are frighten to get punished. As a result, when the hazard fades away, the old problem will emerge. To make them pay attention to their works once and for all, giving them rewards after they accomplish their study can lead to a permanent result. They will try their best to finish their work in order to get the prize. By virtue of the desire of owning the reward, they will never lose their concentration on the schoolworks. Take my friend for an example. My friend used to be bored with study. Nonetheless, my teacher never gave up on him. My teacher would treat him a cake after he finished his homework. At the begining, stimulated by the desire of the cake, my friend would try to finish his work. As time went by, he became a diligent boy, who always had a outstanding academic performance. Therefore, I prefer to reward students for learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are two different methods to motivate students to learn. However, I prefer the second method to first one. I think students should be encouraged to study rather than force them. When a student study happily, he would like to spend more time reading books and he will concentrate on it. On the contrary, when a student is forced to read books, he won't focus on it even though he spends the same time with the former one.
Take me for instance, when I studied in the senior high school, my parents always punished me. Angry they were, I still made bad performance on my studies. However, when they sent me to a cram school, I became more diligent. There was a teacher called Lisa in my cram school. She always encouraged me to study hard and asked me not to disappoint her. As a result, I began to studied hard. Whenever I had time, I always studied hard to prepare for my college academic exam. When the result came out, I was the top three in the school. I chose to join the military academy because my teacher told me that I could have an opportunity of studying abroad and the government would pay all the money and give me extra money for me to live in the America. Therefore, I spent all my holiday studying English and exercising. As a consequence, I can study abroad now. I will leave Taiwan on August tenth to study in the Citadel military academy.
To sum up, students who are encouraged to study will concentrate on studying and will study happily just like me. I am intreasted in studying now especially English. I always spend a lot of time learning new knowledge.

subject: HW1001
content:
Education is the most important fundation in a country. Students grow up and become a mature adult through a proper education system. However, in the modern time, there are two oppisite voices of education in our society. In my opinion, I prefer the rewarding side. According to the whole mankind history, love and forgive are always the winners, since they are the elements which build our family and country. Love is the one that keeps the students look up and optimistic. By rewarding students, they can be more active to elevate themselves, not just for the prizes they get, but for the honor and victory in their hearts.
Sam is a little boy in the elementary school. Odd enough, he is the rotten apple in his math teacher's eyes but the model student in this English class. During the math class, the teacher always uses the punishment to force students' learning motivation. However, it ends up that Sam is scare to death all the time. Only thinking not to be punish, Sam can't even release his tension and press, not to mention studies math well. On the contrary, his English teacher makes good use of the candies and small gifts, successfully catches the hearts of the students. Sam enjoys every English class and always completes the homework on time. As the result, Sam's English makes an obvious progress and he is never afraid of speaking English.
Though there are two methods of teaching students, I believe that rewarding students for learning can always lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content: As we know that the physical punishment is banned in all the public schools, based on the new policy announced by the government, who claims to provide a safer educational enviroment for the students without fear and harm. But for me, as a cram school teacher in Kaohsiung, still reguards that it still functions to some naughty students with an effective punishment, which gives the teacher power and right to warn the naughty and impolite ones. How to make the punishment rules is the hardest issue for all the teachers though. Maybe we should gather together to do more discussion and estimate what kind of punishment is useful and more civilized to help the teachers correct and stop students' wrong behavior at school. All in all, either giving punishment or rewarding could benifit both teachers and students. Now what we need to do is to adjust our teaching manners, start over thinking if the punishment is necessary to some certain but common cases happening at school, and show a teacher's mercy to help the students who should deserve being well-educated better and more.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, should teachers punish students in school is a popular issue. With the changing of the era, many parents don't insist on the conventional way in teaching their children. On the contrary, they are used to encouraging their children instead of blaming them for their poor behavior.
In my opinion, I think the best way to teach students is rewarding them to create better results. According to the research, high persentage of students do rebel against their parents and teachers in their adolenscence. To deal with this problem, I think we should encourage them to change their poor behavior. If we just force them to follow our regulations, I guess it may lead to miserable results, such as suicide and commit sins. It's too late when it comes to regret.
About one month ago, I read a report about how to get along with teenagers in their growing process. It is no surprise that communication and encouragement are the most essential parts. From that article, I have learned that in a school, there is a student who had poor performance and it seemed that almost nobody could change his terrible act. Fortunately, he encountered a patient tutor who persisted in her way to teach the student to lead a better life. To our surprise, the teacher made it finally. The student is no longer a rude and selfish one and he becomes active in learning now.
I think we shouldn't control students' behavior by punishing them seriously because it may influence the way they deal with problems and they could resort to violence when facing difficulties in the future. To prevent these situations from happening, I consider the method we punish our children is a worth considering issue.

subject: HW1001
content:
Teachers nowadays usually use punishments to control students' behaviors. They would give students physical punishments when they make mistakes to warn them to behave well. Teachers may think that will contribute to a wonderful results. In my opinion, however, we should reward children instead of just punishing them. All the people have one thing in common-they like to be praised rather than insulted. Given everyone likes to be rewarded, we shouldn't have to use too much punishments. Giving kids award can motivate them to study harder and make them have more sense of achievement.
When I was in elementary school, I met a nice teacher. She often encouraged us to study hard instead of ordering us. The way she won our hearts was to reward us by giving presents. If we had a great performance, she would gave us either candies nor pencils to praise us. Because of her method, my score was rising higher and higher. Eventually, I got the first prize when I graduated and kept the sense of achievement until now. So I appreciated her very much.
Although punishing students may get some effects, it may also cause a great number of problems. In my opinion, rewarding students is more effective and gives rise to better results. Kids are very sensative and vulnerable, if we are patient to teach and encourage them, they will end up having a bright future.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I've used both. But the rewarding is more effective. I was educated in the way of punishment in my childhood. If I did something wrong, no matter at home or school, I would be punished. To be honest, I was fearful when I made mistakes. However, I don't believe that someone can grow up without any mistakes. The punishment might be the efficient method to effect the students' grades but their learning motivation.
I am an English cram school teacher now. Since the reason that I mentioned above, I deeply believed that I should use the punishment to control my students. Although most of them got good grades at school. I seldom saw their happy faces. Once there was a new teacher who demostrated her teaching plans in my class, I found my students were so happy. Because the teacher prepared some stickers and little gifts, every student paid much attention in class and tried to answer her questions. I was totally surprised that all of them could answer the questions and passed the following quiz.
That teacher not only gave my students a lesson but me. Now I have practiced this method of rewarding for several years. All my students and I have happy hours in class now.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think rewarding students for learning can lead to better results, and punishment often makes students disappoint themselves.
When I was a junior high school students, the math grades of our class was the worst in the school. Our math teacher, Mr. Lee, suffered a lot of pressure from the master and our parents. To improve our math grades, he put all students into three levels, A, B and C. The A level included the best 9 students and the C level included the worst 9 students. In every levels, there were even three small groups, so we had 9 small groups (A1, A2, A3 B1, B2, B3 etc...). Mr. Lee told us that we just competed with the classmates in the same level, and that if the math grades of our group were the highest in the level, he would bought some drinks to us. With his encouragement and appealing rewarding, all of us studied math diligently. At the next exams, the math grades of our class even rised to the second place. Not only did Mr. Lee and us but also the master surprised at the result. We were both excited and pleasant. We could do it!
Now, I still appreciated Mr. Lee. What made our class improved a lot is not only this encouragement but also his wisdom. If he hadn't come up the method to cheer us up, we would have disappointed ourselves on math in the rest of our life. And I think that rewarding students is the best way to encourage them to study hard.

subject: HW1001
content:
I deeply believe that students should be only encourged to learn through positive ways rather than negative punishment. according to numerous research, students' academic performances are highly related to the way the teachers treat them. That is, the positive motivations are able to foster students' attitudes to learn and also prompted they to have a better performance. The negative punishment, on the other hand, could possibly lead them to detest the specific subject, and give up the whole schooling for the sake.
Back to high school, I was not very good at math and the math teacher always apply harsh punishment when students didn't get a good grades on tests. I always have to receive her punishment after each test, but things never get better. I would say I would never perform well in math no matter how many punishment I receive.
In conclusion, only positive motivations and rewardings are able to arouse students' interests to learn rath than giving them bitter punishment.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, rewarding students for learning is more effective. Teacher who uses punishmet might get carried away and become the student abused. There are at least two points to support my opinion. First, when we rewarding students, they will have more confident to learn things. If the teacher can reward their students when they learn well, they will be very delectable. Even just a candy or a smile, It still means a lot to them. In addition, students will start to learn things or study hard just for the rewarding. Because students always feel great when teacher reward them at the front of the class, so they will desperate to do well on learning only to enjoy the moment that they are being rewarded by teacher at the front of the class. This is kind of a stimulation. Because of the aforementioned reasons, I strongly believe that rewarding students for learning will be the more effective way to motivate them to learn.

subject: HW1001
content: In Taiwan, some teachers insist that they use punishment to motivate students to learn. However, others teachers suggest that rewarding students is the best way to educate our children. As far as I am concerned, as a student, I prefer rewarding to punishment. The reason for it is that punishment sometimes make our feel depressed because even we make effort to do everything; however, if we fall, we still receive punishment. On the contrary, after working hard, we receive rewards. It is definitely correct that we will be motivated and work harder next time. For example, when I prepared the entrance exam, my dad gave me a promise to buy new motorcycle if I score well. As a result, to attain my goal, I studied harder than before. However, it furstrated me that there was a little margin to reach my goal as the result came out. Nevertheless, my dad still sent me a new motorcycle and beyond me expactation, I scored better than I had performed before. Thus, in my experience, rewards play a significant role in my phase of learning. Even though we have difficuty in learning, we still take a positive attitude to sign for the next challenges by receiving our parents or teachers rewards. Finally, I'm sure that rewarding students is the best choice to motivate us.

subject: HW1001
content: Punishment is part of the tradition in the education system in Taiwan. No matter teachers use sticks to make students aware of their bad grades, or ask them to rewrite something for memorizing, punishment is all around our daily life in Taiwan. I still remember my junior high school teachers. Not because they were kind or beautiful, but for their strict attitude about me. I was in a school that everybody cared about score, and I happened to be in one of the higher grades classes. Our teacher gave us a lot of tests every day, and made qualified points for everyone in my class. She hit us on the palms with the sticks when we failed to reach the points. I got a lot of hits, and I wondered why she treated us so strictly then. I didn't like her way to make students better, and I didn't like her in person. But after the important exam in the third grade, my class had the most numbers of students who would be able to enter the best senior high schools. I realized what she did made us better than we could be. The other day, I read about an investment which was about how students think about teachers. There was an interesting result that most student think the teachers who give punishment are good teachers and the students would want them to be their own teachers instead of those who don't punish students. Students believe teachers who use sticks would make them reach their goal. I am a teacher now, and I truly believe that no kids will be good no matter in their behavior or in their grades without punishment. It is all about how we give the punishment in the right way and let the students know why we punish them. After all, we just want them to be responsible for what they have to do.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I think that rewarding students for learning can lead to better result than using punishment. Punishment may make students unhappy and scare, but rewarding students can make them do more hard to get the reward instead of afraid of punishment. Rewarding students has more benefits than using punishment. In one hand, overpunishment may cause physical or even psycological damage of student. It won't makes students do better next time but afraid of doing same work instead. And teachers which punish students should take the responsibilities too if they hurt students. Punishment isn't a proper way in teaching. In the other hand, teachers which reward students may make students do harder to get the reward. The student who gets the reward may be very happy. Others will do even harder to get the reward next time. Instead of using punishment, teachers which rewarding students don't have to take any responsibilities. both teachers and students can get what they want. And students can learn more and better in a happy environment. I think rewarding students is a better way than using punishment in teaching.

subject: HW1001
content: As far as I am concerned, I think to reward students for their good performances is the better way to help students learn. I believe that there is little use to punish students because the punishment may cause students to fear and feel stressed rather than spur them to learn. However, every students like compliments, in that praises make them feel the sense of achievement and make them feel confident. Take me for example, when I got a full score, my mother would give me additional allowances as a reward, and I could use the money to buy whatever I wanted. As a result, as long as I want something desirably, I will work hard to get good points, and I also know that my hard work will pay off. By rewarding students for learning can encourage students to learn and also help them take initiatives in their studies. Positive attitudes toward learning lead to better results absolutely. In addition, instead of forcing them to learn, rewarding students can let them learn the true-meaning of knowledge rather than just recite what they learn. Besides, rewarding them can make them realize that hard work is needed and that it will pay off as well. Well goes the proverb, "You will reap what you sow today." Thus students will be more willing to learn to reach success with happy learning and imaging their bright future.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, reward students for learning can lead to better results. The main reason I reject punishment is that teacher may be sued by student's parents. So, don't do that. Teacher's duty is that protect students not hurt them. According to education theory, reward is that give students who they want and punishment is that give what they dislike. By giving what they want, teacher can motivate students. But, punishment have some side effect, students will hate teacher and school and refuse go to school. Punishment will produce more and more education problems. There is a example, a high school teacher punished student, and the student felt be insulted, so he fight back. The result of the event, teacher and student sued each other. Punishment will not motivate any student but will bring more education and society problems. However, reward would motivate students and make benefits for our society.

subject: HW1001
content: How to teach students is really an important issue for teachers and parents nowadays. People always take this question seriously and argue against each other. In my opinion, I think teaching students with not only praises and patience would be a more effective way. Because there are less and less children these days, kids are always the single child in their family. Everything belongs to him. Parents give all of love to him. As a result, he does not like others to blame him for mistakes. If teachers use punishment to treat this child, he would do something even worse to fight against elders' advice. When I was an elementary school student, I had a special classmate. He always yelled to his parents and did lots of bad behaviors such as taking away others' chairs and making them fall to the ground. Therefore, he seldom got praises and love from elders except my patient teacher. She often talked with him in a friendly way. Everytime he did something bad, she just helped him finish it and did not scold him. Finally, he cried, saying lots of gratitude to my teacher. Since then, he had have been an excellent student, and all of us loved him. Teaching with love is not that difficult, but it does need plenty of time. Most of the students can be successful; however, teachers play an important role on them.

subject: HW1001
content: Some teachers and parents still believe that punishment is still the best way to teach students. The effects are quite good. After getting punishment, most of the students are tend to perform well on their study and behavior. However, some people doubt this idea; especially, they are doubt about the effect of pysical punishment. I have the same opinion with them. In my opinion, punishment is not as efficetive as they imagine. At the moment the students who get punishment will follow your rules because their are afraid to get another one. However, one day, when they grow up, they are no longer afraid of punishment. Therefore, they are no longer under your control. Thus, we need to find a more effective way to teach them. According to my opinion above, punishment is needed, but it needs to comes with other enspiration. Parents need to praise their kids when they perform well on studying so that the kids are willing to spend more time studying. Also, parents need to read more at home instead of watching TV. That is a good immitation for kids. Moreover, you may discuss the contents of books with them. Day by day, kids will find reading interesting. When kids have poor behavieor, they deserve punishment, but not pysical punishment. Parents need to teach them good manners and talk to them very often. Thus, pavents need to perform well at home as well. Remember, you are model of your kids. They will immitate all of your behavieors. In short, students deserve punishment to be controled. However, that is not totally effective way of teaching. Spend more time on them and talk to them will be the way to motivate them.

subject: HW1001
content: Well, what's my viewpoint about these two reports? In my opinion, I don't think it is a good way for teachers to use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior.
