Partly because I am a seniour high school student, I don't like to be punished and partly because I think students would be very sad if their teacher punished them to do well instead of praising them. Many teachers belive that, well goes a saying "Spared the road and spoiled the child." With the old saying goes, they would punish students to urge them to behave well. In my opinion, though there are adventages and disaventages between these two method, I think teachers who believe that rewarding students for learning is more effective. My reasons are as fallows. First of all, as a student, I think I would rather fallow what a kind teacher ask me to do than fallow what a mean teacher who punished me ask me to do. The more the teachers punished them, the more disobedient the students would be. In addition, I think students would behavior better through the praise of teachers. For example, my mother is a teacher, and she is always kind to her students. Once the students made errors, my mother never punish them. Instead of punishing, my mother always encourages them and praise them to behavior well. The students who are tought by my mother now behave better than before. Finally, I think teachers' encourageous is the pillar of students to learn well and behave well. The above mentioned that are my shallow opinions, but they stand for what I am thinking about now.

subject: HW1001
content: Traditional education believes punishment is more effective than rewarding, but nowaday it's a reverse situation. Punishment is indeed a quick and effective method to get in control with misbehavior students. Since students are normally afraid of getting scolded or spanked, they behave better after being punished. But as long as students couldn't truly understand why they were punished, they will keep making the same mistake again and again. On the other hand, rewarding provides a even better solution to controling students. Students are rewarded for instance, their well-behavior and improving grades. This make students focus on the positive things they've done right and are more willing to cotinue their efforts. Students will go all lengths and try their best to seek rewards and these agressive actions may lead to a better learning results and better behaviors etc. Rewarding is a comparatively effective way to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. It gives students better recognition of what to do and what not to do. Moreover, it provides the positive motivations for students to seek for the best and push themselves to the limit. Therefore, comparing to punishment, rewarding is defenitely the best method.

subject: HW1001
content: I think children needs to be encouraged. They are curious about almost everything they feel. They are pure and sensitive. The reasons they make mistakes are usually blamed for their innocence. They can't imagine how great of damages they can cause. So I think teachers should be patient with their students. They shouldn't be easily bored with their students. Teachers should wear a smile usually although sometime it's difficult to do. Teachers should try to get close to their students. If children are not afraid of you and like you, they will be controled easier. In my opinion, the punishment is the last method to use on the children. Once you punish a child, he or she will remember it for a very long time. Though you make him or her kick the bad habit temporarily, it just because they are scared. They can't understand the reason they get punished. So once they forget the pain, they are possible to make the same mistake. I have a sister who is three years younger than me. When we were young, I tried to teach her Chinese words. One time, an idea comes to my mind. I make a promise that if she recognizes every word I teach her, I will give her an award. The method works, she remembers the whole new words in a time which is shorter than any time I teach her. I was impressed and proud. And this experience makes me believe in rewarding is a better method than punishing.

subject: HW1001
content: It is common for teachers to use punishment and rewards to give feedback on students' behavior in classroom. Besides, these two ways own their advantages and disadvantages. However, in my opinion, I prefer the later one to the former one, and there are my reasons at the following composition. First, the effect of giving rewards lasts longer than using punishment. Pains on language or action abusement may work right away. Nontheless, in the long run, students will not see them seriously. The regret will be replaced by other things soon. On the contrast, acclaiming students' correct behavior brings continual positive effection to students, and they will bear teachers' encouragement for good. Second, rewards play more powerful roles than using punishment for students to pursue excellence. For example, if a teacher keeps scolding a student for his poor grades on schoolwork, this may end up being a learning obstacle and the student may give himself up on studying because he think he will not do good on examinations. Nevertheless, once a teacher uses rewards to encourage students, it will provide a mighty motivation to them to work even harder. Furthermore, teachers can discuss the forms of rewards with students, and I think it would be a positive and harmony communication between each side. In conclusion, giving rewards cannot be too emphasized. Therefore, these are my reason to agree rewards instead of punishment when teachers treat students.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, the rewarding students for learning is more effective. Most of students like to get reward, and no one wants their teachers to give them some punishment. I think the method of rewarding can motivate students to learn more and increase their performance in class. Besides, they are willing to try and learn, because they can get win-win suitation in their learning. One is their learning improved and they gain more confidence from their learning. I believe that not only teachers are pleased to see the result, also parents will feel happy to know their children perform well in their class.

subject: HW1001
content: In Taiwan, teachers use punishment seem normally of our generation, and in the elders' generations. But now, it is inapropriate when hurting students. I am of the opinion of punishment is more effective. Because students should do something to change theirself. Teachers can provide some way to punish student. And the most important is that punishment isn't equal to bat on the students or make the students feel guilty, sad or embarrased. When I was in junior high school, one of my classmate talking in class, and our teacher punish him by making him giving us a speech. The classmate can't give a good speech, and the only thing can he do is standing there, and keep quiet. From that time, the classmate of us never talking in the class again. Not all of the punishment are bad for students, on the other side, a good and also reasonable punishment is useable. One man can learn a good experience from mistakes and punishment, but can't learn anything from spoil love.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior by rewarding them can lead to better results than punishing them. If the students are old enough, they should have the ability to control themselves. If teachers still punish them to make them behave themselves, students may get upset and start to fight agaist the teachers by making more troubles. I am sure that it is not the teachers want when they punish their students. On the other hand, if teachers reward students who study very well and behave themselves, other students will try their best to do so in order to get the rewards as well. Students always do better when they are willing to do something. That way, students won't get unpleasant and the teachers get what they want. I am a high school student now. When I was in junior high school, my homeroom teacher used to make us behave well by punishing us. That really annoyed us, so we started to do bad things like throwing fruits and playing baseball in the classroom. We never did our teacher's punishment and we did our best to make her unsatisfied. Looking at her angry face, we feel like winners. In my second year in junior high school, we had another homeroom teacher. Instead of punishing us, she encouraged us and rewarded us when we did something good or got a good grade. As a result, we always put a lot of efforts on controling ourselves and studying hard. Students, especially teenagers want to be adults, so they expect others to treat them like grown-ups. If parents or teachers try to punish them to get to do something, it makes them feel like a children and they won't obey to their parents or teachers. To sum up, I think rewarding is better than punishing while teaching.

subject: HW1001
content: I support that teachers use proper punishment can motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. As a university student now, I have experienced the period of being punished. I could recall vividly that when I was a primary school student, I had once flunk my math test, because my mind was preoccupied with soup operas. I thought I could still ace it if I pulled the all nighter and cramed for it the night before the test. And the result was I got sixty-five points. As you could imagine, I was being punished. Besides, I also corrected all mistakes and rewrote each mistake for one hundred time. It was a horrifying nightmare for a little girl. From then on, in order to avoid being punished, I studied harder then ever to get good grades which could protect myself and satisfy the teacher. Besides the schoolwork and grades, it's important to educate children well and proper behavior and manners. The best way to let children know that such behaviors like stealing, cheating, getting into fights, and so on are not allowed is through punishment. Sometimes punishment can be considered the warning and the most direct way to have children know and tell how to behave. I will not deny the importance of rewarding students for learning. But how if students feel nothing of teachers' rewards when they grow older? Only by adequate punishments can lead to better result in the longrun. And students and children will one day realize what teachers had done for them and be gratful to who had ever blamed and punished them.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. There are two examples to support my thought. First, I will use the rewarding card system to my students. If they do good things or behave well, such as helping classmates to solve the homework or picking up the money and returning it back to the owner, I will sign my name on the card. If they collect ten of my signatures, I will give them a small gift to make them happy. In this way, they may learn to behave well day by day. The second one is praising them in the class. In general, people like to be praised. So, if students are praised in class, their self-esteem would raise and they would want to do more good things to get another chance of being praised in class. Therefore, students may also behave well gradually.
I think people are good in their natures, so if I have to teach them behave well, I will choose rewarding my students. After all, students are good in their natures in my mind.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I am for rewarding students for learning. By rewarding students, they can know where their advantages are and go on to improve themselves. Take myself for example, when I was in elementary school, I was too energetic so that sometimes I might chat with my friend in class. Everytime feeling my noise, my teacher always asked me to present what I say to the whole class, as long as my words were entertaining, my teacher always gave me a compliment and told me that talking is good, but it should be on the right time. So she asked me next time when I want to say something in the class, I should raise my hand first and share it to everyone. No one can't live without making a mistake. When students do something wrong, teachers should first notice them when is the right time the behavior should appear in a rewarding way, thus, they won't consider you as an opponent and are willing to listen to your advice.

subject: HW1001
content: According to one survey on happiness of students in Taiwan, it showed many students are not happy in school. One of the reasons is that most of students get low achievement in learning. Some of them are even afraid to go to school because of the fear of punishment from teachers. This phonomenon is worth our attention. Is punishment the only way to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior? In my opinion, there must be more methods working on students. It is obvious that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. No students love to learn under the pressure even though it did occur in our education. Students can learn better if they are encouraged to do so. It is not hard to find that many students lost their confidence in learning at school because of punishment. Take the children as example, when parents teach their kids, what will they do? Punishment or encouragement? I think parents will encourage their kids as possible as they can. Students need it, too. So, reward works better in education.

subject: HW1001
content: There are many methods that teachers arould the world use to improve the students' learning behavior. Some teachers claim that only by using punishment can students learn well. While others believe that encouraging students to learn new things is much better. In my opinion, as a freshman, I think rewarding students for learning can result in better results. Take me for an example, when I was in the elementary school, I behaved bad in grades. But everything changed until I met Miss Huang. Even though I did bad on learning, she often gave me great suggestion and encourged me to study harder. Because of her, I was willing to read books and began realizing the great knowledges in books. The most important thing of all, I gradually enjoyed the fun of learning. Even though she retired after I graduated from the school, the charming and friendly face still lingered in my mind. Now when I think of her, it always reminds me of the real purpose of studying and learning. It has a great influence on me when I stayed late in the midnight in order to enter a good university.

subject: HW1001
content: In the past, teachers are the emblem of absolute power. Pupils were required to obey all the instructors ordered and taught, with no defiance. However, the role of teachers has changed greatly. They start to befriend with students, learning from each other. Though some teachers still conventionally motivate their students to learn and correct their mischief via all kinds of punishments physically or psychologically, others root for encouraging those instructed by awards ranging from chocolate or candies for kids to praise for adolescent students. In my personal perspective, I strongly believe the latter will be more effective than the former. I will outline two reasons for my claim. Some teachers remain totalitarians, believing all-time supervision and slapping bottom can bring those naughty students to heel, but in vain. For me, punishment would force them to listen for only a while, and then everything returns. Besides, it will indirectly decimate students' ability to contemplate why they should be punished or spanked and what they have done wrong. But through communication and proper rewarding, the results will be intriguingly effective. Secondly, according to an article published in Time Magazine, spanking kids will only lead to more aggressive behavior. Thus, it is why I abominate those punishment-led teaching methods making students machines to obey, not human beings to create. Fortunately, the cult now seems to be on the track of what I have expected and preferred.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, it is using punishment that more effective than rewarding. Take myself as an example, when I was a child, I knew nothing about this world. I could reminisce it clearly that I had a bad behavior on taking any thing in my sight into my mouth, even if it was on the floor. Then, how could I know any hygienic knowledge! But my dad apparently did. He hit on my hand when this behavior was about to occur. Thus, on following days, when I'm going to take the things into my mouth, the punishment he given to me flashes into my mind, which reminds me it is not allowed. And I could not envisage that without his punishement, what man I am now Punishing students is the same, too. When a student behave bad, teacher can hit on his hand. Evidently, the pain will go with him ever after, which reminds him of not-allowed behavior. Actually, he might hate you then. But after his growing up and knowing the context of this incident, he's likely to thank you all of his life! As a good teacher, how can you spare the stick!

subject: HW1001
content: I consent to the method that teachers use punishment to teach students what' right and what's wrong. Punishments do physical and mental harms to students and that are what failure results in. When students are naughty in school they recieve punishments and when they behave bad in the society, they undergo miserable failure. Thus, punishments bring the cruel experiences of failure to students earlier, so that this painful memories can inscribe in their mind. Then, the next time they want to do bad things which the social morality couldn't bear, the experiences of being punished remind them, and they will stop doing bad things. I had a classmate, Joe, in my junior high school year who was notorious for his violence to my classmates. In the first grade, my teacher gave him compliments or, sometimes, little reward like movie tickets, when he got along with my classmates well. However, when my teacher forgot to give him movie tickets, he began to swear at the teacher and punched my classmates to release his anger. In the second grade, another teacher who was strict and mean. A time, after Joe hit my classmates as usual, the new teacher came and hit Joe with a wooden stick. The punching sound was and so was the screaming from Joe that students from other class came and looked. After that, Joe never hit any one, he was afraid of the teacher, so as any punishments in the society. In conclusion, punishments have an permanent effect to one person, but rewards won't. Because no one gives you rewards after you leave school. However, the law and failure will always punish you when you behave bad.

subject: HW1001
content: Whether punishment is effective has long been an issue that bothered all the teachers in the world. Not only teachers, most parents are desired to know what is the best method to teach their own children. In my opinion, I agree more about rewarding students than punishing them. As a student in Taiwan almost everyone has the experience of being punished by teacher for all kinds of reasons such as being late for school, handing in the homework after the deadline, and maybe the more serious-cheating on the exam. My junior high teacher used to punish us by hitting us on the palm when we got a bad grade in the test. The result is everyone studied hard to avoid being hit instead of getting more knowledge-we studied for the teacher instead of ourselves. And we forgot them right after the exam. Though many teachers in Taiwan are still use the traditional method to teach student, I want to suggest them that rewarding is more effectiving than punishment!

subject: HW1001
content: An arguement that teachers should punish students or reward is always being discussed in our society. Some people say that punishment is a good method to lead children on the right way, while others think rewarding is exactly the best educating way. In my opinion, I think rewarding is much better than punishing. If teachers often reward their students in the learning process, it may undoubtedly arouse students' learning interest. Children will be aggressive in courses and classes. On the other hand, if teachers give the students anything but reward and encouragement, children may feel discouraged and that their performance is so terrible that they just can get punishment. Gradually, they feel frustrated and then they grow to hate learning, even their teachers. My mother always encourage me whether I achieve my goal or fail. Last time, I failed my math montly test, and I was really upset. When I was back home, I told my mom the truth. Beyond my expectation, my mom didn't scold at me but give me a big hug. I soon bursted into tears. I realized my mom trust me. She thought I studied hard. So I set a goal that I would be more active in learning and cautious in the following tests for meeting not only Mom's expectation but mine. In conclusion, children always learn from mistakes, so don't blame at them when they do mistakes. Parents and teachers should teach them how to do it and encourage them to overcome the challenges by themselves.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, education is a profession. And how to use punishment is one of the most difficult and subtle skills in it. I think in a classroom a teacher can properly use some kind of punishment for two main purposes: the first is to impress the mistake maker that s/he has done something wrong; the second: there are rules that need to be obeyed and it has to have discipline in the class. However, those student who can face and honestly admit their faults should be forgiven. And teachers should not punish students for the mistakes in their homework and poor academic performances. I oppose to corporal punishment, because it implies violence, and violence could become severer and severer. One of the most serious consequences is corporal punishment could be a cycle, from person to person, from generation to generation. One of the most obvious examples about corporal punishment in our society is the beating to the children in families and to the subordinate soldiers in the military. Because such a punishment is connived, so such a problem still persits today. Finally, I strongly agree to the reward method. Because in the method, students are valued and respected. That is something everybody loves.

subject: HW1001
content: The problems of using punishment to motivate students to learn or rewarding them has existed for many years. As far as I am concerned, rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. The above is the reason why I say so. First of all, I think that using punishment or tending to control students will make them feel uncomfortable and unhappy. Only by punishing students can not let them learn things; on contrary, it may make students hate to study or doing bad things in purpose. However, if teachers change their way to treat students, the situation will become different. Take me for example, my English teacher always encourage students to express our opinions. No matter what we say, she will praise us first for our bravely expression. As a result, all students in her class will automatically express our ideas instead of being called by teacher to answer questions one by one. This is a good example to prove that rewarding students for learning is better than punishing them or try to control their behavior. In conclusion, I think teachers should change their ways to teach students instead of complaining how bad students are or punishing them. And just remember that a praise or compliment can sometimes change students' concept and encourage them to be better or even change their life.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I think it is more effective to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior through punishment. Judging from our society, people tends to be affraid of things which may hurt them. Think about your parents who grew up in the generation which punishment was often used in the school. They have recieved more messages about what should do and what shouldn't do when being punished. For another example, try to recall your childhood in the school. Everytime when you were late to hand in your homework, teacher would ask you to do things such as clean the floor or do some "exercises". Next time, you would be able to hand in your homework in time. If teacher gives candies to students who handed in their homework on time instead of punishing those who didn't do so, more and more students would be late to hand in their homework. Therefore, in my opinion, I think punishment is quit important when teaching students.

subject: HW1001
content: Traditionally, it was believed that using punishment was the best way to motivate students to learn and control their behavior. For many ordinary people, their memories of their school lives were filled with the vivid image of being punished by their strict teacher. As the proverb goes "There is no success without punishment. " many parents and teachers deeply believed in this rule; however, the concept has changed dramatically as many experts found out it was more effective by rewarding students for their behavior. Studies have shown that by praising students for what they have done rather than punishing them for their mistakes can motivate student in a more effective way to perform better. Besides, it is more comfortable to listen to nice words than negative ones. For instance, if a teacher praise his students for his neat handwriting, as a result, the student would be likely to hand in his assignments with a more beautiful handwriting next time as he knows that his teacher appreaciate the way he writes. In my opinion, praising others is the most powerful way to change a person tremendously. Hearing negative words only leads to a worser results. To sum up, it is always a best way to reward students.

subject: HW1001
content: When I was a high school student, my teacher used punishment to push us to learn. Some of my classmates got high progress, and some of them gave up learning for escaping high pressure. Now I am a teacher at school, and I try two methods in my class. In my research, the diversed effects are acted on different students. For active students, they accept punishments when they don't do well. They push themself to study for avoiding punishment. Contrast to students under average level, they aren't confident in learning new things. They need more time to understand everything so that I teach them in paticience and make clear direction step by step. After reaching their study goal, I reward them with praise or some prices to build up their confidence, and they could study in a relax environment with low pressure. This discovery is useful in English class. The two teaching methods are used by students' learning styles. No matter which method is effective, the best one is to respond to students' need.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion punishment and reward are both very important. A good teacher should always know when it's right to punish or reward a student. I can still remember when I was little, my math teacher always punish me when I don't get a good grade on my math exam, then I became very afraid to math, so I started to hate math and doesn't practice it any more, soon my math grade was worse then before. So my mom decided to find a new teacher for me. The new teacher punishes me only when I'm not paying attendtion in class, but most of the time when my grade has improved she buys me chocolate chip cookies as a reward. And because I always want the reward, I study math very hard, soon I started to like math again and my grades improved very quickly. I think teachers should only punish student when they do something wrong or when they have a bad behavior instead of punishing them everytime, even when they are doing something correct. And some parents should learn how to punish their childern when they make a big mistake, like stealing! If you keep rewarding them they will think that their doing the right thing, so I think both punishment and reward are very important, if you always reward your children and never punish, you'll have a spoiled child very soon!

subject: HW1001
content: You may see lots of news on TV about teachers punish their student by physical punishment. Physical punishment is used commonly at Taiwanese schools, especially at elementary schools and junior high schools. In fact, I am also one of the victims. Therefore, I think that rewarding is more efficient than the punishment. Following are some reasons that I think rewarding is better than the punishment when teaching students no matter on their learning or controlling their behaviors. First, I believe that students will understand whether what they have done is right or not by rewarding. They must be willing to listen to what teachers if teachers reward them instead of punishment. For example, If teachers always teach them by punishment, those students do not make mistakes just because they are afraid of being punished. Therefore, it is one of my opinions that the rewarding is more efficient. Second, students will not learn better or get high scores on exams by the punishment. I think that they will learn and study on their own by the moment that they want to do. Thus, it is no use if teachers ask them for studying by punishment. In this way, they will be furious and reluctant to study, and even hate to study. Take me for example. I do not like my parents and teachers punish me just because I get a poor grade on tests or sometimes I do not study but play TV games. I will tell them that I just need to take a break, and I will continue to study after relaxing. Consequently, I think the rewarding is better and more efficient than the punishment when teaching students. Students will not perform better on tests by the method of punishment. In contrast, they do perform better on the method of rewarding just because this method will make them be willing to study and learn, not the fears by punishment to make them do so.

subject: HW1001
content: In recent news, we can see many reports about the teachers using excessive punishments to their students. These events arouse two different opinions in the society. Some people think teachers should teach in a peaceful way, while others prefer that the punishments are essential. As far as I am concerned, I support the teacher teach students by rewarding instead of blaming. There are some reasons as follows why I agree it. First, students can find their interests in learning. If teachers keep encouraging their students, the students will feel the joy of learning and they can quickly find what they major in. second, students can have brave and optimistic mind when facing difficulties. As we all know, childhood is an important time of people, so the time at school may have a big impact on one's future. Rewards can help the students to reduce the feelings of uncertainty and cultivate their confidence. Third, free learning makes students to think of more ideas. Special and unique thoughs are always come from an unconstrained situation or environment. To sum up, I agree the students can lead to better results by teaching with rewards. In this way, there may be more creations and elites generated in the society.

subject: HW1001
content: Nowadays in Taiwan what bothers teachers the most in teaching is how to make their teaching more effective. In other words, teachers are concerned about which teaching method can really help their students learn well and get good grades on tests. In my opinions, I believe that appropriate punishment and rewarding can both motivate students to have a better performance in learning. When it comes to punishment, people may think of physical punishment. Though I agree with using punishment, physical punishment will definitely be my last choice. There are plenty of ways to punish your students without hurting them physically and spiritually. Take me for example, if my students don't behave in class, they are not allowed to play during the break time. Also, they need to use the ten-minute break to memorize some new vocabulary. Besides, if they are really out of control in class, I will ask them to stand up for a while until they are able to answer my pop-out questions. Therefore, I don't agree with any physical punishment, but I use some other ways to make them behave in the classroom. I love to reward my students any time when they behave well or get good grades on exams. Students deserve encouragement and rewarding for their good performances and behaviors. In order to build up their good character, I always encourage my students to help one another with learning by giving them some drinks, such as buble tea once in a while. In addition, they can participate in some fun outdoor activities with me (approved by their parents) if they do well on their tests. To sum up, I believe that the most efficient way to motivate students to learn is to use punishment and to reward students at the same time. Too much punishment may discourage them while too much rewarding may spoil students. So the best way to teach your students is to make good use of both punishment and rewarding.

subject: HW1001
content: Everyone desires to be praised, trusted and loved, thus I think rewarding is more effective than punishment on students. Though many people think negative enforcements like regulations and laws were the easiest way for people to behave well, people won't know what to do if encouragment is ignored. For students who are growing up and learning to perform well at school, positive enforcement in front of their classmates and friends can make them feel respected, accepted and happy to learn. Last year, I was the tutor of one junior high school student. Because I could easily focus on my school work, I took his concentration for granted. However, it's not that case. My student easily "got lost" on his math textbook; also he seldom finished the assignment. At first, I made the regulation: unfinishment of one page counted for no TV and no PS2 playing of one hour. It worked-but only once! Thus, I couldn't help but use the education of love: finishment of one page counted for extra leisure time of one half hour plus one cup of drink-his favorite boba milk tea. To my surprise, it worked! From then on, I deeply believe rewarding is the best policy of teaching boring math.

subject: HW1001
content: Thanks to the technology of all sorts, over the past few decades, our life has become so convenient and so enjoyable. However, students have started to become lazy and reluctant to study, for the life was too easy. As a result, teachers have started to take actions to motivate students to study. Some teachers punish students if they get poor grades, thinking that they would study harder for the next exam. On the contrary, others reward students for getting good grades, thinking that they would study as hard as possible to get the reward once again. As far as I am concerned, rewarding would be a better method to motivate the students. Take my bosom friend, Jackson, as an example: When he was in junior high, he often got poor grades, but his home room teacher kept encouraging him instead of punishing him. By degrees, he started to study harder and harder; eventually, he entered Kaohsiung senior high school, which is the best high school in Kaohsiung. When it comes to motivating students, rewarding would be the most appropriate method. I sincerely hope that teachers who punish students can cease it, and start thinking about how to reward their students.

subject: HW1001
content: To be frank, my junior high school teacher motivated us to elaborate our studying by utilizeing the punishment, for example scolding us for not accompling assignments; being extremely strict, and only utilizing the "stick" policy. As a consequence, I did study blow-by-blow in class and absob myself in studying; however, I was suffering from the colossal pressure from her and loathe going to school every single day. On the contrary, in high school, teachers permit us to study on our own, which requires highly self-control. With less tests and no more frightening sticks, I've finally taste the flavor of the "carrot". To sum up, as a student experiencing both method of teaching, I acknowledge I like the latter better; however, lacking of the intensive stress and tense test agenda, I surprisingly commence to lust for the former way back! After deeply pondering, I realize it's imperative to combine both. Only taking drastic measures to students is far from mercy; nevertheless, abandoning students to study all by themselves is not a brilliant way, either. I assume teachers nowadays should come up with a method which can strike a balence, and that will absolutely be the most effective way of all time.

subject: HW1001
content: In Taiwan, punishing students is still controversial at different fields. Some experts believe it's the best way to motivate and inspire students to learn and behave, the others contend rewarding is the best way. As far as I'm concerned, I'm in favor of rewarding students. Here are two reasons below: First, students can achieve greater sence of success. Under relaxing situation with no pressure, they can learn to express their ideas and creativity with free will through providing incentive. Every child has unique talent of their own. When we encourge them instead scolding, they will know what their potencial are earlier than the others and set their life goal. Second, students will be more confident and happier. Some social problems rise from people childhood. Rewarding can build children's confidence on the positive way in their life. Ray Charles was blind after he got a illness. His mom build him up by rewarding and inspiring during his childhood. So that he became one of the greatest jazz musician. Students are our future hope and treasure in our country. Rewarding can help them achieve success with strong confidence.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opion, I think rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. Many teachers like to punish students when they do something wrong or have bad grade on tests. They think it is a good way to motivate students working hard on their study, because many students are afraid of taking punishement. But sometimes teachers are too stern to the students just because they don't get good grades on their tests. And after punishing many times, some students will lose their confidence on learning, even start to skip classes. So, I think teachers should reward students rather than punishing them. When I was in elementary school, I always got poor grade on English. My mother was worried that I couldn't catch up the class, so she decided to sent me to an English cram school. I was scared because I had to speak English to communicate with teachers and classmates. In first day, I didn't say a word to my English teacher whatever he asked. However, my English teacher is a kind man, he encouraged me to interact with the students and always made compliment on me when I got good grade on quizs. Futhermore, he rewarded students not only on study, but also their behavior. Gradually, I built up the confidence on learning English. Even my mother was surprised my progress. To sum up, as a student, I think rewarding students is a better way to motivate students instead of punishing them all the time.

subject: HW1001
content: People in many countries emphasize education, and the most important people in these countries for education are teachers. There are a lot of methods for teachers to teach their students. Some of them punish their students for motivating them but some reward their students for better results. I prefer punishing to rewarding. When the teacher uses punishment, the student will realize that he must do better next time. For example, when I was young I learned the violin. At first, my first teacher told me that I will get some rewards if I play well. For a period of time, I did not progress, because I knew that if I spend more time practicing my fingers will be very hurt. When I changed to another teacher who may punish me then I knew that it may be more pain if I don't play well. After two years, I got the champion in the competition with people from many places in Taiwan. Maybe it hurts when the teacher uses punishment, however, to me using punishments is still the best method to motivate students effectively.

subject: HW1001
content: There are great differences between the teaching methods during the past few years. In the past, most teachers chose to punish students to control their behavior. However, in my opinion, it would be better to reward students for learning. Of course, severe punishment and harsh scolding would be more effective than rewarding. Nevertheless, the result of it often ends up with a tragedy. Students don't know why they study, and they just follow teachers' advice. This way usually kills the curiosity and interest of students and does great damage to their minds. On the other hand, if we reward students instead of punishment, they would find their interest in some subjects. What's more, students can regain their confidence and have their motivation for learning. My sister is a very good example. My parents always scolded her and made she feel very frastrated. Under such great pressure, my sister could neither get out of depression nor have a good grade. If my parents could replace their punishment with rewarding, I am sure that my sister would be happier and perform better in academic performance. In conclusion, I am of the opinion that taking care of students with love and rewarding. Students would find out their interests and urge themselves to lead a colorful lives in this way. Only with patient and love can we create a better tomorrow for our educational system.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. When I was child, my parents never put pressure on my study. But they rewarded me if I got good grades. Therefore, I felt relaxed when I was studying because of no pressure. Moreover, I felt cheerful because I knew that I would receive some presents from my parents after working hard. Sometimes, I would discuss the math problems with my father or appreciate literature with my mother. It is a good memory. In the end, the consequence was brilliant, I performed well in almost every subject, and my relationship with my parents is wonderful. Meanwhile, I have learned to study by my own motivative instead of being forced to. However, if teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and control their behavior, students will feel scared, sad and angry. These emotions will make them be scared of making mistakes and they will lose their courage to face difficulties. On the contry, rewarding students, like giving water to flower, can bring hopes to students. Then, they will feel confident and be willing to try something difficult instead of giving up in the beggining. I, as a student in Taiwan, know that teachers still punish students sometimes. Meanwhile, our educational system is not perfect at all. I wish I can see all students study in the happy learning enviroment and enjoy their childhood.

subject: HW1001
content: In my opinion, rewarding students is more effective than punishing them. Students are sometimes lazy learning and not well-behaved. But they are only kids. All people love to be encouraged, especially the young kids. If a teacher punish a student, the student might gets improving on the fault. On the other hand, the student may be afraid of learning or making mistakes. At last, he will just wants to get away from the teacher or the subject. I like to give my students stamps when they answer my questions or behave well and they can change some gifts with their stamps. That means, the more stamps you get, the more gifts are able to obtain. Besides, oral encourgements are useful as well. The students are trying their best to get the teacher's attention in class and studying harder to get good grades. I found smiles on their faces and in their shining eyes. They love to learn, not forced to learn. A good teacher inspires the students instead of putting terrible stress on them. So, I strongly agree with that it is more effective for a teacher to reward the students.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the 21st century, the birth ratio becomes lower and lower on account of various reasons. Therefore, parents pay more attention to their cherished children. I believe rewarding is more efficient than punishment regarding coping with education.
In my opinion, every kid is unique. A well-qualified teacher is supposed to observe the indiviual difference instead of ruling them by strict regulations. If the teachers are likely to be patient with their students, they will seize more concepts about how to transform kids' inadequate behaviors into sufficient performance. It's easier to limit or estimate poorly-improved students. When a nice teacher opens a bright window for these kids, they will be rescued and their life will start a new page.
After students can feel teacher's love, a professional teacher ought to set upper expectations for them. By pursuing and reaching the expectations step by step, kids are motivated to improve obviously. It's also a great honor to witness students' progress in behaviors and academic achievements.
As a teacher, don't be shy to show your enthusiasm. Educational caltivaters are optimistic about any possibilities on the students. Ging more rewarding, gaining more positive feedback. Teachers contribute to encouraging more confident students so that our country will be more competitive. Pass the power to every family; furthermore, more parents will cooperate with teachers. Our society will be filled with more energy. Living in a better-develepoed and peaceful society is pleasant, isn't it?

subject: HW1001
content:
Because we are increasingly effectted by Western cultures, our traditional education way also changed. Many parents begin not to punish their children, but in a "love way" to teach them when their children do something wrong. But I think some punishments are nessassary.
When I went to some public occassion, I found that there were many children annoying others and they also spoke to adults without polites. Because their parents thought that punishing them was not a perfect way to educate their children, they should teach their children some lessons and make them know what are right or fault. But if the children are so young that they can't know the lessons, I think punishments are important in this situation. It can make them understand that they can't do that again next time.
If the children grow up, maybe the parents can stop the punishments. Because they are adolescens, they are big enough to think about what they did and distinguish what's wrong. In this time, parents should do commucation with their children, and teach them some lessons they should know in their life.
Actually, my mom teach me in these ways. When I was small, I was afraid of her punishment so I wasn't going to do bad things. When I grew up, I knew that I should do what I should do and disscussed with my parents. I'm thankful for that I grew up in this way, so I was happy and satisfied myself now.

subject: HW1001
content:
Everyone had been punished by teacher when we were still in school, and teachers' have no exception. Compared with reward, punishment is more efficient and powerful to manage a group following what you asked for.
Following what you're saying efficiently is what a teacher always dream of. It's not only easy but also efficient! So verbal or coporal punishment had became their rulling tools.
For example, cheating on the test is not availible. To know why is a long journey, and kids don't care about what cheating do harm to them. At the moment, we take the shortcut-not to explain "why" but to let them know "this is prohibited." And this is how we punish students.
Example mentioned above tells how efficient to use fear of students. After all, you can't just punish and do nothing! It's important to let them know why it can't be acceptable. So as a tool, I vote for punishment as a permently efficient one.

subject: HW1001
content:
During your school time, have you ever been punished because you didn't get a good score? How miserable it is when teaching becomes violence. In my opinion, rewarding student for learning will be the better choice.
That many students don't like to learn is that they don't understand how happy learning a thing is, so in order to make them feel happy when studying, we can set a goal which is not too high so that they can reach the goal and get the prize; moreover, for the purpose of getting the prize, students may compete each othe positively, which can also raise their scores.
However, some people may argue that if teachers don't push the students to learn or to study, they never open the text books and study it. Nevertheless, teaching by punishment only make studen'ts hate learning more. That we should know why students don't want to study or learn is the question we have to figure out.
In conclusion, It's very important for students to feel happy when they are learning. Pushing, threatening and even forcing students to study are not good ways because they only have the students scared of learning. Finally, except punishments, we still have a wide various decision to make.

subject: HW1001
content:
I think it is obvious that rewarding students for learning can lead them to control their behavior. Because when a teacher punish a student for his/her mistakes, the student will think how to do these things without being seen rather than not to do these things. In contrast, when a teacher encourage a student to do something good and reward him/her after he/she does that, the student will be very happy and confident. Then, he/she will think it is right to do what the teacher hopes him/her to do.
Taking dog training for example. In my school, my club's job is to take care of the school dogs (the dogs lived in my school for a long time). To make them become more popular in my school, the other club members and I trained them to sit, shake hands and stop barking. We always use cookies as a reward to train them and it does make good effects. However, the school dogs are sometimes too excited that they only want to play with us, so we have nothing to do but to yell at them. When we do this, they will be affraid of us and run away as fast as they can, or start to bark and sometimes even want to bite us. Therefore, I think it is definitely wrong to teach a student by punishing him/her to force him/her doing what he/she should do.

subject: HW1001
content:
I'm convinced that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results, and it should be done as early as possible in a students' life.
When punished, kids may be scared, hurt or even start to dislike the teachers but they not necessarily learn lessons. All they learn is that the teachers don't like them because they are bad kids; but still, they don't understand why the behavior should be forbidden. On the contrary, when rewarded, kids can feel trust from the teachers and become more confident. Once they make mistakes, they don't run away from the teachers with fear and the teachers can then explain what they have done wrong. As a result of the nice atmosphere between the teachers and the students, the students not only avoid making the same mistake but also take interest in learning.
Jim was my classmate in the elementary school. He was chobby, so everyone made fun of him; that's why he was violent and hated going to school. Fortunately, my homeroom teacher, Mrs. Chen kept encouraging him with all kinds of rewards. As time went by, Jim became a straight-A student and remained close with Mrs. Chen to this day. The story is why I'm in favor of rewarding students instead of punishing them.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, students should be punished or not becomes a serious issue we have to think about. The news that teachers being sued because of punishing or scoling students have been seen everywhere whenever you turn on the television. Is it necessary that teachers should reward students more instead of punishment?
As far as I am concerned, I don't agree that punishment needs to be totally canceled. Take myself for example. I have my own experience being punished. I was hit by "A hand of love", which was used to punished students among many teachers; what's more, in front of all my classmates. I got that because I was irritated and insulted my classmate. I would never forget my very first time being punished. However, looking on the bright side, it will always remind me to be nice to everyone when I think about it.
On the other hand, rewarding is like hanging a carrot in front of a dunkey. It can provide motion for students to improve themselves. Rewarding, or even a simple praising, will make students more confident about themselves, which is especially Taiwanese students are lack of.
Needless to say, both punishment and rewarding have to be appropriate. Over punishment to student might make them afraid of going school or changing themselves, yet too much rewarding might make students "too confident". Hence, finding the balance between punishment and rewarding is what we should learn about.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers motivate students to learn and to control their behavior by using punishment. However, other teachers believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, the better and more effective way is rewarding.
Using punishment is not an appropriate and effective way to motivate students to learn and control their behaviors. The reason why it's not a good idea is punishment brings fears to the students. It may also make students to think that learning is not interesting. On the other hand, rewarding students can encourage them to learn and behave well. Take my 11-year-old cousin for example. When she was in the third year of elementary school, she used to think learning was not interesting because when her teachers punished her when she got poor grades. This made her think that if she had studied hard, she would not have been punished. However, now, she thinks that learning is interesting and is willing to learn. Her teacher praises her and rewards her when she performs well. This makes her to be an active learner.
Rewarding students is better and more effective than punishing them as a way to motivate them to learn and control their behavior.

subject: HW1001
content:
The way of teaching our students plays an important role in education. The elders believe that using corporal punishment can make children much better. However, new generation seemingly doesn't agree this point. From my perspective, to be honest, punishment results in great achievement to some extent. But it also kills the feelings of joy in learning. Therefore, I prefer to reward as well as encourage students rather than scold them just due to low grades. When students fail the exams or do mistakes, we should guide and help them find the right direction in life so that they may feel better and then be willing to correct the behavior.
The memory that I got a zero on my test has never faded away in my mind. At that time, fear was creeping on my spine. I thought the teacher was about to punish me immediately. Nevertheless, he didn't hit me. Instead, he encouraged me with a kind of soft voice which made me look on the bright side in my life. After that event, I tried my best to achieve the goal. Much to my happiness, I have brilliant performance in my field. No matter what other people think about this issue, I still credit my success to rewarding method to teach students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Different teacher has different rules for students. Some teachers use physical punishment to motivate students to lean and some use reward to lead students to better results. In my opinion, I think that rewarding students for learning is much more effective than using punishment for two reasons.
First, giving positive reward can make students have a sense of achievement. If they are praised by the teacher, they will have the motivation to do better next time. Take myself as an example, when I was in my senior high, I got the second place in my study and my teacher gave me a little present and praised me in front of the whole class. I felt very happy and confident at that time; therefore, I studied much more harder and got the first place in the next semester.
Second, using punishment might leave bad impression to the students and some students would feel frustrated. Because no one like to be punished, it would only make them feel afraid or hate the teachers. Use my own experience as well, when I was in junior high, our science teacher used to do physical punishment to those students who fail the test. I was one of them because I really don't like science and did a bad job. However, after being punished, I didn't improve the next time. I still hate science and even the teacher. Therefore, using punishment would not gain my interest in the subject. It would only make me feel the hate to the teacher.
In short, based on the two reasons that I mentioned, I believe that rewarding students is much more effective than punishing students because no one like to be hurt and using positive reward can make student have a sense of achievement.

subject: HW1001
content:
Years ago in Taiwan, some teachers used to punish students in order to motivate them or control their behavior. Nowadays, more and more teachers reward the students for behaving well.
In my opinion, I think that it's more effective to reward the students rather than punishing them. Some students who behave badly, though being punished by their teachers, don't seem to behave well. Other bad students, who were rewarded due to some of their good behavior, would often change into good students.
Just like my junior high school classmates, one of the boys who was naughty, was often punished by the teachers. In spite of being punished, he hadn't changed for all three years, and kept on to be naughty after he graduated. Another student from the next class was totally a bad student, but his teacher didn't punish him. Instead, the teacher often rewarded him for some good behavior. In the end, he became a good student and was rewarded during the graduation ceremony. To everyone's surprise, he even entered the best school in Kaoshiung!
Because of those examples, I deeply believe that it's more effective to rewarded students than to punish them, and I'm really glad that there are some laws against punishing students in Taiwan.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are many ways to motivate students to learn and control their behavior. Some use punishment, others choose to reward.
Yet both of the methods seem to reach the purpose of getting students to behave and study harder, I would choose the latter one if I were a teacher.
Since punishment is sometimes cruel and unacceptable, rewards sound so friendly to many of us. If we get real great scores or do some great effort at school, we may be rewarded with scholarship or get praised by people, and they might say, "Keep the great job!" if you really hate to do chores but your mom made you do it, you will probably feel unhappy. However, after you cleaned up the mess and you actually did well, your mom took out a piece of cake from the fridge as a reward and would say, "It isn't that hard, huh?"
In my opinion, punishment is just like the law. It is something that you're afraid of, and wish to keep yourself away from breaking. On the other hand, rewards make people feel confident and get them motivated in a good way.

subject: HW1001
content:
We often see in newspapers, that some teachers and students have difficulty in accepting the way each other behaves. Teachers think that students don't respect them and are rude to them, and students think that the teachers don't treat them well and picks on them. The ways of motivating students to study often leads to disagreements between teachers, students, and even parents.
There are pros and cons in both ways of motivating-punishing and rewarding. If you use punishments on students they would probably dislike you very much, but it is effective indeed sometimes, or maybe it will cause other problems. Some students (expecailly teenagers) get angry when they are punished, and they do things the opposite ways you want them to.
On the other hand, rewarding has both good sides and bad sides, too. Students like rewarding teachers, but they soon will do nothing unless they are rewarded. They are also picky about the prizes, and they won't react to prizes they don't want.
My opinion is that we should use both. Students should be rewarded if they do well on studying but also punished if their atitude is bad. This way, students have a goal to study for, and they also won't have a bad atitude if they don't like the prize.
Teaching ways are very important for students. If the teacher teaches well and the classes are interesting, students would naturally want to learn more. So, is punishing or rewarding really so important?

subject: HW1001
content:
Using punishment in education is really terrible. I myself am the victim of this kind of teaching method, and the memory is just too horrible to recall. I was only fourteen years old when I faced a serious punishment given by my teacher. It was only because I got eighty in an English quiz. The teacher thought that I should have got one hundred in "such a small quiz." My hands were hit violently by a wooden rule and thus have difficulty to write anything. The punishment did work, I strove to get better score in order to avoid the punishment. But just like other students being afraid of punishment, since then I have viewed the subject as an enemy till now. I just hate it.
Elder people often consider that "No pain, nogain." so that physical punishment is also a kind of "pain" we should suffer. But why? The method leaves more and more wounds on our hearts and sometimes even triggers conflicts between students and teachers. It's time for everyone to leave the prejudice behind.
On the other hand, what about giving students awards instead of a wooden rule or a belt (for punishments)? My classmates in senior high school can prove that the method is, without a doubt, useful. One of my friends, Kelly, had a serious problem in counting things. And of course, she got poor grades on math exam and felt depressed. What our teacher did was to give her a hand. She spent a lot of time staying with Kelly after school to solve the problem and encouraged her that counting things is just a piece of cake. Kelly also worked hard to overcome the problem. In the end, everyone was surprised to know that the math teacher praised Kelly for her improvement. She passed all the quiz of the month and strived to catch up with other students. Kelly now enjoys solving math questions with us.
Physical punishment should be no longer avaiable, for that it creates negative thoughts in students' mind. In the future, awarding students will be a better choice for the teachers, so that students won't be afraid to go to school and learn.

subject: HW1001
content:
In mordern times, teachers don't use punishment to treat their students. They use their patience to teach students and give them more chances to fix their bad behavior. But rewarding students is more useful than punishing them? It is a good question which we should figure out.
In my opinion, punishing is a better way to let the students learn a lesson. Rewarding them when they fix the wrong things they had done can't give them a lesson. The students would forget it soon and do the same things again. So, the best way to treat students is not only punishing but also rewarding. For example, teachers should punish a student when he broke a window, but after he apologized and learned a lesson, the teacher could encourage him.
To me, I have a bad memory when I was in junior high school, our class always made lots of trobles. At first, our teacher tought us not to play such bad tricks to others, but we didn't listen. We just kept doing those things and didn't obey the school rules. One day, our teacher got nearly insane to us, because we had thrown a bottle that was full of water from third floor, and hit a classmate. Then the teacher took out a stick and ordered us stand in line and hit us one by one. After that terrible incident, we have learned an impressive lesson-we should not do anything that is banned from school rules.

subject: HW1001
content:
Actually, I do not think using punishment to motivate students to learn or to control their behavior is a good idea. Maybe punishment can enhance students' motivation in learning, but that kind of improvement only remains a short time. Students just simply do not want to be punished; they are not studying for their own good. Thus, while punishment will probably result in a high-pressure learning, I prefer using encouragement to motivate students in learning.
In the first grade of my little brother's junior high school, I taught him English. At first, if my brother did bad on his school's tests, I would punish him by scolding or ask him to copy the content in the text for more than ten times. During the time, my brother's learning results were in fact not bad. Until one day, my poor little brother cried to my parents and said he was unhappy very much and even hated me! Since then, I realized using punishment to force a student to learn would not only break the nice relationship therebetween but also make a student lose his real interest in learning.
When I started rewarding my brother for learning, his score in English still keeps outstanding. In addition, our relationship becomes close. He does not think learning English is a painful task. Even better, he volunteers to raise questions once he does not understand. Therefore in my opinion I think rewarding students for learning is more effective.

subject: HW1001
content:
I believe either teachers punish students or reward them, there is only a destination-they don't want students to go astray but hope them to become great person in the future.
In my point of view, punishment is usually more effective and essential. It not only lets students know they are doing the not appropriate things but also deletes their guts from making the same mistake again. But, punishment has to be when enough is enough. Over-reacting often causes children's to bleed and damages teachers' reputation immediately.
Take me for instance, I was not an active kid in the age of eleven. Then I was learning English in the cram school. The teacher there was ever strict, if I didn't hand in my homework punctually, I would get caned. It turned out that I was so naive at the thought of finishing half of homework that I definitely won't get caught. As teacher found out what I did, she was mad, and punished me. But, she told me why she had to do this and promised me if I finish all my homework she won't treat me like this anymore. After that, I always hand in mine first and progress a lot. And, that is what I learn from punishment. Like my teacher always says-No punishment no growth. I totally believe in this, and that's why I grow so much after eleven.

subject: HW1001
content:
In this modern age, as our technology and living standard improve, the competition around the world is becoming more and more intensive. Therefore, Taiwanese students have to make more effort to cultivate their ability to compare with the countless top students all over the world.
In order to make students study harder, many teachers choose to use punishments to motivate students, while others prefer to reward them instead. In my opinion, I don't agree with those who are prone to punishments because I think that it may be effective in a short time; however, once the students can't stand it anymore and gather to rebel, there will probably be much more serious problems waiting to be solved. On the other hand, those who choose to reward students may get a better feedback. Firstly, I believed that encouragement's potential is nable to estimate, encouragement will improve a student's confidence and make them have more energy to work harder next time. Take myself for instance, when I was little, the reason why I studied hard was that I would like to get the presents only given to the top 3 students in class and I also enjoyed the honor that my teacher gave me. Therefore, I think it might be the main reason why all schools hold the rewarding ceremonies after every big examinations. Secondly, rewards are not only for those top students, they also encourage those who always fail not to give up and let them volunteer to learn continuously.
In conclusion, I think that everyone would like to be accomplished rather than punished. Therefore, in order to make our students study harder and be more courage, there is nothing more effective than rewarding properly.

subject: HW1001
content:
Recently, there's filled with lots of news concerning excessive punishment. In the news, some teachers teach students by using punishment. Afterward corporal punishment arouse debate on society. However, I am of the opinion that proper punishment is more effective on teaching students, because of educational concern.
First of all, educational concern is the upper most thing. Teachers may use punishment to teach students what is right or wrong. For example, some teenagers smoke in the campus. At that time, teachers should control their misbehavior and educate them about the fact that smoke is detrimental by punishment.
However, sometimes teachers could set clear limits. Teachers may use punishment appropriately, not excessively. Sometimes, the excessive punishment would hurt students' minds and cause bad consequences.
To sum up, I think proper punishment is necessary on education. Through punishment, teachers can educate students about their dicipline and control their bevavior. However, the one point to pay attention is the excessive punishment would influence students' minds. Therefore, proper punishment is better on educating students.

subject: HW1001
content:
To reward students for learning is better than to punish them. The rewards inspire students to study hard but the punishments only make them feel afraid. Rewards make children learn happily in contrast of punishments.
The punishments such as slapping the bottom easily leave harm to students or even cause the permeant harm in their mind. I have watch the news that one students got serious bruises on his bottom because he forgot to bring his assignments. However, the teacher got mad about this so she hit him in front of the whole class. After that, the poor student needed to take a long rest and he refused to go to the school. In short, the punishments usually make thing get worse and make students get hurt physically or even mentally.
In conclusion, the rewards give students a positive goal to study hard but the punishments only scare the students. Many students even have got injured on their body or in their mind. Therefore, punishment is the worse way to make students study hard.

subject: HW1001
content:
Recently, there has been lots of debating over whether or not to use punishment to movitvate students. At present, there are two major groups debating it and coming a deadlock.
One side is parents and teachers from last generation, which support using punishment. In their minds, their are at least one reason for this. To start with, they have inherited a kind of concept which means that only by using punishment can childs become well-behaved and polite.
The other side is parents of latest generation. They persist that teachers should educate students by other way such as rewarding. To them, punishment only makes students reluctant to learn and lead to escape from it eventually on account of their deep experiences.
Personally, both methods aren't perfect and there are ins and cons of them. Using punishment may motivate students to get better, yet if it's overdone, students will have reluctance to learning. On the other hand, without punishment, students are indulged because there is nothing but threatening them. Therefore, I think that we should strike a balance between them.
In the long run, the reason why I think that we should strike a balance is my deep experiences. My aunt promots love education and never punish her childs. However, my cousins not only become bad students but refuse to listen to their mother's suggestion. On the other hand, I often read newspapers and find that some teachers use punishment so serious that not only students' body but their minds are hurt and they refuse to go to school in the end. Therefore, I hope we can find a way out which can strike a balance to prevent the following events from happening again.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding student for learning can lead to better. However, this two methods both play important role to students.
Take me as an example. I am a teacher in cram schools. During the class, I like to give my students "apples" to motivat them to learn. They could get a small gift when they collect enough "apples".
As a teacher, I also have right to take away their "apples" as punishment to control their behavior in the class. Sometimes I would give them more homework as punishment too and it alway works.
There are a lot of way for teachers to teach. I couldn't choose one of those two methods and say which one is more effective. If teachers use punishment to students, they would learn just because they are afraid of punishment and if teachers use rewarding to students, they would take recieving gifts as granted. Both punishment and rewarding are important to students.

subject: HW1001
content:
There is no denying that learning is important to not only children but the countries. But how to motivate students to learn is controvercial these days. In my opinion, motivating students by rewarding can lead to better results.
The first reason is that learning should be a joyful thing. If we keep using punishment to make students learn, they might not be able to build the interest of learning. As they graduate, they might not be willing to learn anymore. I think too much punishment will leave people unhappy memories of learning and makes them can not achieve "learning as living." Second, using reward rather than punishment can teach students be responsible to themselves and build their confidence to their future. Although punishment can control students' behavior, teachers can not stay with students forever and punish them whenever they do wrong. The best way is that we should reward students when they be good making them feel achievement and confident. Then in the future, they might be willing to do good things and study hard. Moreover, some educational tests also prove that rewarding students can help them be responsible to themselves in the future.
From above, we can find that motivating to learn by rewarding is best to students not only in the present but in the future. Finland's education is the best proof of it. Their teachers use reward to motivate learning and make students enjoy learning. And from OECD's exam, Finland's educational result is the best in the world. Therefore, Taiwan should take Finland's experience as learning model and use reward to motivate learning rather than punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
When it comes to the manners for motivating students to learn and controling their behavior, as far as I am concerned, I will choose the one that rewarding students instead of the other one that punishing students certainly. In the experience of myself, teachers that want to control students by means of scold and punishment are in vain. Moreover, I think those teachers are to blame.
For instance, when I was a senior high school student, I had a crush on a girl who was my classmates then. Unfortunately, my tutor knew it by chance, and he banned me for falling in love by scolding me and even insulting me. I felt really frustrated and lost all of my confidences. By degrees, my behavior in school became worsen and worsen, I even intended to suicide and left the world for good. At a close call, my parents were aware of my awful condition and then they change a tutor for me. The incoming tutor was very friendly and she encouraged me a lot. By means of this, I escaped from the pessimistic condition and entered to a optimistic world, I also study more harder than before. Eventually, I passed the exam and had the qualification to enter the National Taiwan universty which is the best college in Taiwan.

subject: HW1001
content:
When it comes to how to stimulate students to learn, I am of the opinion that rewarding students is a better way. When students are punished, they may feel depressed and whatever they do is wrong. As a consequence, they may quit to learn. Neverthess, if we reward them, they may feel so much acheivement and eager to study harder to get the praise. Hence, I have every reason to say that rewarding students is better than punishing them.
Tom, one of my friends, used to like to study. However, not getting good grade, he usually punished by his severe parents. Gradually, he lost his passion to learn. What worse, he goes astray. Today, he never goes again. My other friend, Jimmy, used to be a naughty boy. One day, he was rewarded by helping a teacher. He was so happy. Therefore, he changes. He becomes so polite and likes to help others. So punishing students may make them bad, rewarding may change the students good.

subject: HW1001
content:
As to me, I am for using punishment. It is no deny that everyone is afraid of punishment. And it's sure that they will try their best to get away from it. So I think that punishment should be a more effective to prevent students from doing misbehavior. Through punishment, teachers can leave the awareness in students' mind. Then as the students are going to do something wrong, the scary of physical hurt will chill their bone and will soon wake them to what the teachers have taught them. When it comes to rewarding students for learning, I think it can easily spoil students. Since there is no any fear when they're doing something wrong, it's less likely for them to bear the rules in mind. Besides, maybe they will behave well in the purpose to receiving praise. What's worse, when the reward can not satisfy them, will them ask more? So I am not agree with this method.
The examples which are for my opinion are common in our life. In school, as a student is going to break the rules, the teachers are usual to tell him what punishment he would suffer if he do so. Surly, the student may soon stop doing so and obey the rules. If the teachers convinced him not to do so by giving him compliment or something else, the student is tendency to take a consideration about which thing is more benefit to him. If there is any hesitate, it can't be effective. I really think punishment is greater than rewarding, since it can pracisely stop students doing misbehavior.

subject: HW1001
content:
