Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion and my teaching experience, I consider rewarding students for learning could have better results.
I am an elementary teacher, and I've been teaching for over twenty years. When I started teaching twenty years ago, I'd like to use punishment to motivate my students. Because they afraid to be punished, so they did well. But gradually, I could felt they didn't like me, instead, they hated me, and wish I got sick, so they could have a good time in school.
One day, I read a book, its name was "How to talk to your students in the classroom." And I found that I was wrong, I used bad words to hurt my students and punished them for so many years. So I decided to change myself to be a polite and caring teacher in my class. At first, I had a little bit afraid that if I didn't push them or punish them, how could my students get good score? But when I started to encourage my students, and preciated them when they did good, the surprise was happed, almost all my students got great score and getting happy in my teaching class.
Several years ago, one of my lovely students came to see me, having conversation with me. She said "Teacher Nina, do you know, I really don't like you at first, because you are so strick to us, and always punished us trying to improve our grade in subjects, but I can tell you, it didn't work. Then you become a nice teacher, always care for us, complement us and trust us without any punishment we can do better. That's work! As a student, I like to be respected and trusted from teachers."
From that time, I know I am in right way now.

subject: HW1001
content:
Punishment will not be the only way when it comes to education.
In my opinion, punishments is the worst method to motivate students to learn or to control their behavior because when I was a little boy I got hit by the teacher a lot of times, and that made me become afraid of the teacher and the school then refused to go to school for a long time until my parents took me to see the doctors. So punishment is really ther worst method when it comes to education.
Rewarding students for learning can always lead to better results. No one want to be treated badly. As for me, I have two kids and I don't want them to be treated like I have been to when I was young so I always encourage them to take part the group activities which teachers planned when they are in the kindergarten. I know it works when I see the smiles on their faces everyday on our way home.
I still remember the bad things which happened to me when I was a little boy and I don't want them happen again. I know I am successful because my children let me know.

subject: HW1001
content:
Having been a student for almost 20 years, I did received physical punishment and mental punishment as well. In recent years, I start my teaching job, and I become the one who enable to use punishment. From that on, I think back of my experience of receiving punishment in my school days; therefore, I decide not to do the same on my students.
There are two reasons that I oppose for punishment. First, I admit that punishment is effective for motivating students to learn, but the duration of the effectiveness is not lasting long. Once the punishment is canceled, students will have no motivation to carry on. Instead, the teacher should use means to develop students' inner power, such as their dignity, their sense of self-fulfillment, etc. what's more, there is always a positive aspect of bad things. Maybe the teacher can perform punishment on students in good ways. For instance, the teacher makes the student who did not hand in his assignment on time read the text on class. In the case, the student did finish his homework in another way.
As we know, the punishment in school, especially physical one, is banned by law. Since the purpose of punishment is to motivate students to learn, a good deed. Why not thinking of some good methods which replace those bad and unpleasant ones? We may remain as many good deeds as we could.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, teachers try to encourage their students to study with many kinds of ways. Some teachers tend to use punishment to discipline students while anothers like to reward students.
For teachers who like to use penalties to motivate students to learn, punishing students is the most efficient way to control their behavior. A famous saying goes like this, "Spare the rod, spoil the child." Students will stop being naughty and will focus on their study because they don't want to be punished. However, because students usually follow what teachers say reluctantly, the relationships between students and teachers may get bad to the worse.
For some teachers, using reward is more useful than using punishment when teaching. When teachers using reward rather than punishment, students tend to study actively. Nevertheless, some students are so lazy that they don't study hard even if they can get some benefits from learning.
In my opinion, rewarding students is more effective than punishing them. When I was a junior high school student, my math teacher was a stern man. He punished students when they didn't do well on the math test even though they had made a progress. As a result, math was the subject I hated most when I was in junior. On the contrary, my English teacher was so kind that she usually sent small cards to encourage the students who made progresses or to comfort those who were upset about their bad performance. Since then, English has become my favorite subject at school.
With what I mentioned above, rewarding students is really better than punishing them. If possible, I hope teachers can reward their students more and punish them less.

subject: HW1001
content:
When I was little, I was a naughty girl. One day I put a sworm on a teacher's chair and waited for the teacher to sit on it. About five minutes later, the teacher came, but he found the sworm before he sit on it. I felt disappointed and walked to the teacher, telling him that the sworm was mine. Instead of scolding and punishing me, he put the sworm back to the tree and told me that I sholdn't do this, then he told me that I should respect every live even it's a sworm. With his teaching, I knew that my behavior was wrong, and I promised him that I would respect animals and won't do such things again. After this event, I learned a lesson and became a good girl.
Every time I memoried this event, I was grated to the teacher because he told me why my behavior is wrong instead of scolding or punishing me.
In my opinion, punishment may make the children feel terrible about learning, though it may control their behavior, it can't change their mind. On contrary, rewarding or encouraging students not only gives students anergy to learning but also changes their thinking, they will know which behavior is good or bad and why, then they will change themself into a mature and better person, such as me.

subject: HW1001
content:
In schools, all teachers hope that students can behave well. They may try to use many methods in the classroom to make learning efficiently. Some of them use the positive ways to teach pupils, but some of them may use the punishment in teaching. In my opinion, I think that it could be more effective by using the positive ways like giving gifts or encouragement to students.
Why is the punishment worse to control students' behaviors? If teachers punish students like beating them, it may result in some problems. First, students may start to hate teachers and don't want to attend school. Then, their study could be worse, and it may discourage them a lot. They feel that it's very boring to stay at school, so they start to skip classes and commit crimes in society. These are not good results if teachers always teach students like that. However, if teachers use positive ways in teaching, the situation could be changed. Rewarding students is a better way. Students love to get gifts, praise or encouragement because of their human nature. The more praise teachers use, the more motivation students will have. Therefore, it can increase their learning and it's better to their mental health.
Take one student for an example. Originally, he wasn't a good student because he liked to talk in class. In the past, I always used the punishment to control him but in vain. Then, I changed my way to teach him by giving a gift if he could sit quietly on the seat. As a result, it worked and it also improved his learning.
Therefore, rewarding students is a better method in teaching. Teachers need to use it more and it also helps them to motivate students' learning also. It's a good method, isn't it?

subject: HW1001
content:
Punishing or rewarding students to get better results is very controvercial. However, in my opinion, rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.
Rewarding can encourage students and give them more confidence However, punishing will increase hatred. Take my younger sister for example. My mother used to punish her for getting bad grades. My sister thought that she did study hard but nobody saw that, so she felt disappointed and helpless In this case, punishment make the situation worse. She started rebelling, she even handed in the text paper which only had her name on it.
Things changed when my mother started encouraging her My mother brought my sister to movies if she did better Now, my sister loves studying and always gets good grades Rewarding can let students know they are respected and useful. That's why I think rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I would say that rewarding is better than punishing. In spite of the phrase "Spare the rod and spoil the child", I think using punishment is just not a proper way to teach our next generation. Some may see the instant effect when giving punch or extra homework, but they forgot the long-term influence to the students. Students who are punished constantly will begin to loose their self-confidence as well as give up learning. In the condition that even worse, some students may regard the punishment as a only way to solve the problem. A negative mind is not a result that all of us are pleasant to see.
If we give more reward and praise instead of punishment when teaching students, their may feel good about themselves and obtain the motion to behave even better. Take my mom's students for an example. She serves as a teacher in an elementary school and has a class of about thirty students. In order to make them read, she prepares some snacks for them when they read a book and finish the handout about the book. After a few months, most of her students will reach for the books even if there are no reward.
I think reward is a way to let the students make a good habit. Proper praise when they're learning will definitely result in good feed-backs.

subject: HW1001
content:
Teachers play an important role in the life of a student, and they use either punishment or rewarding to try to guide the students. In my opinion, rewarding is more effective than punishment. Though punishment is a method to let the students be afraid of doing bad things, it can not change their behavior for ever. When they graduate from school, they will not be punished anymore. In the contrary, rewarding can change the behavior deeply through the right way.
My mother is an elementary school teacher, and she often shares stories about her students in school with me. I remembered a story about a boy she told me before. She said that the boy was misbehaving and had always made troubles. My mother punished the boy but nothing had changed. So my mother changed her attitude toward the boy and started to reward the boy whenever he did something good. After a few months, my mother said that the personality of the boy had changed so dramatically that she can't even believe it herself.
In a nutshell, I think that rewarding is more effective than punishing, because it can touch a student's heart by the passion and kindness that the teacher gives. No one is perfect, so the teacher has the resonsibility to guide the through a right way, and that is-rewarding.

subject: HW1001
content:
First of all, it goes without saying that both methods have their pros and cons. It is hard to argue which one is better by having totally different educational background though, through my own experience, rewarding students for learning is more effective. In the following paragraphs, I will tell you the opinion I have toward these methods.
When studying in the elementary school, I had a really pleasant studying experience. The reason I said that is because every time I had a decent score on my test, I would earn extra credit because of that. It really motivated me to study harder and harder. Furthemore, it really elevated my whole studying interest, on the contrary, I had a terrible experience by meeting my junior high teachers. Every time I did wrong on my test, they just never stop
It is obvi

subject: HW1001
content:
Teachers around the world have different ways to motivate students, some of them might punish students, while others may have a softer way, such as giving reward. And I believe that it is always a better idea to give reward than to punish.
I started to learn the piano when I was at the age of seven. My first teacher was nice and patient. She always gave me gifts when I did well but never did she punishe me when I didn't pactice. Because of the gifts and encourages, I never forgot to practice the piano, and I was always fond of the day to have piano lessons at that time. Unfortunately, my teacher went abroad and I got another teacher who was always mad at me and punished me alot. Soon, I found no interest in piano and started to refuse to go to class after no longer than a month.
In my opinion, teacher who give reward often make students willing to learn. And while learning happily, students can find more interest in learning, but not think of learning as something painful and exhausting.

subject: HW1001
content:
I do think that rewarding students for learning motivates students to learn and control their behavior better. Students who do not learn well aren't stupid; it's just that they don't have the motivation to urge them to learn. Rewarding them is a passive way to make them push themselves.
My brother used to get bad scores at school. He sits around all day and did nothing to improve himself. However, ever since his homeroom teacher started to take students who behaves well to the McDonald's, my brother began to learn actively. He no longer allows himself to watch TV all night the day before tests; instead, he studies his textbooks and keeps a regular life. The change of his attitude affected his academic scores. He is now one of the top students in his class.
Another example of learning well due to the rewards is me myself. My grandparents usually gives me money representing scholarships when I do well on a test. This indeed urges me to work harder while preparing for a test.
There are a lot of examples testifying rewards being an effective way to motivate learning. However, it can be the more effective, but definitely not the perfect way. Motivations for learning should be changable depending on the individual's way of learning.

subject: HW1001
content: Nowadays, education becomes more and more important to the children. However, they just can't understand why they have to sit at school eight hours a day. They only think about the entertainment so many teachers use punishment to motivate them. I don't consider that as a good method. When I was still in elemantary school, teacher punished me like all time. But every time he punished me, it not only doesn' make me want to study but also increase the angry in my heart. One day, I couldn't stand anymore. He didn't have the right to punish just because I got a bad score on my monthly exam. That's they day I shouted at him and also the day I chanslated to another school. In the new school, I met a teacher that I still felt thankful for him. He was strict, but he talked to me like my father. He never used any punishment and everytime someone did something that was great, he awarded them. Even though sometimes it just words it gave me the strength to earn the award. Since then I study harder, I control my temper and I was graduated at the first place in school. From my own experience, I can strongly tell any of the teacher that every students want to be awarded in front of their classmates; not being punished. In general, I believe that punishment can probably create "good" students but rewarding is what makes great students.

subject: HW1001
content:
In some private school, including elematary to senior high school, teachers support the idea of "using punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior". Of course, it might work in some sort of ways, but will it cause any negative effect to students? It is a paradox, I think.
I believe "Rewarding" students to learn is a better way. I don't support this viewpoint for I am a student, but for I have seen a lot examples in my life or in movies. Once, I saw a movie produced from Singapore, it was about educating. At first, the teacher scold his students and punished them for not doing well on the test, but then, he found out that the more pressure he put on them, the less effective results he got. So, he decided to change a different way. He started to praise them on every detail of their life, including having a progress on their score only for two points. As a result, the students not only got their confidence back but looked more up to their teacher.
From this example, we can learn that students need more positive motivation to complete their accomplishment. Though sometimes it's still necessary to punish students for doing wrong, rewarding them is a better way to lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
I work as a teacher, too. In my opinion, I think teachers they have to use these two methods depend on what their students like. I teacher in a cram school. It is better to reward students. I believe that everyone needs compliment, and they can do better job. When students hear the teaches say that they're doing a great job, they will be confident to themselves. And they will do better and better. This method is more effective. But some students they're different. You need to give them some punishment that they will remind themselves that if they didn't do the better job, they will be punished by the teacher. But still, I think saying something good to students is better.
When I teach in the cram school, I will encourage them instead of laughing at them. I have a student that he has some problems to memorize vocabularies. I teached him one by one and help him memorize the vocabularies with K.K phonics. I kept telling him that he can do it, if he pass the test next time, I can give him some reword. And he did it. I have another student who doesn't like to write composition. I encouraged him that I believe he can do it. And now he is interested in writing. Above all, I believe that it is better to give students reward than punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the past, there were lots of teachers use punishment to motivate student to learn and to control their behavior. Nowadays, more and more teachers change the mind that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.
I am a high school student now. I remember when I was in elememtary school, our classroom teachers often used punishment when we forgot to bring or write homeworks. In this reasons, I didn't like this teacher and was afraid of her. After I was in the fifth grade, we had to change into a new class and our homeroom teacher became Ms. Wang. Ms. Wang was a nice lady, she was young and just got married. She treated us just as if we were her children, and rewarded us when we did a good job on the homework and got good grades. Although the lessons were getting harder and harder when we got into the high grade, we were happy to learn more. This made me remember that once our class got the first place on the English test, Ms. Wang bought everyone a cup of ice tea. It wasn't something very expensive, but it made us realize that our teacher was proud of us and wanted us to keep better.
I prefer rewarding rather than punishment when teaching young students. When a teacher treats me badly, it make me hate to go to school and doesn't enjoy learning. On the other side, if the teacher gives me rewards, I would like to study harder and receive the present from the teacher. Every student is teachable, I hope that teachers can reward more and punish less when teaching.

subject: HW1001
content:
Punishing and Rewarding are two different ways to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Each of them has its own advantages and disadvantages.
Traditionally, ancient Chinese supposed that children or students would never make progress without being punished. According to behaviorists, punishment can only stand for negative reinforcement for change of students' behavior. If I were a teacher, punishment would be my last choice to deal with students' problems.
Some contemporay educators tend to make good use of alternate methods to improve students' behavior, and rewarding is included. Therefore, contemporary teachers are able and willing to understand students' needs and to analyze students' characters. Punishment may result in mental or physical harms to students, but rewarding will not.
To sum up, no method is absolutely more effective than others. Teachers are supposed to try to understand their own students and students' interest and personalities, and then to choose apropriate and ideal methods to improve students' behavior. How could teachers not thoughtful and helpful to their own students?

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays, the job-finding process is getting worse. Many parents are very worried about the hopeless future of their children. Therefore, they chose to have their children get higher grades, always get the first place of all subjects, and get into the top university. But the problem is, how can their endless wishes come true?
In order to realize the wishes parents asked, teachers began to think of a way to make students study harder. Some use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding can lead to better results. As for my opinion, I think the second choice would be better. If we use punishment to make students study, the only result we could get is-nothing. Students would do whatever they could to avoid being caught by their teachers, whom they all consider monsters that destroy their happy education. And for this, it would also start the hate between teachers and students.
Here's an example. One of my friends in elementary school went to a private junior high school when graduated. At first, I thought that teachers in private school are strict, and they can even "punish" students with illegal ways-without catching by the government. But later on, my friend told me that no one cares about those stupid rules made by the school. They even think of many ways to avoid the punishment of their teachers, like hiding in the bathroom when teachers are approaching, or practicing how to tight their hair up in three seconds, etc. Their teachers can never catch them doing illegal things-even if they already did.
So, as I mentioned, punishment can only make students "smarter", for they have to think of thousands or hundreds of ways to avoid being caught by their teachers. Therefore, I should agree on the fact that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
We are in the 21th centry, with time changing, the old school mentality should just stay in the past, so is the punishment. This generation grew up with love form their parents, almost everyone were spoiled. Once they got punished by the teachers, they just can't stand the pressure. And the parents simply won't let their children go through this pain. That's why we see the news title "Teacher being sued" all the time. On the other hand, rewarding students can be useful while they still learn something. I consider it a more proper way.
During my time in elementary school, I was a naughty kid. I'm not afraid of getting punished, I even argued with the teachers. But, when my teacher found it impossible to scared me, she changed her methods. She told the whole class that if we all behaved well, she'll give us a point. With the more points, we can get the bigger reward by the end of the school year. Since then we all do our best to get the points, and had learned that well behavior is the most important of all.

subject: HW1001
content:
Does punishment do benefit to students? The issue has been in doubt for several years. As to my personal point of view, I believe punishment causes less effect toward student, that is to say, I think rewarding is more effective on learning.
The different results of the two methods are obvious. When I was in elementary school, my teacher used to give me books or encouragement when I had good behaviors or got good grades. Every time I received the rewards from my teachers, I knew I did well and should keep it up, so I studied harder and tried to do everything well; in the end I did it, I reached my goal and became the person I wanted to be. I deeply know how rewarding could promote a student to study hard and to seize chances to prove him/her self.
As to the oppsite method I've seen many teachers used punishment to control student's behaviors. To tell the truth, there is nearly no successful example of using the method to "turn the student back". I received a mistaken punishment once at middle school, I didn't do anything "out of the comfort zone", but my teacher wanted to punish me. At that moment I did feel bad of it, and there was a very clear thought acrossed my mind: "You say No, and I'll do so." For every student who is on learning, he or she needs comfortable surroundings and the atmosphere of safty. Science reports have shown that the above things will make student persue good results on studying, while punishment only make students lose their faith and interest on learning.
Combine the experiences I have with the knowledge I've gained, rewarding is generally thought as more effective when it compares to punishment. Rewarding is easier to lead students have good results on studying, and keep them "on track" of their learning paths.

subject: HW1001
content:
Recently, there are more and more cases on TV and newspapers which are about the abuse of punishment on the campus. These cases have been raising our attention to the educational system.
While some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior, others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. So, the debate between punishment and reward has already begun.
In my opinion, I prefer the method of rewarding the students instead of punishing them. First, students are not animals. While animals might follow the instructions people give them after being whipped, people never do. If we punish the students for their bad performances instead of teaching them, they may try to escape from school. Second, once the students grow up, and become parents, this might be a duplication to the next generations.
My uncle, Sam, used to be punished by his teachers seriously at school. Thus, he is duplicating the way to his children, who are my cousins at the same time. Both of my cousins have already quit schools and idled around. The older one even commited a crime last year.
To sum up, I support the method of encouraging students to learn and to behave themselves. After all, love can change the world.

subject: HW1001
content:
We all agree that education plays an irreplaceable role for improving a country. There are so many methods to make the learning more efficient. Some teaches would like to use punishment while others prefer the rewarding. But which of them is the more effective way?
I would be more likely to support the later method. First, I think it's inappropriate to punish student to urge them to study. most of students are young and venerable, the may get hurt physically and mentally. Second, it's alway not right to use violence. What if the students regarded this as the only way to solve problems? this can become a very serious problem. the students may lose the correct moral values, and grow into a crucial and violete adult.
Though some people may think that rewarding students for learning would make the students study only for the benefit. But I believe that to educate and reward them at the same time will be a nice solution. We can tell them that the final goals of learning is to give back to the country.
To sum up, I advocate to teach the student with appropriate adwardig. This can encourage them to learn but not transform them into unmoral persons.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. In my opinion, rewarding is more effective way for students to learn.
The reason I believe rewarding is better way than punishment is, students will raise their motivation by someone's encouragement in order to gain rewarding. This kind of thought will lead them willing to learn in order to get what they want. Besides, by this way, it help students think and pay more attentions on learning.
However, if we blames students with punishment, it will make them afraid of learning because they will worry whether they will be punished if they learn not well. It will make them learning under lots of pressure and grow with negitive thought.
Learning should be a happy thing because it makes you understand things that you don't know. And teaching by rewarding will lead students to have positive thought. That's why I believe it can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior, while others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. This question has been argued for a long time. In my opinion, rewarding students for learning is more effective.
Every student expects to be noticed. When a student gets good grades or does something good, teachers or parents giving children some prizes can motivate the innocent kids to study hard or act well. When I was little, I used to help my mother do household chores. My mother was very glad, and gave me a piece of cake as a prize. In consequence, I liked to help her better.
Using punishment is the worst resolution to teach students, especially phisical punishment, which shows that the teacher has no confidence. Therefore, he or she just uses punishment to control students' behavior. Beside, students may use violence to solve problems because their teachers use punishment to teach them. Therefore, those innocent children may think that violence may be the only way to tackle problems.
To make our education and society better, we should abandon punishment.

subject: HW1001
content:
As more and more people are concerning about the educational issues of their children, the method of how to make children discipline is a serious debate that can't be overemphasized. I believe that nobody likes to be punished, and so do i. so I totally agree that we should be rewarded to get a better results.
For my personal experience, there's a vivid memory that was deeply carved in my mind. My elementary school's homeroom teacher is a severe woman who always punishes us when we preform badly on our grades or behaviors. She was so scary to me then that although I did everything well, I dreamed of her appearing in my nightmare and scolded me for doing badly very often. Also, some of my classmates even cheated on the exam in order to escape from the punishments. From this experience, I don't think it's a good idea for teacher to use punishment.
From my point of view, I think it is important to let the students feel that learning is a happy thing. This will last longer instead of the temporary punishment. Also, it's important to install into the thought that everyone has their own personal trait and specialty. We shouldn't emphasized merely on the academic performance, but many of the good traits, such as art, sport, relationship or politeness. I believe that can also help students to explore their own interest. By doing so, maybe there'll be more Taiwanese stars glittering on the global stage!
In conclusion, it's really a critical issue and worth public awareness. For me, I firmly believe that rewarding require much advantages over punishments.

subject: HW1001
content:
When it comes to the methods teachers use to teach their students, some of the teachers like to punish students, they use authorities, while others believe rewarding students is the better way. To me, rewarding students is better, and I will show my opinion in the following paragraph.
No man is perfect, we would all do something that is incorrect. I don't think doing punishment can really makes us do better. As a teenager, I hate to be punished, it would make me a worse person and don't want to cooperate. But if you praised me when I do something rewardable, I will be very happy, and to get more reward, I would do something better. That is, student who get a lot of rewards often turns out to be successful while those who are often be punished become out of control in their behavior at last.
No matter you agree or not with my opinion, this is what I think. Maybe somebody thinks that it is better to punish students, but to me, giving them reward and praise is just the very best way to bring them to the right road!!

subject: HW1001
content:
We often hear news about teachers punishing students when they misbehave. Whenever hearing about this kind of news, I always find out why the teacher punishes the student. Then I will think in my mind if there are better ways to deal with the situation than just using punishment. The main reason for me to do this is because I am a teacher myself. Hence, I can think about what would I do when facing the same problem.
Punishing students to motivate them was never a first choice for me when teaching. Because it did not motivate me when I was a student. My teacher would punish me if I got bad grades, and by using this kind of method did not make my grades higher. Therefore, rewarding students for learning became my favorite way to motivate and even control naughty children. Giving out stickers to girls and handing out treats to boys are one of the best way to reward students.
I think nobody likes to be punish. So when teaching students, rewarding them is more effective. In my opinion, I think everyone likes to have a good treat or applause.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, I think that rewarding students for learning is a better way to educate them.
According to the statistics, children are likely to have less achievment when they recieve the education by punishment. Under the heavily pressure of teachers, children tend to be afraid of speaking out their ideas. Thus, it is possible for them to lost their ability to think independently. In today's information-exploding society, being able to think independently is quite important to cultivate a sense of telling right from wrong. In that case, those children who recieve the education by punishment would probably go astray. In addition, the education by punishment would make students be to shy to contact other people, and that would cause a problem of their future interpersonal relationships.
In the versus, education by rewarding is a much better way to students. Children will be encouraged to learn and try something new. Under encouragements of teachers, children can have more oppotunities to discovery and know themselves. Moreover, children tend to look things at bright side and be more optimistic about their lives.
In short, educating children takes love and care instead of punishment and blaming.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. As far as I am concerned, I prefer the later one. But generally speaking, punishment and rewarding are both effective. Which is more effective should depend on students' personality. Those who are not afraid of punishments, teacher should better encourage them instead of blaming on them.
It's hard to tell, take myself for example, I'm really afraid of punishment but I seldom be punished. I supposed students should behave theirselves.

subject: HW1001
content:
Given the choice between useing punishment to motivate students and rewarding students for learning, which one will I choose? I think it is better to reward students and inspire them.
First of all, students feel really upset when teachers punish them or blame on them. In most cases, students will abandon themselves into despair, when a teacher punishes them. In this way, students may lose the motivate to learn.
What is more, students feel pleasant when teachers reward them. For example, my English is a friendly person. She always praised me and went out of her way to help me. Soon my English really improved. And I have no problem talking to a forigner now. In view of this, teachers' praise is much more useful than punishment.
Last, students can do much better if teachers rewarded them. Students will feel glad when teachers praise them. In this light, students may study harder to make their teachers happy as a gift return.
All in all, it is not punishing that tells so much as rewarding. Thus, it is better, for a teacher, to praise the students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Talking about "education", some teachers believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results, while others think that using punishment to motivate students is more effective. In my opinion, I agree that using punishment is more "effective", but I don't think it's the better method.
When I was in grade 6 of elementary school, my teacher was very strict. She prefered punishment to reward. She would hit we stududents on hands or buttum by sticks if we didn't get good grades or didn't follow her rules. All of us were so afraid of her that we "pretended" we were good students. But when she was not here, we started to try to break the rules.
However, when I was in junior high school, my teacher was such a nice gentleman that he had never punish students. But if any students did well on big exams, he would gave those students a hand-made rewarding card. If one collect enough cards, he/she can get a special gift. In those days, most of classmates-including me-worked very hard for ourselves.
In conclusion, I think using punishment is a more effective method, but it can only "force" the students into doing something they don't want to do. Rewarding students can train the students work hard for their own profits, and it might good to the future of students.

subject: HW1001
content:
Recently, there are more and more negative news about schools on TV everyday. For instance, the problems of gansters, drugs and misbehaviors have been existed in schools commonly. In my opinion, not only the teachers, but also the government should take it seriously. Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. There are some pros and cons. On one hand, the students would be more obedient if the teachers use punishment such as doing push-ups, running around the playground, writing lessons and so forth. These are the better ways to get them pay more attention in class. On the other hand, the students would be more disobedient if the teachers use impropriate punishment to control their behavior. For example, hitting them by using sticks or scolding them in public are not proper ways to encourge them to study.
When I was eight years old, I went to a cram school to learn English. I was too shy to speak English and express myself. At that time, my teacher, Bela, encourged me to practice in class. She made me feel confident to conquer the fear of speaking English in public. I feel greatful so that I am able to speak freely and communicate well with foreigners.
To sum up, I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content: Rewarding students for learning is the best way to support students to learn and to control their behavior. To my knowledge, no one likes to be punished, so teacher should use less punishment and more reward on students. Hence, there are several ways that teacher can do to help students to get on the right track. First and foremost, if a student who makes a mistake, try not to punish him. Secondly, if a student is in the progress, please reward the student for being diligent on studies. Last but not least, try to phraise student during the class. It can make student be more confident. Doing what I have mentioned will not only make students behave well but also lead students to the door of happiness.

subject: HW1001
content:
In the past, the teachers used to employ a lot of punishment to motivate students and shape their behavior. However, how many of them would still keep the habit of reading after they left school? I personally believe that rewarding students for learning would change the results. There are some examples to account for my statement.
First of all, it is no doubt that everyone loves reward but nobody likes punishment. In Taiwan, not only parents but also teachers put too much emphasis on tests and grades. If a student are learning under such a great pressure, how can he or she learn well and happily?
Secondly, the government nowadays has promoted an idea that the teachers should teach students the ways of learning but what they should learn. If one is lucky enough to pick up a couple of learning tips such as note-taking, he will benefit from it for his whole life on learning.
In other words, as a teacher, his or her compliment or smile at students will be far more powerful to encourage student rather than a serious punishment which make student afraid to learn.
In conclusion, learning is the reason for itself. Using punishment cannot arise students' willingness or intest on learning. Only by rewarding students can really grow their confidence in learning and make them enjoy learning.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some people believe that students should be punished if they made mistakes. Others believe that rewarding students can ecourage them. I think both are important.
I have been working in cram school for many years. I can tell you that students are different. They all have different personality. Punish or reward, it deponds on what kind of students you are dealing with. There are some naughty students, they are sometimes out of control in the class time. If the teacher can't stop those kids immediatly, the despline of the class will be ruded. The teacher should punish the student as a warming. What I mean punish, doesn't mean hit them. You can give them more homework or clean up the classroom as a punishment. Also when the students have improved a little bit, then the teacher should encourage them in front other kids. Giving some nice rewards is definatly making students to work harder. However, teachers shouldn't reward students everytime, otherwise they will only study for prices.
Both of them are very important. When the teacher find out the student is making a mistake, the teacher should teach him or her to correct it. If the student still doing the wrong thing, the teacher should punish the student. When he or she has improved a little, then encourage the student. I believe by doing this, students can learn better.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are many ways to educate students. The two ways that are normally used are punishment and rewarding.
Through the punishment, it definitely will remind the students of the result if next time they want to do the thing again. However, some punishment is not that suitable for the students, especially the physical publishment. Because some students may not just get the physical hurt but also get the shadow of this event. For example, I know one of my classmates gave up on himself after being smacked the legs by his teacher because he didn't score high enough.
In terms of rewarding, I think of it as a good way to practice the humanism. People is different form animals, so we don't need to be treated like the lion in the circus. Besides, students will motivate themselves to study hard and control their behavior more automatically through the rewarding than the punishment.
Take myself for example. My civic teacher once told me if I can score A-plus in the big test this time, she will give me an unique gift that she had bought in Japan. Although I just score A that time, she still gave me the gift, which made me think I must study harder next time to teach my teacher's expectation. (I really scored A-plus next time!)
In conclusion, suitable punishment is acceptable for me, but I still prefer rewarding. Because I think we should hold a positive attitude toward studying, not a negative one which punishment usually causes!
Happy learning! That's my wish!

subject: HW1001
content:
It was really common to hear teachers punishing their students for what they had done wrong in the past. But now, the education in Taiwan prefers encouraging and rewarding students to physically-punishing them.
I think that both of the educational methods have their advantages and disadvantages. For punishing students, it is a more effective but more extreme way to motivate students, in my opinion. Since physical punishments can sometimes be out of control, leading to an unchangeable harm, I suggest using another less harmful way to punish students.
In a word, teachers should alter the proper way to motivate students according to the students' personalities or something else.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students for learning is definitely the best way to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Since everyone likes to be treated with kindness rather than rudeness, a good motivation will always be a candy, not a slam on the face. As far as I am concerned, even a really brief complement can do ten times efficiency as a good variety of punishments. Not to mention that the latter one can easily make you lose your face and thus destroy your confidence. Punishments will only be effective in the beginning, but after you get used of it, it will never have any impact on you.
There are two examples that can support my opinion. First, you can think about the way you treat new born babies. How do you treat them when they are learing how to stand or to walk? What's your action when you "motivate" them to smile at the camera? By yelling at them? Definitely no! You wear a shining smile on your face and do funny behaviors. When they finally smile at you, you praise them and clap your hands! It is evident that the best way to teach or to motivate others is by giving rewards such as smile or complements. The second instance happened to be myself. I didn't have good grades when I was in elementary school. Nevertheless, my grades became better after I was taught by a beautiful English teacher who always praise others and have a really positive thinking. She told me that I should have more confidence in myself and never quit. She usually encouraged me to try everything such as speaking on the stage, and no matter how great or bad I performed, she always gave me a big smile and clapped her hands loudly. It is her encouragement that makes me become the leader of the debate club in senior high. As a consequence, to me, giving rewards is always be superior to giving punishments when you try to motivate others in learning or achieving high levels.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. Others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.
In my opinion, positive methods are most likely to lead to positive results. In other words, I believe that rewarding students PROPERLY may elicit students' autonomy to learn and encourage them to perform mature behaviors as well. On the contray, punishment can only demotivate students to learn because of negative asscociation of bad learning experiences.
Being an elementary school teacher, I myself just had two examples to report here. One of my students usually failed to hand in his homework regularly, so I punished him to stay after school to make up all his homework due. However, afterwards, he decided to stay after school every day instead of handing in his homework on time. From then on, I think I was the one being punished not him. The other positive case is a boy pupil, too. Once I praised him for doing his sanitary job without being supervised in public. He did his job even harder from that time on. I knew that I just did a right thing to encourage him to perform an expected behavior.

subject: HW1001
content:
These days, tons of ink have already spilt over this issue, which is whether teachers should use punishment to motivate students to learn or reward them for a better learning outcome.
Some research papers conducted by domestic famous scholars point out both teaching methods can be profitable in different regards in terms of long-term or short-term goals toward learning.
In my point of view, I prefer to utilize rewarding to motivate students. I firmly believe it is more effective than using punishment. According to H. Douglas Brown, students' motivations can be categorized into two sectors, intrinsic motivation and extrinsic motivation. Athough both rewarding and punishment are the driving force which facilitates students' motivation externally, I think rewarding can have them be more confident, self-disciplined, and step by step trigger their intrinsic motivation toward learning. As students' learning motivations reach new height, their learning results will outshine those who are de-motivated.
Take one of my students from English corner of Shih Hsin University as an example. As a potential English teacher, I have observed whether students learning can be successful depends on if they are truly intrigued by the teaching materials and activities. My student, Sam, attains to my class each tutoring session, and participate every activity being tailor-made by me. Once he made a mistake about the paradigms of a sentence when we did a small talk, I smiled back to him. And suddenly he came to an epiphany that he made a slip of grammar. He referred to a smile as a rewarding, an encouragement. I prefer to apply rewarding, such as smiles, candy bars, or applauses, to tutoring my students filled with potential. For me, I have seen a couple of cases indicating that punishment sometime ruins students' learning motivation and hurts them mentally and physically. Even if there are a few of exceptions, I do insist on rewarding as one of the most effective way to be implemented. As a result, my student, Sam, has made a great improvement in the four arts of English under the rewarding teaching circumstance.
To build human capacity and enlarge students' intellectual ability, I truly believe one of the most beneficial ways for them to improve their learning results is be taught by rewarding. In this sense, we can cultivate more talented tycoons or scholars devoting to our society in the future.

subject: HW1001
content:
How to educate our students and children is an important issue in our society. At school, some teachers punish their students to motivate them to learn and control their behavior. Meanwhile, some teachers believe that rewarding students can be a better idea. In my opinion, I strongly agree with the second statement that teachers should encourage their students by rewarding them instead of punishment.
The first reason I would like to express is that while students are learning or facing problems, they become less confident. If teachers punish them or use a harsh way to make them study, the result will impossiblely be postive. Also, when people are rewarded and encouraged, they feel happy. Therefore, they are willing to get alone with others, and they would like to learn more knowledge and participate in class.
I would like to share my experience about working in a cram school. I have seem both ways that teachers used to educate their students. There was a little boy who was in the third grade. He was very naughty and was always not paying attention in class. One of his teachers was very strict and punished him a lot, but he still behaved the same way. However, he changed to a different class. The second teacher tried to talk and gave him a little gift or stickers when he did well in class. In a few weeks, he became polite and his grades improved.
As a result, I think teachers should encourage and reward their students more. It would make our education better.

subject: HW1001
content:
Today, teachers are not the same as teachers when I was a elementary student. Teachers have so many differences from our parent's generation. They are young and they have new thoughts of education. In the modern society, children are less than the old farmer society, so the parents are very care about their children. It makes much pressures on teachers when they try to teach their students.
In my opinion, I think it can lead to better results if teachers reward students for learning. Because I think the students will afraid to go to school if their teachers use punishment on them. People need to be respected and loved, so if teachers use punishment on students to learn and to control their behavior, they maybe just doing well in front of teacher not from their inner thought to think it is right to do such things. If teachers reward their students for learning, they will happy and try hard of their best to win the rewards from their teachers. It is a encouragement for them to learn and to control their behavior.
When I was a student, I meet two kinds of method which used by teacher. If my teacher use punishment in our classemates, they will fight back to teachers. But on the other hand, teacher rewarded our classmates, they were requested themselves to study hard to win the rewards from teachers. So I think rewarding is better than punishing students while teachers are educated their students.

subject: HW1001
content: Most teachers that carry a traditional teaching method tend to use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior. However, with a society that is striking its way into modernity now requires a different style of teaching. Most parents now view their children as their first priority, they tend to educate their children with love and care. As a result, students nowdays might oppose against the teachers when the punishments hurt their dignities, which might even lead to strong complaints from the parents. So why not change the style of motivating students with punishment into rewarding them? Such as praising the best performed student of a school project in the presence of the class or preparing a small present for the students that reach teachers' requirments. As a student myself, I prefer learning from a more positive source of motivation than gaining it out of fear for punishments. From the example and reasons mentioned above, I believe rewarding students for learning can lead to better results while motivating them to perform well.

subject: HW1001
content: When a student is having a hard time on learning, or a student doesn't know how to control his behavior, what should we do to help? Should we punish them or should we incourage them and reward them? My own notion is that we should incourage more and punish less. Punishing won't change the problem and sometimes even gets the situation worse. I once saw a news on TV, a student suicided because of great pressure. His pressure came from the teacher's punishing. Students usually live in fear when we threaten to punish them, so incouraging them is a better way to help. Set a goal for them to reach, reward them when they reach it. This is exactly what my parents do to me. In this case students will try harder to get the reward, and that's the reason students improve. Incourage them at the right time, help them a bit when they face difficulties. Soon they'll gain knowledge and courage to deal with different troubles in their life. Remember this when you teach your kid, incourage more and punish less!

subject: HW1001
content:
How many students are there, and there will be how many ways to teach them. Since we grow up in different kinds of family, everyone develops a unique individual and has their own personalities. This kind of teaching method may work on some students, but doesn't work on others. In my opinion, punishment is not the best way to make students study hard or behave well. For some lazy students, you can do some punishment just for reminding or controling them in a short time. However, the more important thing is to raise students' interests of learning and get into the habbit of studying in their daily life.
As a teacher, at first, I thought punishment is the most effictive way to make students get good grades and be good. However, when I noticed that they started losing their smiles and we got into a bad relationship. I realized that I should use another better teaching method to fix it. I try my best to make the lessons I teach as fun as possible. When students do well on their tests, I give them gifts as rewards. Although I still do some punishment, my students enjoy learning and behave well for themselves. No matter what kind of way you use to teach kids, let them know you do it for their own good and they will appreciate you one day.

subject: HW1001
content:
Compared to thirty years ago, the students in this generation are much smarter, or even, franking, more artful because of the impact brought by the advanced technology and the Internet. These allure have been having students more hunger for rewards than usual.
As a teacher and based on the previous reasons, I believe that slight punishment for students from time to time is an unavoidable solution.
One of my students dropped out school once and came back to my class later. He was smart but extremely lazy. In the beginning I gave him good words and lots of rewards, but the results couldn't last long. Months later, I changed my approaches and gave him simple punishment and rewards of the same time, I found out that he could behavior better, and the most important of all, he realized that studying was not as boring and difficult as he had thought.
Right now, though he is not the first one in my class, but at least, he won't drop out for those entertaining allure outside the school.

subject: HW1001
content:
Date back to our childhoods, aren't there any naughty or bad classmates liked to play tricks on others? Yes, there are some whenever we were in elementary school or junior high school. In the past decades, teachers always punished them by sticks, to let them feel hurt and remembered to not to do those things ever again.
Nowadays, more and more teachers are convinced by the conception of rewarding students to lead better results. However, in my opinion, I disagree with this method. There are two phenomenons could be the evidance. First, those children who have done awful things will not get punishments right away, they will think they can do it again and again. They regard our scold and spare as nothing. Maybe next time they will do more than like this. Secondly, treats are presents to good students, but not for those bad. They can not want a reward, but can not stop doing "funny" tricks or violence on their fellows.
Punishments or rewards? They both have their own advantages and disadvantages. In conclusion, doing too over of each methods is not the best way to educate our children.

subject: HW1001
content:
We can read the news that some teachers punished their students in an unappropriate way on the newspaper from time to time. As a teacher, I think the punishment given to students must be limited in some kinds, and rewarding students is more effective to encourage their study motivation.
In my opinion, the punishment could be warning in words, asking students to write something in the books or standing for a while to calm down. When my students did something wrong, I would cut the awards originally prepared for them and told them why it made me upset. Communicating with students in a positive way usually leads to pleasant results. On the other hand, punishing them usually leads to nervous relations between us.
To sum up, I believe that rewarding students for learning and well-behaving is more effective than punishment. All teachers should remember that only the punishment which ends up with rewarding can be effective and accepted by students.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, education is the top priority to a country. A good education system is the key to strong country. I prefer the way to award students instead of punish them.
The reason is that punish them will only make the situation worse. I have a cousin who is two years junior than me. He used to be a obedient kid. However, his parents are too strict to him. Whenever he did well in tests, he never got any present even a praise. But they punish him seriously as long as he made a tiny mistake. As time went by, he didn't study anymore. Worst of all, he became a troublesome students who often be caught by police officers. It's the so cruel to see his parents crying for him.
On the other hand, more encouragements are efficient to students. As my own experience, my homeroom teacher is such a great teacher that I love her so much. She treats us like friends. She only blames students as long as they did terrible fault such as cheating. She praises students a lot. Most students like her so, whatever she said, they will keep in mind. Hence, the class she teaches is always the best behavior class of all school.
Through the two examples that close to me, I can definitely believe that rewarding students is more efficient than punish them.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behavior is not very good method. I have two more better methods. First, we should talk to them and try to communicate with them, tell them that this thing is wrong, we should not do that, and tell them what trouble will happen if they do that. Second, I would reward student for their good behavior. By rewarding student, they will more be happy to listen to their teacher, and then teacher can teach them and lead to better results.
If we used to punish students without rewarding, they will out control and have bad effective certainly. Their are some real example in my life, and it is my brother's story. My brother didn't like study and his grade is very poor. My parents always punish him because his poor grade. Gragually, he is not only dislike to study, but also hate study. His grade become more poor and even don't want to go to school. My parents was very worry about that, so they change their methods. They rewarded my brother without punishment, and tell him how improtant about study. Gradually, he received and changed his mind. Please congradulate to my brother!!! He is now working at big famous company!!! If my prarents kept to punish my brother not reward, I think my brother will not change himself. So we should believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.

subject: HW1001
content:
Each teacher has his or her own way to teach students. Some punish students and some reward students. As for me, who wants to be a teacher in the future, I prefer to rewarding students. The first reason is that rewarding students can build a good relation between teachers and students. With the good relation, teachers are able to have a good communication with students. Then teachers can know what students are thinking and what difficulties students are facing. If teachers just punish students, students would not reveal their inner thought to teachers. The second reason is that rewarding students give students a goal to strive for. They know they can get rewarding if they do well in school. I believe this can motivate students to learn.
My younger sister is the best proof of what I've said in the first paragraph. She is seven years younger than me, so I have to teach her homework. Initially, I would forbid her from watching TV if she got bad grades; however, her grades still didn't improve. Then I changed my method; I said to her that if her grades could improve next time, I would give her whatever she wants. Surprisingly, my sister's grades did improve. She told me that she wanted to go to the movies and I brought my promise down to earth. From then on, I realize that rewarding is indeed better than punishment. Rewarding gives students a positive goal, but punishment just make students hate to study.

subject: HW1001
content:
Nowadays goverments are telling teachers to reward students more. In my opinion, it is a good thing. Why do I say it is a good thing? Being a student, if I want to study a certain subject, and get a good grade, the first thing I need to do is arouse the interest of this subject.
Once a teacher punished a student that didn't do well in his or her test, the student would lose appetite for studying. Once a student lost impulse to study, he wouldn't get good grades next time, too. And still he would be punished.
When I was in junior high school, my English teacher punished students by hitting their hands with a stick. Oh! That really hurt. One of them lost interest in learning and never like English any more. I felt sorry for this student, and doubt the teacher's way of teaching.
On the contrary, I met a good Math teacher in senior high school. The teacher was awesome. She rewarded us when we were good and encouraged us when we didn't do well in the exam. Her teaching style made me love Math more, I even summoned my nerve to practice difficult Math problems. As a result, I got 90 in one of my Math exams. The score really made me happy, because I never did well in Math before. I love this teacher, I really do.
Finally, we arrived at a conclusion-rewarding is better than punishing. Everyone likes to be praised, it gives us motivation to keep going, it makes us to work hard. The next thing is that you will have interest in all subjects. You will also gain passion in learning new things.
Afterall, the pleasure of learning is immense!

subject: HW1001
content:
Many teachers in Taiwan still use punishment to force students to score high on any exam, or to push students to behave themselves. However, I think that this kind of way to warn students is not a positive method. Teachers should try to come up with other ways to make their students have their own goals or motivations about schoolwork and lives. Rewarding students, encouraging students, and saying positive words can also contribute to better effects.
First, if students are rewarded by their teachers because of their good deeds, they will do the good things again and gradually lead themselves to better behaviors. They may constantly do so and what's better, they can have an influence on others. Moreover, when they grow up to become others' teachers or even parents, they will treat their students or children good because they have a positive and optimistic attitude towards other people. They will not just scold or punish strictly to achieve the effects they want.
Even though many people now still choose to use punishment to gain effective results, I always support the encouraging and rewarding measures.

subject: HW1001
content:
There are two main methods in teaching young, punishing and rewarding. Both of them are widely used around the world.
Punishing is a very clear and direct way to teach the children that they are doing wrong and should never act like that again. The pain that children receive can make them remember deeply what kind of consequences will they have if they do the wrong things.
In the other hand, rewarding is to give some good stuffs or compliment after the children done something right. It not only makes them happy but also strengthens their motivations to do the right things again and again.
As you can see, punishing tells the children what is wrong while rewarding tells them what is right. The differences between these two methods appear after the children grow up.
One of my classmates comes from a high school which has strict teachers using punishments to teach the students. After he came to the college, he lost the pressure from teacher. Although he knows what kind of things he should not do, he doesn't know what should he do. As a result, he has a poor life in college.
In my opinion, rewarding is totally a more effective way to teach students. It gives students motivations and the ability of facing future. Therefore, teachers should try to reward students instead of punishing them.

subject: HW1001
content:
Many teachers punish students because they don't study or have worse behavior. Every night, many news like that is on TV. The teacher punishes the student and his parents fight with teacher and his school. Now, many people start to care about that the teachers should punish the students or not.
I think the punishment is a good way to teach students, but not to punish too heavy. Now the children are difficult to teach, because the internet and the television can change their behavior. Maybe use the punishment and the presents that if they done well together will be better. I was a teacher before. I still punished my students but I also gave them a little toy to made them happy. So that, they knew what they should did and when they became naughty they will have punishment. I think this is a good way to teach student. Always punishes students will make your students just like a robot. One order, one move. Try this method, I believe it will be very useful. So that, I can seldom watch this kind of news on the television.

subject: HW1001
content: Punishment is commonly used in schools and at home to teach children to behave, but I doubt its necessity and efficiency. Personally, I prefer rewards over punishments. First of all, punishment does not work on all children. A naughty, undisciplined student may not be intimidated by beatings, detention and extra work. In this case, no matter how harsh and unpleasant the consequences, the student still will not learn. For example, my cousin brother currently in high school often gets in trouble for helping his friends. He argues with teachers to support his friends and is willing to accept a zero on his test to help a friend cheat. He has misbehaved for the last three years and still behaves in this manner. However, even if the method was effective, the child has only learned to avoid the treatment, if so, once the punishment is removed, the child would be aimless. Another reason punishment is ineffective is the temporary effects it may leave behind. Certain punishment may be too harsh and unconsciously affect the child in later years. The motivation to perform an activity would be fear instead of a positive force. Although I prefer rewarding, rewards should not be materialistic and should be given randomly. In other words occassional compliments or surprises, to prevent spoiling the child.

subject: HW1001
content:
The important of teaching can not be emphasized more. With time going by, teachers and parents have been bombarded with various information about how to motivate children. Some say punishment can lead to responsible kids as they then know what are not right. Others oppose as they see punishment a negative way of teaching and will discourage the creativeness of kids. Rewarding on the other hand can be more effective.
I personally agree with the latter. Everyone, even kid has dignity and self-esteem. I believe by using punishment as the mean of teaching will gradually erode one's dignity. The result may be lack of confidence, unwilling to take responsibility as they're afraid to try. On the contrary, if we motivated kids with rewards, they would be more positive in attitude. They will repeat the right behaviors to get rewards. They will also be more confident, outgoing and motivated.
I'm the mother of two. I have a twenty-year old son and a seventeen-year old daughter. When my son was a little boy, I didn't understand the better way of teaching hence use punishment more. The situation was different when I taught my daughter as I used encouragement and rewarding more. The results are very different. My son tends to be more reluctant in taking responsibility while my daughter is another story. She's positive and creative.
For teachers and parents, I'll always give advice on applying rewarding as I know from my experience that it will be more effective.

subject: HW1001
content:
Lack of motivation to learn is usually the main problem for all students. Punishment and rewards are normally the two methods to deal with the problem. In my opinion, the latter is the better. When a student being punished, the ordinary result is that he learns harder, but this is due to your authority. Without your authority, they won't learn by themselves. The motivation they have is to escape from punish. On the other hand, when reward is what he gets when he learns well. At first, he works hard to get the reward, but gradually the motivation changes. It becomes to impress others and fulfill his esteem. Learning becomes a self-motivated fun, not just a difficult demand. In this way, he would continue to learn so on forever.
I used to help my younger sister to learn better. Punish is what my parents used to do with her, but they failed. My sister loves to work on her own little things in leisure time, so I tried to talk my parents in for giving her longer time on her own if she learned better. The time she studied increased and she started to ask me to help her. Eventually she got better grades and now my parents need not to concern about her learning status anymore.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, rewarding students for learning and praising them for their good deeds is definitely a more effective method. Because there are no students but like to be rewarded. Everyone wants to be treated in a positive and friendly way. Positive words can motivate students to work more diligently while passive words only make them feel angry or depressed. For the same reason, rewarding students can definitely lead to better results than punishing them.
Take my father's experience for example. My dad is a physics teacher in senior high school, who has over twenty years of teaching experience under his belt. At the beginning of his teaching career, he used to punish students a lot and scold them for the mistakes they made. Therefore, the relationship between my dad and his students was extremely unpleasant. However, my father started to practice a new teaching method recently. He rewarded students for their good performances on schoolwork and praised them for their well behavior. He discoverd that students became more obedient and friendly to him under this kind of teaching method.
To sum up, I think teachers should treat their students in a positive and rewarding way. Not only can this kind of teaching method makes relationships between both sides better, but it can also motivate and inspire students more.

subject: HW1001
content:
Playing a good role of teacher is like an art. Therefore, I conceive that punishing and rewarding students are both important. Teacher can use those in balance. There is my experience below and I am going to share it with you.
When I teach students who can't behave themselves, I try to give them oral warning. Sometimes it works. And it depends on students' reactions. The more serious misbehaviors are, the more punishments I will give students.
In the contrast, there are also good students in my class. I encourage students to learn as more as posible. I carry on the "token economy", and I find they enjoy the rule very much.
In sum up, my suggestion is that the teachers should be student-centered. Teachers can observe students' performance and then give them feedback. In this way, students' learning condition may become better.

subject: HW1001
content:
It has been forever debated whether a child raised by "whips" will stand a better chance at succeeding in life, or a child raised by "lips"! In the past, people mostly had the same stereotype, that if you "spare the rod", you "spoil the child". As a result, I often hear my parents brag about how hard it was for them and how well they did with all the punishments of their time. Every time I do, I feel angry, startled and, most of all, relieved that I was born in a different generation than theirs.
Personally, I hate punishments and strongly opt for rewards. There are millions of ways to mistakes but there's only one way of doing things right! If we do this statistically, the odds of getting something done correctly would be harder than getting hit by an asteroid! Despite my exaggeration, it is irrevocably true that humans are prone to make mistakes. Even Homer nods, let alone the students in school who haven't even got a true glance at the world! To add punishment to their already-depressed-hearts could only worsen the condition.
Instead, why not use encouragement, one of the powerful and effective meathods ever? I remember a line Denzel Washington said in one of his movies "Crimson Seas". At times of tension, what men need is a kick in butt, or a pat on the back!" I truly believe the benefits of rewarding students outweighs that of punishing them.
Nevertheless, punishment still holds gravity in the journey of a child's education. It provides discipline and order and even yet obedience which even encouraging won't bring. It is apparent the punishment can't be completely neglected. An aggressive student may pay no heed to sincere words but cower before the wrath of the stick. There are, I am sad to admit, times when speech becomes meaningless and only strict penalties may triumph and serve their just cause.
Having thoroughly thought about the pros and cons, it becomes evident to me that the two styles are both irreplaceable in their own way. While rewards can motivate students to work hard and accomplish challenges by their own passion and will, punishments may enforce regulations and rules that just can't be broken. So my conclusion is to use both in a very clever, well-balanced way. Only by striking a balance between the two can a student really recieve a good education.
My own homeroom teacher is the best of examples. She is a young-aged woman who understands and better yet identifies with us. Though she mainly uses kind words and calm tones with us, she does emphasize sternly the importance of obeying class rules. Whenever a student, whether deliberate or not, errs, she still would execute punishment. She later then explains to the student why she did that, and explains what he should do to improve. A loving teacher with good approaches as such is just what our education system needs today! In short, the "balance" is crucial!

subject: HW1001
