content: In my opinion, punishment is more effective than reward for students. Because nowadays, students' live are better than students in the past: They can get whatever they want from their parents. Therefore, the reward which is provided by teacher might be too common to attract the children. Moreover, rewarding students for learning could probably give students a wrong concept that once they study hard, they will definitely receive some rewards. For instance, when I was still in elementary school, my teacher usually punished students who would not study hard instead of rewarding students for learning. She seldom gave rewards for us. And she also considered that punishment would force you to beware of what you were doing. Therefore I agree with the idea that punishment is more effective than reward.

subject: HW1001
content:
In my opinion, teachers play an very important role in our lives. What they do or what they say might affect students forever. I think teachers should punish students only when they have bad behaviors. However, when it comes to "bad grades", I don't think teachers should blame students for having a bad grade. Not every student has interests in studying, so they should encourage them to find another interests instead. It might make it worse if teachers keep pushing students to do something they don't even want to do.
On the contrary, if teachers could reward students for doing something impressive or remarkable, students might be willing to try something different but not scare to be punished. They might find their own ability and interest during the pursuit of being rewarded. I think rewarding might be a better method than punishment.
When I was a little girl, I saw my teacher use her ruler to punish my best friend. The tears and horrified face on her face sticked with me until now. I can't get rid of the terrible memories at all and I am still trembling when it crosses my mind. Not to mention what happened to my best friend then. She became so angry and hated everything. Because of the teacher, she can't feel happiness anymore. Punishment is not the only way to motivate or teach students. Rewarding is a better way to encourage students to do something they actually can do and will do the best effort they could.

subject: HW1001
content:
Some teachers use punishment to motivate students to learn and to control their behaviour. Others believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results.
In my opinion, though, I firmly believe that the latter can achieve better outcomes. I have a number of supporting points to prove and explain my perspective. Firstly, speaking from my own experience, I have reason to believe that punishment is only detrimental. In my childhood, there was one teacher who believed in physical punishment. He beat naughty children, threatened them and verbally abused them whenever possible, to no result at all. To sum up, he somehow turned my first year at elementary school into a nightmare.
On the other hand, I have also met the most caring and loving teacher anyone's ever had. Year seven was the best school year of my life thanks to Miss Stewart. She prayed for each of us every morning, and helped out every single problem that came through. Most importantly, she used rewards to help us focus on our goals. That year, I was awarded three trophies all due to her help. As you can see, rewarding students is a far better way to encourage and motivate the students than to beat them and resulting in lack of confidence.

subject: HW1001
content: I believe that rewarding students for learning can lead to better results. When you set a goal and tell the students they will get an iPhone 4 as a reward. They will study harder for the iPhone. On the other hand, punishing the students is the worst thing. In this moment, kids are carefully protected by their parents. They can't be punished, otherwise parents will sue the teacher. Punishing them can also reduce their motivation. In my own cram school, there is a teacher who scold students almost every moment. You can hear his voice even you're still 100 meters away. Therefore, every student is unwill to study, so they get poor grades. The other one, who is tender and patient. She always encourages students with positive words, and provides notebooks, pens and so on as reward when they really do well on their study. That's why I believe rewarding and encouraging students for learning will lead to better results.
